50. अनवद्य-अङ्गी
अनवद्य = faultless, flawless, beyond criticism
अङ्गी = one possessing limbs/body
51. सर्वाभरणभूषिता (Sarvābharaṇa-bhūṣitā)
Pada Cheda

सर्व-आभरण-भूषिता

Word-by-Word Meaning
सर्व = all
आभरण = ornaments, adornments
भूषिता = adorned, decorated
Vigraha

सर्वैः आभरणैः भूषिता।

Overall Meaning

"She who is adorned with every kind of ornament."

52. शिवकामेश्वराङ्कस्था (Śiva-kāmeśvarāṅkasthā)
Pada Cheda

शिव-कामेश्वर-अङ्क-स्था

Word-by-Word Meaning
शिव = Śiva
कामेश्वर = Kāmeśvara
अङ्क = lap, bosom
स्था = seated, abiding
Vigraha

शिवकामेश्वरस्य अङ्के स्थिता।

Overall Meaning

"She who is seated on the lap of Śiva-Kāmeśvara."

53. शिवा (Śivā)
Pada Cheda

शिवा

Word-by-Word Meaning
शिवा = Auspicious One; feminine form of Śiva
Vigraha

शिवं कल्याणं ददातीति शिवा।

or

शिवस्य शक्तिरूपा शिवा।

Overall Meaning

"The Auspicious Goddess, the Divine Power of Śiva."

54. स्वाधीनवल्लभा (Svādhīna-vallabhā)
Pada Cheda

स्व-अधीन-वल्लभा

Word-by-Word Meaning
स्व = her own
अधीन = devoted to, under the influence of
वल्लभ = beloved, husband, dear one
Vigraha

स्वाधीनः वल्लभः यस्याः सा।

Overall Meaning

"She whose beloved Lord is completely devoted to her."

Combined Meaning

"The Goddess whose entire form shines with a rosy-red hue, whose limbs are flawless, who is adorned with all ornaments, who is seated on the lap of Śiva-Kāmeśvara, who is the auspicious Divine Power of Śiva, and whose beloved Lord is completely devoted to her."

सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था श्रीमन्नगरनायिका । चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था पञ्चब्रह्मासनस्थिता

---

## सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था श्रीमन्नगरनायिका । चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था पञ्चब्रह्मासनस्थिता

*sumeru-madhya-śṛṅgasthā śrīmannagara-nāyikā । cintāmaṇi-gṛhāntasthā pañcabrahmāsana-sthitā*

55. सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था (Sumeru-madhya-śṛṅga-sthā)
Pada Cheda

सुमेरु-मध्य-शृङ्ग-स्था
sumeru-madhya-śṛṅga-sthā

Word-by-Word Meaning
सुमेरु (sumeru) = Mount Meru, the golden axial mountain (सु = excellent, golden + मेरु = Meru)
मध्य (madhya) = middle, central
शृङ्ग (śṛṅga) = peak, summit
स्था (sthā) = abiding, dwelling, seated
Vigraha

सुमेरोः मध्यशृङ्गे स्थिता या सा।

Overall Meaning

"She who dwells on the central peak of Mount Meru." — Of Meru's three summits, the middle one bears Her city.

56. श्रीमन्नगरनायिका (Śrīman-nagara-nāyikā)
Pada Cheda

श्रीमत्-नगर-नायिका
śrīmat-nagara-nāyikā

Sandhi: श्रीमत् + नगर → श्रीमन्नगर। The final त् before the nasal न् assimilates in nasality (Pāṇini 8.4.45, यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा), giving न् + न → न्न। The visible न्न is thus a joint, not a doubled root consonant.

Word-by-Word Meaning
श्रीमत् (śrīmat) = possessing श्री — splendour, auspiciousness, prosperity (श्री + मतुप्; nominative श्रीमान्, stem श्रीमत् in composition)
नगर (nagara) = city — here Śrīnagara / Śrīpura, the city on Meru's middle peak, where the previous nama has just placed us
नायिका (nāyikā) = mistress, sovereign lady, leader (feminine of नायक, from नी "to lead": नी + ण्वुल् → नायक)
Vigraha

श्रीमतः नगरस्य नायिका। — ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa.

Overall Meaning

"The Sovereign Lady of the resplendent City."

Two readings are current:

1. Descriptive — श्रीमत् qualifies नगर: the city possesses श्री, and She rules it.
2. Proper name — श्रीमन्नगर taken as the city's own name (Śrīmannagara = Śrīnagara / Śrīpura), hence "the Lady of Śrīnagara." Bhāskararāya reads the compound this way.

Note: 55–58 form a nested descent inward — Meru's middle peak (55) → the city upon it (56) → the cintāmaṇi palace within the city (57) → the pañcabrahma seat within the palace (58). This nama is the second ring. The root नी here also anticipates Her sovereign and commander namas in the Bhaṇḍāsura war section.

57. चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था (Cintāmaṇi-gṛhāntaḥ-sthā)
Pada Cheda

चिन्तामणि-गृह-अन्तः-स्था
cintāmaṇi-gṛha-antaḥ-sthā

Word-by-Word Meaning
चिन्ता (cintā) = thought, wish
मणि (maṇi) = gem → चिन्तामणि = the wish-fulfilling gem
गृह (gṛha) = house, palace, mansion
अन्तः (antaḥ) = within, inside
स्था (sthā) = abiding, seated
Vigraha

चिन्तामणिगृहस्य अन्तः स्थिता।

Overall Meaning

"She who abides within the palace built of wish-fulfilling gems." — The Cintāmaṇi-gṛha stands at the heart of Śrīnagara.

58. पञ्चब्रह्मासनस्थिता (Pañca-brahmāsana-sthitā)
Pada Cheda

पञ्च-ब्रह्म-आसन-स्थिता
pañca-brahma-āsana-sthitā

Word-by-Word Meaning
पञ्च (pañca) = five
ब्रह्म (brahma) = the Brahmas — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva
आसन (āsana) = seat, couch
स्थिता (sthitā) = seated, established, firmly abiding
Vigraha

पञ्चब्रह्ममयम् आसनम्, तस्मिन् स्थिता।

Overall Meaning

"She who is seated on the couch formed of the five Brahmās." — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara form its four legs; Sadāśiva is the plank (फलक) on which She rests.

Combined Meaning

"She who abides on the central peak of Mount Meru, the Sovereign Lady of the resplendent City, dwelling within the palace of wish-fulfilling gems, seated upon the couch formed of the five Brahmās."


महापद्माटवीसंस्था कदम्बवनवासिनी । सुधासागरमध्यस्था कामाक्षी कामदायिनी

59. महापद्माटवीसंस्था → महा-पद्म-अटवी-संस्था

महा = great, vast
पद्म = lotus
अटवी = forest, wilderness
संस्था = fully abiding (सम् intensifier + स्था)
"She who abides in the vast forest of great lotuses."

60. कदम्बवनवासिनी → कदम्ब-वन-वासिनी

कदम्ब = the kadamba tree
वन = grove, forest
वासिनी = she who dwells (from वस्)
"She who dwells in the grove of kadamba trees."

61. सुधासागरमध्यस्था → सुधा-सागर-मध्य-स्था

सुधा = nectar, ambrosia
सागर = ocean
मध्य = midst
स्था = abiding
"She who abides in the midst of the ocean of nectar."

62. कामाक्षी → काम-अक्षी

काम = desire, love; also Kāma
अक्षी = eye, eyes
"She whose eyes are filled with love" — or, taking काम as the object given, "whose glance grants what is desired."

63. कामदायिनी → काम-दायिनी

काम = desire, the thing desired
दायिनी = bestower (from दा)
"She who bestows all that is desired."

Note on 59: the compound splits at पद्म + अटवी (a → ā), so the surface महापद्माटवी hides a four-member sequence rather than three. And संस्था here carries the सम् prefix, a slight intensification over the plain स्था used in the previous verse's namas.


64. देवर्षिगणसंघातस्तूयमानात्मवैभवा → देव-ऋषि-गण-संघात-स्तूयमान-आत्म-वैभवा

देव = gods, celestials
ऋषि = seers, sages (देव + ऋषि → देवर्षि, अ + ऋ → अर्)
गण = host, troop, band
संघात = assemblage, massed multitude (सम् + घात)
स्तूयमान = being praised, being hymned (passive participle of स्तु "to praise")
आत्म = own, her own self
वैभव = glory, majesty, greatness
"She whose own glory is hymned by the massed hosts of gods and sages."

Vigraha: देवर्षिगणसंघातैः स्तूयमानम् आत्मवैभवं यस्याः सा।

65. भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्तशक्तिसेनासमन्विता → भण्डासुर-वध-उद्युक्त-शक्ति-सेना-समन्विता

भण्ड = Bhaṇḍa, the demon's name
असुर = demon → भण्डासुर = the demon Bhaṇḍāsura
वध = slaying, killing
उद्युक्त = girded up, ready, intent upon (उत् + युक्त; वध + उद्युक्त → वधोद्युक्त)
शक्ति = the Śaktis, Her divine powers
सेना = army, host
समन्विता = accompanied by, attended by (सम् + अनु + इता)
"She who is attended by the army of Śaktis girded for the slaying of Bhaṇḍāsura."

Vigraha: भण्डासुरस्य वधाय उद्युक्ताभिः शक्तिसेनाभिः समन्विता।


66. संपत्करीसमारूढसिंधुरव्रजसेविता → सम्पत्करी-समारूढ-सिन्धुर-व्रज-सेविता

सम्पत् = wealth, abundance; करी = maker (fem.) → सम्पत्करी = Sampatkarī, commander of Her elephant division
समारूढ = mounted upon (सम् + आ + रूढ, from रुह्)
सिन्धुर = elephant
व्रज = herd, troop
सेविता = attended, served
"She who is attended by the elephant host led by Sampatkarī, seated upon it."

67. अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वकोटिकोटिभिरावृता → अश्वारूढा-अधिष्ठित-अश्व-कोटि-कोटिभिः-आवृता

अश्व = horse; आरूढा = mounted → अश्वारूढा = Aśvārūḍhā, commander of Her cavalry
अधिष्ठित = marshalled, presided over (अधि + स्थित)
अश्व = steed
कोटि = a crore → कोटिकोटिभिः = by crores upon crores (instr. pl.)
आवृता = surrounded, encompassed (आ + वृत्)
"She who is encompassed by crores upon crores of steeds marshalled by Aśvārūḍhā."

Nama 66 pairs with 65: the Śakti army named there is now itemized by division — elephants under Sampatkarī, cavalry under Aśvārūḍhā.

One correction to the pasted line: you had कोठिकोटिभिः; it's कोटिकोटिभिरावृता (ट, not ठ). I used the corrected form in the file. The सिंधुर/सिन्धुर difference is just anusvāra vs. conjunct spelling — both are current, and I kept your anusvāra form in the verse line while using the conjunct in the split.


68. चक्रराजरथारूढसर्वायुधपरिष्कृता → चक्रराज-रथ-आरूढ-सर्व-आयुध-परिष्कृता

चक्र = wheel, disc; also the Śrīcakra
राज = king, chief → चक्रराज = Cakrarāja, the sovereign cakra, here the name of Her own nine-tiered chariot
रथ = chariot
आरूढ = mounted upon, having ascended (आ + रूढ, from रुह्)
सर्व = all, every
आयुध = weapon
परिष्कृता = fully equipped, furnished, decked out (परि + कृता, with ष् by the ruki rule)
"She who, mounted upon the chariot Cakrarāja, is fully equipped with every weapon."

Vigraha: चक्रराजरथम् आरूढा सर्वायुधैः परिष्कृता।

69. गेयचक्ररथारूढमन्त्रिणीपरिसेविता → गेयचक्र-रथ-आरूढ-मन्त्रिणी-परिसेविता

गेय = that which is to be sung, song, music (from गै "to sing")
चक्र = wheel, cakra → गेयचक्र = Geyacakra, the "chariot of song"
रथ = chariot
आरूढ = mounted upon
मन्त्रिणी = the Minister — Śyāmalā (Rāja-mātaṅgī), Her prime minister (feminine of मन्त्रिन्)
परिसेविता = closely attended upon, waited on all round (परि + सेविता)
"She who is closely attended by the Minister Śyāmalā, mounted upon the Geyacakra chariot."

Vigraha: गेयचक्ररथम् आरूढया मन्त्रिण्या परिसेविता।

Note: these two open the chariot sequence — 68 is the Goddess's own Cakrarāja, 69 the Geyacakra of Her minister Śyāmalā, and 70 follows with the Kiricakra of Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī).


70. किरिचक्ररथारूढदण्डनाथापुरस्कृता → किरिचक्र-रथ-आरूढ-दण्डनाथा-पुरस्कृता

किरि = boar, hog → किरिचक्र = Kiricakra, the "boar chariot" of Vārāhī
चक्र = wheel, cakra
रथ = chariot
आरूढ = mounted upon (आ + रूढ, from रुह्)
दण्ड = staff, rod, chastisement
नाथा = mistress, lady → दण्डनाथा = Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī), commander-in-chief, wielder of the rod of punishment
पुरस्कृता = placed in front, led by, honoured (पुरः + कृता)
"She who is preceded by Daṇḍanāthā, mounted upon the Kiricakra chariot."

Vigraha: किरिचक्ररथम् आरूढया दण्डनाथया पुरस्कृता।

71. ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तवह्निप्राकारमध्यगा → ज्वाला-मालिनिका-आक्षिप्त-वह्नि-प्राकार-मध्यगा

ज्वाला = flame, blaze
मालिनिका = the garlanded one (मालिनी + ka) → ज्वालामालिनिका = Jvālāmālinī, the Śakti garlanded with flames
आक्षिप्त = flung up, cast out, projected (आ + क्षिप्त, from क्षिप् "to throw")
वह्नि = fire
प्राकार = rampart, enclosing wall, fortification
मध्य = middle, centre
गा = abiding in, situated in (from गम्) → मध्यगा = she who dwells at the centre
"She who abides at the centre of the rampart of fire flung up by Jvālāmālinī."

Vigraha: ज्वालामालिनिकया आक्षिप्तस्य वह्निप्राकारस्य मध्यगा।

Note: 70 closes the chariot triad (Cakrarāja, Geyacakra, Kiricakra); 71 turns to the fiery rampart Jvālāmālinī threw up around the host in the war against Bhaṇḍāsura.

भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्तशक्तिविक्रमहर्षिता । नित्यापराक्रमाटोपनिरीक्षणसमुत्सुका

72. भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्तशक्तिविक्रमहर्षिता → भण्ड-सैन्य-वध-उद्युक्त-शक्ति-विक्रम-हर्षिता

भण्ड = Bhaṇḍa, i.e. Bhaṇḍāsura
सैन्य = army, host, forces (from सेना)
वध = slaying, slaughter
उद्युक्त = girded up, ready, intent upon (उत् + युक्त; वध + उद्युक्त → वधोद्युक्त)
शक्ति = the Śaktis, Her divine powers
विक्रम = valour, prowess, heroic stride
हर्षिता = delighted, gladdened (from हृष् "to rejoice")
"She who is delighted by the valour of the Śaktis girded for the slaughter of Bhaṇḍa's army."

Vigraha: भण्डसैन्यवधाय उद्युक्तानां शक्तीनां विक्रमेण हर्षिता।

73. नित्यापराक्रमाटोपनिरीक्षणसमुत्सुका → नित्या-पराक्रम-आटोप-निरीक्षण-समुत्सुका

नित्या = the Nityās, the fifteen eternal Śaktis of the lunar days
पराक्रम = might, valour, martial prowess (परा + क्रम)
आटोप = swelling, exuberance, imposing magnitude
निरीक्षण = beholding, looking on, witnessing (नि + ईक्षण)
समुत्सुका = keenly eager, full of longing (सम् + उत्सुका)
"She who is eager to behold the swelling valour of the Nityā deities."

Vigraha: नित्यानां पराक्रमाटोपस्य निरीक्षणे समुत्सुका।

Note: 72 answers 65 — there She is attended by the Śaktis girded to slay Bhaṇḍāsura himself, here gladdened by their prowess against his army. In 72–73 the Goddess is watcher rather than combatant: delighted, then eager to watch on.



74. भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालाविक्रमनन्दिता → भण्ड-पुत्र-वध-उद्युक्त-बाला-विक्रम-नन्दिता

भण्ड = Bhaṇḍa, i.e. Bhaṇḍāsura
पुत्र = son → भण्डपुत्र = the sons of Bhaṇḍāsura (thirty, per the Lalitopākhyāna)
वध = slaying
उद्युक्त = girded up, intent upon (उत् + युक्त; वध + उद्युक्त → वधोद्युक्त)
बाला = Bālā, the young Goddess Bālā Tripurasundarī, Her nine-year-old daughter
विक्रम = valour, prowess
नन्दिता = gladdened, made joyful (from नन्द् "to rejoice")
"She who is gladdened by the valour of Bālā, girded to slay the sons of Bhaṇḍāsura."

Vigraha: भण्डपुत्रवधाय उद्युक्तायाः बालायाः विक्रमेण नन्दिता।

75. मन्त्रिण्यम्बाविरचितविषङ्गवधतोषिता → मन्त्रिणी-अम्बा-विरचित-विषङ्ग-वध-तोषिता

मन्त्रिणी = the Minister, Śyāmalā (Rāja-mātaṅgī)
अम्बा = mother, revered lady → मन्त्रिण्यम्बा = Mother Mantriṇī (मन्त्रिणी + अम्बा → मन्त्रिण्यम्बा, ई + अ → य्अ)
विरचित = wrought, accomplished, brought about (वि + रचित)
विषङ्ग = Viṣaṅga, Bhaṇḍāsura's brother and general
वध = slaying
तोषिता = pleased, gratified, satisfied (from तुष् "to be content")
"She who is gratified by the slaying of Viṣaṅga wrought by Mother Mantriṇī."

Vigraha: मन्त्रिण्यम्बया विरचितेन विषङ्गवधेन तोषिता।

Note: 74–75 continue the spectator sequence, now naming who kills whom — Bālā takes Bhaṇḍāsura's sons, Mantriṇī takes his brother Viṣaṅga, and 76 gives Vārāhī the other brother, Viśukra.


76. विशुक्रप्राणहरणवाराहीवीर्यनन्दिता → विशुक्र-प्राण-हरण-वाराही-वीर्य-नन्दिता

विशुक्र = Viśukra, Bhaṇḍāsura's brother
प्राण = life, vital breath
हरण = taking away, carrying off (from हृ "to seize")
वाराही = Vārāhī, i.e. Daṇḍanāthā, the boar-faced commander-in-chief
वीर्य = might, heroism, valour
नन्दिता = gladdened, made joyful (from नन्द् "to rejoice")
"She who is gladdened by the might of Vārāhī in taking the life of Viśukra."

Vigraha: विशुक्रस्य प्राणहरणे वाराह्याः वीर्येण नन्दिता।

77. कामेश्वरमुखालोककल्पितश्रीगणेश्वरा → कामेश्वर-मुख-आलोक-कल्पित-श्री-गणेश्वरा

कामेश्वर = Kāmeśvara, Śiva as Her consort
मुख = face, countenance
आलोक = a look, glance, beholding (आ + लोक; मुख + आलोक → मुखालोक)
कल्पित = fashioned, brought into being, created
श्री = auspicious, glorious (honorific)
गणेश्वर = Lord of the gaṇas, Gaṇeśa → गणेश्वरा (feminine bahuvrīhi: "she by whom he was made")
"She who brought forth Śrī Gaṇeśvara by a glance at the face of Kāmeśvara."

Vigraha: कामेश्वरमुखालोकेन कल्पितः श्रीगणेश्वरः यया सा।

Note: 76 closes the roll of slain commanders — Bhaṇḍāsura's sons to Bālā, Viṣaṅga to Mantriṇī, Viśukra to Vārāhī. 77 turns to Viśukra's Jayavighna yantra, which had struck the host with torpor: at Her glance upon Kāmeśvara's face Gaṇeśa arose and broke the obstruction.



78. महागणेशनिर्भिन्नविघ्नयन्त्रप्रहर्षिता → महा-गणेश-निर्भिन्न-विघ्न-यन्त्र-प्रहर्षिता

महा = great
गणेश = Gaṇeśa → महागणेश = Mahāgaṇeśa, the great Gaṇeśa born of Her glance
निर्भिन्न = shattered, split apart, broken through (निः + भिन्न, from भिद् "to cleave")
विघ्न = obstacle, obstruction
यन्त्र = yantra, mystic device → विघ्नयन्त्र = the Jayavighna yantra of obstruction
प्रहर्षिता = greatly delighted, thrilled (प्र + हर्षिता, intensive of हृष्)
"She who was thrilled when Mahāgaṇeśa shattered the yantra of obstruction."

Vigraha: महागणेशेन निर्भिन्नं विघ्नयन्त्रं, तेन प्रहर्षिता।

79. भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तशस्त्रप्रत्यस्त्रवर्षिणी → भण्डासुर-इन्द्र-निर्मुक्त-शस्त्र-प्रत्यस्त्र-वर्षिणी

भण्डासुर = the demon Bhaṇḍa
इन्द्र = chief, foremost, lord → भण्डासुरेन्द्र = Bhaṇḍāsura, lord of the asuras
निर्मुक्त = released, discharged, let fly (निः + मुक्त)
शस्त्र = weapon, hurled or hand-held arm
प्रत्यस्त्र = counter-missile, answering astra (प्रति + अस्त्र)
वर्षिणी = she who rains down, showers forth (from वृष् "to rain")
"She who rains down counter-missiles against the weapons discharged by Bhaṇḍāsura, lord of demons."

Vigraha: भण्डासुरेन्द्रेण निर्मुक्तेषु शस्त्रेषु प्रत्यस्त्राणि वर्षतीति।

Note: शस्त्र and अस्त्र are not interchangeable — शस्त्र is the ordinary weapon, अस्त्र the missile impelled by mantra, so प्रत्यस्त्र is the mantra-answer to what he throws. 79 is also where the Goddess stops watching and enters the fight Herself.


80. कराङ्गुलिनखोत्पन्ननारायणदशाकृतिः → कर-अङ्गुलि-नख-उत्पन्न-नारायण-दश-आकृतिः

कर = hand; अङ्गुलि = finger; नख = nail → कराङ्गुलिनख = Her fingernails
उत्पन्न = sprung forth, arisen (उत् + पन्न)
नारायण = Nārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu
दश = ten; आकृति = form → दशाकृतिः = the ten forms, the ten avatāras
"She from whose fingernails sprang forth the ten forms of Nārāyaṇa."

81. महापाशुपतास्त्राग्निनिर्दग्धासुरसैनिका → महा-पाशुपत-अस्त्र-अग्नि-निर्दग्ध-असुर-सैनिका

महा = great, supreme
पाशुपत = of Paśupati (Śiva) → महापाशुपतास्त्र, Śiva's supreme missile
अस्त्र = mantra-impelled missile
अग्नि = fire
निर्दग्ध = burnt utterly (निः + दग्ध, from दह्)
असुर = demon; सैनिक = soldier → सैनिका, feminine to agree with Her
"She by whom the demon soldiery was burnt to ash in the fire of the great Pāśupata missile."

Nama 81 chains three a + a → ā joins in a row (पाशुपत+अस्त्र, अस्त्र+अग्नि, निर्दग्ध+असुर), which is why the surface form hides so many members.

OCR fix: करागुलि → कराङ्गुलि — the ङ्गु ligature dropped its ङ्, a common loss in scanned Devanagari. Note also that 80 ends in a visarga (दशाकृतिः, an -i stem nominative), unlike the -ā endings around it; worth keeping when you recite the pair.
कामेश्वरास्त्रनिर्दग्धसभण्डासुरशून्यका । ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवसंस्तुतवैभवा

82. कामेश्वरास्त्रनिर्दग्धसभण्डासुरशून्यका → कामेश्वर-अस्त्र-निर्दग्ध-स-भण्डासुर-शून्यका

कामेश्वर = Kāmeśvara, Her consort → कामेश्वरास्त्र = the Kāmeśvara missile
अस्त्र = missile, weapon impelled by mantra
निर्दग्ध = burnt down utterly, reduced to ash (निः + दग्ध, from दह्)
स = together with, along with (the prefix स in the sense of सह)
भण्डासुर = Bhaṇḍāsura → सभण्डासुर = together with Bhaṇḍāsura
शून्यक = Śūnyaka, Bhaṇḍāsura's capital city (शून्य = empty, void) → शून्यका (feminine bahuvrīhi, agreeing with Her)
"She by whom Śūnyaka, along with Bhaṇḍāsura himself, was burnt to ash by the Kāmeśvara missile."

Vigraha: कामेश्वरास्त्रेण निर्दग्धं सभण्डासुरं शून्यकं यया सा।

83. ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवसंस्तुतवैभवा → ब्रह्म-उपेन्द्र-महेन्द्र-आदि-देव-संस्तुत-वैभवा

ब्रह्म = Brahmā (ब्रह्म in compound; ब्रह्म + उपेन्द्र → ब्रह्मोपेन्द्र)
उपेन्द्र = Upendra, Viṣṇu — "the younger Indra" (उप + इन्द्र)
महेन्द्र = Mahendra, the great Indra (महा + इन्द्र)
आदि = beginning with, and the rest
देव = gods, celestials
संस्तुत = fully extolled, praised in chorus (सम् + स्तुत, from स्तु)
वैभव = glory, majesty, greatness → वैभवा (feminine bahuvrīhi)
"She whose glory is extolled by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra and the other gods."

Vigraha: ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिभिः देवैः संस्तुतं वैभवं यस्याः सा।

Note: 82 ends the war — the city Śūnyaka burns with its lord. 83 answers 64: there Her glory was hymned by the massed hosts of gods and sages, here by the chief gods named one by one, with the victory now behind it.



84. हरनेत्राग्निसंदग्धकामसंजीवनौषधिः → हर-नेत्र-अग्नि-संदग्ध-काम-संजीवन-औषधिः

हर = Hara, Śiva, "the remover"
नेत्र = eye — here the third eye
अग्नि = fire → नेत्राग्नि = the fire of that eye
संदग्ध = wholly burnt, consumed (सम् + दग्ध, from दह् "to burn")
काम = Kāma, Manmatha, the god of love
संजीवन = restoring to life, reviving (सम् + जीवन)
औषधिः = healing herb, medicament (संजीवन + औषधि → संजीवनौषधि, अ + औ → औ)
"She who is the life-restoring herb for Kāma, burnt to ash by the fire of Hara's eye."

Vigraha: हरनेत्राग्निना संदग्धस्य कामस्य संजीवनौषधिः।

85. श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटैकस्वरूपमुखपङ्कजा → श्रीमत्-वाग्भव-कूट-एक-स्वरूप-मुख-पङ्कजा

श्रीमत् = glorious, resplendent (श्रीमत् + वाग्भव → श्रीमद्वाग्भव, त् → द् before voiced व)
वाग्भव = the Vāgbhava kūṭa, first segment of the Pañcadaśī mantra (वाक् = speech + भव = origin, "the source of speech")
कूट = peak, segment, cluster — a kūṭa of the mantra
एक = one, sole, single (कूट + एक → कूटैक, अ + ए → ऐ)
स्वरूप = own form, essential nature
मुख = face
पङ्कज = lotus (पङ्क = mud + ज = born) → मुखपङ्कजा = she whose face is a lotus
"She whose lotus face is one in essence with the glorious Vāgbhava kūṭa."

Vigraha: श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटस्य एकस्वरूपं मुखपङ्कजं यस्याः सा।

Note: 84 pivots from war to grace — the Kāma burnt in the old myth is revived by Her. 85 opens the mantra-body sequence: the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī are mapped onto Her form, Vāgbhava as the face here, Kāmarāja from neck to waist in 86, and the Śakti kūṭa below the waist in 87.


86. कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्तमध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी → कण्ठ-अधः-कटि-पर्यन्त-मध्य-कूट-स्वरूपिणी

कण्ठ = throat, neck
अधः = below, beneath (कण्ठ + अधः → कण्ठाधः)
कटि = waist, hip
पर्यन्त = extending as far as, up to (परि + अन्त)
मध्य = middle
कूट = segment of the mantra → मध्यकूट = the middle kūṭa, i.e. the Kāmarāja kūṭa
स्वरूपिणी = she who has that as her very form (स्वरूप + इनी)
"She whose form from below the throat down to the waist is the middle, Kāmarāja, kūṭa."

Vigraha: कण्ठात् अधः कटिपर्यन्तं मध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी।

87. शक्तिकूटैकतापन्नकट्यधोभागधारिणी → शक्ति-कूट-एकता-आपन्न-कटि-अधः-भाग-धारिणी

शक्ति = Śakti, power → शक्तिकूट = the third segment of the Pañcadaśī
कूट = segment, peak
एकता = oneness, identity (एक + ता; कूट + एकता → कूटैकता, अ + ए → ऐ)
आपन्न = attained, come into, arrived at (आ + पन्न; एकता + आपन्न → एकतापन्न)
कटि = waist
अधः = below (कटि + अधः → कट्यधः, इ + अ → य्)
भाग = part, portion
धारिणी = she who bears, carries (from धृ "to bear")
"She who bears the portion below the waist as having become one with the Śakti kūṭa."

Vigraha: शक्तिकूटेन एकताम् आपन्नं कट्यधोभागं धारयतीति।

Note: 85–87 close the triad — Vāgbhava as the face, Kāmarāja from throat to waist, Śakti kūṭa below it. The three namas together say that the Pañcadaśī mantra and Her body are one thing, so that reciting the mantra is itself the worship of Her form.


88. मूलमन्त्रात्मिका → मूल-मन्त्र-आत्मिका

मूल = root, original, fundamental
मन्त्र = mantra → मूलमन्त्र = the root mantra, the Pañcadaśī (or Ṣoḍaśī)
आत्मिका = whose self or essence it is (from आत्मन्, feminine)
"She whose very self is the root mantra."

Vigraha: मूलमन्त्रः आत्मा यस्याः सा।

89. मूलकूटत्रयकलेबरा → मूल-कूट-त्रय-कलेबरा

मूल = root → मूलकूट = the kūṭas of the root mantra
कूट = segment, peak
त्रय = triad, the three
कलेबर = body, bodily frame (variant of कलेवर) → कलेबरा (feminine)
"She whose body is the three kūṭas of the root mantra."

Vigraha: मूलमन्त्रस्य कूटत्रयं कलेबरं यस्याः सा।

90. कुलामृतैकरसिका → कुल-अमृत-एक-रसिका

कुल = the Kula, the Kaula lineage and its inner meaning
अमृत = nectar, ambrosia (कुल + अमृत → कुलामृत)
एक = one, sole, alone (अमृत + एक → अमृतैक, अ + ए → ऐ)
रसिका = she who savours, relishes, has a taste for (from रस "flavour, relish")
"She who delights in the nectar of Kula alone."

Vigraha: कुलामृतम् एकम् एव रसयतीति।

91. कुलसंकेतपालिनी → कुल-संकेत-पालिनी

कुल = the Kaula tradition
संकेत = secret sign, esoteric convention, agreed code (सम् + केत)
पालिनी = protectress, guardian (from पाल् "to protect")
"She who guards the secret conventions of the Kula tradition."

Vigraha: कुलसंकेतं पालयतीति कुलसंकेतपालिनी।

Note: 88–89 carry the mantra-body identity of 85–87 to its conclusion — first the mantra as Her self, then its three kūṭas as Her frame. 90–91 then turn to the Kaula transmission that guards it. कलेबर and कलेवर are both attested; the ब/व interchange is normal, and LSN editions usually print कलेबरा.



92. कुलाङ्गना → कुल-अङ्गना

कुल = family, noble lineage; in Śrīvidyā, the Kula — Śakti, the mūlādhāra
अङ्गना = woman, lady, one of graceful limbs (from अङ्ग "limb")
"The Lady of the Kula" — she who is the woman of that noble house.

93. कुलान्तस्था → कुल-अन्तः-स्था

कुल = the Kula (also read as the mūlādhāra, or the assembly of tattvas)
अन्तः = within, inside
स्था = abiding, seated
"She who abides within the Kula."

Vigraha: कुलस्य अन्तः स्थिता।

94. कौलिनी → कौलिनी (vṛddhi derivative of कुल)

कुल → कौल = belonging to the Kula, of the Kaula path
कौलिनी = the presiding Goddess of Kaula worship; the Śakti in the mūlādhāra who joins kula (Śakti) to akula (Śiva)
"She who is the Deity of the Kaula path."

95. कुलयोगिनी → कुल-योगिनी

कुल = the Kula
योगिनी = yoginī, female adept; she who is joined, who unites (from युज् "to yoke")
"The Yoginī of the Kula."

96. अकुला → अ-कुला

अ = not, beyond (negative prefix)
कुल = kula → अकुल = that which is past kula; in Kaula usage Akula is Śiva, seated in the sahasrāra, as Kula is Śakti
"She who is Akula — beyond the Kula, one with Śiva."

97. समयान्तस्था → समय-अन्तः-स्था

समय = the Samaya doctrine and its worship; literally agreement, convention — also read as सम + अय, the state in which Śiva and Śakti are equal
अन्तः = within
स्था = abiding
"She who abides within the Samaya path."

Vigraha: समयस्य अन्तः स्थिता।

98. समयाचारतत्परा → समय-आचार-तत्परा

समय = the Samaya doctrine (समय + आचार → समयाचार)
आचार = practice, observance, prescribed conduct
तत्पर = intent upon, holding that as highest (तत् + पर) → तत्परा (feminine)
"She who is devoted to the observances of the Samaya path."

Note: 92–96 belong to the Kaula reckoning and 97–98 to the Samaya, the two being the outer and the inner worship — Samaya performed within the six cakras and held the higher by Bhāskararāya. The sequence honours both, and 96 अकुला is the hinge: having been named through Kula five times, She is then named as what lies past it. अन्तस्था in 93 and 97 is अन्तः + स्था with the visarga assimilated, as in 57 चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था.



99. मूलाधारैकनिलया → मूल-आधार-एक-निलया

मूल = root
आधार = support, base, foundation → मूलाधार = the root-support cakra at the base of the spine
एक = one, sole, alone (आधार + एक → आधारैक, अ + ए → ऐ)
निलया = abode, dwelling; she whose abode it is (नि + लय)
"She whose sole abode is the mūlādhāra."

Vigraha: मूलाधारः एकः निलयः यस्याः सा।

100. ब्रह्मग्रन्थिविभेदिनी → ब्रह्म-ग्रन्थि-विभेदिनी

ब्रह्म = Brahmā → ब्रह्मग्रन्थि = the Brahma-knot, first of the three obstructing knots, at the mūlādhāra
ग्रन्थि = knot, node, tie (from ग्रन्थ् "to bind")
विभेदिनी = she who splits open, pierces, sunders (वि + भेदिनी, from भिद् "to cleave")
"She who pierces the Brahma-knot."

Vigraha: ब्रह्मग्रन्थिं विभिनत्तीति।

101. मणिपूरान्तरुदिता → मणिपूर-अन्तः-उदिता

मणि = gem, jewel
पूर = filled, replete; also city → मणिपूर = the navel cakra, "the one filled with gems"
अन्तः = within, inside (मणिपूर + अन्तः → मणिपूरान्तः; अन्तः + उदिता → अन्तरुदिता, visarga → र् before a vowel)
उदिता = risen, arisen, come forth (उत् + इता, from इ "to go")
"She who rises up within the Maṇipūra cakra."

Vigraha: मणिपूरस्य अन्तः उदिता।

102. विष्णुग्रन्थिविभेदिनी → विष्णु-ग्रन्थि-विभेदिनी

विष्णु = Viṣṇu → विष्णुग्रन्थि = the Viṣṇu-knot, second of the three, at the heart (anāhata)
ग्रन्थि = knot, node
विभेदिनी = she who pierces, splits open (वि + भिद्)
"She who pierces the Viṣṇu-knot."

Vigraha: विष्णुग्रन्थिं विभिनत्तीति।

Note: from 99 the namas trace the kuṇḍalinī ascent, and they alternate — a cakra reached, then the knot above it broken. The three granthis are Brahma at the base, Viṣṇu at the heart, Rudra at the brow, and 103–104 complete the pattern with आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालस्था and रुद्रग्रन्थिविभेदिनी before the sahasrāra is reached in 105.

103. आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालस्था → आज्ञा-चक्र-अन्तराल-स्था

आज्ञा = command → आज्ञाचक्र, the wheel of command at the brow
चक्र = wheel
अन्तराल = the interior, intervening space (अन्तर + आल)
स्था = abiding
"She who abides in the interior of the Ājñā cakra."

104. रुद्रग्रन्थिविभेदिनी → रुद्र-ग्रन्थि-विभेदिनी

रुद्र = Rudra → रुद्रग्रन्थि, the last knot, at the brow
ग्रन्थि = knot
विभेदिनी = she who pierces (वि + भिद्)
"She who pierces the Rudra-knot."

105. सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा → सहस्रार-अम्बुज-आरूढा

सहस्र = thousand; अर = spoke → सहस्रार, the thousand-petalled crown cakra
अम्बुज = lotus (अम्बु = water + ज = born)
आरूढा = having ascended (आ + रूढ, from रुह्)
"She who has ascended the thousand-petalled lotus."

106. सुधासाराभिवर्षिणी → सुधा-सार-अभिवर्षिणी

सुधा = nectar, ambrosia
सार = essence, choicest extract
अभिवर्षिणी = she who showers down abundantly (अभि + वृष्)
"She who showers down the very essence of nectar."

Clean Devanagari — nothing to fix.

Two things worth noting in this verse. The ascent completes at 105 and then reverses direction: 106 pours the amṛta back down. And the root वृष् recurs from nama 79 — counter-missiles rained on Bhaṇḍāsura there, nectar on the devotee here. Likewise आरूढा, last seen mounting war-chariots in 67–70, now mounts a lotus.


---

## ब्रह्माणी ब्रह्म जननी बहुरूपा बुधार्चिता । प्रसवित्री प्रचण्डा ऽऽज्ञा प्रतिष्ठा प्रकटाकृतिः

*brahmāṇī brahma jananī bahurūpā budhārcitā । prasavitrī pracaṇḍā ājñā pratiṣṭhā prakaṭākṛtiḥ*

Verse 155, namas 821–830. Ten namas, not the nine most editions count here — this text keeps ब्रह्म and जननी apart.

821. ब्रह्माणी → ब्रह्म-आणी

ब्रह्म = Brahmā, the Creator (stem ब्रह्मन्)
आणी = the feminine formant that makes consorts' names — आनी, with ण by ṇatva after the र् of ब्रह्म- (Pāṇini 8.4.2, रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे)
"Brahmāṇī — the Śakti of Brahmā."

Vigraha: ब्रह्मणः शक्तिः ब्रह्माणी। or ब्रह्मणः पत्नी ब्रह्माणी।

The suffix is the one that gave भवानी at 112 and gives इन्द्राणी and रुद्राणी elsewhere; here the न् retroflexes because a र् precedes it inside the word. Bhāskararāya offers three readings, and only the third is the obvious one. (1) ब्रह्मा + अणि, "tail of a bird" — She is the Brahman forming the tail of the ānandamaya sheath, on the Vedānta Sūtra's ānandamaya section (I.1.12–19), where the sheath is figured as a bird and its puccha is the ground. (2) ब्रह्मा + अनि, "gives life" — so the Devī Purāṇa, "she is called Brāhmaṇī because she creates or gives life to Brahmā." (3) Brahmā the grandsire, and She his spouse.

822. ब्रह्म → ब्रह्म

ब्रह्म = Brahman, the Absolute — literally that which expands, grows vast (from बृह् "to grow, to swell")
"She who is Brahman itself."

Vigraha: बृहत्त्वात् ब्रह्म।

The nama drops all feminine marking — not ब्रह्मी nor ब्राह्मी but the neuter ब्रह्म, the Absolute named without gender. Standing straight after 821, the pair moves from Brahmā's Śakti to Brahman itself: the personal form first, then the impersonal ground. Bhāskararāya glosses it as what the liberated attain, or as knowledge of the undifferentiated Self, citing the Viṣṇu Purāṇa — "that knowledge is called Brahman which annihilates duality, mere being, transcending speech, cognised by the Self alone."

823. जननी → जननी

जननी = mother, she who gives birth (from जन् "to be born," causative जनय् "to beget," with the suffix अन and the feminine ई)
"The Mother — she who brings all to birth."

Vigraha: जनयतीति जननी।

Bhāskararāya notes this nama may be compounded with the previous one and read as ब्रह्मजननी, "the mother of Brahmā" — which is how most editions count it, giving one nama where this text gives two. Read apart, 822 and 823 set Brahman and the Mother side by side without joining them; read together, they say She gave birth to the Creator.

824. बहुरूपा → बहु-रूपा

बहु = many, manifold, much
रूपा = form, shape, visible appearance (रूप with the feminine आ)
"She of manifold forms."

Vigraha: बहूनि रूपाणि यस्याः सा।

The Devī Bhāgavata resolves the apparent quarrel with the formless namas: "she is formless because she is supreme, she is many-formed because of her activity" — the multiplicity belongs to Her acting, not to Her being. The Gauḍapāda Sūtra (8) makes it concrete: "though one, she becomes many in order to destroy Bhaṇḍāsura." The war-forms of 65–82 are what this nama abstracts. A second reading makes Her consort of the countless Rudras, on the Rudrādhyāya's "there are countless Rudras in the world" — the Varāha Purāṇa counting nine crore Cāmuṇḍās (tamas), eighteen crore Vaiṣṇavīs (rajas), and Brahmā's sattva-śaktis beyond number, Rudra husband to all; the Nṛsiṃha Purāṇa condensing it to "Umā alone in many forms is the wife."

825. बुधार्चिता → बुध-अर्चिता

बुध = the wise, the awakened, one who knows (from बुध् "to wake, to know"); also Mercury
अर्चिता = worshipped, honoured, adored (from अर्च् "to worship")
"She who is worshipped by the wise."

Vigraha: बुधैः अर्चिता।

Sandhi: बुध + अर्चिता → बुधार्चिता (अ + अ → आ, Pāṇini 6.1.101 अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः). Bhāskararāya cites Bhagavad Gītā 7.16 — four kinds of good men worship Me: the afflicted, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the jñānī. This nama singles out the last. Since बुध also names Mercury, the compound admits "worshipped by Budha."

826. प्रसवित्री → प्र-सवित्री

प्र = forth, forward — the prefix, here intensive
सवित्री = the begetter, she who brings forth (from सू "to generate," with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्; the masculine is सवितृ, the Sun)
"The Progenitrix — she who brings all forth."

Vigraha: प्रसूते इति प्रसवित्री।

सवित्री is the feminine of सवितृ, the Sun as generator, so the nama makes Her the begetting power of which the Sun is the masculine figure; प्र carries it to "bringing forth in full." Bhāskararāya: mother of the world made of ether and the rest, or of its people. The Viṣṇudharmottara — "because she generates the beings she is called Savitā." The Bhagavatī Purāṇa — "from her proceeded all things, from Brahmā down to the inanimate, and from Mahat to substance."

827. प्रचण्डा → प्र-चण्डा

प्र = exceedingly, in the highest degree — the intensive prefix
चण्डा = fierce, wrathful, violent (चण्ड with the feminine आ)
"The exceedingly Fierce One."

Vigraha: प्रकृष्टा चण्डा प्रचण्डा।

Bhāskararāya grounds the wrath in scripture rather than temperament: Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.8.1, "for fear of Him the wind blows"; Kaṭha Upaniṣad 6.2, "it is a great terror, a raised thunderbolt," where the Vedānta Sūtra (1.3.39) reads the thunderbolt as Brahman. Kāmandaka supplies the political sense — one who possesses no portion of anger, and whom the people do not fear, cannot enforce righteousness. A wholly different reading takes प्र as "fond of" and चण्डा as the śaṅkha flower — the Viśva gives चण्ड the senses of a perfume, the śaṅkha blossom, and anger — yielding "she who loves the śaṅkha flower"; the same lexicon glosses प्रचण्डा as a white karavīra and as a brilliant person, hence also "the Shining One."

828. आज्ञा → आ-ज्ञा

आ = towards, upon — the prefix
ज्ञा = from ज्ञा "to know"; with आ, that which is made known — a command, ordinance, injunction
"The Divine Ordinance."

Vigraha: आज्ञापनम् आज्ञा।

The text prints this nama as ऽऽज्ञा. The double avagraha is the edition marking an elided आ in प्रचण्डा + आज्ञा → प्रचण्डाज्ञा (आ + आ → आ, Pāṇini 6.1.101); the nama itself is आज्ञा. Bhāskararāya takes it as the Lord's will expressed in the Vedas as injunction and prohibition, quoting the Liṅga Purāṇa: She is neither Prakṛti nor Jīva nor Vikṛti, but "my eternal five-faced holy ordinance, which delivers the world from fear, proceeded of old from my mouth." A second reading divides the words differently and takes the nama as ज्ञा, the Knower — the Person who is enjoyer of the guṇas (Liṅga Purāṇa), the lexica giving ज्ञ the senses of Brahmā, Mercury and a wise man, and Śvetāśvatara 6.2 calling Him "the death of death, omniscient."

829. प्रतिष्ठा → प्रति-स्था

प्रति = towards, firmly against — the prefix
स्था = standing, from स्था "to stand" → प्रतिष्ठा, that on which a thing stands: a foundation, a firm base
"The Foundation — that on which all things stand."

Vigraha: प्रतितिष्ठति अस्यां सर्वम् इति प्रतिष्ठा।

Sandhi: प्रति + स्था → प्रतिष्ठा। The स् retroflexes to ष् after the इ of प्रति (Pāṇini 8.3.59, आदेशप्रत्यययोः), and the थ् follows it to ठ् (8.4.41). Bhāskararāya: the foundation of the whole universe, on the Śruti "she is the foundation of the extended universe" and the Sūta Saṃhitā "this supreme consciousness is the foundation of all things." प्रतिष्ठा is also the name of the sixteen-syllabled Vedic metre; and of the kalā resident in the water-tattva, which the Śaivāgama says "gives manhood and increases devotion to Śiva" — so called because it establishes one firmly in the Lord. The Viśva adds the sense of a four-syllabled quarter-verse.

830. प्रकटाकृतिः → प्रकट-आकृतिः

प्रकट = manifest, evident, open to all (प्र + कट)
आकृतिः = form, shape, outward configuration (आ + कृ "to make")
"She whose form is manifest."

Vigraha: प्रकटा आकृतिः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: प्रकट + आकृतिः → प्रकटाकृतिः (अ + आ → आ, Pāṇini 6.1.101). Bhāskararāya reads प्रकट as "experienced by all" and आकृति as Her nature, citing the Sūta Saṃhitā (1.8.36): all men know Him as the sense of "I," yet through delusion do not recognise Him as Śiva. A technical reading takes the Prakaṭas to be the yoginīs of the Śrīcakra's first enclosure, of whom She is the आकृति. Others divide against the grain — अप्रकटा, the hidden one; or अप् + प्रकटा, "manifested in water," on the Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad's "all this was indeed water."

Note on the verse. The movement is from person to principle and back. 821 names Her as a consort, 822 strips the gender away and names Her as Brahman, 823 restores the person as Mother — and the commentary's own remark that 822–823 may be read as one nama shows how thin the seam is. 824 then multiplies the forms, 825 names who recognises them, and 826 makes Her the source of all of them. The last four turn to how She stands towards the world: bringing forth (826), terrifying (827), commanding (828), upholding (829), and finally simply visible (830).

The root स्था in 829 has run through the seat-namas — 52, 55, 57, 93, 97, 103 — each time as Her abiding somewhere. Here it inverts: She is not what stands, but what everything else stands on.

Two textual notes. आज्ञा at 828 appears in the printed text as ऽऽज्ञा, and प्रकटाकृतिः at 830 carries the verse number ॥१५५॥ with it; neither belongs to the nama.


---

## प्राणेश्वरी प्राणदात्री पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी । विशृङ्खला विविक्तस्था वीरमाता वियत्प्रसूः

*prāṇeśvarī prāṇadātrī pañcāśatpīṭharūpiṇī । viśṛṅkhalā viviktasthā vīramātā viyatprasūḥ*

Verse 156, namas 831–837.

831. प्राणेश्वरी → प्राण-ईश्वरी

प्राण = breath, vital air; the vital breaths; also the senses (प्र + अन् "to breathe")
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady (ईश् "to rule" with वर, feminine ई)
"The Mistress of the vital breaths."

Vigraha: प्राणानाम् ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: प्राण + ईश्वरी → प्राणेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, Pāṇini 6.1.87 आद्गुणः). Bhāskararāya takes प्राण in three senses. As the senses, on Vedānta Sūtra 2.4.14, "there is guidance of the prāṇas by fire and the rest," from which a ruling deity over each is established by argument — She is that ruler. As the five vital breaths, on the Śruti "he is the breath of breath." A third reading divides प्र + अन, taking अन as the Vedas and प्र as exalted, with Kaṭha Upaniṣad 2.15, "all the Vedas point out the same abode."

832. प्राणदात्री → प्राण-दात्री

प्राण = breath, life; also the eleven senses, the ten together with mind
दात्री = the giver, she who gives (दा "to give" with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्; the masculine is दातृ)
"The Giver of the life-breath."

Vigraha: प्राणान् ददातीति प्राणदात्री।

The computed pada in this file read प्राणद-अत्री, which invents a stem प्राणद and a suffix अत्री; the joint is प्राण + दात्री. दात्री is built exactly as सवित्री was at 826, six namas back — तृ with ङीप्, naming Her by an act. Bhāskararāya reads प्राण here as the eleven senses, citing the Śruti "all the prāṇas follow the prāṇa when it goes out" and Vedānta Sūtra 2.4.5, "the prāṇas are seven, on account of this being understood from scriptural passages and of the specification of those seven." Read with 831, the pair moves from ruling the breaths to bestowing them.

833. पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी → पञ्चाशत्-पीठ-रूपिणी

पञ्चाशत् = fifty
पीठ = seat; a pīṭha, one of the sacred seats of the Goddess
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying (रूप + इन्, feminine ङीप्)
"She who is embodied as the fifty Seats."

Vigraha: पञ्चाशतः पीठानां रूपिणी।

Bhāskararāya's point is that "fifty" here stands for fifty-one, and Harṣadīkṣita reads it so in commenting on the opening verse of the Śāradātilaka. The pīṭhas run from Kāmarūpa to Chāyāchatra and are enumerated at Yoginīhṛdaya 3.39–46; the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa directs that "the fifty-one pīṭhas... possessed with the order of letters should be established in their proper places of letters." Since the pīṭhas are set in the places of the mātṛkās and the alphabet runs from अ to क्ष, the count is fifty-one. The author of the Sundarīmahodaya makes them fifty by leaving क्ष out of the reckoning, which Bhāskararāya rejects on the authority of the Jñānārṇava and the rest.

So the nama identifies Her with the alphabet quite as much as with the geography — each pīṭha a letter, the whole set of sacred places being the mātṛkā-garland. The same identification of body with mantra underlies 85–87.

834. विशृङ्खला → वि-शृङ्खला

वि = away, without — the privative prefix
शृङ्खला = a chain, fetter, shackle
"The Unfettered One."

Vigraha: विगता शृङ्खला यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya takes the fetters to be karma, good and bad alike, and quotes the saying: "Lord, destroy my good actions as well as my bad; when the fetters are on the feet it makes no difference whether they are of gold or of iron." Injunction and prohibition apply only to the ignorant, so being unfettered here is not lawlessness but standing past the reach of law. A second reading takes विशृङ्खला as unbound in the sense of unclothed, She being seen in that form at Ālambura and other sacred places.

835. विविक्तस्था → विविक्त-स्था

विविक्त = separated, set apart — hence solitary; and hence also discriminated, sifted apart (वि + विच् "to sift, to separate")
स्था = abiding, dwelling
"She who dwells in solitary places."

Vigraha: विविक्ते तिष्ठतीति विविक्तस्था।

The root विच् "to sift" gives विविक्त both its senses at once — a place sifted clear of people, and a mind that has sifted self from not-self — and Bhāskararāya uses both. As solitude: the Kośa gives विविक्त for lonely and for holy places, and the Hārīta Smṛti says "the ground is everywhere holy where no people are seen." The word covers the region of the righteous as well as the uninhabited place, but here means the latter, since neither a bad place nor a crowded one inclines the mind to meditation. As discrimination: the विविक्त are those able to distinguish self from not-self, and She dwells in such persons.

स्था again — the same root turned to प्रतिष्ठा six namas back at 829.

836. वीरमाता → वीर-माता

वीर = hero, warrior; in Tantric usage the foremost among devotees; also the vessel holding the ritual mead; also Vīra, a proper name
माता = mother; or, from मा "to measure," the measurer
"The Mother of heroes."

Vigraha: वीराणां माता।

Bhāskararāya reads वीर as the chief among devotees, or as those slain in battle, and माता as mother because She benefits them. The Viśva gives वीर the sense of the vessel that contains the mead, in which case माता is taken from मा "to measure" — She who measures it out, a reading that belongs to Kaula ritual rather than to the battlefield.

वीर is also a proper name, and the Padma Purāṇa gives him a story. Śiva says, "this Vīra, O Devī, is always dear to my heart, he is the teacher of wonderful feats, he is worshipped by multitudes of Gaṇeśas" — at which Devī asks when she shall have such a son, and Śiva grants that this one be hers; delighted, the daughter of Himavat sends her servant Vijayā to fetch him. On that reading She is वीरमाता quite specifically: the mother of Vīra.

837. वियत्प्रसूः → वियत्-प्रसूः

वियत् = sky, ether, space — ākāśa (from वि + इ "to go apart, to extend")
प्रसूः = she who brings forth, mother (प्र + सू "to generate")
"The Mother of ether."

Vigraha: वियतः प्रसूः।

Bhāskararāya cites Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2.1, "the ether is originated from the Self." Ākāśa is the first of the five elements to issue from Brahman, so naming Her mother of ether names Her as the origin of the whole elemental series and not of one element only.

प्रसूः is the same प्र + सू that gave प्रसवित्री at 826 — there the agent-noun in तृ, here the bare root-noun. The two verses close and open on the same act of bringing-forth.

Note on the verse. It divides at the daṇḍa by sound as much as by sense: three namas on प, then four on व. The प-group concerns life and its seats — She rules the breaths, She gives them, She is the fifty-one places where She is sought. The व-group concerns freedom and origin — unfettered, solitary, mother of heroes, mother of ether. 831 and 832 pair as ruler and giver of the same प्राण; 836 and 837 pair as mother in the near sense and in the cosmic one.

Textual note. The verse table in index.html gives this verse as namas 830–837. It should be 831–837: प्रकटाकृतिः at 830 closes verse 155, and was assigned here because the verse number ॥१५५॥ was captured into its dev field.


---

## मुकुन्दा मुक्तिनिलया मूलविग्रहरूपिणी । भावज्ञा भवरोगघ्नी भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी

*mukundā muktinilayā mūlavigraharūpiṇī । bhāvajñā bhavarogaghnī bhavacakrapravartinī*

Verse 157, namas 838–843.

838. मुकुन्दा → मुकुन्दा

मुकुन्द = a name of Viṣṇu, traditionally derived as मुकुं ददाति, "he who gives mukti"; the Viśva also gives it for a precious stone
मुकुन्दा = the same in the feminine — she who gives liberation
"Mukundā — she who gives liberation."

Vigraha: मुकुं मुक्तिं ददातीति मुकुन्दा।

The name is Viṣṇu's, taken in the feminine, and Bhāskararāya does not treat that as a loan. He justifies it from the Tantrarāja's account of the Gopāla mantras: Lalitā "once appeared in a male body as Kṛṣṇa," slept and left the world uncontrolled, then surrounded herself with her own energies in the form of Gopīs and divided her form into six in order to sport with them. On that reading the nama claims Kṛṣṇa as one of Her forms rather than borrowing his epithet.

839. मुक्तिनिलया → मुक्ति-निलया

मुक्ति = release, liberation (from मुच् "to loose")
निलया = abode, dwelling, resting place (नि + ली "to settle down")
"She who is the abode of liberation."

Vigraha: मुक्तेः निलया।

Bhāskararāya says only that there are five kinds of liberation, without naming them; the Āgamic set is usually sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya, sāyujya and kaivalya. The nama covers all five rather than choosing one. निलया returns from 99 मूलाधारैकनिलया, where the abode was a place in the body; here it is a state.

840. मूलविग्रहरूपिणी → मूल-विग्रह-रूपिणी

मूल = root, origin, base
विग्रह = body, bodily form — that which is held together (वि + ग्रह् "to grasp")
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying (रूप + इन्, feminine ङीप्)
"She whose form is the root-body of all."

Vigraha: मूलविग्रहः रूपं यस्याः सा।

मूलविग्रह is a technical term, not a description: the Rājarājeśvarī Śakti, root of all the other śaktis — Bālā, Bagalā and the rest. Bhāskararāya notes that ten of the Gauḍapāda Sūtras treat of it, the second dividing the one Vidyā into Śāmbhavī, Vidyā and Śyāmā, with the succeeding sūtras deriving many energies from each of the three. So the nama places Her as the trunk from which the whole pantheon branches.

रूपिणी recurs from 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी, seven namas back, and मूल from 88–89 and 99 — but there the root was the mantra or the cakra, and here it is the form itself.

841. भावज्ञा → भाव-ज्ञा

भाव = thought, intention, disposition; existence, nature, state of being — a word of very wide range
ज्ञा = knowing, she who knows (from ज्ञा "to know")
"She who knows the heart's intention."

Vigraha: भावं जानातीति भावज्ञा।

This is the widest word in the verse and Bhāskararāya lets it run. The Amarakośa (476) gives भाव as existence, nature, intention, action, self, birth; the Amaraśeṣa adds womb, sage, wealth, compassion, sport, dominion. Yāska makes it the six modifications — being, birth, growth and the rest (Nirukta 1.1.3) — and the logicians' six categories are also called bhāvas. Pāṇini 4.3.95 gives भाव the sense of devotion, which yields the reading usually taken: She knows the devotee's inward feeling. A play on the syllables gives भा "light" and व "to go," the sun and the luminaries depending on Her.

The technical sense is the sharpest. भावार्थ is the first of the six interpretations of the mantra listed at Yoginīhṛdaya 2.15 — bhāvārtha, sampradāyārtha, nigarbha, kaulika, sarvarahasya and mahātattvārtha. On that reading भावज्ञा is She who knows the first of the mantra's six depths. ज्ञा itself returns from 828, where the alternative reading of आज्ञा was ज्ञा, the Knower.

842. भवरोगघ्नी → भव-रोग-घ्नी

भव = worldly existence, saṃsāra
रोग = disease, sickness (from रुज् "to break, to afflict")
घ्नी = she who slays, destroys (from हन् "to strike"; feminine of घ्न)
"She who destroys the disease of worldly existence."

Vigraha: भवरोगं हन्तीति भवरोगघ्नी।

The printed text and the dev field in index.html both read भवरोगनी, dropping the घ्. The nama is भवरोगघ्नी, from हन् — and the file's own gloss, "destroyer of earthly existence," confirms the reading. This is the third artifact of its kind in these three verses, after ऽऽज्ञा at 828 and प्रकटाकृतिः ॥१५५॥ at 830.

The metaphor is medical and Bhāskararāya presses it: the Rāmāyaṇa (Book VII), "I see no medicine except Vṛṣabhadhvaja"; the Śiva Purāṇa, "just as the remedy for all diseases is naturally in opposition, so Śiva is foe of the pains of saṃsāra." A cure works by being contrary to the disease, and that contrariety is the logic of the nama.

843. भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी → भव-चक्र-प्रवर्तिनी

भव = worldly existence, saṃsāra; read as भाव, Bhava — Śiva
चक्र = wheel; in one reading, the mind
प्रवर्तिनी = she who sets in motion, who causes to turn (प्र + वृत् "to turn," in the causative)
"She who turns the wheel of worldly existence."

Vigraha: भवचक्रं प्रवर्तयतीति भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी।

Manu 12.124: "he, pervading all the beings by the five forms and constantly making them, by means of birth, growth and decay, revolves like a wheel." The Devī Bhāgavata: "thou art alone the Lord of the bondage and release of the whole universe."

Read as भावचक्र the compound points instead to the anāhata, the heart-cakra, so called because it is the seat of Bhava. Bhāskararāya digresses at length on whether it may properly be called a cakra at all, since the Tantras define a cakra as having angles while the anāhata has only petals — a figure of petals alone being a lotus, and of angles alone a yantra. The commentator on the Vidyāratna answers that the pericarps of these lotuses do contain angles, which is why the mūlādhāra and the rest are properly cakras, like the bindu-cakra and the other components of the Śrīcakra.

A further reading takes भव as Śiva and चक्र as mind, on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa's "Viṣṇu bears in his hand mind in the form of a disc, constantly in motion, swifter than wind" — so She is the one who directs Śiva's mind.

Note on the verse. It is built on two syllables. मु- opens it three times: liberation given (838), liberation housed (839), and the root-form from which all śaktis come (840). भ- closes it three times, and the verse plays on the length of the vowel — भाव at 841, भव at 842 and 843, with the commentary reading 843 both ways.

Each of the three भ-namas takes a different figure for the same existence: known, cured, turned. Set beside 114 भवारण्यकुठारिका, the Sahasranāma's metaphors for saṃsāra now stand as a forest to be felled, a disease to be cured, and a wheel She herself keeps turning. The last is the sharpest, because it makes Her the cause of the bondage as well as its cure — which is what the Devī Bhāgavata line says outright.

## छन्दःसारा शास्त्रसारा मन्त्रसारा तलोदरी । उदारकीर्तिरुद्दामवैभवा वर्णरूपिणी

*chandaḥsārā śāstrasārā mantrasārā talodarī । udārakīrtiruddāmavaibhavā varṇarūpiṇī*

Verse 158, namas 844–850.

844. छन्दःसारा → छन्दः-सारा

छन्दः = metre; the Vedas; also unrestrained conduct, free desire (छन्दस्, from छन्द् "to please")
सारा = essence, marrow, pith; also strength, fixity, rule (सार with the feminine आ)
"She who is the essence of the Vedas."

Vigraha: छन्दसां सारा।

The visarga stands unchanged before स्, and the edition prints छन्दः सारा with a space for that reason; it is one nama. The Paiṅgala Tantra gives छन्दस् for the Vedas, or for the Gāyatrī and the other metres. The Viśva gives it four senses — metre, Veda, unrestrained conduct, desire — and सार six: strength, marrow, fixity, rule, water, superiority. Bhāskararāya works the pair in nearly every combination.

Taking छन्दस् as Veda and सार as fixity: Her nature is what stands established in the Upaniṣad portions. Taking छन्दस् as the metres: among them the Gāyatrī is the essential one and the Pañcadaśī is the Gāyatrī's essence — a chain he sets out in his own Varivasyārahasya (1.2–4), where fourteen means are promulgated, the Vedas essential among them, the Gāyatrī essential in the Vedas, and that Gāyatrī having two forms, one uttered by all and one concealed in the four Vedas and spoken only in symbols. Tripurā Upaniṣad 16 gives it so — "Kāma, Yoni, Kamalā, Vajrapāṇi, Guha, Hasā, Mātariśvā, Abhra, Indra, again Guhā, Sakalā, with Māyā, thus is the ancient Vidyā, the universal mother of the world" — which indicates the Kādi-vidyā.

The third reading, छन्दस् as unrestrained motion of the mind, takes the nama into Kaula ethics and Bhāskararāya defends it at length. The Vijñānabhairava: "wherever the mind finds pleasure, thither it is directed; this supreme bliss becomes manifest." Whatever delights the perfected devotee is dharma. Paraśurāma's Kalpa Sūtra bounds the Smṛti precepts — "ethical precepts are to be observed until perfection"; the Kaula Upaniṣad, "righteousness is unrighteousness, unrighteousness is righteousness"; Yoginīhṛdaya 3.208, "whether he drinks or dances or vomits or eats or meditates on the supreme unity, let him follow his own inclinations in peace." But he fences it carefully. Manu 2.6 makes dharma what the Śrutis and Smṛtis ordain, the custom of holy men, "and that in which the mind delights" — and the mind meant is the one absorbed in contemplation, "otherwise licence would be permitted."

845. शास्त्रसारा → शास्त्र-सारा

शास्त्र = scripture, authoritative teaching — that which instructs (शास् "to teach, to command" with the suffix त्र)
सारा = essence, pith
"She who is the essence of the scriptures."

Vigraha: शास्त्राणां सारा।

Bhāskararāya says this nama and the next are to be explained like the one before. शास्त्र he takes as the Vedas, on Vedānta Sūtra 1.1.3, "from its being the source of śāstra." The Tantric doctrine makes śāstra whatever lays down vidhi; or else the Mīmāṃsā and the rest, which follow the vidhi-śāstra. The Bhāmatī defines it widest: "that is called śāstra by which, whether revealed texts or otherwise, men are instructed to act or to refrain."

846. मन्त्रसारा → मन्त्र-सारा

मन्त्र = mantra, sacred formula — traditionally मननात् त्रायते, that which saves by being thought (मन् "to think" with the suffix त्र)
सारा = essence, pith
"She who is the essence of the mantras."

Vigraha: मन्त्राणां सारा।

Bhāskararāya allows मन्त्र three ranges: the Vedas, the mantras of the Tantras, or the sixty-four books on mantra.

The three सार-namas narrow as they go — metre, scripture, mantra: the whole Veda, then the texts that instruct, then the single syllable. She is the pith of each. And since the mantra is what saves by being thought, मन्त्रसारा names the saving power inside the syllable rather than the syllable itself.

847. तलोदरी → तल-उदरी

तल = surface, flat expanse; also the palm, the sole; also a tala, one of the nether worlds
उदरी = bellied, having a belly (उदर with the feminine ई)
"She who is flat-bellied — slender of waist."

Vigraha: तलम् इव उदरं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: तल + उदरी → तलोदरी (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, Pāṇini 6.1.87 आद्गुणः). The plain sense is descriptive, तल being a flat surface — this is the one physical epithet in a verse otherwise made of abstractions.

Bhāskararāya converts even that to cosmology by prefixing a syllable: with अ the name becomes अतलोदरी, and Atala-loka is Her waist when She assumes the Virāṭ form. The slender waist and the lowest of the nether worlds become the same thing seen at two scales.

848. उदारकीर्तिः → उदार-कीर्तिः

उदार = exalted, noble, magnanimous, munificent (उत् + ऋ "to rise")
कीर्तिः = fame, renown (from कीर्त् "to mention, to celebrate")
"She of exalted fame."

Vigraha: उदारा कीर्तिः यस्याः सा।

That is the plain reading. Bhāskararāya then divides the syllables five further ways, each turning on अर.

उद् "exalted" + अ "all-pervading" + अर "quickly obtained" + कीर्ति — fame quickly obtained by worshipping Her, the Kośa (28) giving अर for lightness and quickness. Or रि the mother of the devas, whose sons are the आरs, with उद् "beyond": Her fame exceeds theirs. Or अर as Maṅgala and the like, with उद् "dispels": uttering Her name dispels the influence of those malign deities. Or उद् as the golden Person residing in the sun (Chāndogya 1.6.6) and अर a kind of weapon: Her fame is a weapon against him, and worshipping Her wins fame exceeding his. Or अर as one of the two lakes of nectar in the city of Brahman called Aparājitā — Chāndogya 8.5.4, "there are two lakes of nectar resembling oceans, by name Ara and Ṇya" — with उद् "exalted": Her fame equals theirs, and Vedānta Sūtra 4.4.22 makes that state one of non-return.

849. उद्दामवैभवा → उद्दाम-वैभवा

उद्दाम = unrestrained, unbounded — literally beyond the tether (उत् + दाम "rope, cord")
वैभवा = glory, majesty, might (vṛddhi derivative of विभव)
"She whose glory is unbounded."

Vigraha: उद्दामं वैभवं यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya's entire gloss is the etymology: "दाम, rope, that which limits; उद्, beyond." The image is a tethered animal, and the glory is what has slipped the rope. दाम is the same word as in दामोदर — which, two namas after तलोदरी, puts both halves of that name in this verse.

In the printed text this nama appears as रुद्दामवैभवा. The initial र् is not part of it: उदारकीर्तिः + उद्दामवैभवा gives उदारकीर्तिरुद्दामवैभवा, the visarga becoming र् before the following vowel, and the word-division has been taken one letter late. Correspondingly 848 has lost its visarga, printed as उदारकीर्ति.

850. वर्णरूपिणी → वर्ण-रूपिणी

वर्ण = letter, phoneme; also colour, and social class (from वृ "to cover")
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying (रूप + इन्, feminine ङीप्)
"She whose form is the letters."

Vigraha: वर्णाः रूपं यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya: there are sixty-four letters, and these make up Her form. The Pāṇinīyaśikṣā — "according to the Sāmbhava school there are sixty-three or sixty-four letters, these promulgated by Svayambhū in the Prākṛta or the Saṃskṛta tongue."

The nama closes the verse where 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी stood: She embodied as the alphabet. There the letters were counted as the fifty-one pīṭhas, here as the sixty-four varṇas — a difference of which enumeration is in view, not a disagreement. रूपिणी has now carried three times in this stretch, at 833, 840 and 850.

Note on the verse. Three सार-namas open it and narrow as they go, from the whole Veda to the single saving syllable. तलोदरी breaks the pattern with the verse's one physical epithet, and even that is converted to cosmology. The last three return to magnitude — fame, glory, and the letters that are Her form — so the verse moves inward to the syllable at 846 and back out to the alphabet at 850.

Textual note. Two of the seven namas here are mis-divided at the same joint: उदारकीर्तिः has lost its visarga to the following word and उद्दामवैभवा has gained the resulting र्. Fourth artifact of this kind in the run, after ऽऽज्ञा (828), प्रकटाकृतिः ॥१५५॥ (830) and भवरोगनी (842).


---

## जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी । सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका

*janmamṛtyujarātaptajanaviśrāntidāyinī । sarvopaniṣadudghuṣṭā śāntyatītakalātmikā*

Verse 159, namas 851–853.

851. जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी → जन्म-मृत्यु-जरा-तप्त-जन-विश्रान्ति-दायिनी

जन्म = birth (from जन् "to be born")
मृत्यु = death (from मृ "to die")
जरा = old age, decay (from जृ "to grow old")
तप्त = scorched, burnt, tormented (past participle of तप् "to burn")
जन = people, men
विश्रान्ति = rest, repose — the ceasing of weariness (वि + श्रम् "to be weary")
दायिनी = she who gives, bestower (दा + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who gives rest to those scorched by birth, death and old age."

Vigraha: जन्ममृत्युजराभिः तप्तानां जनानां विश्रान्तिं ददातीति।

Sandhi: जरा + तप्त → जरातप्त (आ + अ → आ, Pāṇini 6.1.101 अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः). The dev field in index.html breaks this seven-member compound with a space after जन; it is one nama, and the longest in this run.

विश्रान्ति is precisely chosen. वि + श्रम् is the undoing of weariness, so the word does not mean peace in general but the ceasing of effort — and Bhāskararāya's one-line gloss makes it "happiness in oneself," rest that needs nothing outside itself. तप्त turns the three torments into a burning, so what is offered is a cooling.

जन्म, मृत्यु and जरा are the classical triad, which the Gītā extends with व्याधि, disease. That fourth member has already been used, nine namas back at 842 भवरोगघ्नी, where saṃsāra itself was the disease. दायिनी returns from 117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी.

852. सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा → सर्व-उपनिषद्-उद्घुष्टा

सर्व = all
उपनिषद् = Upaniṣad, the secret teaching — उप "near," नि, सद्: that which seats the Self near Brahman
उद्घुष्टा = loudly proclaimed (उत् + घुष् "to sound forth, to proclaim")
"She who is proclaimed aloud by all the Upaniṣads."

Vigraha: सर्वाभिः उपनिषद्भिः उद्घुष्टा।

Sandhi at both joints: सर्व + उपनिषद् → सर्वोपनिषद् (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, Pāṇini 6.1.87 आद्गुणः), and उपनिषद् + उद्घुष्टा → उपनिषदुद्घुष्टा.

The dev field reads उद्धुष्टा, with ध where the text needs घ. The root is घुष् "to proclaim," which the Kośa glosses as "loudly proclaimed," and Bhāskararāya spells the word out in his own gloss — so उद्घुष्टा.

He quotes Śaṅkara's derivation of उपनिषद्: it is so called from "bringing the Self near (उप) to Brahman, which is opposed to duality, and destroying (नि-षत्) ignorance and what arises from it." On Chāndogya 1.1.10 the word carries its other sense, the secret — "whatever one does by knowledge, by faith, by upaniṣad, that alone becomes very powerful."

उद् he reads as the exalted, meaning Unity, and this is where सर्व earns its place. Each Upaniṣad ordains a different worship, but without real difference — Vedānta Sūtra 3.3.1, "the cognitions intimated by all the Vedānta texts are identical on account of the non-difference of injunction and so on." So the nama does not say that many Upaniṣads praise Her; it says all of them proclaim one thing, and that thing is She.

853. शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका → शान्ति-अतीत-कला-आत्मिका

शान्ति = peace, quiescence; also the name of the fourth of the five kalās
अतीत = gone beyond, transcended (अति + इ "to go")
कला = a part, a portion; in Śaiva doctrine one of the five kalās of the tattvas
आत्मिका = having the nature of, being the very self of (आत्मन् + क, feminine आ)
"She whose nature is the Śāntyatīta kalā."

Vigraha: शान्त्यतीता कला आत्मा यस्याः सा।

Sandhi at both joints: शान्ति + अतीत → शान्त्यतीत, the इ becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि); and कला + आत्मिका → कलात्मिका (6.1.101).

शान्त्यतीता is a technical term rather than a description — the last and highest of the five kalās of Śaiva cosmology: निवृत्ति, प्रतिष्ठा, विद्या, शान्ति, शान्त्यतीता. Bhāskararāya places it: "the kalā in the ether is called Śāntyatīta," and the Śaivāgamas describe it as annihilating duality and bestowing bliss.

That set reaches backwards. प्रतिष्ठा, the second of the five, was nama 829, and Bhāskararāya noted there that "a certain kalā which resides in the water tattva is also called Pratiṣṭhā." So two of the five kalās stand as namas in this stretch — the water one at 829, the ether one here — and 837 वियत्प्रसूः had already named Her mother of that ether.

Note on the verse. Three namas, and they ascend by level. 851 works at the scale of the suffering person: birth, death, age, and rest for those burnt by them. 852 moves to scripture, where all the Upaniṣads proclaim Her. 853 ends in the ether at the highest of the five kalās, where duality is annihilated. Affliction, revelation, transcendence — and the verse needs only three namas because each one is built long enough to hold a whole level.

Textual note. Two more artifacts here: 851 breaks its compound with a space after जन, and 852 reads उद्धुष्टा for उद्घुष्टा. Seven namas in these five verses are now affected — 828, 830, 842, 848, 849, 851, 852 — which is frequent enough that the other 993 are probably worth a sweep.

## गम्भीरा गगनान्तस्था गर्विता गानलोलुपा । कल्पनारहिता काष्ठा कान्ता कान्तार्धविग्रहा

*gambhīrā gaganāntasthā garvitā gānalolupā । kalpanārahitā kāṣṭhā kāntā kāntārdhavigrahā*

Verse 160, namas 854–861.

854. गम्भीरा → गम्भीरा

गम्भीरा = deep, profound, unfathomable; also, concretely, a deep pool of water
"The Fathomless One."

Vigraha: गम्भीरा अगाधा।

Bhāskararāya takes the word in its concrete sense — a deep tank, the महाह्रद — and reads the nama through Śiva Sūtra 1.23, "by meditating on the Mahāhrada one gains the experience of mantra-power." The commentary there makes महाह्रद the supreme divine energy, meditation the feeling of being merged in it, and mantravīrya the cognition of पूर्णाहन्ता, complete I-ness. Elsewhere: "the supreme queen is knowledge; she emanates first the energy of desire, then gross objects and souls with their qualities" — hence Mahāhrada means Devī, who pervades the universe and is beyond space and time. The depth in this nama is therefore not a figure for inscrutability but a named object of meditation.

A syllabic reading takes गं as the Gaṇapati-bīja, भि as fear and र as driving out — She who drives fear away.

855. गगनान्तस्था → गगन-अन्तः-स्था

गगन = sky, ether, ākāśa
अन्तः = within, inside
स्था = abiding, dwelling
"She who abides within the ether."

Vigraha: गगनस्य अन्तः स्थिता।

Sandhi: गगन + अन्तः → गगनान्तः (आ by 6.1.101), then the visarga assimilates before स् — the same formation as 57 चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था, 93 कुलान्तस्था and 97 समयान्तस्था.

Bhāskararāya gives गगन three ranges: the ether within the heart, the elemental ether, and the supreme ether, with Śvetāśvatara 3.9, "he is the one abiding like a firm tree, in the sky."

A second parsing takes अन्त as destruction rather than interior — गगन-अन्त-स्था, She who remains even after the ether is destroyed. Since ākāśa is the last of the elements to dissolve, that makes Her the survivor of the whole dissolution.

A third reading is phonetic and turns on a pun. गगन is taken as the syllable ह, and अन्तस्थ is the grammarians' name for the semivowels य, र, ल, व — which together with ह are exactly the bījas of the five elements: ह ākāśa, य vāyu, र agni, व jala, ल pṛthvī. The technical अन्तस्थ, "the letters standing between," is being played against अन्तःस्था, "she who stands within."

856. गर्विता → गर्विता

गर्विता = proud, exulting (from गर्व "pride"; the participle in -इत)
"The Proud One."

Vigraha: गर्वः अस्याः अस्तीति गर्विता।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is a single line and it locates the pride exactly: "supreme egoism concerning the creation of the universe." Not vanity, then, but the अहम् of a creator — the I-ness without which nothing is made.

Read with 854 this is pointed. There, meditation on the Mahāhrada yielded पूर्णाहन्ता, complete I-ness, as its fruit. Two namas later She is गर्विता, and the pride is that same I-ness. What the devotee attains by meditating on Her, She simply is.

857. गानलोलुपा → गान-लोलुपा

गान = song, singing, music (from गै "to sing")
लोलुपा = greedy for, avid, eagerly desirous (a reduplicated intensive of लुप्/लुभ् "to covet")
"She who is avid for song."

Vigraha: गाने लोलुपा।

लोलुप is a strong word — not "fond of" but greedy, and reduplicated at that — so the nama claims She hungers for music rather than merely being pleased by it.

Bhāskararāya specifies what गान covers: the four classes of instrument — तत (stringed), आनद्ध (covered with skin, drums), घन (solid and struck) and सुषिर (hollow, wind); or one of the two kinds of Sāman; or śārīra, the voice, and gāndharva, the instrumental art.

She has been named to music before. At 69 गेयचक्ररथारूढमन्त्रिणीपरिसेविता it was Mantriṇī — Śyāmalā, the goddess of music — riding the Geyacakra, the chariot of song. गेय and गान are the same root गै.

858. कल्पनारहिता → कल्पना-रहिता

कल्पना = imagination, mental construction, fabrication (from कल्प् "to arrange, to fashion")
रहिता = devoid of, free from (from रह् "to abandon")
"She who is free of all mental construction."

Vigraha: कल्पनया रहिता।

Bhāskararāya glosses कल्पना as "the waves of the objective world, because they are only imagined," and quotes the Aṣṭāvakragītā: "in me, who am the infinite ocean of consciousness, the souls like waves naturally rise, beat, play and return — wonderful." The nama denies not Her activity but the substantiality of what the activity throws up.

A wholly different division reads कल्प + नर + हित. कल्प is the dissolution; नर is Brahman, "for as he leads (नयति), the eternal Brahman is called Nara," the souls being नरs because they belong to Nara; and हित is friend, doer of good. So: She who does good to souls even at the universal dissolution, by holding them in Her belly as vāsanās, latent tendencies. Bhāskararāya notes drily that Her benevolence during creation and preservation needs no arguing — it is the pralaya that wanted explaining.

859. काष्ठा → काष्ठा

काष्ठा = the goal, the final limit, the utmost point of a course; also a measure of time; also Dāruharidrā, a wood
"The Goal — the final limit."

Vigraha: काष्ठा परा गतिः।

The primary sense is the finishing-post, the end of a course. Bhāskararāya makes it the final doctrine set forth in the Vedānta passages, citing the Sūta Saṃhitā — "whether visible or invisible, real or unreal, it is the supreme Śiva; this final declaration of the Vedānta passages is called Kāṣṭhā" — with Kaṭha Upaniṣad 3.11, "she is the goal, she is the supreme way." The lexical senses are allowed too: a period of time, which Sastry renders as eighteen minutes, and the wood Dāruharidrā.

The Liṅga and Vāyu Purāṇas give काष्ठा as a proper name: the wife of the supreme Śiva in his ether-form called Bhīma, "who gives space for all things animate and inanimate," with Svarga their son. Read so the nama is a genealogy — and it stands four namas after 855, where She abode within that same ether.

A last reading takes काष्ठा as she who stands having crossed over, on Śvetāśvatara 3.14, "he stood ten inches beyond," and Gītā 10.42, "I abide, pervading this entire universe with a single portion."

860. कान्ता → कान्ता

कान्ता = beloved, desired, lovely; hence a beautiful woman, a wife (past participle of कम् "to desire")
"The Beloved."

Vigraha: कम्यते इति कान्ता।

The plain sense is the participle of कम् — she who is desired, therefore beloved, therefore wife.

index.html carries no commentary for this nama, only the gloss "End of sin. Aka, sin and pain." That preserves a syllabic reading: अक is a lexical word for sin and pain, अन्त is end, so the nama is read as that in which sin comes to an end. With the body missing the full argument cannot be recovered here.

कान्त returns at once in 861, but as Śiva. The two namas turn the one word both ways — She the beloved, then He.

861. कान्तार्धविग्रहा → कान्त-अर्ध-विग्रहा

कान्त = beloved, husband — here the supreme Śiva
अर्ध = half, a part, a division
विग्रहा = body, bodily form — that which is held together (वि + ग्रह्)
"She who is half the body of her Beloved."

Vigraha: कान्तस्य अर्धं विग्रहः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: कान्त + अर्ध → कान्तार्ध (आ by 6.1.101). This is the Ardhanārīśvara, and Bhāskararāya's first gloss is simply "कान्त, the supreme Śiva."

A syllabic reading turns the compound inside out: क is the syllable क and अन्त its end — that is, the syllable ख, which also means heaven; अर्ध is a division; so heaven is a portion of Her body. Chāndogya 3.12.6 is quoted for it: "the beings form only one portion of him, the three immortal portions are in heaven."

विग्रह returns from 840 मूलविग्रहरूपिणी, where the body was the root-form from which all śaktis branch. The word means literally what is grasped together, so both namas turn on a holding-together — there as origin, here as union.

Note on the verse. Eight short namas, four on ग and four on क, and the halves answer each other. The ग-group is depth and abundance: fathomless, abiding in ether, proud with the creator's I-ness, avid for song. The क-group is limit and completion: free of construction, the goal, the beloved, half of the Beloved's body. The verse moves from what has no bottom to what has an end.

Bhāskararāya reaches for syllabic readings unusually often here — गं-भि-र at 854, ह with the semivowels at 855, क-अन्त at 860 and again at 861. Four in eight namas, where the preceding verses offered one or two.

Textual note. The index.html entry for 859 काष्ठा carries 858's gloss and a duplicate of 858's commentary; the काष्ठा material sits inside both bodies, introduced by a stray "859. Goal." And 860 कान्ता has no body at all, only its gloss. Neither is a sandhi artifact like the seven noted in 828–852 — this is OCR block-duplication, a different failure.

## कार्यकारणनिर्मुक्ता कामकेलितरङ्गिता । कनत्कनकताटङ्का लीलाविग्रहधारिणी

*kāryakāraṇanirmuktā kāmakelitaraṅgitā । kanatkanakatāṭaṅkā līlāvigrahadhāriṇī*

Verse 161, namas 862–865.

862. कार्यकारणनिर्मुक्ता → कार्य-कारण-निर्मुक्ता

कार्य = effect; that which is to be brought about (कृ "to do" with the gerundive ण्यत्)
कारण = cause; that which brings about (also from कृ)
निर्मुक्ता = wholly released, set free (निः + मुक्ता, from मुच् "to loose")
"She who is free of both cause and effect."

Vigraha: कार्यात् कारणात् च निर्मुक्ता।

Both members are built on the one root कृ, so the compound sets the two poles of a single act — the making and the made — and then frees Her from both. Bhāskararāya identifies them technically: कार्य is the tattva-series beginning with Mahat, कारण is Mūlaprakṛti. In Caitanya these do not exist, and the Śruti says of Brahman that "he has neither cause nor effect."

निर्मुक्ता returns five namas later at 867 क्षयविनिर्मुक्ता, with वि added — freed from causality here, freed from decay there.

863. कामकेलितरङ्गिता → काम-केलि-तरङ्गिता

काम = desire; here a name — Bhāskararāya glosses it Kāmeśvara
केलि = play, sport, amorous dalliance
तरङ्गिता = rippling, billowing, moving in waves (तरङ्ग "wave" with the suffix -इत)
"She who ripples with the play of love."

Vigraha: कामकेलिभिः तरङ्गिता।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is a single word: काम is Kāmeśvara. So this is not desire in the abstract but Her Lord by name — the one on whose lap She sat at 52 शिवकामेश्वराङ्कस्था, and who was wholly won to Her at 54 स्वाधीनवल्लभा.

तरङ्गिता carries the nama. तरङ्ग is a wave and the participle makes Her wave-like: not moved by the play but consisting of its motion. That answers 858 कल्पनारहिता, five namas back, where Bhāskararāya quoted the Aṣṭāvakragītā on souls rising and returning "like waves" in the ocean of consciousness. There the waves were what She is free of; here they are what She is made of.

864. कनत्कनकताटङ्का → कनत्-कनक-ताटङ्का

कनत् = glittering, shining (present participle of कन् "to shine, to be bright")
कनक = gold
ताटङ्का = a large ear-ornament, an earring (ताटङ्क with the feminine आ)
"She who wears glittering golden earrings."

Vigraha: कनत् कनकताटङ्कं यस्याः सा।

The dev field in index.html reads फनत्कनकताटङ्का, with फ for the initial क, and the verse text carries the same error. The word is कनत्, participle of कन् — the file's own gloss ("wearing shining gold earrings") and the fragment "(Kanatkana-" left stranded in its body both confirm the reading. This is the eighth artifact in this run and the first that is a plain letter-confusion rather than a sandhi or spacing fault.

कनत् and कनक chime on purpose: the glitter and the metal share their first syllable. Bhāskararāya passes the nama without comment, which he seldom does — it is one of the few purely ornamental namas in this stretch.

Her earrings have been named once before, at 22 ताटङ्कयुगलीभूततपनोडुपमण्डला, where the pair of them were the orbs of the sun and the moon. Set beside that, the gold here is a deliberate descent in scale: the same ornament, described as jewellery rather than as cosmology.

865. लीलाविग्रहधारिणी → लीला-विग्रह-धारिणी

लीला = play, sport; effortless action
विग्रह = body, bodily form; in Bhāskararāya's gloss, the several incarnations
धारिणी = she who bears, holds, assumes (धृ "to hold" + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who assumes bodies in play."

Vigraha: लीलया विग्रहं धारयतीति।

Bhāskararāya glosses लीला as "without effort" and विग्रह as "the different incarnations," which makes the doctrinal point exactly: Her incarnations cost Her nothing. She takes bodies the way one plays, not the way one labours.

लीला is also a proper name and he notes it — Līlā is the queen of Padmarāja in the Yogavāsiṣṭha: "there was in this royal family one named Padma; he had a beautiful chaste wife named Līlā." Read so, the nama names Her as that Līlā, bearing a body.

विग्रह for the third time in a short span: 840 मूलविग्रहरूपिणी, the root-body from which all śaktis branch; 861 कान्तार्धविग्रहा, half Her Beloved's body; and now the body taken up in play. Origin, union, sport.

Note on the verse. Four namas alternating between the metaphysical and the frankly physical. 862 frees Her from causality altogether; 863 has Her rippling with Kāmeśvara's love-play; 864 describes her earrings; 865 makes the body itself a game. The verse states its own tension and then dissolves it — if She stands outside cause and effect, then the waves, the gold and the body are all play, which is what 865 says.

Two threads run in from the preceding verses: विग्रह, now on its third turn, and the wave-image that 858 had used to deny what 863 affirms.

Textual note. Two faults here, and the second is new in kind.

864's dev reads फनत् for कनत् — a letter substitution, where the seven artifacts at 828–852 were sandhi and spacing errors.

More consequentially, the verse table is corrupted at this row. The entry for 862–865 exists and carries the right text and range, but its verse number reads 169 instead of 161, duplicating the genuine verse 169 at 912–917. It is not the only such fault: the row for 971–976 carries n=977, a nama number leaked into the verse-number field, and n=182 appears twice at the end of the table, above the 179 verses the stats claim. Verse numbers in that table cannot be relied on as an index.
