## दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा । कौलिनीकेवला अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी

*dakṣiṇādakṣiṇārādhyā darasmeramukhāmbujā । kaulinīkevalā anarghyakaivalyapadadāyinī*

Verse 171, namas 923–926.

923. दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या → दक्षिणा-अदक्षिणा-आराध्या

दक्षिणा = the right; a sacrificial fee, an offering; and the wise, the adept (from दक्ष "able, skilful")
अदक्षिणा = the not-dakṣiṇa — the unskilled, the foolish; or, on one reading, the knowers of Brahman
आराध्या = to be worshipped, to be propitiated (आ + राध्)
"She who is worshipped by the adept and the inept alike."

Vigraha: दक्षिणैः अदक्षिणैः च आराध्या।

The compound is doubly readable, and both readings produce the identical written form — which is what makes the nama. दक्षिणा + दक्षिणा and दक्षिणा + अदक्षिणा both give दक्षिणादक्षिणा, because आ + अ → आ (6.1.101) collapses into the same long vowel as आ + आ. The affirmation and the negation are indistinguishable on the page, and Bhāskararāya reads it both ways.

On the first reading दक्षिणा is the offering and दक्षिणा the wise: worshipped with offerings by the wise. On the second the member is negated — दक्षिणा the wise and अदक्षिणा the foolish — so She is worshipped by both. A third turns the negation on its head: दक्षिणा are those ever desirous of knowing the karmas, the ritualists, and अदक्षिणा those who know Brahman, on the Śruti "by knowledge ascetics ascend to where desires cease, which do not reach the Dakṣiṇas nor foolish men." Read so, the un-adept are the higher party. One string, three theologies of access.

He closes with Gītā 7.16, the four kinds who worship — the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise. That is the same verse used at 825 बुधार्चिता, where only the last of the four was in view; here all four are.

The nama also resumes 912 सव्यापसव्यमार्गस्था, eleven namas back, where सव्य and अपसव्य were the Dakṣiṇa and Vāma paths of worship. There the two were distinguished and ranked, with penalties for confusing them. Here both reach Her without preference.

924. दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा → दर-स्मेर-मुख-अम्बुजा

दर = a little, slightly; also a conch shell; also fear (from दृ)
स्मेर = smiling, faintly smiling (from स्मि "to smile")
मुख = face
अम्बुजा = lotus (अम्बु "water" + ज "born")
"She whose lotus face wears a faint smile."

Vigraha: दरस्मेरं मुखाम्बुजं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: मुख + अम्बुजा → मुखाम्बुजा (आ by 6.1.101). दर in the sense of "slightly" is what the primary reading needs — a smile just beginning, not a broad one; and स्मेर is itself the faint smile rather than laughter.

But दर has two other lexical senses, and Bhāskararāya uses both. As the conch shell: her face shines white as a conch, or her neck is shaped like one. As fear: her face is smiling even in the time of fear — "even at the final dissolution, when the faces of others become pale with fear, the face of the Mother alone remains smiling." That is the best of the three, because it turns a decorative epithet into a claim about what She is like at the end of the world.

A fourth takes दर in the sense of protecting: her face is always gracious to her devotees.

अम्बुज returns from 105 सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा, where the lotus was the crown cakra; here it is her face. The same flower, once cosmological and once bodily — as पाटल two namas earlier was at once a blossom and a colour.

925. कौलिनीकेवला → कौलिनी-केवला

कौलिनी = the Goddess of the Kaula path (vṛddhi derivative of कुल, feminine ङीप्)
केवला = alone, sole, unmixed, absolute; devoid of attributes
"She who is Kaulinī, and alone."

Vigraha: कौलिनी च केवला च।

केवल is the word standing behind कैवल्य in the next nama, so 925 and 926 are joined at the root: She is केवला, and what She gives is कैवल्य.

Bhāskararāya's senses of केवल are unusually wide, and one of them reaches outside his own tradition. केवल is the knowledge of Īśvara, "because we often see it thus used in the Jaina Tantras" — a rare citation of Jaina usage here, where kevala is of course the technical term for omniscience. Or केवल is devoid of all attributes, or freed from pleasure and pain: Śiva Sūtra 3.35 names Śiva as the Kevalin, "freed from those two." The Viśva's list is then given — a certain kind of knowledge; one, complete; decision; deception — of which he says the first three are to be taken here, declining the fourth.

A further reading takes केवल as "decided": She is settled upon, determined, by the Kaulas. And a variant reading of the nama itself gives कालिनी केवला, "she is the pure time."

कुल and its derivatives are now on a third pass — the seven namas at 90–96, then 897 कुलरूपिणी, and here the कौलिनी of 94 returning by name. At this point Bhāskararāya has a discussion of how the names are to be divided, which Sastry's translation explicitly drops.

926. अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी → अन्-अर्घ्य-कैवल्य-पद-दायिनी

अन् = not (नञ् before a vowel)
अर्घ्य = having a price, purchasable, to be valued (from अर्घ "price, worth") — hence अनर्घ्य, priceless
कैवल्य = absoluteness, isolation, final liberation (the abstract of केवल)
पद = place, station, state
दायिनी = she who gives, bestower (दा + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who bestows the priceless state of Kaivalya."

Vigraha: अनर्घ्यं कैवल्यपदं ददातीति।

The dev field reads ऽनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी with an initial avagraha. The nama is अनर्घ्य-; the avagraha marks the अ elided in कौलिनीकेवला + अनर्घ्य → कौलिनीकेवलानर्घ्य (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101). Third artifact of that class in the text, after ऽनवद्याङ्गी at 50 and ऽऽज्ञा at 828.

अर्घ्य was the word for the oblation eight namas back, at 918 चैतन्यार्घ्यसमाराध्या — and it comes from अर्घ, worth: what is offered is what has value. Here the same stem negated makes liberation priceless, beyond the worth of any offering. The text sets them close.

Bhāskararāya glosses अनर्घ्य as unlimited rather than merely costly, and कैवल्यपद as the fifth state of salvation — which places it within the set of five he had declined to name at 839 मुक्तिनिलया, where he said only that there are five kinds. This nama names the last of them. Some, he adds, prefix अ, on which reading आ means "everywhere."

दायिनी for the third time — 117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी, 851 जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी, and here. What She gives has escalated across them: good fortune, then rest, now the final state.

Note on the verse. Four namas in two pairs. 923–924 concern how She is approached and how She appears — worshipped by the competent and incompetent alike, and smiling faintly through all of it. 925–926 are joined at the root केवल: She is alone, and what She gives is aloneness.

923 is the finest piece of construction in this run. Because आ + अ and आ + आ collapse to one long vowel, दक्षिणादक्षिणा is at once "dakṣiṇa and dakṣiṇa" and "dakṣiṇa and a-dakṣiṇa," and nothing in the writing can decide between them. The choice is not cosmetic: on one reading She is worshipped with offerings by the wise, on another by wise and foolish equally, on a third the a-dakṣiṇas are the knowers of Brahman and outrank the ritualists altogether.

Read with 912, the direction of travel is plain. There the Vāma and Dakṣiṇa paths were carefully distinguished, ranked, and fenced with penalties. Eleven namas later the distinction is dissolved in a compound that cannot be made to hold it.

And 924's reading of दर as fear deserves keeping on its own account: at the dissolution, when every other face goes pale, hers alone is smiling.

Textual note. 926's dev carries the avagraha of the preceding sandhi as if it belonged to the nama — third instance of that class, after 50 and 828. 925's commentary is abridged by the translator at the point where Bhāskararāya takes up the division of the names.


---

## स्तोत्रप्रिया स्तुतिमती श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा । मनस्विनी मानवती महेशी मङ्गलाकृतिः

*stotrapriyā stutimatī śrutisaṃstutavaibhavā । manasvinī mānavatī maheśī maṅgalākṛtiḥ*

Verse 172, namas 927–933.

927. स्तोत्रप्रिया → स्तोत्र-प्रिया

स्तोत्र = a hymn of praise, a eulogy (स्तु "to praise" with the suffix त्र)
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in hymns of praise."

Vigraha: स्तोत्रं प्रियं यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya first gives the six constituents of a worldly stotra: नमस्कार salutation, आशिस् blessing, सिद्धान्तोक्ति praising the attainments, पराक्रम praising exploits, विभूति rehearsing glory, प्रार्थना prayer for prosperity.

And then he does something this commentary almost never does — he assigns namas of this very text to the six as instances. Nama 627, "worshipped by the three worlds," for namaskāra; 928 for the second; 735 for the third; 658 इच्छाशक्ति for the fourth; 692 for the fifth. So the Sahasranāma is read as a specimen of the genre it belongs to, and one of the instances cited is the next word in this very verse.

A second reading takes स्तोत्र as Vedic praise, the rehearsing of the gods' attributes in the mantras that celebrate them. A third extracts अप्, water — "the waters which are to be praised" — and identifies those waters as Devas, Pitṛs, men and Asuras, on the Śruti "these are the four waters," with Chāndogya 5.3.3, "in the fifth oblation the water becomes men," and Mahānārāyaṇa 14.1, "all this indeed is water."

प्रिया for the seventh time in this run — 115, 881, 887, 898, 909, 919, and here.

928. स्तुतिमती → स्तुति-मती

स्तुति = praise, a hymn (from स्तु "to praise")
मती = possessing (the suffix मतुप्, feminine ङीप्)
"She who possesses praise — the recipient of hymns."

Vigraha: स्तुतिः अस्याः अस्तीति स्तुतिमती।

मतुप् is the same possessive suffix as in श्रीमत् at 56 — possessing śrī there, possessing praise here.

Bhāskararāya's alternative reads मति as knowledge instead of as the possessive: स्तुति "by praising her," मति "knowledge, and dominion, are obtained." On that reading the nama names the fruit of praise rather than its object.

This is the nama he had just cited under 927 as the text's own instance of the second mark of praise. The verse holds both the theory and one of its examples, side by side.

929. श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा → श्रुति-सम्-स्तुत-वैभवा

श्रुति = the Veda, what is heard (from श्रु "to hear"); also, as a numeral word, four
सम् = fully, completely
स्तुत = praised, celebrated (past participle of स्तु)
वैभवा = glory, majesty, might (vṛddhi derivative of विभव)
"She whose glory is celebrated by the Vedas."

Vigraha: श्रुतिभिः संस्तुतं वैभवं यस्याः सा।

The third स्तु-nama in succession — स्तोत्र, स्तुति, संस्तुत — the one root carried through two nouns and a participle.

The Amarakośa (501) gives संस्तुत the sense of experience, so Bhāskararāya reads the compound as her greatness being experienced by the scriptures rather than merely spoken of by them.

A second reading takes श्रुति as the numeral four: her glory is experienced in four ways — the Person in the body, the Person in the metres, the Person in the scriptures, and the great Person described in the Bahvṛca Upaniṣad. She is thus in four vyūhas. The Kūrma Purāṇa supplies a matching four: "Devī has four Śaktis, declared to be her own nature, and she is the support of these four — Śānti, Vidyā, Pratiṣṭhā and Nivṛtti. Hence the supreme Lord is said to be four-formed; by these four Śaktis the supreme Lord enjoys his own bliss."

Those four are the five kalās of 853 शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका with the highest removed. There the five were निवृत्ति, प्रतिष्ठा, विद्या, शान्ति and शान्त्यतीता, and She was named as the last of them; here the lower four are Her śaktis and She their support. The same scheme approached from its two ends — and प्रतिष्ठा, the second of the five, had been a nama in its own right at 829.

930. मनस्विनी → मनस्-विनी

मनस् = mind (from मन् "to think")
विनी = possessing (the suffix विन्, feminine ङीप्)
"She who possesses mind — the intelligent."

Vigraha: मनः अस्याः अस्तीति मनस्विनी।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is five words: "the mind depends upon her." He reads the possessive as a dependence — not that She has a mind, but that mind has Her.

मनस्विन् in ordinary Sanskrit means high-minded, spirited, wise, and the nama takes that colour too.

931. मानवती → मान-वती

मान = pride, self-regard, honour; also a measure, a means of proof; and per the commentary, elevation of mind, regard, and the expression that indicates forgiveness of sin
वती = possessing (मतुप् after a vowel-final stem, feminine ङीप्)
"She who possesses dignity."

Vigraha: मानः अस्याः अस्तीति मानवती।

Bhāskararāya lists the senses of मान without choosing among them: elevation of mind, regard, the expression indicating forgiveness of sin, proof, or measurement. The last two belong to logic — मान is a standard word for a means of valid knowledge — so the nama reads as "she who possesses the means of cognition" quite as readily as "the proud."

मान as pride returns from 856 गर्विता, where the pride was located precisely as "supreme egoism concerning the creation of the universe." Here it is left unspecified.

928, 930 and 931 are three possessives in a row — मती, विनी, वती — the same grammatical move made three times with three suffixes.

932. महेशी → महा-ईशी

महा = great (महत् in composition)
ईशी = mistress, sovereign lady (from ईश् "to rule")
"Maheśī — the Great Sovereign."

Vigraha: महती ईशी महेशी। or महेशस्य पत्नी महेशी।

Sandhi: महा + ईशी → महेशी (आ + ई → ए by guṇa, Pāṇini 6.1.87 आद्गुणः).

The Devī Purāṇa gives three reasons in a single clause, and they do not agree with one another: "as she was born from Mahādeva, and worshipped by great men, and as she is the wife of Maheśa, she is called Maheśī." Daughter, object of worship, and wife — three relations to the same मह, offered without any attempt to reconcile them.

ईश्वरी had stood at 831 प्राणेश्वरी, sovereign over the breaths. The bare ईशी here makes the sovereignty absolute rather than over something.

933. मङ्गलाकृतिः → मङ्गल-आकृतिः

मङ्गल = auspicious, blessed; welfare, good fortune
आकृतिः = form, shape, outward configuration (आ + कृ "to make")
"She whose form is auspiciousness."

Vigraha: मङ्गला आकृतिः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: मङ्गल + आकृतिः → मङ्गलाकृतिः (आ by 6.1.101). index.html carries no commentary for this nama beyond the verse marker.

आकृति returns from 830 प्रकटाकृतिः, where Her form was manifest; the two are built identically, an adjective with आकृति in a bahuvrīhi. And the sense repeats 116 भद्रमूर्तिः almost exactly — भद्र with मूर्ति there, मङ्गल with आकृति here, both saying that Her very form is auspiciousness. The Sahasranāma states it twice, eight hundred namas apart, changing both words.

The verse ends where 115–117 had ended, at the auspicious. There the movement was delight in it, then being it, then conferring it; here it is simply asserted.

Note on the verse. Seven namas in two groups, marked by sound: three on स्तु — the hymn, the praise, the Vedic celebration — and four on म — mind, dignity, sovereignty, auspicious form. The स्तु-group concerns how She is addressed, the म-group what She possesses, with three possessive suffixes running before the last two drop the pattern.

The moment worth marking is at 927. Bhāskararāya lists the six marks of a stotra and then names namas of this text as instances of each — 627, 928, 735, 658, 692 — so the Sahasranāma is being read as a specimen of its own genre, with one of the instances falling as the next word in the verse. The commentary rarely stands outside the text like this.

929's four śaktis are the second half of a scheme this run has now seen twice. Śānti, Vidyā, Pratiṣṭhā and Nivṛtti are four of the five kalās named at 853, where She was the fifth and highest; here the lower four are Hers and She is their support.

And 933 repeats 116 in different words — a useful reminder that the thousand names are not a thousand distinct claims.

Textual note. This verse is clean — the third, after 162 and 168. 933 has no commentary body.


---

## विश्वमाता जगद्धात्री विशालाक्षी विरागिणी । प्रगल्भा परमोदारा परमोदा मनोमयी

*viśvamātā jagaddhātrī viśālākṣī virāgiṇī । pragalbhā paramodārā paramodā manomayī*

Verse 173, namas 934–941.

934. विश्वमाता → विश्व-माता

विश्व = all, the whole, the universe; also Viṣṇu
माता = mother
"The Mother of the universe."

Vigraha: विश्वस्य माता।

Bhāskararāya adds only the alternative: विश्व is Viṣṇu, on the authority of the Śruti — so "mother of Viṣṇu." That claim has already been reached twice in this run by other routes: at 892 वैष्णवी, as the second of the Devī Purāṇa's four senses, and at 894 अयोनिः, by taking अ as Viṣṇu and योनि as mother. Three namas within forty arrive at the same statement by three different divisions.

विश्व for the fourth time in this stretch — 889 the universe She turns, 890 the universe She eats, and now the universe She mothers. Turner, devourer, mother.

935. जगद्धात्री → जगत्-धात्री

जगत् = the world — literally "the moving" (from गम् "to go")
धात्री = she who bears, sustains, upholds; also a nurse (धा "to place, to bear" + तृ, feminine ङीप्)
"The Sustainer of the world."

Vigraha: जगतः धात्री।

Sandhi: जगत् + धात्री → जगद्धात्री, the त् voicing to द् before ध्.

The compound sets motion against support: जगत् is the world named by its restlessness, and धात्री is what holds it still. The Devī Purāṇa gives the etymology outright — "the root धा means to bear, sustain, hence she is called by the wise the sustainer of the Universe" — and adds, "wherefore you sustain the world and assign functions to them."

धात्री also means a nurse, and Bhāskararāya takes it so: nurse, because she protects. Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.22 — "he is the protector of the world, he is the firm bridge for the sake of preserving the order of the beings."

धात्री is formed as सवित्री was at 826, दात्री at 832 and कर्त्री at 882 — the तृ agent-noun with ङीप्, a formation this stretch of the text uses constantly. And the support-thread runs on: 829 प्रतिष्ठा, what all things stand on; 877 निरालम्बा, herself unsupported; 884 धर्माधारा, support of the law; and here the world's sustainer.

936. विशालाक्षी → विशाल-अक्षी

विशाल = wide, broad, spacious (वि + शाल); also a place-name
अक्षी = eyed, having eyes (अक्षि with the feminine)
"She of the wide eyes."

Vigraha: विशाले अक्षिणी यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: विशाल + अक्षी → विशालाक्षी (आ by 6.1.101). The plain sense is descriptive, and this is one of very few purely physical namas in this stretch — the last was the faint smile at 924.

But Bhāskararāya reads it as a pīṭha. Viśālākṣī is, per the Padma Purāṇa, the deity worshipped at Benares; and विशाल also names a place, taken here as the Nepāla-pīṭha rather than Badarikāśrama, both lying in the Himālaya. The Brahmāṇḍa and other Purāṇas direct, in the Pīṭhanyāsa, that the Nepāla-pīṭha be meditated upon as situated in the eyes. So विशाल is the pīṭha and अक्षि the eyes: Her eyes are that pīṭha in Her universal form.

This is the same logic as 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी, where the fifty-one pīṭhas were Her form and were set in the places of the mātṛkās. There the whole set was named at once; here one of them is located in a particular feature of the body.

937. विरागिणी → वि-रागिणी

वि = away, without — the privative prefix
रागिणी = passionate, having राग — attachment, desire; and also colour (from रञ्ज् "to be dyed, to be coloured")
"The Dispassionate One."

Vigraha: विगतः रागः यस्याः सा।

The pada carried in this file reads विरा-अगिणी, which invents both members; the split is simply वि + रागिणी, the ordinary privative on राग. index.html has no commentary for this nama.

राग means passion and colour alike, since it comes from रञ्ज् "to dye" — so विरागिणी is literally the uncoloured as well as the unattached. That is worth noting fifteen namas after 922 तरुणादित्यपाटला, where colour was made a function of the meditation rather than of Her. The two namas agree: no colour is properly Hers.

The nama also sits oddly beside 863 कामकेलितरङ्गिता, where She rippled with the play of love. The text does not reconcile them — and by its own doctrine at 922, it need not.

938. प्रगल्भा → प्र-गल्भा

प्र = forth, exceedingly — the intensive prefix
गल्भा = bold, confident, resolute (from गल्भ् "to dare")
"The Bold One."

Vigraha: प्रकृष्टा गल्भा प्रगल्भा।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is one line and it fixes the sphere of the boldness: "she is strong in the action of creation and the rest" — creation, preservation, destruction. Not boldness of temper, then, but of function.

The prādi formation is the same as 827 प्रचण्डा, where प्र intensified fierceness. Both namas name a forceful quality, and both are given a cosmological rather than a personal reference.

939. परमोदारा → परम-उदारा

परम = highest, supreme
उदारा = generous, munificent, noble; and per the Amarakośa, great (उत् + ऋ "to rise")
"The supremely generous."

Vigraha: परमा उदारा।

Sandhi: परम + उदारा → परमोदारा (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, Pāṇini 6.1.87 आद्गुणः).

The Amarakośa (470) gives उदार as "great," and Bhāskararāya takes the greatness as extension: "she is great in space and time," with the Śruti "he is like ether, all-pervading, eternal."

Then three re-divisions, and the syllable र does duty as "gives" once again. परा supreme, मोद bliss, अ on all sides, र gives — She who gives bliss on every side. Or परम much, उद water, meaning the ocean and here the ocean of worldly existence, आरा weapons — She is the destroyer of Her devotees' saṃsāra. Or prefix अ to get अपरम, divided as अप "gone" and राम "joy," meaning the miserable: and to such persons She is उदारा, generous.

उदार returns from 848 उदारकीर्तिः, where the same stem was divided five ways on the syllable अर. And the prefix-अ device makes its sixth appearance — 830, 847, 868, 905, 926, and here.

940. परमोदा → परम-उदा

परम = highest, supreme
उदा = delight, joy
"The supremely delightful."

Vigraha: परमा उदा।

Bhāskararāya glosses आमोद, taking the compound as परम + आमोद, "sweet smell," and hence fame — fragrance being the standard figure for renown. Or he divides आ "on all sides" with मोद "happiness."

939 and 940 share their first member and lie in adjacent senses, so the pair reads as a doubling: supremely generous, supremely delighting. And there is a closer relation than that. Bhāskararāya's own re-division of 939 had already extracted मोद, bliss, from within परमोदारा — so 940 is that extraction standing as a nama in its own right. The text does this repeatedly; the clearest earlier instance was 892 वैष्णवी and 893 विष्णुरूपिणी, where the fourth sense of the one became the whole of the other.

941. मनोमयी → मनस्-मयी

मनस् = mind (from मन् "to think")
मयी = made of, consisting of (the suffix मय, feminine ई)
"She who consists of mind."

Vigraha: मनसा निर्मिता मनोमयी।

Sandhi: मनस् + मयी → मनोमयी, the अस् becoming ओ before a voiced consonant, as regularly with मनस् in composition — मनोरथ, मनोहर.

The formation matches 907 तत्त्वमयी, मय with the feminine, "made of." There it was the tattvas; here the mind.

Bhāskararāya's first reason is practical: "because the pure Brahman is to be fixed in the mind." Then the Vasiṣṭha Rāmāyaṇa, which is the sharpest citation in the verse — "that Bhairava, Śiva, is said to be Cidākāśa; his own Spandaśakti is known as Manomayī." Sastry's footnote adds that the Spandaśakti is the śakti manifesting from Earth to Śiva. So the nama names Her as the vibrating power of the consciousness-ether, not merely as mental stuff.

A second reading makes mind the chief instrument, on Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.19 — "by mind alone it is to be seen" — manas being the principal means in the production of self-knowledge.

मनस् for the second time in twelve namas, after 930 मनस्विनी. There the mind depended upon Her; here She consists of it.

Note on the verse. Eight namas in two quartets, वि- and then प- with म-. The वि-group descends from the cosmic to the bodily: mother of the universe, sustainer of the world, wide-eyed, dispassionate. The second quartet ascends the other way, from quality to constitution: bold, supremely generous, supremely delighting, made of mind.

934–935 make the better pair. जगत् is "the moving" and धात्री "the bearer," so one compound holds restlessness and support together — and the two namas together set mothering beside sustaining.

930 and 941 do at small scale what 906–907 did at large. There it was beyond the tattvas and made of the tattvas; here it is mind depending on Her and Her consisting of mind.

940 shows the commentary's own re-division turning into the next nama: Bhāskararāya extracted मोद from परमोदारा as an alternative reading, and परमोदा is that alternative standing on its own.

And 937 is worth a pause. राग is passion and colour both, from रञ्ज् "to dye," so the nama says She is uncoloured as much as unattached — which is precisely what 922 had spent a long note establishing.

Textual note. This verse is clean — the fourth, after 162, 168 and 172. Two smaller matters: 937's computed pada reads विरा-अगिणी, inventing both members where the split is only वि + रागिणी, and 937 has no commentary body.


---

## व्योमकेशी विमानस्था वज्रिणी वामकेश्वरी । पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी

*vyomakeśī vimānasthā vajriṇī vāmakeśvarī । pañcayajñapriyā pañcapretamañcādhiśāyinī*

Verse 174, namas 942–947.

942. व्योमकेशी → व्योम-केशी

व्योम = sky, ether, space (व्योमन्)
केशी = haired, having hair (केश with the feminine ई)
"She whose hair is the ether."

Vigraha: व्योम केशाः यस्याः सा।

The primary reading belongs to the Virāṭ form: in Her universal body the ether is Her hair. That is the same procedure as 936 विशालाक्षी six namas back, where a pīṭha was located in Her eyes, and as 847 तलोदरी, where Atala-loka was Her waist. The universal form is being assembled feature by feature across the text.

Bhāskararāya's alternatives. She is wife of Vyomakeśa, Śiva, whose hair is the sky. Or व्योमक is read as "small" with ईशी as ruler — she rules even the atoms, which inverts the scale of the compound entirely. Or Vyomakeśa is Śiva in his ether-form and She his wife in the form of the quarters of space.

व्योम here, गगन at 855 गगनान्तस्था, वियत् at 837 वियत्प्रसूः — three words for the same ether and three relations to it. She is its mother, She dwells within it, She wears it.

943. विमानस्था → विमान-स्था

विमान = a celestial car; and by division, वि with मान — measure, proof, protection, or limitation
स्था = abiding, standing
"She who abides in the celestial chariot."

Vigraha: विमाने तिष्ठतीति विमानस्था।

The primary reading is not that She rides in one, but that She is not other than those who do: "vimānasthā are the Devas who remain in the celestial chariot; she is not different from them." The same identification made of Kubera at 885 and of the Vipras at 888.

Then six divisions on वि + मान — and मान is precisely the word Bhāskararāya had listed without choosing at 931 मानवती. Here he spends all of its senses. वि "much" with मान "protection" and स्थ "engaged": engaged in protecting her devotees. Or वि "much," म "light," अन "chariot": She rides radiant cars such as the Kiricakra. Or वि "without" with मा "limitation" — the unconditioned Brahman, in which She abides; or She who limits Brahman; or She who is herself unlimited. Or वि "much" with मा "measures," making विमान the scriptures: She is described in the Vedas. Or विमान as proof not opposed to the Vedas, in which She abides as Dharma. Or विमान as the fourteen Vidyās — Purāṇa, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā and the rest — with Jaimini's Sūtra 1.3.5–6 cited on whether an inferential statement may override: "no, because a system has its own limits."

The Kiricakra reading reaches back to 70 किरिचक्ररथारूढदण्डनाथापुरस्कृता, where that car was Daṇḍanāthā's in the Bhaṇḍāsura war. And the fourteen Vidyās had been named at 902 विज्ञानकलना, where the Kūrma Purāṇa made विज्ञान their retention in the mind.

944. वज्रिणी → वज्र-इणी

वज्र = the thunderbolt, Indra's weapon; a diamond; and per the Śruti, Brahman
इणी = the possessive suffix इन् with the feminine ङीप्, the न् retroflexed to ण् after the र् of वज्र (Pāṇini 8.4.2, रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे)
"She who bears the thunderbolt."

Vigraha: वज्रम् अस्ति अस्याः इति वज्रिणी।

The formation is exactly कुण्डलिनी's at 110 — the possessive इन् with ङीप् — differing only in that the र् of वज्र retroflexes the न्, by the same ṇatva rule that gave ब्रह्माणी its ण at 821.

Three readings stand in the gloss: the wife of Indra, who holds the vajra; or She who bears the vajra in her own hand; or She who is adorned with diamonds, वज्र being also the stone.

The fourth is the one Bhāskararāya develops. In the Śruti वज्र means Brahman — the "great terrible thunderbolt" — and She is वज्रिणी as related to Brahman as its limitator. That is the relation one reading of 943 had just proposed, of Her limiting the unconditioned. Two consecutive namas make Her the bound of the boundless.

The thunderbolt as Brahman had already been used at 827 प्रचण्डा, where Kaṭha Upaniṣad 6.2's "raised thunderbolt" was read as Brahman on Vedānta Sūtra 1.3.39 — the same identification put to opposite work. There it explained Her terror; here, Her office.

945. वामकेश्वरी → वामक-ईश्वरी

वामक = of the Vāma, belonging to the Vāma path; and by a second reading, from वम् "to create" — hence a progenitor
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady
"Vāmakeśvarī — Sovereign of the Vāma."

Vigraha: वामकानाम् ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: वामक + ईश्वरी → वामकेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

Vāmakeśvara is the name of a Tantra, and वाम are those who follow the doctrine it teaches. Bhāskararāya's gloss of वामक is unexpectedly harsh: contemptible, "because they do not perform the five sacrifices." The very next nama is पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया, She who delights in those five sacrifices.

The juxtaposition repeats the position taken at 912. There the Vāma follower was said to need no pañcayajñas, since whatever he offers goes to the deity of that path — and the verdict was nonetheless that "the Dakṣiṇā path is better." Here She is named sovereign of the Vāma in one breath and lover of the five sacrifices in the next, with nothing said to join them.

A second reading takes वामक from वम् "to create": Dakṣa and the other progenitors of the race. On that reading She is their sovereign and the Tantra drops out of the nama altogether.

946. पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया → पञ्च-यज्ञ-प्रिया

पञ्च = five
यज्ञ = sacrifice (from यज् "to sacrifice")
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in the five sacrifices."

Vigraha: पञ्चयज्ञाः प्रियाः यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya lists six competing sets of five, and that is the substance of the entry: the number is fixed and its content is not.

By the Śruti — Agnihotra, Darśapūrṇamāsa, Cāturmāsya, Paśu, Soma. By the Smṛtis — the deva-, pitṛ-, brahma-, bhūta- and manuṣya-yajñas. By the Pāñcarātra Āgama, five branches of worship — abhigamana, approaching the guru; upādāna, receiving instruction; ijyā, sacrifice; svādhyāya, repetition of mantras; and yoga, meditation. By the Kaula Āgama, five kinds of worship — Kevala, Yāmala, Miśra, Cakrayuk, Vīrasaṅgraha. By the Nityā Tantra, the five beginning with madya, which accomplish all desires. And by the Brahmatantra-kaumudī with its text the Mantramahodadhi, five kinds of women — Āturī, Sautakī, Daurbodhī, Trāsisādhanā, Bhāvinī.

Two further readings follow. The five oblations of water which, per Chāndogya 5.3.3, form a man's body at the last — the five places of sacrifice being Somaloka, Dyu, earth, man and woman. Or पञ्च taken as "extended" with यज्ञ as the abode of the world's creators.

That Chāndogya passage has now been cited three times within twenty namas — at 927 स्तोत्रप्रिया for the four waters, here for the five oblations, and again in the nama that follows this verse. The pañcāgni-vidyā is doing steady work in this stretch.

प्रिया for the eighth time in this run.

947. पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी → पञ्च-प्रेत-मञ्च-अधि-शायिनी

पञ्च = five
प्रेत = a corpse, one departed — literally gone forth (प्र + इ "to go")
मञ्च = a couch, a platform, a raised seat
अधि = upon, over
शायिनी = she who lies, who reclines (शी "to lie down" + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who reclines upon a couch of five corpses."

Vigraha: पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चे अधिशेते इति।

Sandhi: मञ्च + अधि → मञ्चाधि (आ by 6.1.101). प्रेत is literally "gone forth," so the five are not carrion but the departed — gods become inert.

Bhāskararāya names them precisely. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara are the four legs of the couch and Sadāśiva is the mattress; the Bhairavayāmala's fuller account adds the pillow — "on that great and pleasant couch whose pillow is Maheśāna, of whose four legs are Brahmā and the rest, and whose mattress is Sadāśiva, reclines the great Tripurasundarī, the great Queen." Saundaryalaharī 91 gives the same image: "Hari, Rudra and Īśvara became the four legs of your couch, and Sadāśiva became the pure white sheet."

This is the plainest statement of the doctrine the whole run has been circling. Kubera holds his office as Her at 885; the Vipras are Her form at 888; Viṣṇu is Her form at 893; Śiva is Her part at 910. Here the five highest gods are furniture. It is the same claim carried to its limit, and the image gives it a bluntness no gloss could.

Sadāśiva returns from 911 सदाशिवकुटुम्बिनी, thirty-six namas back, where She was his consort. Here he is her bedding, and the text does nothing to soften the transition.

Note on the verse. Six namas, four on व and two on पञ्च. The व-group concerns where She is and what She holds — ether for hair, the celestial car, the thunderbolt, sovereignty over the Vāma. The पञ्च-pair concerns the five: five sacrifices loved, five corpses lain upon.

The sharpest thing here is the seam between 945 and 946. वामक is glossed "contemptible, because they do not perform the five sacrifices," and the next nama makes Her the lover of exactly those five. Bhāskararāya had taken the same double position at 912, ranking the Dakṣiṇa path above the Vāma while allowing both to reach Her. Here the two attitudes stand adjacent with nothing said between them.

943 and 944 also pair, and less obviously. One reading of each makes Her the limitator of Brahman — विमान divided as वि + मा, either without limit or the limiter of the limitless; and वज्र taken as Brahman, with Her as its bound.

947 is where the run's governing doctrine reaches its limit. The five highest gods have been called Her office-holders, Her form, Her part; here they are the legs, mattress and pillow of Her couch.

Textual note. This verse is clean — the fifth, after 162, 168, 172 and 173. One small matter: 946's computed pada reads पञ्च-यज्ञप्रिया, merging the last two members where the compound has three.

## पञ्चमी पञ्चभूतेशी पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचारिणी । शाश्वती शाश्वतैश्वर्या शर्मदा शंभुमोहिनी

*pañcamī pañcabhūteśī pañcasaṅkhyopacāriṇī । śāśvatī śāśvataiśvaryā śarmadā śambhumohinī*

Verse 175, namas 948–954.

948. पञ्चमी → पञ्चमी

पञ्चमी = the fifth (feminine ordinal of पञ्चन् "five")
"The Fifth."

Vigraha: पञ्चानां पूरणी पञ्चमी।

The nama continues 947 directly. In the order Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva, the fifth is Sadāśiva — whose four lower members were the legs of the couch in the previous nama — and Her being पञ्चमी makes Her his consort. But Bhāskararāya at once uses the Sūta Saṃhitā to say that even the fifth needs Her: "Rudra is the best of the three; Sadāśiva, who is with the Mother and is possessed of permanence, is better than the omniscient Śiva, the possessor of Māyā. Of this there is no need of discussion." Sadāśiva outranks Śiva because he is with Her.

A second sense is conventional rather than derivative: पञ्चमी means Vārāhī by rūḍhi, established usage. Bhāskararāya works the point carefully. The word is often used derivatively — She is the fifth in the order of Brāhmī and the rest, and the last of the Pañcaratna deities as of the five sheaths — yet in the Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā and elsewhere it is plainly conventional: "one should worship the son of the fifth," "one should meditate in his heart on the Pañcamī," "the Pañcamī yantras are very difficult to obtain in the three worlds." He allows either.

Then the Kaula reading. पञ्च with म — She is the fifth M, which is bliss. The Kalpa Sūtra (Parā 1.12): "bliss is the form of Brahman, that is established in the body; there are five M's which indicate that, and the worship of Devī by these five is secret." Or She is the five M's taken collectively. He refers them to the Tripurā Upaniṣad, "and their meaning, namely gift, purification and so on, must be learned from the guru." That is the second time in this stretch he refers the reader to a teacher; the first was the light of the two samādhis at 907.

Two further senses close the entry. पञ्चमी as the fifth oblation, the offering of semen in the woman, on Chāndogya 5.3.3 — "in the fifth oblation the water forms person." Or पञ्चमी as the fifth state of salvation, which is the कैवल्यपद named at 926, twenty-two namas back.

949. पञ्चभूतेशी → पञ्च-भूत-ईशी

पञ्च = five
भूत = an element; a being; literally what has become (past participle of भू "to be")
ईशी = mistress, ruler (from ईश् "to rule")
"She who rules the five elements."

Vigraha: पञ्चभूतानाम् ईशी।

Sandhi: भूत + ईशी → भूतेशी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87). भूत is literally "become," the elements named as what has come into being, so the compound sets Her over the whole of becoming in its five parts.

Bhāskararāya's alternative is unexpected and entirely material. पञ्चभूत means "fivefold," and what is fivefold is the Vaijayantī garland, made of five elements and five gems. The Viṣṇu Purāṇa: "the club-bearer's garland is five-formed as it consists of five elements; it is also called the element-garland." The Viṣṇu Rahasya assigns the stones to their elements — "from earth comes the blue-black gem, from water pearl, from fire the Kaustubha, from air Vaidūrya, from ether Puṣparāga" — the five jewels being given elsewhere as pearl, māṇikya, marakata, sapphire and diamond. So a nama about rule over the elements turns into a description of Viṣṇu's necklace.

ईशी returns from 932 महेशी, where the sovereignty was absolute; here it has an object again.

950. पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचारिणी → पञ्च-सङ्ख्या-उपचारिणी

पञ्च = five
सङ्ख्या = number, enumeration (सम् + ख्या "to reckon")
उपचारिणी = she who is served, attended upon (उप + चर् "to move towards, to serve")
"She who is worshipped with the five services."

Vigraha: पञ्चसङ्ख्यैः उपचारैः उपचरिता।

Sandhi: सङ्ख्या + उपचारिणी → सङ्ख्योपचारिणी (आ + उ → ओ by guṇa, 6.1.87).

The five are named plainly: scent, flowers, incense, lamp, and the offering of food — the pañcopacāra of ordinary daily worship. After the six competing sets of five at 946 and the secret five M's at 948, this is the domestic and uncontested five.

उपचार is literally a moving-towards, उप + चर् — service understood as approach. The same root gave आचार at 98 समयाचारतत्परा.

Bhāskararāya drops a counting marker here: the thirty-second verse divides fifty names. index.html's body for this nama also carries a passage on the guru-lineage meditation — "meditate in your pure heart on the succession of Gurus from Śiva to one's own Guru, who are the suns of all good qualities, lords of the Devas, the destroyers of the four kinds of births, the givers of four kinds of bliss (Dṛḍha, Āmoda, Ghana and Sukha), the expounders of the Vedas" — which reads as an interpolated benedictory verse rather than as commentary on this nama, and is garbled at its close.

951. शाश्वती → शाश्वती

शाश्वती = eternal, perpetual, everlasting (vṛddhi derivative of शश्वत् "again and again, continually")
"The Eternal."

Vigraha: शश्वत् भवा शाश्वती।

The derivation is worth having, because it makes eternity out of repetition. शश्वत् means "again and again," and शाश्वत is its vṛddhi derivative: the everlasting is what keeps recurring.

Bhāskararāya takes exactly that sense and turns it towards the devotee — शश्वत् "frequently," so She is worshipped continuously by her devotees, with Kaṭha Upaniṣad 5.12: "to them alone belongs eternal attainment, not to others." The eternity is thus read as much in the worship as in Her.

952. शाश्वतैश्वर्या → शाश्वत-ऐश्वर्या

शाश्वत = eternal, perpetual
ऐश्वर्या = lordship, dominion, sovereignty (vṛddhi derivative of ईश्वर)
"She whose dominion is eternal."

Vigraha: शाश्वतम् ऐश्वर्यं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: अ + ऐ → ऐ by vṛddhi (Pāṇini 6.1.88 वृद्धिरेचि) — the same rule the Nityā Tantra applied at 872 to derive त्रयी's ऐ from the opening letters of the three Vedas.

Bhāskararāya's alternative divides the compound quite differently, by prefixing a syllable — the seventh use of that device in this run. Prefix इ and read ईश as the rulers of the universe, Brahmā and the rest, that is, the five corpses; अश्वत as the condition of being a horse, a vehicle; and ऐश्वर्य as dominion. The five corpses form Her seat. So a nama about eternal sovereignty is made to restate 947's couch, five namas back.

ऐश्वर्य is built on ईश्वर, the stem behind ईश्वरी at 831 and ईशी at 932 and 949 — the fourth turn of ईश् in this stretch.

953. शर्मदा → शर्म-दा

शर्म = happiness, joy; and shelter, refuge (शर्मन्)
दा = giving, she who gives (from दा "to give")
"The Giver of happiness."

Vigraha: शर्म ददातीति शर्मदा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

शर्मन् carries shelter as well as joy — it is what covers, and so what comforts — so what the nama gives is a refuge rather than a pleasure. The bare दा is the simplest of the giving-forms this run has used, after दायिनी at 117, 851 and 926, and दात्री at 832.

954. शंभुमोहिनी → शम्भु-मोहिनी

शम्भु = Śambhu, the benign — the one from whom well-being comes (शम् "well-being" + भू "to be")
मोहिनी = she who bewilders, enchants, infatuates (from मुह् "to be confused," in the causative)
"She who bewilders Śambhu."

Vigraha: शम्भुं मोहयतीति शम्भुमोहिनी।

index.html carries no commentary here beyond the verse marker.

मुह् is the root that gave मुग्धा at 868, where She was the bewildered one — the Viśva's two senses, "beautiful and ignorant," both from that root. Here She is the bewilderer, and the object is Śiva. The reversal is the same device as 894–895, a term first applied to Her and then turned outward.

So the verse ends where several in this run have ended, on Her precedence over Śiva stated as a fact of relation. He was Her part at 910, her mattress at 947; at 948 the Sūta Saṃhitā ranked Sadāśiva above Śiva precisely because Sadāśiva is with Her; and now She bewilders him.

Note on the verse. Seven namas: three on पञ्च, four on श.

The पञ्च-triad completes a long sequence. 946 loved the five sacrifices, 947 lay upon the five corpses, and 948–950 give the fifth, the five elements and the five services — six consecutive namas built on one number, with the sets of five multiplying as they go: six competing sets at 946, the secret five M's at 948, and the plain domestic five at 950.

948 is the densest of them and gathers several threads at once. Sadāśiva is the fifth of the series whose four lower members were couch-legs in the previous nama. The fifth state of salvation is the कैवल्यपद of 926. The fifth oblation is Chāndogya 5.3.3, now cited three times in this stretch. And the fifth M is bliss, which Bhāskararāya will not expound, referring the reader to the guru as he had for the light of the samādhis at 907.

951's etymology deserves marking. शाश्वती is the vṛddhi derivative of शश्वत्, "again and again," so eternity here is built out of recurrence — and Bhāskararāya reads it in that direction deliberately, making eternal attainment a matter of continuous worship.

And 954 closes on the reversal of 868. There मुग्धा made Her the bewildered; here मोहिनी makes Her Śiva's bewilderer. With 910, 947 and 948, that is four namas within fifty asserting Her precedence over him — as his part, his overlord, his bed, and now his confusion.

Textual note. This verse is clean — the sixth. Three smaller matters: 950's body carries an interpolated benedictory verse on the succession of gurus, garbled at its close, belonging neither to this nama nor to the commentary proper; and 953 and 954 have no commentary bodies at all.

## धरा धरसुता धन्या धर्मिणी धर्मवर्धिनी । लोकातीता गुणातीता सर्वातीता शमात्मिका

*dharā dharasutā dhanyā dharmiṇī dharmavardhinī । lokātītā guṇātītā sarvātītā śamātmikā*

Verse 176, namas 955–963.

955. धरा → धरा

धरा = the earth — she who bears (from धृ "to hold, to support")
"The Earth."

Vigraha: धरति इति धरा।

धरा is from धृ, the same root as धात्री at 935 and आधारा at 884, the earth named simply as the bearer. The support-thread reaches its plainest member here: 829 प्रतिष्ठा, what all things stand on; 877 निरालम्बा, herself unsupported; 884 धर्माधारा, support of the law; 935 जगद्धात्री, sustainer of the world; and now the earth itself.

Bhāskararāya's alternative is supporter of the universe. Then a phonetic identification: धरा is the letter ल, which represents her form. The Jñānārṇava — "the letter ल is the goddess of the earth, with mountains, forests and deserts, and having the fifty sacred places, and all the places of pilgrimage."

ल is the pṛthvī-bīja, and it had already been named as such at 855, where गगन was taken as ह and the semivowels य र ल व supplied the bījas of the five elements. The same letter, there one item in a list, here a nama. And the fifty sacred places in that quotation are the pīṭhas of 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी — so the earth-letter is made to contain the whole set.

956. धरसुता → धर-सुता

धर = a mountain — that which bears (from धृ); here Himavat
सुता = daughter (from सू "to bring forth")
"Daughter of the Mountain."

Vigraha: धरस्य सुता।

धर is the bearer, and the mountain is so named for the same reason the earth is — so 955 and 956 use one root for the earth and for her father. Her parentage is given by the root rather than by the name: Himavat is not mentioned, only "the bearer."

index.html carries 955's gloss and a duplicate of 955's body on this nama, so the commentary proper to धरसुता is not preserved. This is the fourth block-duplication in the run, after 858–859, 881–882 and 887–888, and here it starts a one-nama offset that runs on into 957.

The nama also sits against 932 महेशी, where the Devī Purāṇa explained the name partly as her being "born from Mahādeva." Daughter of the mountain here, daughter of Śiva there, and the text does not choose.

957. धन्या → धन्या

धन्या = fortunate, blessed, wealthy (from धन "wealth"); also a technical name for one of four kinds of meditation
"The Fortunate."

Vigraha: धनं यस्याः अस्ति सा धन्या।

index.html carries 956's gloss on this nama; its own heading survives at the head of its body, so the offset that began at 956 corrects itself here.

The plain readings first: fortune; or possessing wealth; or धन्या as a particular yoginī named in the Jyotiṣa Śāstra alongside Maṅgalā and Piṅgalā.

Then the substantial reading, which is a whole doctrine. धन्या is the third of four kinds of thought arising in the last stage, चरमकालीन — आर्त, रौद्र, धन्य and शुक्ल — and the Bhāgavata-uttara Purāṇa defines each. आर्त is the meditation in which illusion breeds desire for dominion, beds, seats, women, scents, garlands, jewels, cloths and ornaments. रौद्र is that in which desire rather than indifference arises even after wounds, fire, beating, cruelty and the breaking of limbs. धन्य is that in which, by following the meaning of the Upaniṣads and by performing the great vows, thought arises concerning the causes of bondage and liberation, of coming and going, of the tranquillity of the five senses, and of compassion for all beings. शुक्ल is that in which, by the yoga which destroys constructive imagination, the senses remain untainted by material objects and the inner Self is fixed on its unity with the one reality.

The fruits are then graded: the practiser of आर्त becomes an animal or a mineral, of रौद्र descends lower still, of धन्य goes to the Devas and attains good results, of शुक्ल is freed from further birth. "Therefore in meditation the wise man should cultivate the Śukla state, which removes the pain of rebirth, enables one to cross the ocean of existence, and calms passion."

So the nama names the third of four, and the commentary at once recommends the fourth. She is called by the name of the state that is good but not the best.

958. धर्मिणी → धर्म-इणी

धर्म = dharma, right order; and in logic, an attribute or property
इणी = the possessive suffix इन् with the feminine ङीप्, the न् retroflexed to ण् after र् (Pāṇini 8.4.2)
"She who possesses dharma."

Vigraha: धर्मः अस्याः अस्तीति धर्मिणी।

The formation is exactly वज्रिणी's at 944 — इन् with ङीप्, and ण by ṇatva after the र्.

Bhāskararāya reads धर्म in its logical sense, as attribute rather than duty: "the possessor of such attributes as experience of bliss, eternity and the rest." धर्मिन् is the standard technical term for the substrate that bears properties, set against धर्म the property itself — so the nama makes Her the bearer and not the virtue.

धर्म returns from 884 धर्माधारा, where She supported the law and Bhāskararāya gave dharma its customary definition. Here it is the logicians' sense; the next nama takes the moral sense again.

959. धर्मवर्धिनी → धर्म-वर्धिनी

धर्म = righteousness; and per the second reading, the conditions of the objective world
वर्धिनी = she who increases, who causes to grow (वृध् "to grow," in the causative); or, as the commentary takes it, she who cuts
"She who increases righteousness."

Vigraha: धर्मं वर्धयतीति धर्मवर्धिनी।

The Vāmana Purāṇa supplies the mechanism, and distributes three qualities among three deities: "control of the senses, purity, and wifehood with devotion refer respectively to Śaṃkara, the Sun, and to Devī — Śiva and his spouse, meditated upon by men, increase in them these three qualities." The increase works by meditation on the pair.

The second reading reverses the nama outright. वर्धिनी is taken from the root in its sense of cutting, so She is the destroyer of धर्म read as the conditions of the objective world. Increaser of righteousness, or cutter-away of conditionedness — and that is the third sense of धर्म in three consecutive namas.

विवर्धिनी had stood at 886 धनधान्यविवर्धिनी, increasing wealth and grain, where the growth was material and admitted no such reversal.

960. लोकातीता → लोक-अतीता

लोक = a world, a region; also the people, the jīvas
अतीता = gone beyond, transcended (अति + इ "to go")
"She who transcends the worlds."

Vigraha: लोकान् अतीता।

Sandhi: लोक + अतीता → लोकातीता (आ by 6.1.101). The first of three अतीता-namas in succession, each widening its object.

Bhāskararāya makes the transcendence topographical and precise. The lokas run from Indra's to Viṣṇu's; beyond them She resides in Paraśiva's city, Mahākailāsa. The Śivadharmottara places it — "above the abode of Viṣṇu, one should know the great divine city of Śiva." That city is called अपद, and men devoted to works return again from it. Above it are three supreme seats, "eternal, ever-pure, resorted to by Skanda, Umā and Śiva," and those who attain them by meditation do not return: "they become omniscient, omnipresent, pure, merged in Maheśvara, possessed of the strength of Śiva."

The distinction drawn there is between works and meditation — the city of Śiva is reached by works and does not hold; the three seats above it are reached by meditation and do. That is the same discrimination made at 913, where those who fall from both paths were provided for, and at 923, where the ritualists ranked below the knowers of Brahman.

A second reading takes लोक as the jīvas: transcending them.

961. गुणातीता → गुण-अतीता

गुण = a quality, an attribute; specifically the three guṇas — and literally a strand or thread
अतीता = gone beyond, transcended
"She who transcends the guṇas."

Vigraha: गुणान् अतीता।

index.html has no commentary for this nama, and its computed pada reads गुणा-अतीता, lengthening the first member where the split is गुण + अतीता.

गुण is literally a single strand of a cord, and the three guṇas are so named as the strands twisted into the rope of Prakṛti — so transcending them is getting free of a cord rather than of a quality. She has been placed beyond attributes twice already by other words: 862 कार्यकारणनिर्मुक्ता, free of cause and effect, and 906 तत्त्वाधिका, beyond the tattvas.

And the Śvetāśvatara verse cited at 866 अजा — अजाम् एकां लोहितशुक्लकृष्णाम्, the one unborn, red and white and black — had made those three colours the three guṇas. That verse's अजा stands as a nama; its guṇas are transcended here.

962. सर्वातीता → सर्व-अतीता

सर्व = all; and per the commentary, all words
अतीता = gone beyond, transcended
"She who transcends all."

Vigraha: सर्वम् अतीता।

The third and widest of the triad — after the worlds and the guṇas, everything.

But Bhāskararāya narrows it, and the narrowing is the point: सर्व means all words. The Jñānārṇava — "know Parabrahman, which transcends speech and is beyond counting, as ourself." So "transcending all" is read specifically as transcending language, which makes the nama a statement about the limits of the text it stands in: a thousand names for what no name reaches.

963. शमात्मिका → शम-आत्मिका

शम = tranquillity, quietude, the ceasing of activity (from शम् "to be quiet"); and per a second reading, bliss
आत्मिका = having the nature of, being the very self of (आत्मन् + क, feminine आ)
"She whose nature is tranquillity."

Vigraha: शमः आत्मा यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: शम + आत्मिका → शमात्मिका (आ by 6.1.101).

Bhāskararāya defines शम not as a mood but as an operation: "tranquillising the activity of the world." The Māṇḍūkya (7) and the Nṛsiṃhatāpinī (2) are cited together — "they hold that it is tranquillity of the activity of the world, peace, non-dual, the fourth." The fourth is turīya, so शम here names that state.

आत्मिका returns from 853 शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका, and that nama's शान्ति is this nama's शम, both from शम्. There She was what transcends śānti; here She is śama itself.

Note on the verse. Nine namas, the longest in this run, in two halves: five on ध, then the अतीता-triad and its resolution.

The ध-group turns on two roots. धरा the earth-bearer and धर the mountain-bearer both come from धृ, as did धात्री and आधारा before them. Then धर्म is taken three times in three namas — the logician's sense at 958, the moral sense at 959, having had its customary sense at 884 — and 959's second reading reverses even that, making वर्धिनी a cutter rather than an increaser.

960–962 are a graded ascent: beyond the worlds, beyond the guṇas, beyond all. And 962's gloss is the sharpest thing in the verse, because Bhāskararāya narrows "all" to "all words," citing the Jñānārṇava on the Parabrahman that transcends speech. In a text of a thousand names, a nama asserting that She is past naming is doing something pointed — and 948 had already refused to expound the five M's, and 907 the light of the samādhis, on the ground that a guru is needed.

963 then closes on identity instead of transcendence, and on the fourth state, which is where the ascent had been going.

957 is worth marking for its own reason. धन्या is the third of four kinds of last-stage meditation, and the commentary defines all four, grades their fruits, and recommends the fourth. She is named by the state that is good but not best.

Textual note. 956 carries 955's gloss and a duplicate of 955's body — the fourth block-duplication in this run — and begins a one-nama offset that corrects itself at 957, whose gloss is 956's while its body opens with its own heading. 961 has no commentary body, and its computed pada reads गुणा-अतीता for गुण-अतीता.

## बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या बाला लीलाविनोदिनी । सुमङ्गली सुखकरी सुवेषाढ्या सुवासिनी

*bandhūkakusumaprakhyā bālā līlāvinodinī । sumaṅgalī sukhakarī suveṣāḍhyā suvāsinī*

Verse 177, namas 964–970.

964. बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या → बन्धूक-कुसुम-प्रख्या

बन्धूक = the bandhūka tree and its blossom — per the commentary a tree of the Vaṅga country, its flower very red
कुसुम = flower, blossom
प्रख्या = resembling, having the appearance of; literally well-known, celebrated (प्र + ख्या "to make known")
"She whose hue is that of the bandhūka blossom."

Vigraha: बन्धूककुसुमम् इव प्रख्या यस्याः सा।

The dev field reads बन्धक- where the word is बन्धूक-, the ऊ lost. Bhāskararāya spells it out: "Bandhūka is a tree in the Vaṅga country, and its flower is very red." The gloss field for this nama also carries the tail of 963's commentary, "Atma, her," along with a verse marker.

प्रख्या is literally "well-known" — प्र + ख्या, to proclaim — used here for likeness, as what a thing is known to resemble. The same root gave सङ्ख्या at 950.

This is Her third red in the run, and each has been a different one. 891 विद्रुमाभा was coral, and coral is Her substance. 922 तरुणादित्यपाटला was the rose of the young sun, which the commentary there made the colour of the śṛṅgāra aspect specifically. Here it is the deep red of a named tree in a named country. And between the second and the third stands 937 विरागिणी, where राग is dye as much as passion — no colour properly Hers at all.

965. बाला → बाला

बाला = a girl, a young woman, a child (feminine of बाल)
"The Girl."

Vigraha: बाला कुमारी।

बाला is also the name of a particular goddess in the Śrīvidyā system, the Bālā-tripurasundarī whose mantra is distinct from Lalitā's — and She had been named at 74 भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालाविक्रमनन्दिता, where Bālā's valour in slaying Bhaṇḍa's sons delighted Her. There Bālā was another; here the name is Her own.

Bhāskararāya cites Śvetāśvatara 4.3, "thou art boy or girl," and the Tripurā Siddhānta: "O beloved one, as thou dost play like a child thou art called Bālā." The girlhood is read out of the playing, which makes the following nama its explanation.

The Śvetāśvatara has now stood three times in this run — at 866 अजा, behind the guṇa-verse at 961, and here. Its "thou art boy or girl" is the same universalising move as the ajā verse's red and white and black.

966. लीलाविनोदिनी → लीला-विनोदिनी

लीला = play, sport; also a proper name
विनोदिनी = she who takes delight, who diverts herself; also she who removes, drives away (वि + नुद् "to push away")
"She who delights in play."

Vigraha: लीलया विनोदते इति।

विनोद is from वि + नुद्, "to push away" — diversion in its literal sense, the setting aside of whatever is not the game. So the delight of this nama is itself an act of putting things aside.

लीला returns from 865 लीलाविग्रहधारिणी, where She assumed bodies in play. Bhāskararāya gave the same two readings there — the play of the universe's activity, and Līlā as a proper name — and here he tells the story he had only gestured at. Līlā, wife of Padmarāja in the Yogavāsiṣṭha, worshipped Sarasvatī, received knowledge from her, and brought her husband back to life. On that reading विनोदिनी takes its other sense: She leads that queen into right action.

A third reading takes लीला as a separate nama meaning Lakṣmī, on the Devī Purāṇa's etymology — "Lakṣmī is called Līlā because she fondles (lalana)."

With 965 the two make statement and cause: She is called a girl because She plays, and this nama says what the playing is.

967. सुमङ्गली → सु-मङ्गली

सु = well, very, beautifully
मङ्गली = auspicious, fortunate; and in ordinary usage a woman whose husband is living (मङ्गल with the feminine ई)
"The Auspicious One."

Vigraha: सुष्ठु मङ्गला सुमङ्गली।

Bhāskararāya's division is theological rather than intensive: सु "beautiful" and मङ्गल "Brahman." The Viṣṇu Purāṇa supplies the identification, and it is operational rather than descriptive — "that, by remembering which, drives away misfortune from men and gives much benefit, that supreme Brahman they know as Maṅgala." मङ्गल is thus not a quality but a name of Brahman, defined by what remembering it does.

The Atri Smṛti then gives an ethical definition beside it: "the performance of right action and avoiding wrong action is called Maṅgala by the Ṛṣis who speak of Brahman." Auspiciousness as conduct, not as luck.

मङ्गल returns from 933 मङ्गलाकृतिः, where Her very form was auspiciousness, and behind that from 116 भद्रमूर्तिः. And in its ordinary sense सुमङ्गली names a woman whose husband lives — which is exactly what 970 सुवासिनी says, three namas on.

968. सुखकरी → सुख-करी

सुख = happiness, ease (traditionally सु + ख, the good aperture — running smoothly, as of an axle-hole)
करी = she who makes, who causes (from कृ "to do")
"She who makes happiness."

Vigraha: सुखं करोतीति सुखकरी।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The traditional etymology of सुख is worth keeping, since it makes happiness a matter of things turning freely rather than of pleasure felt: सु with ख, the well-bored axle-hole. Its opposite दुःख is built the same way, and the pair name good and bad running.

करी is the briefest of the agent-forms this run has used, after कारिणी at 889, कर्त्री at 882, and the तृ-forms at 826, 832 and 935.

969. सुवेषाढ्या → सु-वेष-आढ्या

सु = well, beautifully
वेष = dress, attire, adornment
आढ्या = rich in, abounding in, endowed with
"She who is rich in beautiful attire."

Vigraha: सुवेषेण आढ्या।

Sandhi: वेष + आढ्या → वेषाढ्या (आ by 6.1.101). index.html has no commentary for this nama.

आढ्य means wealthy and governs what it is wealthy in, so the compound is not "beautifully dressed" but "wealthy in fine dress" — a claim about abundance rather than about taste. This is the run's only nama concerning clothing: her ornaments stood at 22 and 864, her colours at 891, 922 and 964.

970. सुवासिनी → सु-वासिनी

सु = well, auspiciously
वासिनी = dwelling, residing (from वस् "to dwell"); in usage, a woman dwelling in her husband's house, hence one whose husband is living
"The Ever-married."

Vigraha: सुष्ठु वसतीति सुवासिनी।

The word is technical in social usage rather than descriptive: a सुवासिनी is a woman whose husband lives, exempt from widowhood. Bhāskararāya's gloss makes the identification directly — Devī is not separate from such women.

That is the same move made of Kubera at 885, the Vipras at 888 and the celestial charioteers at 943: She is not other than the class named. Here the class is a social one, and the nama following this verse, सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता, makes their adoration the thing that pleases Her.

The nama also restates 967 in its plain sense. सुमङ्गली and सुवासिनी name one status in two words, three namas apart.

Note on the verse. Seven namas: three that describe or name Her, then four on सु-.

The first three run from colour to girlhood to play, and 965–966 stand as statement and cause — She is called Bālā because She plays, and लीलाविनोदिनी says what the playing is. The four सु-namas are auspiciousness, happiness, fine dress, and wifehood.

The verse is unusually domestic, and that is its shape. It ends on the married woman, 967 and 970 both name her, and the nama immediately after the verse makes the worship offered by such women Her pleasure.

964 gives Her a third red, and no two of the three are the same red. Coral at 891 is substance. The young sun's rose at 922 is, by the commentary's own account there, the colour of one aspect only. The bandhūka's deep red here belongs to a particular tree in a particular country. And 937 विरागिणी, standing between the second and third, denies that any colour is properly Hers.

967 carries the substantial gloss. मङ्गल is taken not as an adjective but as a name of Brahman, defined by what it does — that by remembering which misfortune departs — and then given the Atri Smṛti's definition in terms of conduct.

Textual note. 964's dev reads बन्धक for बन्धूक, the ऊ lost, which the commentary itself corrects by spelling the word out; its gloss field also carries the tail of 963's commentary and a verse marker. 968 and 969 have no commentary bodies.

And the verse-table row for this verse is one of the corrupted ones: its n field reads 977 — a nama number where a verse number belongs — so the table contains no verse numbered 177. The from–to range, 964–970, is sound.

## सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता आशोभना शुद्धमानसा । बिन्दुतर्पणसंतुष्टा पूर्वजा त्रिपुराम्बिका

*suvāsinyarcanaprītā āśobhanā śuddhamānasā । bindutarpaṇasaṃtuṣṭā pūrvajā tripurāmbikā*

Verse 178, namas 971–976.

971. सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता → सुवासिनी-अर्चन-प्रीता

सुवासिनी = a woman whose husband is living (as at 970)
अर्चन = worship, adoration (from अर्च् "to worship")
प्रीता = pleased, gratified (past participle of प्री "to please")
"She who is pleased by the worship of married women."

Vigraha: सुवासिनीनाम् अर्चनेन प्रीता।

Sandhi: सुवासिनी + अर्चन → सुवासिन्यर्चन, the ई becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि) — the same rule that gave शान्त्यतीत at 853. index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The nama takes up 970 directly and completes a small sequence: there She was not separate from such women, here their worship pleases Her. Offering and recipient are of one class — which is the pattern of 881–883, where She was the sacrifice's lover, performer and patron together.

अर्च् returns from 825 बुधार्चिता and 917 धीरसमर्चिता. There the worshippers were the wise; here they are the married women of a household, and the domestic register of the previous verse carries over.

972. आशोभना → आ-शोभना

आ = wholly, thoroughly; also always
शोभना = beautiful, splendid, shining (from शुभ् "to shine, to be beautiful")
"The wholly Beautiful."

Vigraha: आ समन्तात् शोभना।

The dev field reads ऽऽशोभना with a double avagraha. The nama is आशोभना: the avagraha marks the आ elided in सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता + आशोभना → प्रीताशोभना (आ + आ → आ, 6.1.101). This is the fourth artifact of that class — after ऽनवद्याङ्गी at 50, ऽऽज्ञा at 828 and ऽनर्घ्य- at 926 — and the doubled form matches 828 exactly, since in both a long आ was swallowed rather than a short अ.

index.html has no commentary body for this nama. Its gloss, "ever beautiful," takes आ in the temporal sense rather than the spatial, which the prefix admits.

शुभ् is also the root behind शुभ, auspicious, so शोभना is beautiful and auspicious at once — which sets the nama naturally after 967 सुमङ्गली and, further back, 933 मङ्गलाकृतिः.

973. शुद्धमानसा → शुद्ध-मानसा

शुद्ध = pure, cleansed (past participle of शुध् "to purify")
मानसा = of the mind, mental (vṛddhi derivative of मनस्)
"She of the pure mind."

Vigraha: शुद्धं मानसं यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

मानस is the derivative of मनस्, "belonging to mind," so the compound reaches further than "pure-minded" — it is purity in the whole mental sphere. मनस् has now stood three times in this stretch: at 930 मनस्विनी, where the mind depended upon Her; at 941 मनोमयी, where She consisted of it; and here, where it is pure.

The bahuvrīhi would also admit a reading about the devotee — She whose devotees are pure of mind — on the pattern Bhāskararāya used at 868 with अमुग्धा.

974. बिन्दुतर्पणसंतुष्टा → बिन्दु-तर्पण-सम्-तुष्टा

बिन्दु = a drop, a point; here the Bindu at the centre of the Śrīcakra; also, in a second reading, the wise
तर्पण = the satisfying offering, a libation (from तृप् "to be satisfied," causative)
सम् = fully
तुष्टा = pleased, satisfied (past participle of तुष् "to be pleased")
"She who is fully satisfied by the libation at the Bindu."

Vigraha: बिन्दुतर्पणेन संतुष्टा।

तर्पण and तुष्टा are near-synonyms from different roots — तृप् and तुष्, both "to be satisfied" — so the compound doubles the satisfaction: the satisfying thing offered, and the satisfaction had of it.

Bhāskararāya identifies the Bindu as the Sarvānandamaya cakra, the ninth and innermost enclosure — which he had already given as one identification of the बैन्दव at 905 बैन्दवासना. There She was seated upon it; here She is fed at it.

The tarpaṇa is then specified by class, and the substances differ while the rite does not: Brāhmaṇas offer milk, Kṣatriyas ghee, Vaiśyas honey, Śūdras mead. This commentary grades things often — the speeds of grace at 869, the four meditations and their fruits at 957, the two paths at 912 — and always in the same way, by holding the act single and varying the fitness of the doer.

A second reading takes बिन्दु to mean the wise, so that She is pleased by their offerings — the sense of 917 धीरसमर्चिता restated.

तुष्टा returns from 921 सदातुष्टा, where She was ever content and no cause was named. Here the cause is precise.

975. पूर्वजा → पूर्व-जा

पूर्व = prior, former, first; also eastern
जा = born (from जन् "to be born")
"The First-born."

Vigraha: पूर्वं जाता पूर्वजा।

जा is the same root-noun that stood negated at 866 अजा, "the Unborn." The two namas are exact opposites in form — अ-जा and पूर्व-जा — and the text holds both: not born at all, and born before everything else.

Bhāskararāya cites "it is She whom the sages recognise as the first," and Taittirīya 3.10.6, "I am the first-born of Truth."

And then a reading that cuts against the honour: पूर्वजा may mean the first creation, which was without intelligence. Being first is therefore not necessarily being highest — the same reversal 957 produced with धन्या, where the nama named the third of four meditations and the commentary recommended the fourth.

976. त्रिपुराम्बिका → त्रिपुरा-अम्बिका

त्रिपुरा = Tripurā — the deity of the eighth cakra; and by division, त्रि "three" with पुर, taken as city, or state, or the jīva
अम्बिका = mother (an affectionate diminutive of अम्बा)
"Tripurāmbikā — Mother of the Three."

Vigraha: त्रिपुरायाः अम्बिका।

Sandhi: त्रिपुरा + अम्बिका → त्रिपुराम्बिका (आ by 6.1.101).

Bhāskararāya identifies Tripurā by office first — the deity of the eighth cakra of the Śrīcakra — and then divides the name. त्रि "three" with पुर as the अवस्थाः, the states: waking, dream and deep sleep, of which She is mother. Or पुर is the jīva, "because he has three states," with Kaivalya Upaniṣad 14, "the soul who plays in the three cities," and Kauṣītaki 3.3, "like sparks from fire." Or त्रिपुरा names the cities Vāmā and the rest.

The name had been derived quite otherwise at 905, where the Jñānārṇava concluded that "as Devī is joined to the three Bindus, she is named Tripurā" — three Bindus, not three cities. And 875 त्रिपुरमालिनी had made her goddess of the inner ten-cornered enclosure. Three namas, three accounts of one name, and no two agree.

अम्बिका is the diminutive of अम्बा, and it is the word the text will close on: nama 1000 is ललिताम्बिका.

Note on the verse. Six namas, dividing at the daṇḍa into worship and origin.

971–973 carry on the domestic register of the previous verse — the worship of married women pleases Her, She is wholly beautiful, Her mind is pure. 974–976 turn first technical and then cosmogonic: the libation at the Bindu, the first-born, the mother of the three.

974 is the substantial nama. The Bindu is the Sarvānandamaya, the innermost enclosure She was seated upon at 905, so across the two namas She is both the seat's occupant and the offering's recipient there. And the tarpaṇa's material is graded by class while the rite stays one — milk, ghee, honey, mead.

975 sets up the sharpest contrast in the verse and does not remark on it. पूर्वजा is अजा of 866 with the negation exchanged for a comparative: not born at all there, born before all here. Bhāskararāya then undercuts the honour himself by allowing that पूर्वजा may name the first creation, which was unintelligent.

976 gives Tripurā a third etymology, and the accounts do not reconcile: three Bindus at 905, the antardaśāra at 875, and here the three states of the jīva. It is among the most worked names in the text.

Textual note. 972's dev reads ऽऽशोभना, carrying the double avagraha of the preceding sandhi — fourth artifact of that class, after 50, 828 and 926. 971, 972 and 973 have no commentary bodies at all. 974's heading is split between its gloss and body fields.
