## दशमुद्रासमाराध्या त्रिपुराश्रीवशंकरी । ज्ञानमुद्रा ज्ञानगम्या ज्ञातृज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी

*daśamudrāsamārādhyā tripurāśrīvaśaṃkarī । jñānamudrā jñānagamyā jñātṛjñeyasvarūpiṇī*

Verse 179, namas 977–981.

977. दशमुद्रासमाराध्या → दश-मुद्रा-सम्-आराध्या

दश = ten
मुद्रा = a seal, a stamp; hence a sign, and in worship a position of the fingers
सम् = fully, completely
आराध्या = to be worshipped, to be propitiated (आ + राध्, gerundive यत्)
"She who is worshipped with the ten mudrās."

Vigraha: दशमुद्राभिः समाराध्या।

The ten are given by their span: from Saṃkṣobhiṇī to Trikhaṇḍā, worshipped in the manner the Nityāhṛdaya lays down. Sastry's note refers the reader to Pūrvacatuṣṣaṭī chapter III for the finger-positions themselves.

समाराध्या for the third time — at 870 अन्तर्मुखसमाराध्या the qualification was the inward-turned face, at 918 चैतन्यार्घ्यसमाराध्या the offering was consciousness, and here the means are ten gestures. The three give three registers of one worship: attention, substance, gesture.

One of the ten is a nama in its own right five namas on — योनिमुद्रा, which the commentary there calls the ninth. ज्ञानमुद्रा at 979 is a gesture too, but not of this set.

978. त्रिपुराश्रीवशंकरी → त्रिपुरा-श्री-वशम्-करी

त्रिपुरा = Tripurā
श्री = splendour, majesty — त्रिपुराश्री being a proper name
वशम् = under control, into subjection (वश "will, control")
करी = she who makes (from कृ "to do")
"She who brings Tripurāśrī under her sway."

Vigraha: त्रिपुराश्रीं वशं करोतीति।

The dev field reads त्रिपुरा श्रीवशंकरी, a space splitting the compound after त्रिपुरा. It is one nama, and the commentary's own gloss both repairs the split and shows what it is for: "Tripurāśrī is the name of the deity which presides over the fifth cakra."

वशंकरी is the regular formation for bringing under control, the accusative वशम् with करी — and it is also the name of one of the ten mudrās just invoked at 977.

The identification is worth setting out, because the commentary's numbering is exact and it joins three namas. The Śrīcakra's nine enclosures have nine presiding Tripurā-deities, and this text names three of them. At 875 त्रिपुरमालिनी Bhāskararāya called her goddess of the Antardaśāra — the sixth enclosure, and Tripuramālinī is sixth in the standard list. At 976 त्रिपुराम्बिका he gave her the eighth cakra, and Tripurāmbā is eighth. Here Tripurāśrī is given the fifth, and she is fifth. Three namas, three enclosures, and the count agrees each time.

What the nama then asserts is subordination: Lalitā subdues one of these, which places her above the enclosure-deities rather than among them. It is the relation the run has asserted of Kubera at 885, of Viṣṇu at 893, and of Śiva at 910 and 947.

979. ज्ञानमुद्रा → ज्ञान-मुद्रा

ज्ञान = knowledge (from ज्ञा "to know")
मुद्रा = a seal, a sign, a finger-position
"She who is the Jñānamudrā."

Vigraha: ज्ञानमुद्रा एव सा।

The gesture is described: the tips of thumb and forefinger joined into a circle, the other fingers extended.

Then two re-divisions, both turning on the last syllable. ज्ञान "by knowledge," मुद् "bliss," र "she gives" — She who gives bliss through knowledge. Or ज्ञान as cit, मुद् as bliss, and द्र "she veils" — which reverses the nama entirely: she who conceals the bliss of consciousness. Giver and concealer of the same thing, out of one string of letters.

The र-as-"gives" device has now appeared at 915 मधु-र, 916 धी-र, in one division of 939 परमोदारा, and here — four times in this run, always on a final syllable.

980. ज्ञानगम्या → ज्ञान-गम्या

ज्ञान = knowledge
गम्या = to be reached, attainable (गम् "to go" with the gerundive यत्)
"She who is to be attained by knowledge."

Vigraha: ज्ञानेन गम्या।

The nama is 113 भावनागम्या with भावना exchanged for ज्ञान — meditation there, knowledge here, the same gerundive in both. At 113 Bhāskararāya had offered a second reading taking गम्या as अगम्या, unattainable, and denying that the path of action reaches Her.

The Kūrma Purāṇa is quoted at length, and its emphasis falls on difficulty: "my unconditioned nature is to be attained by wisdom alone and is bare absolute consciousness, benevolent, freed from all limitations, infinite, immortal, supreme; that supreme abode is to be attained through much difficulty. Those thinking that knowledge is the best means enter me."

That is the same discrimination made at 960 लोकातीता, where the city of Śiva was reached by works and did not hold, while the three seats above it were reached by meditation and did.

981. ज्ञातृज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी → ज्ञातृ-ज्ञेय-स्व-रूपिणी

ज्ञातृ = the knower, the subject of knowledge (ज्ञा + the agent-suffix तृ)
ज्ञेय = the knowable, the object of knowledge (ज्ञा + the gerundive यत्)
स्व = own
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose very form is both knower and known."

Vigraha: ज्ञाता ज्ञेयं च स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

The two members are the agent-noun and the gerundive of a single root — ज्ञा + तृ and ज्ञा + यत् — so the compound is built to exhaust the act of knowing from both ends at once. index.html carries no commentary here beyond the verse marker.

The third term of the usual triad, ज्ञान the knowing itself, is absent from this compound but stands as the first member of both preceding namas. So 979–981 together give knowledge, knower and known — the triad distributed across three namas instead of packed into one.

The move is exactly 908 तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी's. There She was the meaning of "That" and "Thou"; here of knower and known. Both namas identify Her with the two poles of a relation whose collapse is the point, and both use स्वरूपिणी to do it.

Note on the verse. Five namas: two on the mudrās and the enclosure-deities, three on ज्ञा.

The verse begins technical and ends epistemological, and 979 is the hinge because it is both. ज्ञानमुद्रा is a gesture and a kind of knowledge, and the commentary takes it both ways — describing the finger-position, then re-dividing the word to get "giver of bliss through knowledge," and then re-dividing again to get its opposite, the concealer of that bliss.

978 deserves the most attention. Its dev has been broken by a stray space, and the commentary's gloss both repairs the break and explains the nama: Tripurāśrī presides over the fifth enclosure of the Śrīcakra, and Lalitā brings her under control. Set beside 875 and 976, this text names three of the nine cakra-deities, and Bhāskararāya's numbering is right in each case — Mālinī sixth, Ambā eighth, Śrī fifth. The relation asserted is subordination, which is what the run has asserted of every other deity it has named.

979–981 then distribute the knowledge-triad across three namas, with the middle one being 113 भावनागम्या restated with ज्ञान for भावना.

Textual note. 978's dev reads त्रिपुरा श्रीवशंकरी, a space splitting one nama into two — and this is the more consequential sort of spacing fault, since each half is a plausible word on its own and nothing but the commentary shows the join. 979's commentary is duplicated between its gloss and body fields, and 981 has no body beyond the verse marker.


---

## योनिमुद्रा त्रिखण्डेशी त्रिगुणाम्बा त्रिकोणगा । अनघाद्भुतचारित्रा वाञ्छितार्थप्रदायिनी

*yonimudrā trikhaṇḍeśī triguṇāmbā trikoṇagā । anaghādbhutacāritrā vāñchitārthapradāyinī*

Verse 180, namas 982–989. This edition counts त्रिगुणा and अम्बा as two namas, and अनघा and अद्भुतचारित्रा as two, giving eight.

982. योनिमुद्रा → योनि-मुद्रा

योनि = womb, source; the downward triangle; also the veil covering the Bindu; also the place between anus and generative organ
मुद्रा = a seal, a sign, a finger-position
"She who is the Yonimudrā."

Vigraha: योनिमुद्रा एव सा।

The commentary calls this the ninth of the ten mudrās invoked at 977 — the set running Saṃkṣobhiṇī to Trikhaṇḍā — and the next nama names the tenth. So 977 gives the set and 982–983 name its last two members in order.

Four senses of योनि are offered: the ninth mudrā; She who gives happiness in the womb; the veil that covers the Bindu; and the place between the anus and the generative organ. Then Bhāskararāya stops — "the use of the mudrā in removing mistakes in the mantra must be learned from the Guru." That is the third such refusal in this run, after the light of the samādhis at 907 and the five M's at 948.

योनि had been worked at length at 895 योनिनिलया, where it was Prakṛti, Māyā, the causes of the universe, and the downward triangle in which She dwells as the Bindu. The veil-over-the-Bindu sense is new here, and it inverts that: there She was the Bindu within the triangle, here the triangle is what conceals it.

983. त्रिखण्डेशी → त्रिखण्डा-ईशी

त्रिखण्डा = the three-parted — the tenth mudrā; and also the three divisions of the Pañcadaśī mantra (त्रि "three" + खण्ड "part")
ईशी = mistress, ruler (from ईश् "to rule")
"Ruler of the Trikhaṇḍā."

Vigraha: त्रिखण्डायाः ईशी।

Sandhi: त्रिखण्डा + ईशी → त्रिखण्डेशी (आ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87). index.html has no gloss field for this nama; only the body survives.

This is the tenth and last of the mudrās named at 977, completing the pair with 982.

But त्रिखण्डा also names the three divisions of the Pañcadaśī — the kūṭas Vāgbhava, Kāmarāja and Śakti — and on that reading the nama makes Her ruler of the mantra's own structure. Those three were mapped onto Her body at 85–87 and named as her frame at 89 मूलकूटत्रयकलेबरा, and one reading of कूटस्था at 896 placed Her in them. Here She rules them.

ईशी returns from 932 महेशी and 949 पञ्चभूतेशी, the third in this stretch — and like 978's वशंकरी it asserts rule over a named entity rather than in general.

984. त्रिगुणा → त्रि-गुणा

त्रि = three
गुणा = quality, attribute; literally a strand of cord
"She of the three qualities."

Vigraha: त्रयः गुणाः यस्याः सा।

The nama contradicts 961 गुणातीता, twenty-three namas back, where She transcended the guṇas. The Vāyu Purāṇa he quotes supplies the resolution: "this Yogeśvarī creates as well as destroys forms; she has many forms, many functions and many names; by function and by her sport she is threefold in the world, hence she is called Triguṇā." The threefoldness belongs to function, not to nature — the same distinction the Devī Bhāgavata drew at 824 बहुरूपा, "formless because she is supreme, many-formed because of her activity."

The identification is Sāṃkhya: this is Prakṛti, the basis of sattva, rajas and tamas. The Viṣṇu Purāṇa — "I reverence that eternal energy, which is thy energy, which is all beings and in all souls, the basis of the qualities." And the Devī Purāṇa reads त्रि- across three unrelated triads at once: "Bali was bound by three steps, the Gaṅgā came from three places, and by the three qualities she performs creation, preservation and destruction."

Since गुण is literally a strand, and the three are twisted into Prakṛti's rope, त्रिगुणा is the rope where 961 was the escape from it.

985. अम्बा → अम्बा

अम्बा = mother
"The Mother."

Vigraha: अम्बा माता।

The dev field reads ऽम्बा. The avagraha marks the अ elided in त्रिगुणा + अम्बा → त्रिगुणाम्बा (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101). Fifth artifact of that class.

And with this instance the six such namas in the text resolve into a rule. Where a short अ was swallowed, the text prints a single avagraha — 50 ऽनवद्याङ्गी, 926 ऽनर्घ्य-, 985 ऽम्बा, 988 ऽद्भुत-. Where a long आ was swallowed, it prints two — 828 ऽऽज्ञा, from प्रचण्डा + आज्ञा, and 972 ऽऽशोभना, from प्रीता + आशोभना. The correlation holds in all six cases. The number of avagrahas therefore encodes the length of the elided vowel, and each of these namas can be reconstructed from the mark alone.

Bhāskararāya reads this nama as consequent upon the last: since the previous nama made Her endowed with the three qualities, this one makes Her their cause. The Tantrarāja identifies that cause with the mantra's life — "the three qualities are the cause of Tejas, of the forms of Śakti, and of the Universe; the cause of these is that Devī... that Samyaktva is called the strength of the mantra, or the soul of the mantras," सम्यक्त्व being the attainment of perpetual contemplation of That. So अम्बा is glossed as मन्त्रजीव, the soul of the mantras.

Or simply: She is Ambā, mother of all the worlds. अम्बिका had stood nine namas back at 976, and the text closes on it at 1000.

986. त्रिकोणगा → त्रि-कोण-गा

त्रि = three
कोण = a corner, an angle
गा = going to, resorting to, abiding in (from गम् "to go")
"She who abides in the triangle."

Vigraha: त्रिकोणं गच्छतीति त्रिकोणगा।

The commentary is a single clause and it identifies the triangle: Trikoṇa is the Yonicakra — the eighth enclosure of the Śrīcakra, and the same downward triangle that 895 and 982's third sense had named. Three namas in this stretch place Her with respect to it: dwelling in it as the Bindu at 895, veiled by it at 982, and going to it here. Occupant, concealment, destination.

गा is the bare root-noun of गम्, the same root that gave गम्या at 113 and 980. There it was passive — She to be reached; here active — She who goes.

987. अनघा → अन्-अघा

अन् = not (नञ् before a vowel)
अघ = sin; and also pain, misery
"The Sinless."

Vigraha: अघं यस्याः नास्ति सा।

Bhāskararāya's whole gloss is lexical, and it widens the nama: "agha means sin, pain, misery." So अनघा is not merely blameless but beyond suffering, which makes it a counterpart to 876 निरामया, where She was free of disease.

The privative namas of this run now make a set: 866 अजा unborn, 876 निरामया diseaseless, 877 निरालम्बा unsupported, 926 अनर्घ्य priceless, 937 विरागिणी uncoloured and unattached, 961 गुणातीता beyond the guṇas, and here sinless. The text defines Her by subtraction quite as readily as by attribute.

988. अद्भुतचारित्रा → अद्भुत-चारित्रा

अद्भुत = wonderful, marvellous; and per the commentary's division, a portent — earthquake and the like
चारित्रा = conduct, character, deeds (from चर् "to move, to behave"); and by that division, चरि with त्र
"She whose deeds are wonderful."

Vigraha: अद्भुतं चारित्रं यस्याः सा।

The dev field reads ऽद्भुतचारित्रा. The avagraha marks the अ elided in अनघा + अद्भुत → अनघाद्भुत (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101) — sixth artifact of that class, and the single form again correctly signals a short vowel.

Bhāskararāya's division turns the nama from praise into protection. अद्भुत is taken as a portent, earthquake and the like; चरि as the bad results thereof; and त्र as "she protects." So: She who protects her devotees during such calamities. The wonder becomes the disaster and the deeds become the shelter.

The त्र-as-"protects" reading matches the र-as-"gives" readings at 915, 916, 939 and 979. Bhāskararāya treats final syllables as verbs consistently, and the two roots he reaches for are दा and त्रै — the same त्रै that gives the traditional derivation of मन्त्र used at 846, मननात् त्रायते.

989. वाञ्छितार्थप्रदायिनी → वाञ्छित-अर्थ-प्र-दायिनी

वाञ्छित = desired, wished for (past participle of वाञ्छ् "to desire")
अर्थ = object, purpose, the thing sought; also wealth
प्र = forth, fully
दायिनी = she who gives, bestower (दा + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who bestows the objects desired."

Vigraha: वाञ्छितान् अर्थान् प्रददातीति।

Sandhi: वाञ्छित + अर्थ → वाञ्छितार्थ (आ by 6.1.101). index.html's body for this nama carries only the opening fragment of 990's heading; its own commentary is not preserved.

दायिनी for the fourth time — good fortune at 117, rest to the scorched at 851, the priceless state of kaivalya at 926, and here whatever is wished for. The escalation from 117 to 926 is reversed at this point: after the final state, ordinary desires. And प्र is added for the first time, making the giving complete rather than partial.

Note on the verse. Eight namas: two closing the mudrā-set of 977, three on त्रि-, two privatives joined by sandhi, and one of giving.

984–985 is the substantial pair. त्रिगुणा makes Her endowed with the three qualities and अम्बा makes Her their cause, and Bhāskararāya reads the second as following from the first. That also resolves, without his saying so, the contradiction with 961 गुणातीता: the Vāyu Purāṇa's line does the work, since She is threefold "by function and by her sport," so the guṇas belong to the acting and not to the actor — which is the distinction the Devī Bhāgavata had drawn at 824 in nearly the same words.

The triangle now carries three namas. At 895 She dwells in it as the Bindu; at 982 the योनि is the veil that covers the Bindu; at 986 She goes to it.

And this verse yields the run's clearest textual finding. Six namas in this text carry a stray avagraha from the preceding sandhi — 50, 828, 926, 972, 985, 988 — and the number of avagrahas is not arbitrary. A single ऽ stands where a short अ was elided, a double ऽऽ where a long आ was, and the correlation holds in every one of the six. The mark is recoverable information rather than noise: any of these namas can be restored from the avagraha alone.

Textual note. 985 and 988 carry avagrahas from the preceding sandhi, the fifth and sixth of that class. 983 has no gloss field. 986's gloss and body hold the same single sentence. 989's body holds only a fragment of 990's heading, so its own commentary is lost.

## अभ्यासातिशयज्ञाता षडध्वातीतरूपिणी । अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिरज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका

*abhyāsātiśayajñātā ṣaḍadhvātītarūpiṇī । avyājakaruṇāmūrtir ajñānadhvāntadīpikā*

Verse 181, namas 990–993.

990. अभ्यासातिशयज्ञाता → अभ्यास-अतिशय-ज्ञाता

अभ्यास = repeated practice, constant application (अभि + अस्)
अतिशय = excess, abundance, pre-eminence (अति + शी "to lie beyond")
ज्ञाता = known (past participle of ज्ञा)
"She who is known through abundance of practice."

Vigraha: अभ्यासातिशयेन ज्ञाता।

Sandhi: अभ्यास + अतिशय → अभ्यासातिशय (आ by 6.1.101).

ज्ञाता is ambiguous by form, since the past participle "known" and the agent-noun "knower" coincide in the nominative feminine — and the nama immediately preceding this verse, 981 ज्ञातृज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी, had used ज्ञातृ for the knower. Here the sense required is passive.

The doctrine is repetition, and every authority quoted is about it. "Till sleep as well as till death one should employ himself in reflection on the Vedānta." Vedānta Sūtra 4.1.1 — "repetition is required on account of the text giving instruction more than once." And the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa: "she, whose limbs are knowledge, whose body is science, and whose abode is the heart, is to be seen by constant meditation; by constant practice in meditation she becomes manifested through the union with the Self."

991. षडध्वातीतरूपिणी → षट्-अध्व-अतीत-रूपिणी

षट् = six
अध्व = a road, a way, a method (अध्वन्)
अतीत = gone beyond, transcended (अति + इ "to go")
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form transcends the six paths."

Vigraha: षडध्वानाम् अतीतं रूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: षट् + अध्व → षडध्व, the ट् voicing before the vowel; then अध्व + अतीत → अध्वातीत (आ by 6.1.101).

The six are named: पदाध्वा words, भुवनाध्वा worlds, वर्णाध्वा letters, तत्त्वाध्वा categories, कलाध्वा parts, and मन्त्राध्वा mantra. And they are then divided between the two poles — the Virūpākṣapañcāśikā assigns words, mantras and letters to Vimarśa, and worlds, categories and parts to Prakāśa. Three ways through speech, three through being.

The Jñānārṇava places them in the cakra: "in this Cakra there are six methods, O Devī, adored by warriors; thus one should meditate by six methods upon the pure Śrīcakra," and the Dakṣiṇā Saṃhitā repeats the instruction. Each अध्वा is a way of meditating on Śiva as manifested in words, in worlds, and so on.

A second reading takes the six as six kinds of devotion, and the Kulārṇava turns them into a sequence of lives: "to him whose mind is purified by the mantras of Śiva, Viṣṇu, Durgā, the Sun, Gaṇapati and Indra, appears the knowledge of Kula." Those who followed any of the six in former births attain devotion to Devī in this one — so the six paths are transcended by being passed through rather than by being set aside.

अतीत returns from the triad at 960–962, where She transcended the worlds, the guṇas, and all; भुवन and तत्त्व, two of the six here, are the objects of two of those three. रूपिणी makes its seventh appearance in this stretch.

992. अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः → अ-व्याज-करुणा-मूर्तिः

अ = not (नञ्)
व्याज = deceit, disguise; hence a pretext (वि + अज्)
करुणा = compassion, pity
मूर्तिः = form, embodiment
"She who is compassion embodied, and without pretext."

Vigraha: अव्याजा करुणा मूर्तिः यस्याः सा।

व्याज is a pretext, so अव्याज is compassion needing no occasion — pity given without a reason being furnished for it. The gloss renders it "without partiality," which is the same point from the other side: where there is no cause there is no preference.

Bhāskararāya's whole comment is an exclamation — "Glory to Devī the compassionate one." index.html preserves little else of the body, the rest having broken into fragments.

मूर्ति returns from 116 भद्रमूर्तिः, and आकृति at 830 and 933 said the same thing in another word. What Her form embodies here is not auspiciousness but compassion.

The dev field reads अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिर, with a र where the visarga belongs. The other half of that fault is in the next nama.

993. अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका → अज्ञान-ध्वान्त-दीपिका

अज्ञान = ignorance, want of knowledge (अ + ज्ञान)
ध्वान्त = darkness
दीपिका = a lamp, that which illumines (दीप् "to shine," in the causative)
"She who is the lamp dispelling the darkness of ignorance."

Vigraha: अज्ञानध्वान्तस्य दीपिका।

This is the most consequential artifact in the run, because it inverts the nama rather than merely disfiguring it. The dev field reads ज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका, without the initial अ — which would make the nama "the lamp of the darkness of knowledge." The nama is अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका, and the darkness belongs to ignorance.

The fault is the familiar visarga mis-division, and this is its third instance. अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः + अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका gives अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिरज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका, the visarga becoming र् before the following vowel; the division was then taken after that र्, so 992 keeps a र which is not its own and 993 loses the अ which is. The same fault produced उदारकीर्ति and रुद्दामवैभवा at 848–849 and अयोनि and यनिनिलया at 894–895 — but in those two the sense survived intact, and here it reverses.

Both the gloss and the commentary preserve the right reading, so the nama is recoverable. The gloss has "the lamp that dispels the darkness of ignorance," and the citation is Gītā 10.11: "out of compassion to them I, residing in their heart, dispel the darkness of ignorance by the lamp of knowledge."

That verse also explains why this nama follows 992. The Gītā line holds both members in order — compassion the motive, the lamp the means — and the Sahasranāma sets अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः immediately before अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका. The two namas are that one verse divided in half, and the sandhi joining them is exactly the sandhi that has been misread.

दीपिका is the causative agent-noun of दीप् — not a lamp that shines, but one that makes things shine.

Note on the verse. Four namas in two pairs, means and grace. 990–991 are epistemic: known by abundance of practice, transcending the six paths of meditation. 992–993 answer the difficulty those raise: unmotivated compassion, and the lamp that removes ignorance.

The pairing is not merely thematic, since Gītā 10.11 contains both halves in order, and the two namas are that verse split at its seam.

990 and 991 also set up the run's sharpest unremarked tension. Here She is known only by unremitting practice, and 980's Kūrma Purāṇa had insisted that the supreme abode "is to be attained through much difficulty" — while at 869 She was क्षिप्रप्रसादिनी, quickly pleased, the Saura Purāṇa there promising freedom within the same incarnation. Quick to be pleased and slow to be known: the commentary asserts both and reconciles neither.

991's six paths are worth keeping for their division rather than their number. Words, mantras and letters belong to Vimarśa; worlds, categories and parts to Prakāśa — three ways through speech and three through being. And the second reading converts them from six methods set aside into six devotions passed through.

Textual note. This verse carries the run's most consequential fault. 992's dev holds a र belonging to the visarga of मूर्तिः, and 993's has lost the initial अ of अज्ञान. It is the third instance of visarga mis-division, after 848–849 and 894–895, and the only one of the three in which the meaning inverts: without its अ, the nama says She is the lamp of the darkness of knowledge. The gloss and the Gītā citation both preserve the correct reading. 992's own commentary survives only in fragments.

## आबालगोपविदिता सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना । श्रीचक्रराजनिलया श्रीमत्त्रिपुरसुन्दरी

*ābālagopaviditā sarvānullaṅghyaśāsanā । śrīcakrarājanilayā śrīmattripurasundarī*

Verse 182, namas 994–997.

994. आबालगोपविदिता → आ-बाल-गोप-विदिता

आ = up to, as far as, including — the prefix marking inclusive extent
बाल = a child; and per the commentary, Brahmā and the rest
गोप = a cowherd, a protector (गो "cow" with प from पा "to protect"); and per the commentary, Sadāśiva
विदिता = known (past participle of विद् "to know")
"She who is known to all, down to children and cowherds."

Vigraha: आ बालगोपेभ्यः विदिता।

आ marks inclusive extent — "as far as, and including" — so the compound names the lowest limit of Her being known and takes it in. The common idiom आबालवृद्धम्, "from children to the aged," is built the same way.

But Bhāskararāya reverses the direction of the range. बाल he takes as Brahmā and the rest, गोप as the protector, that is Sadāśiva — or बालगोप together as Kṛṣṇa. So She is known "to every one from Sadāśiva and Viṣṇu down to children." What reads as a claim about the humble becomes a claim about the whole hierarchy.

The Sūta Saṃhitā (1.8.36) is cited: "all beings recognise Him in the shape of the idea of 'I'." That is the same verse quoted at 830 प्रकटाकृतिः, where प्रकट meant "experienced by all," and the point was identical — what is universally known is known as the sense of self.

995. सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना → सर्व-अन्-उल्लङ्घ्य-शासना

सर्व = all — per the commentary, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest
अन् = not (नञ् before a vowel)
उल्लङ्घ्य = to be transgressed, to be overstepped (उत् + लङ्घ् "to leap over," with the gerundive यत्)
शासना = command, edict, rule (from शास् "to command, to teach")
"She whose command none may transgress."

Vigraha: सर्वैः अनुल्लङ्घ्या शासना यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: सर्व + अनुल्लङ्घ्य → सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्य (आ by 6.1.101).

The dev field reads सर्वानुल्लङ्घयशासना, with य standing free where the conjunct घ्य belongs — the virāma lost, so the gerundive उल्लङ्घ्य becomes the non-word उल्लङ्घय, and the iast repeats the error as sarvānullaṅghaya. This is a new kind of fault in the run: not sandhi, spacing, or a wrong letter, but a broken conjunct.

Bhāskararāya's placement of the nama is an objection and its answer, and he raises the objection himself. Since familiarity breeds contempt, if every person knows that he himself is Devī — which is just what 994 has said — will Her command not then be ignored? This nama is the reply.

The reply is a hierarchy, from Saundaryalaharī 24: "Brahmā creates the Universe, Viṣṇu protects it, and Rudra destroys it; Īśa annihilates all these three as well as himself. And finally, under thy orders indicated by the movement of thy creeper-like brows, Sadāśiva approves of the same." The five of 947's couch, in order, each acting under the one above — and the last of them waiting on the motion of Her eyebrows.

शासना is from शास्, the root that gave शास्त्र at 845 शास्त्रसारा. Command and scripture come from one root: that which lays down.

996. श्रीचक्रराजनिलया → श्री-चक्र-राज-निलया

श्री = splendour, majesty, auspiciousness
चक्र = wheel, disc — here the Śrīcakra
राज = king, chief — चक्रराज, the king of cakras
निलया = abode, dwelling, resting place (नि + ली "to settle")
"She whose abode is the royal Śrīcakra."

Vigraha: श्रीचक्रराजः निलयः यस्याः सा।

चक्रराज had stood at 68 चक्रराजरथारूढसर्वायुधपरिष्कृता, where the Cakrarāja was Her war-chariot in the Bhaṇḍāsura campaign. Here it is Her dwelling — the same term, once a vehicle and once a residence.

Bhāskararāya's identification is bodily rather than spatial. The Śrīcakra consists of Bindu, triangle and the rest, and "the Śrīcakra is the body of Śiva and Devī" — so "just as the jīva resides in the body, so they reside in the Śrīcakra." The abode is not a place they occupy but a body they are.

निलया for the fifth time in this run — 99 मूलाधारैकनिलया, the cakra at the base; 839 मुक्तिनिलया, liberation; 873 त्रिवर्गनिलया, the triads; 895 योनिनिलया, the triangle; and here the whole cakra. The sequence has widened from a single enclosure to all nine.

997. श्रीमत्त्रिपुरसुन्दरी → श्रीमत्-त्रिपुर-सुन्दरी

श्रीमत् = glorious, resplendent, possessing śrī (श्री + मतुप्)
त्रिपुर = the three cities; and per the commentary Paramaśiva, since Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra are his body
सुन्दरी = the beautiful one, a lovely woman
"The resplendent Tripurasundarī."

Vigraha: श्रीमती त्रिपुरसुन्दरी। or त्रिपुरसुन्दरस्य पत्नी।

The dev field reads श्रीमत्रिपुरसुन्दरी with a single त् where the compound requires two: श्रीमत् + त्रिपुर gives श्रीमत्त्रिपुर-. The iast carries the same loss, śrīmatripurasundarī.

श्रीमत् is the same word and the same मतुप् formation as at 56 श्रीमन्नगरनायिका, where त् + न assimilated to न्न. Here त् + त् simply doubles — and it is the doubling that has been lost.

Bhāskararāya reads the compound as a marriage: the wife of Tripurasundara, Paraśiva. And Tripura is Paramaśiva "because the three — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra — are his body." The Kālikā Purāṇa gives the anatomy: by Pradhāna's will Śiva's body became triple, the upper part becoming five-faced Brahmā, four-armed, coloured like the pericarp of the lotus; the middle part blue Viṣṇu, one-faced and four-armed, bearing conch, disc, club and lotus; the lower part five-faced Rudra, four-armed, white as cloud, with the moon as crest-jewel. "As these three Puras are in him, he is called Tripurā."

That is a fourth account of the name Tripurā, and it agrees with none of the earlier three. At 905 the Jñānārṇava derived it from three Bindus; at 875 Tripuramālinī was the sixth enclosure's deity; at 976 the three were the states of the jīva. Here they are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra as the three parts of Śiva's body — which makes Tripura masculine and Her his consort.

And those three are three of the five who were the couch at 947 and the chain of command at 995. Within fifty namas the same set of gods has been furniture, a hierarchy of office, and the anatomy of the husband whose name She bears.

Note on the verse. Four namas: two of knowing, two of place and name.

994–995 are an objection and its answer, and Bhāskararāya frames them that way himself. She is known to all, down to children — and therefore, one might think, held cheap; but Her command is not to be overstepped by anyone, Brahmā and the rest included.

996–997 give the abode and the name, and both are read as identity rather than attribute. The Śrīcakra is not where She lives but the body She and Śiva are. Tripurasundarī is Her name because Tripura is Paramaśiva, whose three parts are the three gods.

Saundaryalaharī 24, quoted at 995, is the verse this run has been building towards without quoting until now. Brahmā creates, Viṣṇu protects, Rudra destroys, Īśa annihilates all three and himself — and Sadāśiva approves it all at the movement of Her brows. The five who were furniture at 947 are here a chain of command, and three of them at 997 are the parts of Her husband's body.

Textual note. Two faults, and one is new in kind. 995's dev has य standing free where the conjunct घ्य is required, turning the gerundive उल्लङ्घ्य into the non-word उल्लङ्घय — a broken conjunct rather than a sandhi, spacing or letter error — and the iast repeats it. 997's dev has lost one of the two त् of श्रीमत् + त्रिपुर, and the iast repeats that too.

Namas 998 and 999 both carry 997's gloss and a duplicate of its body, so three consecutive namas share one commentary. That is the worst duplication in the run, though the material proper to 998 and 999 does survive embedded within the shared block.

## श्रीशिवा शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी ललिताम्बिका

*śrīśivā śivaśaktyaikyarūpiṇī lalitāmbikā*

Verse 183, namas 998–1000 — the last three.

998. श्रीशिवा → श्री-शिवा

श्री = splendour, majesty, auspiciousness — here honorific
शिवा = the auspicious one; the feminine of शिव
"Śrī Śivā — the divine Śivā."

Vigraha: श्रीमती शिवा।

index.html carries 997's gloss and a duplicate of 997's body on this nama. Its own commentary survives only inside that shared block, where it reads "the divine Śivā — the union of Śiva and Śakti," which is really the gloss of the nama following.

शिवा had been nama 53, given there as the Auspicious Goddess, the Divine Power of Śiva, with the vigraha शिवं कल्याणं ददातीति शिवा। The text returns to the same word nine hundred and forty-five names later, adding only श्री.

Placing शिवा third from the end is deliberate. The preceding fifty namas have spent themselves subordinating Śiva — his part at 910, her bedding at 947, bewildered by her at 954, assenting at the motion of her brows at 995 — and now, at the close, the text names Her by his name in the feminine.

999. शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी → शिव-शक्ति-ऐक्य-रूपिणी

शिव = Śiva
शक्ति = Śakti, power
ऐक्य = oneness, identity (the vṛddhi abstract of एक "one")
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is the oneness of Śiva and Śakti."

Vigraha: शिवशक्त्योः ऐक्यं रूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: शक्ति + ऐक्य → शक्त्यैक्य, the इ becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि).

ऐक्य is the abstract of एक — not union as the joining of two, but one-ness as a state — and Bhāskararāya insists on the distinction: "here Union means the supreme equality, the being absolutely without difference." Her nature is the equal essence of both.

The Vāyavīya Saṃhitā: "supreme Śakti becomes one with the Śiva Tattva; again, by the will of Śiva, she manifests at the beginning of creation like oil from the oil-grain." The Saura Saṃhitā makes it an epistemic point: "the Śakti which is separate from Brahman is not different from Brahman itself; it is only called Śakti by the ignorant. It is impossible to distinguish the difference, O wise one, between the Śakti and the possessor of Śakti." And the Vasiṣṭha Rāmāyaṇa: "as there is only one movement of air, only one Oḍhyāna Pīṭha, and only one manifested Cit Śakti, so also there is only one Union."

Three further readings. शिव and शक्ति as the Śiva-cakras and the Śakti-cakras, with ऐक्य their union — the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa: "in the triangle Bindu must be united, the eight-angled one is to be united with the eight-petalled lotus; he who knows the necessary relation between the parts belonging to Śiva and the parts belonging to Śakti in the Śrīcakra is the real knower of the cakra."

Or the nama means the Haṃsa mantra, in which the union is declared. The Sūta Saṃhitā (4.7.2) derives it from the syllables: "Śakti of Him is said to be the end of the syllable śa — that is स — and the end of that, ह, is called Bīja; the Bīja is the Vidyāśakti; that itself is Śiva. Therefore this supreme mantra is said to signify Śiva as well as Śakti." स and ह, the Haṃsa mantra, is the union spelt out.

Or शिवशक्ति means Śiva's five śaktis, with ऐक्य their collective form, which is Devī. The Virūpākṣapañcāśikā assigns each to an element: "Dhūmāvatī veils, Bhāsvatī reveals, Spanda stimulates, Vibhvī pervades, Hlādaśakti nourishes — Dhūmāvatī belongs to earth, Hlādā to water, Bhāsvatī to fire, Spanda to air, Vibhvī to ether; thus the world is pervaded by these." That same text supplied the six paths at 991, and it divides them the same way.

This is the last of ten रूपिणी-namas in this run — 833, 840, 850, 883, 893, 897, 908, 981, 991, and here — and the only one whose object is not a thing but a relation.

1000. ललिताम्बिका → ललिता-अम्बिका

ललिता = Lalitā — she who sports, plays; charming, lovely (from लल् "to play, to sport"); and per the Śabdārṇava, simply beautiful
अम्बिका = mother (an affectionate diminutive of अम्बा)
"Lalitāmbikā — the Mother Lalitā."

Vigraha: ललिता च अम्बिका च।

Sandhi: ललिता + अम्बिका → ललिताम्बिका (आ by 6.1.101).

The Padma Purāṇa's etymology is given, and Bhāskararāya unpacks every word of it: "transcending all worlds she sports (lalate), hence she is called Lalitā." Worlds means Her surrounding lights or deities; transcending means being above their abodes, in the Bindu-place; and sports means shines brilliantly.

Then eight senses of ललिता, offered as the eight human qualities: brilliancy, manifestation, sweetness, depth, fixity, energy, grace, generosity. The Kāma Śāstra adds erotic action and tenderness. And a verse ties the name to Her equipment: "thou art rightly called Lalitā, for thou hast nine divine attendants, and thy bow is made of sugarcane, thy arrows are flowers, and everything connected with thee is lovely (lalita)."

The Padma Purāṇa makes Her the deity worshipped at Prayāga — the last of the pīṭha-identifications in this run, after Viśālākṣī at Benares (936) and Mīnākṣī at Madhurā (915).

अम्बिका closes what अम्बिका at 976 and अम्बा at 985 had opened. The text ends on the plainest word it has for Her.

Note on the verse. Three namas, and they are a summation rather than a description. 998 names Her by Śiva's name in the feminine; 999 makes Her the oneness of the two; 1000 gives Her own name and calls Her mother.

The order matters. Having spent fifty namas placing Her above Śiva, the text closes by making the two indistinguishable — and Bhāskararāya presses it as a point about knowledge rather than about rank: Śakti is called separate "only by the ignorant." The subordination and the identity are both meant, and the sequence puts the identity last.

Closing note on the text. Bhāskararāya's remarks at nama 1000 concern the whole thousand, and they are worth recording here since the work ends at this point.

He gives a structural account. The first three namas indicate Her as creator, preserver and destroyer; the next two as possessing two further functions, annihilation and re-manifestation, "which belong to no other deity"; and from the sixth name to the last, the same deity possessing these five functions is described in various ways, under the name Lalitā, "which is her special name and belongs to no other deity." So the thousand is read as five functions stated in five namas and then elaborated across the remaining nine hundred and ninety-five.

He notes the ritual frame. Om is to be pronounced at the end as at the beginning, and though the two praṇavas are not parts of the names they are repeated for the benediction — "if any mantra is repeated without the addition of Om at the beginning it becomes ineffective, and without the addition of Om at the end it becomes dispersed."

And he closes with the Paribhāṣā verses, which are rules for reciting and counting. Verse 33 gives the opening word of each hundred — Śrī, Maṇi, Sad, Hrīṃ, Vividhā, Gadā, Darā, Deśa, Puṣṭa, Nāda — and states that the text contains no meaningless particle and no repeated name. Verses 35–36 prescribe two divisions: साध्वी is to be split as साधु + ई, and तत्त्वमयी as तत् + त्वम् + अयि. Verse 37 records the gender anomalies: four namas are masculine (Guṇanidhi, Ātman, Rogaparvata, Mahālāvaṇya), two neuter (Tat and Brahman), and two indeclinable (Svāhā and Svadhā).

Two of those rules bear on the work above.

The Paribhāṣā's division of तत्त्वमयी as तत् + त्वम् + अयि — "That thou art, O!" — is not the division given at 907, where the nama was taken as तत्त्व + मयी, "made of the tattvas." Both readings are current, and the difference is not small. On the Paribhāṣā's reading, nama 907 is itself a statement of the mahāvākya, which would make 908 तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी not a fresh move but the explicit form of what 907 had already said — so the pun described under 908 would begin one nama earlier than stated there.

And verse 37's list of neuter namas confirms the reading given at 822, where ब्रह्म was taken as the neuter Absolute named without gender. The Paribhāṣā counts only two such names in the thousand, and that is one of them.

The colophon then closes the work: "thus ends in the Saubhāgyabhāskara composed by Bhāskararāya the eleventh Kalā called Dhāriṇī with the tenth hundred." The ninth hundred had closed at nama 900 नैष्कर्म्या with the Bodhinī Kalā, whose colophon survives in that nama's body. This one closes the tenth hundred, and the commentary.

Textual note. 998 and 999 both carry 997's gloss and a duplicate of its body; their own commentary survives only embedded within that shared block, and both were recovered from it.

The verse-table row for this verse is mislabelled n=182, duplicating the previous verse's number, so the table's last two rows carry the same number and no row is numbered 183. Its from–to range, 998–1000, is sound.

## तटिल्लतासमरुचिः षट्चक्रोपरिसंस्थिता । महासक्तिः कुण्डलिनी बिसतन्तुतनीयसी

*taṭillatāsamaruciḥ ṣaṭcakroparisaṃsthitā । mahāsaktiḥ kuṇḍalinī bisatantutanīyasī*

Verse 40, namas 107–111.

107. तटिल्लतासमरुचिः → तटित्-लता-सम-रुचिः

तटित् = lightning, a flash of lightning
लता = creeper, vine — तटिल्लता, the "lightning-creeper," the branching tendril of a flash
सम = equal to, like, resembling
रुचिः = lustre, radiance, brilliance (from रुच् "to shine")
"She whose radiance is like a creeper of lightning."

Vigraha: तटिल्लतायाः समा रुचिः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: तटित् + लता → तटिल्लता। The final त् becomes ल् before ल् (Pāṇini 8.4.60, तोर्लि), giving the doubled ल्ल.

The simile is exact rather than decorative — not lightning at large but a lightning-creeper, the slender branching filament of a flash, which is how the rising kuṇḍalinī is seen. लता carries the sense of a slender climbing plant, so the image is at once brilliance and thin ascending line.

Bhāskararāya cites Taittirīya Āraṇyaka X.13.2, "bright as the flash of lightning." index.html's body for this nama preserves a stray fragment, "(Tatillekha-", which records the variant reading तटिल्लेखा, a streak of lightning.

108. षट्चक्रोपरिसंस्थिता → षट्-चक्र-उपरि-संस्थिता

षट् = six
चक्र = wheel, disc — the six cakras of the subtle body
उपरि = above, over, beyond (an indeclinable, अव्यय)
संस्थिता = firmly and permanently established (सम् + स्थिता, from स्था; सम् giving "completely, abidingly")
"She who abides above the six cakras."

Vigraha: षट्चक्राणाम् उपरि संस्थिता।

Sandhi: चक्र + उपरि → चक्रोपरि (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, Pāṇini 6.1.87 आद्गुणः).

Bhāskararāya names the six: mūlādhāra, svādhiṣṭhāna, maṇipūra, anāhata, viśuddhi and ājñā. What lies above them is the sahasrāra, where 105 सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा has already seated Her. Where 99–104 climbed the cakras one at a time, this nama states the destination as a single fact, and सम् does the work — not merely situated above but permanently so.

Because उपरि is an indeclinable, editions commonly print षट्चक्रोपरि संस्थिता as two words, and index.html's dev field carries that space. The division is grammatically motivated rather than an error, and the nama counts as one.

109. महासक्तिः → मह-आसक्तिः

मह = festival, celebration; also tejas, radiance — the Viśva gives both senses
आसक्तिः = attachment, devotion, being fixed upon (आ + सक्ति, from सञ्ज् "to cling")
"She who is devoted to the festival."

Vigraha: महे आसक्तिः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: मह + आसक्तिः → महासक्तिः (अ + आ → आ, Pāṇini 6.1.101 अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः). The long आ is a joint, not a महा-, and the whole reading depends on seeing that.

Three senses, all in Bhāskararāya. मह as festival with आसक्ति as devotion — and the festival, he says, is the union of Śiva and Śakti in the sahasrāra. Or मह as tejas: devoted to radiance. Or महत् + आ + सक्ति, read as greatness, on all sides, attachment.

The first reading places the nama exactly. The preceding verse had brought the ascent to the sahasrāra and poured the nectar back down; this nama names Her delight in what happens there. And what happens there is what the text's penultimate nama, 999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी, will make Her very form — so the "festival" of 109 and the ऐक्य of 999 are one thing, named nine hundred namas apart, once as Her pleasure and once as Her nature.

Editions also read महाशक्तिः, "the Great Power," a straightforward महा + शक्तिः. The text followed here reads महासक्तिः, which requires the मह + आसक्ति division above; the two variants differ by a single sibilant and give quite different namas.

110. कुण्डलिनी → कुण्डल-इनी

कुण्डल = a coil, a ring, a circle (from कुण्ड, a bowl or hollow)
इनी = the possessive suffix इनि with the feminine ङीप् — "she who has" (Pāṇini 5.2.115, अत इनिठनौ)
"The Coiled One — she who is possessed of coils."

Vigraha: कुण्डलम् अस्ति अस्याः इति कुण्डलिनी।

कुण्डल + इनि gives the stem कुण्डलिन्, feminine कुण्डलिनी. The split falls at कुण्डल, not कुण्ड — the ल belongs to the stem, not to the suffix. The computed pada carried in index.html reads कुण्ड-लिनी, which divides one letter early and leaves a suffix that does not exist.

The formation recurs much later at 944 वज्रिणी, वज्र + इनि, differing only in that the र् there retroflexes the न् to ण्.

Bhāskararāya's Tantrarāja citation gives the reason for the name: the vital energy, jīvaśakti, sleeps in the mūlādhāra "like a serpent having three and a half coils," radiant, hissing in the centre of the suṣumnā — and a man who cannot hear that sound on stopping his ears is near death. The Yogavāsiṣṭha, in the story of Cūḍālā: "recognise Kuṇḍalinī in your Self, which is the very life of the mind, like the scent in the flower."

The Devī Purāṇa offers a second derivation, from the śṛṅgāṭaka or triangular form, its three angles being icchā, jñāna and kriyā. That triangle is the one three later namas return to — 895 योनिनिलया, where She dwells in it as the Bindu; 982, where it is the veil covering the Bindu; and 986 त्रिकोणगा, where She goes to it.

A third reading identifies कुण्डलिनी with the वाग्भव-बीज. That connects forward to 872 त्रयी, where the Nityā Tantra derives the vāgbhava bīja ऐ by performing sandhi on the opening letters of the three Vedas — so the coiled energy here and the syllable there are given as the same thing.

111. बिसतन्तुतनीयसी → बिस-तन्तु-तनीयसी

बिस = the lotus stalk, the fibrous stem of the lotus
तन्तु = thread, fibre, filament — बिसतन्तु, the thread drawn from a lotus stalk
तनीयसी = the slenderer, the very finest (तनु "thin" + the comparative suffix ईयसुन् → तनीयस्, feminine तनीयसी)
"She who is finer than the fibre of a lotus stalk."

Vigraha: बिसतन्तोः अपि तनीयसी।

तनीयसी is a degree-form, so the compound is not "thin as a lotus fibre" but "thinner even than" one, with the ablative बिसतन्तोः understood.

Bhāskararāya cites Taittirīya Āraṇyaka X.13.2 — "fine as the point of an ear of rice, saffron-coloured, radiant, and like an atom." That is the same passage he cited at 107 for the lightning, so one Śruti verse supplies both the brightness at the head of this verse and the fineness at its close, and the two namas bracket the kuṇḍalinī between two similes of the thin bright thread.

The Vāmakeśvara Tantra makes the figure literal and then gives the procedure: she lies in the mūlādhāra in the form of a serpent, lotus-fibre fine, tail in mouth, joined to the brahmarandhra; the aspirant, seated in padmāsana, contracting the anus, his mind fixed on kumbhaka, forces the breath upward, the fire in the svādhiṣṭhāna blazes, and by that blaze the serpent king wakes, breaks the Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra knots and the six lotuses, and unites with Śiva in the thousand-petalled lotus. That is the sequence namas 99–106 had traced.

He then reads the Aruṇa Upaniṣad as referring to Devī throughout — "arise, sleep not; ye who rejoice in the light, desire the fire" — taking arise as raise the kuṇḍalinī and sleep not as do not let her sleep. And he derives कुमारी for her: कु earth and मृ absorption, that is Kulakuṇḍa, the mūlādhāra. The three stages follow — the girl just risen from the mūlādhāra and crying; the woman ripened by the sun above the anāhata; the wife who has reached Kāmeśvara in the brahmarandhra — with fire the companion at every stage, because the fire liquefies the lunar orb and so causes the nectar to flow.

The commentary marks a structural close at this nama: the names from the ninetieth down to this one form a single group — the kula, cakra and kuṇḍalinī sequence. Nama 112 opens a new run.

Note on the verse. Five namas, and they name directly what the preceding verse had described in action. 99–106 climbed the cakras, pierced the three knots, reached the sahasrāra and poured the amṛta back down; 107–111 give the climber her names.

The frame is 107 and 111, and it is one Śruti verse doing both ends. Taittirīya Āraṇyaka X.13.2 supplies the lightning-flash for the first and the ear of rice, the atom and the saffron colour for the last, so the kuṇḍalinī is bracketed between brightness and fineness — and both figures are of a thread: the branching filament of a flash, and the fibre drawn from a lotus stalk.

109 is the nama that reaches furthest. Its "festival" is the union of Śiva and Śakti in the sahasrāra, which is what the text's second-to-last nama makes Her nature outright. The whole thousand can be read as travelling between those two statements of one thing.

And 111 closes a group of twenty-two names by the commentary's own reckoning, from 90 कुलामृतैकरसिका to here.

Textual note. Three matters, none grave. 107's body carries a stray fragment "(Tatillekha-", which is not corruption but a preserved variant reading, तटिल्लेखा for तटिल्लता. 108's dev has a space before संस्थिता, which is grammatically motivated, उपरि being an indeclinable, and not an error. 110's computed pada reads कुण्ड-लिनी, dividing one letter early and producing a suffix that does not exist; the split is कुण्डल + इनि.
