## मुद्गौदनासक्तचित्ता साकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी । आज्ञाचक्राब्जनिलया शुक्लवर्णा षडानना

*mudgaudanāsaktacittā sākinyambāsvarūpiṇī । ājñācakrābjanilayā śuklavarṇā ṣaḍānanā*

Verse 107, namas 519–523.

519. मुद्गौदनासक्तचित्ता → मुद्ग-ओदन-आसक्त-चित्ता

मुद्ग = the mudga bean, green gram
ओदन = boiled rice, cooked grain
आसक्त = attached to, fixed upon, devoted to (आ + सञ्ज् "to cling")
चित्ता = mind, thought (from चित् "to perceive")
"She whose mind is set on rice cooked with mudga beans."

Vigraha: मुद्गौदने आसक्तं चित्तं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi at both joints: मुद्ग + ओदन → मुद्गौदन by vṛddhi (अ + ओ → औ, Pāṇini 6.1.88 वृद्धिरेचि), then ओदन + आसक्त → ओदनासक्त (आ by 6.1.101). index.html has no commentary for this nama.

आसक्त is the same word that stands at 109 महासक्तिः, where the attachment was to the festival — the union of Śiva and Śakti in the sahasrāra. Here it is to a dish of rice and pulse. The drop in register is not a lapse but the scheme: each of the seven cakra-yoginīs is given a favourite food, and the offering forms part of her identification. This is Śākinī's, whose seat is the mūlādhāra.

520. साकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी → साकिनी-अम्बा-स्व-रूपिणी

साकिनी = Śākinī, the yoginī presiding over the mūlādhāra
अम्बा = mother
स्व = own
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying (रूप + इन्, feminine ङीप्)
"She whose very form is Mother Śākinī."

Vigraha: साकिनी अम्बा स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: साकिनी + अम्बा → साकिन्यम्बा, the ई becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि).

The dev field reads साकिन्यम्चास्वरूपिणी, with च where ब belongs — a plain letter confusion, and the iast repeats it as sākinyamcā-. The word is अम्बा, the same that stands alone at 985 and, as अम्बिका, at 976 and at 1000. index.html has no commentary for this nama either.

This nama closes the Śākinī set. Through this part of the text the seven cakra-yoginīs are named in order — Ḍākinī, Rākiṇī, Lākinī, Kākinī, Śākinī, Hākinī, Yākinī — and each set is closed by a nama of this shape, X-अम्बा-स्वरूपिणी or X-रूपधारिणी.

521. आज्ञाचक्राब्जनिलया → आज्ञा-चक्र-अब्ज-निलया

आज्ञा = command — आज्ञाचक्र, the wheel of command at the brow
चक्र = wheel
अब्ज = lotus (अप् "water" + ज "born")
निलया = abode, dwelling, resting place (नि + ली "to settle")
"She whose abode is the lotus of the Ājñā cakra."

Vigraha: आज्ञाचक्राब्जं निलयः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: चक्र + अब्ज → चक्राब्ज (आ by 6.1.101).

This nama opens the Hākinī set, and index.html's body here carries her whole dhyāna-śloka. That is not misplacement but the commentary's method: the meditation-verse is given at the head of a set, and the namas following are its items.

The dhyāna: "we meditate upon Hākinī, residing between the eyebrows, in the two-petalled Bindu lotus, white, holding the jñānamudrā, drum, lotus, Rudrākṣa bead and skull, residing in the marrow, six-faced, three-eyed, attended by Haṃsavatī and other Śaktis, fond of saffron-flavoured food, doing good to all."

And the correspondence with what follows is exact. शुक्लवर्णा at 522 is her white; षडानना at 523 her six faces; मज्जासंस्था at 524 the marrow; हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता at 525 her attendant śaktis; हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका at 526 the saffron-flavoured food; and हाकिनीरूपधारिणी at 527 closes the set. Namas 521–527 are this one verse turned into names, item by item.

आज्ञाचक्र had already been named at 103 आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालस्था, in the kuṇḍalinī ascent, where She abode in its interior. Here the same cakra is a yoginī's seat.

निलया stands here for the second of six times in the text — 99 मूलाधारैकनिलया, here, then 839 मुक्तिनिलया, 873 त्रिवर्गनिलया, 895 योनिनिलया and 996 श्रीचक्रराजनिलया, widening from a single lotus to the whole cakra.

522. शुक्लवर्णा → शुक्ल-वर्णा

शुक्ल = white, bright, pure
वर्णा = colour; also a letter of the alphabet
"She who is white in colour."

Vigraha: शुक्लः वर्णः यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary; the dhyāna at 521 has already supplied it.

वर्ण means both colour and letter, and the text uses the other sense at 850 वर्णरूपिणी, where Her form is the sixty-four letters. Here it is simply colour — Hākinī's white, as the dhyāna gives it. The scheme at 922 तरुणादित्यपाटला would later make colour a function of the meditation's purpose, white being the colour of the aspect that confers salvation; here it belongs to the yoginī rather than to Her, and no such account is offered.

523. षडानना → षट्-आनना

षट् = six
आनना = faced, having faces (आनन "face, mouth," with the feminine)
"The six-faced."

Vigraha: षट् आननानि यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: षट् + आनना → षडानना, the ट् voicing to ड् before the vowel — the same change as at 991 षडध्वातीतरूपिणी. index.html carries only the verse marker here.

The dhyāna at 521 gives Hākinī six faces along with three eyes, and six-facedness is her mark in the standard iconography.

आनन is the formal word for face, where the text uses मुख at 870–871 and at 924 दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा.

Note on the verse. Five namas, and the verse sits across a seam: 519–520 close the Śākinī set of the mūlādhāra, and 521–523 open the Hākinī set of the ājñā.

The text is at this point working through the seven cakra-yoginīs in order, giving each her cakra, her colour, her faces, her bodily constituent, her attendant śaktis and her favourite food, and closing each set with a nama that identifies Her with that yoginī outright.

The commentary's method shows here more plainly than anywhere else in the text. Bhāskararāya sets the whole dhyāna-śloka at the head of a set, and the namas that follow are its items, one per name. So 521's body is long while 522, 523 and 524 are empty, the commentary having already spoken for them. Read without the dhyāna, 522–527 are a list of unrelated attributes; read with it, they are a single iconographic description broken into seven names.

And the register of 519 is worth noting rather than excusing. आसक्त, the word that at 109 named Her attachment to the union of Śiva and Śakti in the sahasrāra, here names a preference for rice cooked with pulse. The yoginīs are fed, and the food is part of who they are.

Textual note. 520's dev reads साकिन्यम्चा- for साकिन्यम्बा-, a च standing where ब belongs, and the iast repeats the error.

519, 520 and 522 have no commentary bodies, and 523 carries only the verse marker. In this stretch that is a feature of the commentary's arrangement rather than a loss of data, since 521 holds the material for all of them.


---

## मज्जासंस्था हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता । हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका हाकिनीरूपधारिणी

*majjāsaṃsthā haṃsavatīmukhyaśaktisamanvitā । haridrānnaikarasikā hākinīrūpadhāriṇī*

Verse 108, namas 524–527.

524. मज्जासंस्था → मज्जा-सम्-स्था

मज्जा = marrow — that which lies deepest (from मज्ज् "to sink")
सम् = fully, completely
स्था = abiding, presiding (from स्था "to stand")
"She who presides over the marrow."

Vigraha: मज्जायां संस्थिता।

index.html has no commentary for this nama; the dhyāna at 521 has already given "residing in the marrow."

Each of the seven yoginīs is assigned one of the seven dhātus, the bodily constituents, and the two series run in step. मज्जा is sixth of the dhātus — rasa, rakta, māṃsa, medas, asthi, majjā, śukra — and Hākinī is sixth of the yoginīs. The text has been keeping the count: मेदोनिष्ठा at 509 for Kākinī is the fourth, अस्थिसंस्थिता at 516 for Śākinī the fifth, this the sixth, and the dhyāna at 528 will give śukra to Yākinī as the seventh.

मज्जा being from मज्ज् "to sink," the constituent lying deepest, suits the brow-cakra as the last station before the crown.

525. हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता → हंसवती-मुख्य-शक्ति-सम्-अन्विता

हंसवती = Haṃsavatī — she who possesses the haṃsa; the śakti of the letter ह
मुख्य = chief, principal, foremost (from मुख "face" — that which stands at the front)
शक्ति = power, a śakti
सम् = fully
अन्विता = accompanied by, attended (अनु + इ "to follow")
"She who is attended by Haṃsavatī and the chief śaktis."

Vigraha: हंसवतीमुख्याभिः शक्तिभिः समन्विता।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is a single line and it does more work than its length suggests: "the two Śaktis are Haṃsavatī and Kṣamāvatī." Two only — because the ājñā cakra has two petals, as the dhyāna at 521 said, "the two-petalled Bindu lotus."

And the two are named for their letters. In the standard scheme the fifty mātṛkā-letters are distributed over the petals of the six cakras — sixteen at the viśuddhi, twelve at the anāhata, ten at the maṇipūra, six at the svādhiṣṭhāna, four at the mūlādhāra, and two at the ājñā. Those last two are ह and क्ष, and Haṃsavatī is the ह-śakti, Kṣamāvatī the क्ष-śakti.

That makes this nama bear directly on 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी. Bhāskararāya argued at length there that the pīṭhas number fifty-one and not fifty, and named the author of the Sundarīmahodaya as wrong for "having the syllable क्ष out of count." Kṣamāvatī here is precisely the क्ष-śakti, and her place on the ājñā's second petal is what the count at 833 turns on.

मुख्य is from मुख, face — the chief being what stands at the front. मुख appears at 870–871 as the face turned inward or outward, and at 924 as the lotus-face.

526. हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका → हरिद्रा-अन्न-एक-रसिका

हरिद्रा = turmeric, and so the yellow colouring of food
अन्न = food, cooked rice (from अद् "to eat")
एक = one, sole, alone
रसिका = relishing, having a taste for (from रस "taste, savour")
"She who relishes turmeric-coloured food alone."

Vigraha: हरिद्रान्ने एकरसिका।

Sandhi at both joints: हरिद्रा + अन्न → हरिद्रान्न (आ by 6.1.101), then अन्न + एक → अन्नैक by vṛddhi (अ + ए → ऐ, Pāṇini 6.1.88 वृद्धिरेचि).

index.html has no commentary; the dhyāna at 521 gives "fond of saffron-flavoured food." Sastry renders हरिद्रा as saffron throughout, though the word is turmeric — the two are distinct spices, and only the colour is shared.

एक does real work here. Not merely fond of the dish but relishing that alone, which is what makes the offering diagnostic of the yoginī: each of the seven has her own, and 519's मुद्गौदन for Śākinī stood seven namas back.

एकरसिका is the compound of 90 कुलामृतैकरसिका, where the one relish was the amṛta of the Kula. The same shape, once for nectar and once for turmeric rice.

527. हाकिनीरूपधारिणी → हाकिनी-रूप-धारिणी

हाकिनी = Hākinī, the yoginī of the ājñā cakra
रूप = form
धारिणी = she who bears, who assumes (धृ "to hold" + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who assumes the form of Hākinī."

Vigraha: हाकिन्याः रूपं धारयतीति।

index.html carries only the verse marker.

The nama closes the Hākinī set, as साकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी closed the Śākinī set at 520. The two closing formulas alternate through the series — X-अम्बा-स्वरूपिणी and X-रूप-धारिणी — and धारिणी is the milder of the two: bearing a form rather than being one. The text does not press the difference.

धृ is the root of धरा at 955, धात्री at 935 and आधारा at 884. In this text it bears the earth, the world, the law, and here a form.

Note on the verse. Four namas, and every one of them is an item of the dhyāna-śloka set out at 521: the marrow, the attendant śaktis, the food, the yoginī's name. The set opened there closes here.

The arithmetic is what rewards attention. The ājñā has two petals, so Hākinī has exactly two attendant śaktis — and Bhāskararāya names them, Haṃsavatī and Kṣamāvatī, the śaktis of ह and क्ष, which are the two letters assigned to those petals. The scheme is consistent throughout: fifty mātṛkā-letters distributed sixteen, twelve, ten, six, four and two across the six cakras, with ह and क्ष left for the brow.

The dhātu-series runs in step with it, each yoginī presiding over one constituent in order — medas at 509, asthi at 516, majjā here, śukra at 528. Fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh.

And the two threads meet at 833. Bhāskararāya's insistence there that the pīṭhas number fifty-one, and his naming of the Sundarīmahodaya's author as wrong for leaving क्ष uncounted, depends on exactly the letter whose śakti is named in this verse.

Textual note. This verse is clean. 524 and 526 have no commentary bodies and 527 only the verse marker — which, as at 522–523, is the commentary's arrangement rather than a loss, since the dhyāna at 521 speaks for all of them.


---

## सहस्रदलपद्मस्था सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता । सर्वायुधधरा शुक्लसंस्थिता सर्वतोमुखी

*sahasradalapadmasthā sarvavarṇopaśobhitā । sarvāyudhadharā śuklasaṃsthitā sarvatomukhī*

Verse 109, namas 528–532.

528. सहस्रदलपद्मस्था → सहस्र-दल-पद्म-स्था

सहस्र = a thousand
दल = a petal, a leaf (from दल् "to split, to burst open")
पद्म = lotus
स्था = abiding, seated (from स्था "to stand")
"She who abides in the thousand-petalled lotus."

Vigraha: सहस्रदलपद्मे स्थिता।

This opens the Yākinī set, the last of the seven, and index.html's body carries her dhyāna-śloka just as 521 carried Hākinī's. The method is the same — the meditation-verse at the head of the set, its items as the namas following.

The dhyāna: "we meditate upon the beneficent Devī, Yākinī, residing in the moon of the pericarp of the thousand-petalled lotus in the Brahmarandhra, presiding over the semen, armed with all kinds of weapons, facing on every side, attended by the host of the Śaktis of the letters from अ to क्ष — fifty-one — all coloured, fond of all kinds of food, and devoted to the supreme Śiva."

The correspondence holds item by item. सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता at 529 is the letter-śaktis and the "all coloured"; सर्वायुधधरा at 530 the weapons; शुक्लसंस्थिता at 531 the semen; सर्वतोमुखी at 532 the facing every way; सर्वोदनप्रीतचित्ता at 533 the food; and याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी at 534 closes the set.

सहस्रदलपद्म is the sahasrāra, named already at 105 सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा — there with अम्बुज for the lotus and आरूढा for the mounting of it. Here दल is added and the verb is स्था: she has arrived and settled. And the dhyāna's "moon of the pericarp" is the source of the amṛta at 106 सुधासाराभिवर्षिणी, and where 879 सुधासृतिः locates the stream.

529. सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता → सर्व-वर्ण-उप-शोभिता

सर्व = all
वर्ण = colour; and also a letter of the alphabet — both senses are in play
उप = near, upon; and, by Vararuci's numeral rule, ten
शोभिता = adorned, made brilliant (from शुभ् "to shine")
"She who is adorned with all colours."

Vigraha: सर्वैः वर्णैः उपशोभिता।

Sandhi: वर्ण + उप → वर्णोप (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, 6.1.87).

वर्ण bears both its senses at once and Bhāskararāya uses both. As colour: adorned with every colour, which the dhyāna gives as "all coloured." As letter: the fifty-one letters from अ to क्ष, that is the fifty śaktis from Amṛtā to Kṣamāvatī, seated in the petals.

Then comes the arithmetic of the thousand, which is the most ingenious passage in this part of the text. The fifty śaktis counted forwards and backwards give a hundred; each of the hundred resides in ten petals; and a hundred times ten is the thousand. And उप is itself read as the numeral ten — by Vararuci's rule प is one and उ is a cipher — so the compound encodes its own multiplier. Hence, Bhāskararāya notes, some repeat each of those śaktis ten times in the Yoginīnyāsa, to make up the full number.

So the nama says three things at once: adorned with all colours, adorned by the śaktis of all the letters, and here is how fifty becomes a thousand.

The letters are Her form outright at 850 वर्णरूपिणी, where the count is sixty-four rather than fifty-one; and the fifty-one pīṭhas of 833 are this same set. Kṣamāvatī closes the list here as she closed the pair at 525 — the क्ष-śakti whose inclusion is exactly what Bhāskararāya defended at 833.

530. सर्वायुधधरा → सर्व-आयुध-धरा

सर्व = all
आयुध = a weapon (आ + युध् "to fight")
धरा = bearing, holding (from धृ "to hold")
"She who bears all weapons."

Vigraha: सर्वाणि आयुधानि धरतीति।

Sandhi: सर्व + आयुध → सर्वायुध (आ by 6.1.101).

The Rudrādhyāya is cited — "you have thousands of arms and thousands of weapons" — which suits a nama seated in a thousand-petalled lotus.

सर्वायुध had stood at 68 चक्रराजरथारूढसर्वायुधपरिष्कृता, where She was furnished with all weapons upon the Cakrarāja chariot in the Bhaṇḍāsura war. There they were for use; here they are iconographic, the yoginī's attribute.

धरा is the participial "bearing," the same word that stands alone at 955 धरा as the earth, she who bears — and धारिणी three namas back at 527 was its fuller form.

531. शुक्लसंस्थिता → शुक्ल-सम्-स्थिता

शुक्ल = white; and as a noun, semen — the seventh dhātu; and per the Bhāgavata-uttara Purāṇa, the name of a kind of meditation
सम् = fully
स्थिता = abiding, established
"She who presides over the semen."

Vigraha: शुक्ले संस्थिता।

This completes the dhātu-series that has run through the seven yoginīs. Śukla is the seventh and last of the constituents and Yākinī the seventh yoginī — medas at 509, asthi at 516, majjā at 524, and śukla here. The count has held from the fourth to the seventh.

शुक्ल as white had been the nama nine back, 522 शुक्लवर्णा, giving Hākinī's colour. Here the same word is a bodily constituent, which is how the text uses it twice within ten namas without repeating itself.

And Bhāskararāya adds a third sense from a pointed source: "according to the Bhāgavata-uttara Purāṇa, Śukla is the name of a kind of meditation at the time of sexual enjoyment." That is the same Purāṇa and the same term as at 957 धन्या — where śukla is the fourth and highest of the four last-stage meditations, "that in which, by the yoga which destroys constructive imagination, the senses remain untainted by material objects and the inner Self is fixed on its unity with the one reality," and where the commentary recommends it above the other three. Here the same term is located in the act, and in the seventh dhātu.

532. सर्वतोमुखी → सर्वतस्-मुखी

सर्वतस् = from all sides, in every direction (सर्व with the adverbial तस्)
मुखी = faced, having a face (मुख with the feminine ई)
"She who faces in every direction."

Vigraha: सर्वतः मुखानि यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: the visarga of सर्वतः becomes ओ before the voiced म्, giving सर्वतोमुखी.

Gītā 13.13 is cited — "everywhere eyes, heads and mouths" — from the verse describing the Field-knower as all-pervading. Bhāskararāya also drops a counting marker here: the twenty-first verse divides thirty-one names.

This is the third सर्व-nama in this verse alone, with a fourth following at 533: सर्ववर्ण-, सर्वायुध-, सर्वतो-, सर्वोदन-.

मुखी comes nine namas after आनना at 523 — the two words for face, one for Hākinī's six and one for Yākinī's all.

Note on the verse. Five namas, opening the last of the seven yoginī sets. 528 gives the dhyāna and 529–532 are its items, exactly as 521 gave Hākinī's and 522–527 were hers.

The set is built on सर्व, and that is its point. Yākinī sits at the sahasrāra where the series ends, and everything distributed among the lower six arrives here entire: all the letters, all the weapons, all directions, all foods. The lower cakras had sixteen letters, or twelve, or four, or two; this one has all fifty-one.

529 holds the most ingenious passage in this part of the text. Fifty śaktis counted forwards and backwards make a hundred; each of the hundred takes ten petals; and उप in the compound is itself read as the numeral ten, प being one and उ a cipher by Vararuci's rule. The nama encodes the arithmetic that turns fifty letters into a thousand petals — and Bhāskararāya draws the ritual consequence, that some repeat each śakti ten times in the Yoginīnyāsa.

531 completes the dhātu-count, and its third sense joins two namas four hundred apart by way of one Purāṇa. The Bhāgavata-uttara Purāṇa's śukla is at 957 धन्या the best of four last-stage meditations, recommended above the rest; here the same text names śukla as a meditation at the time of sexual enjoyment. Same source, same word, two quite different placements.

Textual note. This verse is clean. Just beyond it, 533 and 534 share one gloss and one body between them, each carrying the other's heading — the block-duplication pattern, falling on the very nama that closes the seven-yoginī series.


---

## सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी । स्वाहा स्वधाऽमतिर्मेधा श्रुतिः स्मृतिरनुत्तमा

*sarvaudanaprītacittā yākinyambāsvarūpiṇī । svāhā svadhā'matir medhā śrutiḥ smṛtir anuttamā*

Verse 110, namas 533–541.

533. सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता → सर्व-ओदन-प्रीत-चित्ता

सर्व = all
ओदन = boiled rice, cooked food
प्रीत = pleased, delighted (past participle of प्री "to please")
चित्ता = mind, thought (from चित् "to perceive")
"She whose mind delights in food of every kind."

Vigraha: सर्वौदनेन प्रीतं चित्तं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: सर्व + ओदन → सर्वौदन by vṛddhi (अ + ओ → औ, Pāṇini 6.1.88 वृद्धिरेचि). The dev field reads सर्वोदन- with ओ, which no rule permits — the guṇa rule that yields ओ operates before इ, उ and ऋ, not before ओ. And 519 मुद्गौदनासक्तचित्ता, fourteen namas back, shows the same joint correctly formed.

The nama completes the food-series of the seven yoginīs, and it completes it by generalising. Each of the six lower had one dish — mudga rice for Śākinī at 519, turmeric rice for Hākinī at 526 — and Yākinī at the crown has all of them, as she has all the letters at 529, all the weapons at 530 and all directions at 532.

प्रीत here, where 519 had आसक्त and 526 रसिका: three words for one relation to food across three yoginīs.

534. याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी → याकिनी-अम्बा-स्व-रूपिणी

याकिनी = Yākinī, the yoginī of the sahasrāra
अम्बा = mother
स्व = own
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose very form is Mother Yākinī."

Vigraha: याकिनी अम्बा स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: याकिनी + अम्बा → याकिन्यम्बा (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि).

This closes the seven-yoginī series, which has run from Ḍākinī at the viśuddhi through to Yākinī at the crown. The formula is the same as 520's साकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी, the series having alternated between it and X-रूपधारिणी.

index.html carries 533's gloss on this nama and one body duplicated across both, each holding the other's heading — the block-duplication pattern, falling on the nama that closes the whole series.

535. स्वाहा → स्वाहा

स्वाहा = the exclamation uttered when an oblation is offered to the gods; and, personified, the wife of Agni
"Svāhā."

Vigraha: स्वाहा इति आहुतिवाचकः शब्दः।

The body for this nama is the single word "Svāhā"; the commentary proper stands under 536, where the two are treated together.

The etymologies Bhāskararāya gathers are many. The Prapañcasāra: स्व is heaven and also the Self, आह attainment. The Taittirīya Śruti: स्व one's own with आहा speech — one's own speech. The Sāmaveda Brāhmaṇa and Yāska's Nirukta: सु well with आह speech, or स्व Self with आह to speak. Others: सु good with आह to be given as oblation. Or स्व one's own people with आह to go — she recognises the people as her own Self. Or सु well, आ Brahmā, हु to go.

And a Purāṇic identity: Svāhā is the wife of Śiva in his fire-form and the mother of Skanda. The Liṅga Purāṇa — "the wife of Śiva in the form of fire is said to be Svāhā; the divine six-faced one is called by the wise the son" — with the Vāyu Purāṇa confirming. The Padma Purāṇa makes her the presiding deity of the city of Maheśvara.

536. स्वधा → स्वधा

स्वधा = the exclamation uttered when oblations are offered to the ancestors
"Svadhā."

Vigraha: स्वधा इति पितृयज्ञवाचकः शब्दः।

Bhāskararāya's note on the pair opens with the transition: "thus having described Her under the forms of the Yoginīs, he proceeds to describe Her with other qualities." So 535–536 begin a new movement in the text — and they begin it with two words that are not names of anything.

The Kośa gives the set of ritual exclamations — Svāhā, Srauṣaṭ, Vauṣaṭ, Vaṣaṭ, Svadhā — used when oblations are offered. The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa: "there are seven words used in the Soma sacrifice, in the oblation and in the cooking; by uttering your name alone, O Devī, the merit of repeating these names is obtained by Brahmavādins." And the Devīmāhātmya: "by uttering your name all the host of gods is satisfied in all sacrifices, for thou art Svāhā and thou art named Svadhā, the word which gives satisfaction to the hosts of Pitṛs."

The division of labour is the point. स्वाहा carries the offering to the gods, स्वधा to the ancestors, so the pair covers both directions of sacrifice and She is both syllables. Bhāskararāya's own split of स्वधा makes it सु well, आ Viṣṇu, धा nourishes.

This bears on 946 पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया, where the pañcayajñas discharge the debts owed to devas, pitṛs and the rest. Here She is the very words by which two of those debts are paid.

537. अमतिः → अ-मतिः

अ = not; and per a second reading, little
मतिः = thought, understanding, intelligence (from मन् "to think")
"She who is without intelligence."

Vigraha: मतिः यस्याः नास्ति सा।

The dev field reads ऽमति, carrying two faults at once. The avagraha marks the अ elided in स्वधा + अमतिः → स्वधाऽमतिः (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101) — the seventh instance of that class in the text, and the single form again signalling a short vowel correctly. And the visarga of अमतिः has gone into the following nama.

The nama is startling and Bhāskararāya softens it three ways. अमति is avidyā. Or अ is "little" and मति knowledge — She is in the form of the knowledge of modifications. Or, with Durgācārya's commentary on the Śukla Yajus, अमति means the knowledge of the Self, the privative turning into its opposite.

Or, as he notes was said before at nama 397, अमति refers to the first creation, which was devoid of intelligence. That is the reading given again at 975 पूर्वजा, where being first-born was allowed to mean the first creation "which was without intelligence" — so the two namas share it, and 538 supplies its sequel.

538. मेधा → मेधा

मेधा = intelligence, mental vigour, retentive understanding
"Intelligence."

Vigraha: मेधा धारणावती बुद्धिः।

The dev field reads र्मेधा, with an initial र् that is not its own. It comes from the visarga of अमतिः: अमतिः + मेधा gives अमतिर्मेधा, the visarga becoming र् before the voiced म्, and the division was taken after it. This is the fourth instance of visarga mis-division in the text, after 848–849, 894–895 and 992–993.

Bhāskararāya's first words make the pair with 537 a sequence rather than a contradiction: "the next creation was accompanied by intelligence." अमतिः is the first creation and मेधा the second, so the two namas are cosmogonic stages and not opposed attributes.

Or मेधा is individual intelligence, on the Devīmāhātmya — "Devī who resides in all beings in the form of intelligence," and "O Devī, thou art intelligence, thou art the essence of all the scriptures." The Padma Purāṇa places the deity Medhā in Kaśmīra.

539. श्रुतिः → श्रुतिः

श्रुतिः = what is heard — the Veda; also hearing, the ear (from श्रु "to hear")
"The Śruti."

Vigraha: श्रूयते इति श्रुतिः।

The dev field reads श्रुति, the visarga lost. Since the following nama begins with स्, the visarga would have been retained before it rather than becoming र् — so the loss here leaves no trace in the next word, unlike at 537–538 and 540–541.

index.html has no commentary body for this nama; the material stands under 540, where श्रुति and स्मृति are treated as a pair.

श्रुति had been the first member of 929 श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा, where Her glory was celebrated by the Vedas — and where Bhāskararāya also read श्रुति as the numeral four. Here it is the Veda itself, and She is it rather than being praised by it.

540. स्मृतिः → स्मृतिः

स्मृतिः = what is remembered — the Smṛti literature; also memory, recollection (from स्मृ "to remember")
"The Smṛti."

Vigraha: स्मर्यते इति स्मृतिः।

The dev field reads स्मृतिर, with a र where the visarga belongs — the other half of the fault at 541.

Bhāskararāya takes the pair together: "the Vedas and the Smṛtis of Manu and the rest are but her form," with the Kūrma Purāṇa — "Ṛk, Yajus, Sāman and Ātharvaṇa are the inherent form of Brahman, thus is the eternal Śakti."

Or श्रुति and स्मृति are the two kinds of knowledge, by hearing and by recollection. The Vāyu Purāṇa gives the etymology — "as She recollects all actions, present, past and future, she is called Smṛti" — and the Devī Purāṇa simply "because she recollects." So the pair is not only the two bodies of scripture but the two faculties that receive them.

541. अनुत्तमा → अन्-उत्तमा

अन् = not (नञ् before a vowel)
उत्तमा = highest, best
"She than whom there is none higher."

Vigraha: न विद्यते उत्तमः यस्याः सा।

The dev field reads नुत्तमा, the initial अ lost. It went with the preceding sandhi: स्मृतिः + अनुत्तमा gives स्मृतिरनुत्तमा, the visarga becoming र् before the vowel, and the division taken after that र्. So 540 keeps a र that is not its own and 541 loses the अ that is — the same fault as 992–993, and like that one it damages the sense, since नुत्तमा is not a word.

The formation deserves a word. अनुत्तम does not mean "not the highest" but "having none higher," the negation falling on any possible superior rather than on Her. Bhāskararāya's gloss is exactly that — "because there is none superior to her" — with Śvetāśvatara 6.8 and Gītā 11.43, "nothing is to be found equal or superior to him."

The Devī Bhāgavata's argument for it is from usage, and it is a good one: "people never say of a man devoid of strength 'he is deprived of Rudra' or 'of Viṣṇu,' but say 'deprived of Śakti'." The word for power is hers, not theirs.

A second division gives अनुत्त "not depending" with म "intelligence or dominion" — one whose intelligence or dominion is not derived from another. That is 877 निरालम्बा's argument in another form, where She could have no support because She supports all.

Note on the verse. Nine namas, and the verse turns a corner in the middle. 533–534 close the seven-yoginī series that has occupied the text since the viśuddhi; 535 begins something else, and Bhāskararāya marks the turn in as many words: "thus having described Her under the forms of the Yoginīs, he proceeds to describe Her with other qualities."

What follows is a run of bare nouns arranged in pairs that answer one another. स्वाहा and स्वधा are the two oblation-words, one for gods and one for ancestors. अमतिः and मेधा are two creations, the first without intelligence and the second with — and Bhāskararāya's single sentence, "the next creation was accompanied by intelligence," turns an apparent contradiction into a sequence. श्रुतिः and स्मृतिः are the two bodies of scripture and also the two faculties that hold them. Then अनुत्तमा stands alone and closes.

535–536 are also the two indeclinable namas which the Paribhāṣā verse at the very end of the text singles out. Verse 37 records that of the thousand names two are avyayas, and these are they — so a nama in this text can be a particle.

Textual note. This verse holds the densest concentration of sandhi faults anywhere in the text: five in five consecutive namas, all of one kind.

537's dev reads ऽमति — carrying the avagraha of the अ elided from स्वधा + अमतिः, the seventh such instance, and having also lost its own visarga. 538 reads र्मेधा, having gained the र् that visarga became before म्. 539 reads श्रुति, its visarga lost without trace, since स् is a sound before which a visarga is retained. 540 reads स्मृतिर, having gained a र in its turn. And 541 reads नुत्तमा, having lost the initial अ of अनुत्तमा at that same joint.

The fault is one throughout — the word-division taken one letter late across a visarga — and these are its fourth and fifth occurrences, after 848–849, 894–895 and 992–993. As at 993, the last of them destroys a word.

Two further matters. 533's dev reads सर्वोदन- with ओ where vṛddhi requires औ, and no rule yields ओ at that joint; 519 मुद्गौदन shows it correctly formed. And 534 carries 533's gloss with a shared body, the block-duplication falling on the nama that closes the yoginī series.


---

## पुण्यकीर्तिः पुण्यलभ्या पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना । पुलोमजार्चिता बन्धमोचनी बर्बरालका

*puṇyakīrtiḥ puṇyalabhyā puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanā । pulomajārcitā bandhamocanī barbarālakā*

Verse 111, namas 542–547.

542. पुण्यकीर्तिः → पुण्य-कीर्तिः

पुण्य = holy, meritorious, sanctifying; merit, good action
कीर्तिः = fame, renown (from कीर्त् "to mention, to celebrate")
"She whose fame sanctifies."

Vigraha: पुण्या कीर्तिः यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is four words — "whose fame sanctifies" — and it takes पुण्य actively: not fame for holiness but fame that makes holy.

The dev field reads पुण्यकीर्त्तिः with त्त doubled. That is an orthographic variant common in older editions, कीर्त्ति for कीर्ति, and not a fault.

कीर्तिः had stood at 848 उदारकीर्तिः, where Bhāskararāya divided the syllables five ways on अर. Here he leaves the compound alone, and the three पुण्य-namas that open this verse are the plainest stretch in a long while.

543. पुण्यलभ्या → पुण्य-लभ्या

पुण्य = merit, good action — here specifically deeds of former births
लभ्या = to be obtained, attainable (लभ् "to get" with the gerundive यत्)
"She who is attained through merit."

Vigraha: पुण्येन लभ्या।

पुण्य Bhāskararāya specifies as "good actions performed in previous births," so the merit is inherited rather than accumulated now. The Devī Bhāgavata: "only those ever-righteous ascetics who are devoted to wisdom see; but the men of desire see not the holy and beneficent Devī."

लभ्या is the gerundive that stood negated and doubly intensified at 871 बहिर्मुखसुदुर्लभा, where the outward-faced found Her exceedingly hard to attain. Positive here, and the condition is merit rather than attention.

544. पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना → पुण्य-श्रवण-कीर्तना

पुण्य = holy, sanctifying
श्रवण = hearing (from श्रु "to hear")
कीर्तना = reciting, proclaiming (from कीर्त्)
"She the hearing and reciting of whom are holy."

Vigraha: पुण्ये श्रवणकीर्तने यस्याः सा।

The commentary is a fragment — "are holy" — the rest lost, but the sense is not in doubt.

The nama is about the text it stands in. श्रवण and कीर्तन are two of the classical acts of devotion, and this says both are sanctifying when their object is Her — so a nama in the Sahasranāma asserts the merit of reciting the Sahasranāma. कीर्ति at 542 and कीर्तना here are from one root, two namas apart: her fame, and the proclaiming of it.

श्रु had given श्रुतिः at 539, eight namas back.

545. पुलोमजार्चिता → पुलोमजा-अर्चिता

पुलोमजा = the daughter of Puloman — Śacī, Indra's wife
अर्चिता = worshipped, honoured (from अर्च् "to worship")
"She who is worshipped by Indra's queen."

Vigraha: पुलोमजया अर्चिता।

Sandhi: पुलोमजा + अर्चिता → पुलोमजार्चिता (आ by 6.1.101).

The story is from the Devī Bhāgavata, Book VI, and Bhāskararāya gives it: when Nahuṣa was ruling heaven and Indra deposed, Indra's wife received the mantra of Devī from Bṛhaspati and "worshipped earnestly Tripurasundarī, by oblations of food, flowers and the rest," that Indra might be restored. So the nama records a particular worshipper on a particular occasion, and the occasion is a usurpation.

अर्चिता is the participle of 825 बुधार्चिता and 917 धीरसमर्चिता, where the worshippers were the wise; here the worshipper is named.

546. बन्धमोचनी → बन्ध-मोचनी

बन्ध = a bond, a fetter; bondage; also imprisonment (from बन्ध् "to bind")
मोचनी = she who releases, who looses (from मुच् "to loose," in the causative)
"She who looses bonds."

Vigraha: बन्धं मोचयतीति बन्धमोचनी।

बन्ध Bhāskararāya takes two ways at once — "bonds of ignorance, or prison" — and both his illustrations are literal imprisonments freed by Her.

From the Harivaṃśa, Aniruddha in Bāṇa's town: "O Śaṃkarī, thou art praised by these and other names by me; by thy grace let me be soon freed from prison. O large-eyed one, behold, I take refuge in thy feet. You are to liberate me from every bond." And "Durgā, the powerful one, thus praised, set free the brave Aniruddha." From the Devī Bhāgavata, Book VI: a princess named Ekāvalī, imprisoned by the Daitya Kālaketu, was freed by Devī, worshipped by Yaśovatī the princess's friend.

मुच् is the root of मुक्ति at 839 मुक्तिनिलया and of निर्मुक्ता at 862 and 867 — release from causality and from decay there, from a cell here. The nama keeps the two senses of bondage side by side without ranking them.

547. बर्बरालका → बर्बर-अलका

बर्बर = curly, crisped, frizzled
अलका = a lock of hair, a curl (अलक with the feminine)
"She of the curling locks."

Vigraha: बर्बराणि अलकानि यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: बर्बर + अलका → बर्बरालका (आ by 6.1.101).

The dev field for this nama is the most corrupt in the text. It reads बर्ब बंधु रालका, with the compound broken into three pieces and a spurious बंधु inserted in the middle — evidently a bleed from बन्धमोचनी in the preceding nama. The iast repeats it as barba baṃdhu rālakā, and there is no commentary body. Only the gloss, "wavy haired," preserves the reading.

Three separate faults in one field, then: two intruded spaces and one interpolated word. Elsewhere in this text a dev field loses a letter or gains one; here it has gained a whole nama-fragment.

Note on the verse. Six namas, three on पुण्य and three of act and appearance. The पुण्य-triad moves outward — Her fame sanctifies, merit attains Her, hearing and reciting Her are holy — and the third of them is about the recitation of this text. Then two named rescues, Śacī's worship and Aniruddha's release, and finally a curl of hair.

The pairing of 545 and 546 is not accidental: both are stories of restoration from confinement, one a god deposed from heaven and one a prince in a cell.

---

## विमर्शरूपिणी विद्या वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः । सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी

*vimarśarūpiṇī vidyā viyadādijagatprasūḥ । sarvavyādhipraśamanī sarvamṛtyunivāriṇī*

Verse 112, namas 548–552.

548. विमर्शरूपिणी → विमर्श-रूपिणी

विमर्श = reflection, deliberation, self-awareness — in Śaiva usage the inherent vibration by which Prakāśa knows itself (वि + मृश् "to touch, to consider"); also significant speech
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is Vimarśa."

Vigraha: विमर्शः रूपं यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya's definition is exact: "Vimarśa is the inherent vibration of Parabrahman who is in the Prakāśa aspect." The Saubhāgyasudhodaya — "in that Brahman there is an inherent Śakti in the form of vibration called Vimarśa; that Śakti produces the animate and inanimate universe, and the same also destroys it." So Prakāśa is the light and Vimarśa the light's awareness of itself, and She is the second.

The pair returns much later at 991 षडध्वातीतरूपिणी, where the Virūpākṣapañcāśikā divides the six paths between them — words, mantras and letters to Vimarśa; worlds, categories and parts to Prakāśa. Three ways through speech and three through being, which is exactly the division this nama's second reading depends on.

For Bhāskararāya also takes विमर्श as significant speech, and the Mātṛkāviveka's argument is a good one: "without Vimarśa, how is thought manifested? Without thought to be spoken of, how can there be speech? Therefore thought is required for the existence of speech, and thought, even when there is self-consciousness, requires speech." Neither term is prior.

549. विद्या → विद्या

विद्या = knowledge, science; a mantra of a female deity; and in Śaiva doctrine the third of the five kalās (from विद् "to know")
"Knowledge."

Vigraha: विद्यते अनया इति विद्या।

Because She is the Vidyā that confers salvation. The Devīmāhātmya — "the holy supreme Devī is Vidyā"; the Gauḍapāda Sūtra — "she herself is Vidyā," she being Devī as described in the preceding sūtra, in the form of absolute consciousness.

Then the technical sense: विद्या is a particular kalā, resident in the Tejas, "consisting of knowledge and action" — "by the discrimination of the products of Māyā one recognises the state of wisdom; that supreme kalā is known as Vidyā." That is the third of the five kalās whose set the text works twice elsewhere: निवृत्ति, प्रतिष्ठा, विद्या, शान्ति, शान्त्यतीता. प्रतिष्ठा, the second, is nama 829; शान्त्यतीता, the fifth, is 853; and the lower four are Her śaktis at 929. Here the middle one stands as a nama in its own right.

And the convention noted at 918 applies: mantras of female deities are called vidyās, those of male deities mantras. So विद्या names Her mantra as well as Her knowledge.

550. वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः → वियत्-आदि-जगत्-प्रसूः

वियत् = sky, ether, ākāśa
आदि = beginning with, and the rest
जगत् = the world — literally "the moving" (from गम्)
प्रसूः = she who brings forth, mother (प्र + सू "to generate")
"The Mother of the world beginning with ether."

Vigraha: वियदादेः जगतः प्रसूः।

Sandhi: वियत् + आदि → वियदादि, the त् voicing before the vowel.

This is 837 वियत्प्रसूः with two members inserted. There She was mother of ether simply; here mother of the world that begins with ether — and the citation is the same Śruti, Taittirīya Upaniṣad II, "ether arose from Ātman." Ākāśa being the first of the five elements to issue from Brahman, आदि does the work of naming the whole series through its first term.

जगत् had stood at 935 जगद्धात्री, where She sustained the moving world. Mother here, sustainer there, and the same root गम् behind the noun both times.

551. सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी → सर्व-व्याधि-प्र-शमनी

सर्व = all
व्याधि = disease, sickness (वि + आ + धा — literally what is laid upon one)
प्र = fully, forth
शमनी = she who quiets, allays, extinguishes (from शम् "to be quiet," in the causative)
"She who allays every disease."

Vigraha: सर्वान् व्याधीन् प्रशमयतीति।

Bhāskararāya reads व्याधि widely — "old age and the rest" — so the diseases include what is not properly disease.

That matters, because व्याधि is the fourth member of the classical set whose other three stand at 851 जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी: birth, death and old age there, disease here, and the next nama takes death again. And the disease-figure has been used of saṃsāra itself at 842 भवरोगघ्नी, with रोग for व्याधि, and denied of Her at 876 निरामया, with आमय. Three words for affliction across three namas of the text.

शमनी is from शम्, the root of शमात्मिका at 963, where She was tranquillity itself. Here the tranquillising is transitive.

552. सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी → सर्व-मृत्यु-नि-वारिणी

सर्व = all
मृत्यु = death (from मृ "to die") — here specifically untimely death
नि = down, away
वारिणी = she who wards off, keeps back (from वृ "to ward off")
"She who wards off every death."

Vigraha: सर्वान् मृत्यून् निवारयतीति।

मृत्यु Bhāskararāya specifies as "untimely death, fatal disease and the rest," which keeps this nama from simply denying mortality. The Śrutis: Śvetāśvatara 4.15, "knowing Him thus, he breaks the nooses of death," and Kaṭha 3.15, "he is freed from the power of death."

निवारिणी is the word of 913 सर्वापद्विनिवारिणी, where वि was added and what was warded off was misfortune entire. The two namas are built alike, and 913's placement — provided for those who fall from both paths — gives the register.

Note on the verse. Five namas in two movements. 548–550 are cosmogonic: She is the self-awareness by which the light knows itself, She is knowledge, She is mother of the world from ether down. 551–552 are protective and paired on सर्व: every disease allayed, every death warded off.

The join is worth marking. Having been named the origin of the elemental series at 550, She is at once named the remover of what befalls what she has originated. Bhāskararāya's widening of both terms — व्याधि to include old age, मृत्यु to mean untimely death — keeps the pair from claiming that Her devotees do not die.

And 548 sets up a distinction the text will use much later. Prakāśa and Vimarśa, light and its self-awareness, are the two poles between which the Virūpākṣapañcāśikā distributes the six paths at 991.

---

## अग्रगण्याऽचिन्त्यरूपा कलिकल्मषनाशिनी । कात्यायनी कालहन्त्री कमलाक्षनिषेविता

*agragaṇyā'cintyarūpā kalikalmaṣanāśinī । kātyāyanī kālahantrī kamalākṣaniṣevitā*

Verse 113, namas 553–558.

553. अग्रगण्या → अग्र-गण्या

अग्र = front, foremost, first
गण्या = to be counted, to be enumerated (गण् "to count" with the gerundive यत्); and, per a second reading, from गण, a host
"She who is to be counted first."

Vigraha: अग्रे गण्या।

The reason given is causal, not honorific: "as she is the root cause of the whole universe she is the first to be enumerated." Being counted first follows from being first.

A second reading takes गण्य from गण, a host — the hosts of Maruts and the rest — making Her their foremost commander.

This is one of three namas for primacy within a few hundred, and they are not alike. 563 मुख्या, ten namas on, is "the first" by rank; 975 पूर्वजा is first in time, and there the commentary undercuts the honour by allowing that पूर्वजा may mean the first creation, which was unintelligent. Here primacy is a consequence of causality.

554. अचिन्त्यरूपा → अ-चिन्त्य-रूपा

अ = not (नञ्)
चिन्त्य = to be thought, conceivable (चिन्त् "to think" with the gerundive यत्)
रूपा = form
"She whose form cannot be conceived."

Vigraha: अचिन्त्यं रूपं यस्याः सा।

The dev field reads ऽचिन्त्यरूपा. The avagraha marks the अ elided in अग्रगण्या + अचिन्त्यरूपा → अग्रगण्याऽचिन्त्यरूपा (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101) — the eighth instance of that class in the text, and the single form again correctly signalling a short vowel.

Bhāskararāya's reason is precise: "because she is free from connection with the qualities, her nature is unthinkable." Thought works by qualities, so what has none cannot be thought. That is the argument of 961 गुणातीता stated as a consequence, and it stands beside 962 सर्वातीता, where Bhāskararāya narrowed "transcending all" to transcending all words.

चिन्ता had given चिन्तामणि at 57; and चित्ता stood at 519 and 533 in the yoginī sets. Here the root is negated.

555. कलिकल्मषनाशिनी → कलि-कल्मष-नाशिनी

कलि = the Kali age, the last and worst of the four
कल्मष = stain, defilement, sin
नाशिनी = she who destroys (from नश् "to perish," in the causative)
"She who destroys the defilement of the Kali age."

Vigraha: कलेः कल्मषं नाशयतीति।

The claim is specific: She destroys the sin which necessarily predominates in the Kali age "and which cannot be destroyed by others." The Kūrma Purāṇa gives it as a natural proportion — "water is able to quench fire, the presence of the sun to dispel darkness, and the repetition of the names of Devī to destroy the multitude of sins in the Kali age." Each remedy matched to its own opponent, which is the same logic as the medical argument at 842, where "the remedy for all diseases is naturally in opposition."

The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa: "the remembrance of the feet of Supreme Śakti is said to be the highest expiation for sins consciously or unconsciously committed."

556. कात्यायनी → कात्यायनी

कात्यायनी = Kātyāyanī — patronymic of Kātya, hence the daughter of the Ṛṣi Kata; and the collective brightness of all the Devas
"Kātyāyanī."

Vigraha: कात्यस्य अपत्यं कात्यायनी।

Three accounts. The patronymic — daughter of the Ṛṣi named Kata. The Vāmana Purāṇa's: the name of the deity who is the collective form of the brightness of all the Devas, "that brightness which is the best and the greatest is known in the world by the name of Kātyāyanī." And the Devī Purāṇa's syllabic reading — क means Brahmā, the head, and the philosopher's stone, and as She rests upon them She is Kātyāyanī. The Kālikā Purāṇa places her at Oḍḍiyāna.

The name has already done work in this text without being a nama. At 893 विष्णुरूपिणी Bhāskararāya cited the Bṛhat-Parāśara Smṛti for the fruit of worship — "he who with delighted mind worships Durgā, Kātyāyanī, Vāgdevatās, obtains the world of Viṣṇu." The rite named there is to the deity named here.

557. कालहन्त्री → काल-हन्त्री

काल = time; and death (from कल् "to reckon")
हन्त्री = she who slays, the killer (हन् "to strike" with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्)
"She who slays Time."

Vigraha: कालं हन्तीति कालहन्त्री।

Bhāskararāya glosses काल as death simply, with Śvetāśvatara 6.2: "omniscient, time of time, possessed of all qualities, all-knowing." कालस्य कालः — the time of time — is the phrase the nama turns into a name.

हन्त्री is the तृ agent-noun of हन्, and the same root gave घ्नी at 842 भवरोगघ्नी, where what was slain was the disease of existence. Slayer of the disease there, of time itself here. The formation is that of सवित्री at 826, दात्री at 832, कर्त्री at 882 and धात्री at 935.

558. कमलाक्षनिषेविता → कमल-अक्ष-नि-सेविता

कमल = lotus
अक्ष = eye — कमलाक्ष, the lotus-eyed, that is Viṣṇu
नि = down, thoroughly
सेविता = served, attended, worshipped (from सेव् "to serve")
"She who is worshipped by the lotus-eyed."

Vigraha: कमलाक्षेण निषेविता।

Sandhi: कमल + अक्ष → कमलाक्ष (आ by 6.1.101); and the स् of सेविता retroflexes to ष् after नि, giving निषेविता.

The Padma Purāṇa is quoted for the fruit: "Viṣṇu ever worships the sapphire Devī, hence he attained his own state." His own rank is owed to worshipping Her — which is the relation the text asserts of Viṣṇu at 893, where he is Her form, and of Kubera at 885, the Vipras at 888, and Śiva at 910.

निषेविता had stood at 518 वरदादिनिषेविता, forty namas back, where the attendants were the four śaktis from Varadā to Sarasvatī.

Note on the verse. Six namas: two of primacy and inconceivability, then four on क.

553 and 554 are a matched pair and the second follows from the first. She is counted first because she is the root cause; and being the root cause, she is free of the qualities; and being free of the qualities, she cannot be thought. Bhāskararāya's two short glosses make one argument across the two namas.

The क-group is a run of specificities after that abstraction — a named age, a named Ṛṣi's daughter, time itself, and a named worshipper. And two of the four turn on someone else's dependence: Kātyāyanī's worship earns the world of Viṣṇu (893), and Viṣṇu's own worship of Her earns him his state (558).

---

## ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा । मृगाक्षी मोहिनी मुख्या मृडानी मित्ररूपिणी

*tāmbūlapūritamukhī dāḍimīkusumaprabhā । mṛgākṣī mohinī mukhyā mṛḍānī mitrarūpiṇī*

Verse 114, namas 559–565.

559. ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी → ताम्बूल-पूरित-मुखी

ताम्बूल = betel — the prepared leaf with areca and lime
पूरित = filled (from पूर् "to fill")
मुखी = mouthed, having a mouth (मुख with the feminine)
"She whose mouth is filled with betel."

Vigraha: ताम्बूलेन पूरितं मुखं यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The betel reddens the mouth, which is why this nama stands immediately before one about a red flower — the two are a single observation divided. मुखी returns from 532 सर्वतोमुखी, where the faces were all directions; here it is one mouth and what is in it.

560. दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा → दाडिमी-कुसुम-प्रभा

दाडिमी = the pomegranate
कुसुम = flower, blossom
प्रभा = radiance, splendour, lustre (प्र + भा "to shine")
"She whose radiance is that of the pomegranate flower."

Vigraha: दाडिमीकुसुमस्य प्रभा इव प्रभा यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya's note is botanical and slightly odd: "the pomegranate is a kind of tree which bears no fruit but only flowers." The variety meant is the ornamental one, grown for the blossom.

This is a fourth red, and as with the others it is a particular one. 891 विद्रुमाभा is coral, Her substance; 922 तरुणादित्यपाटला the rose of the young sun, which the commentary there makes the colour of one aspect only; 964 बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या the deep red of a Vaṅga tree; and here the scarlet of a pomegranate flower. Two of the four are कुसुम-compounds, and 919 चैतन्यकुसुमप्रिया makes the flower consciousness itself.

561. मृगाक्षी → मृग-अक्षी

मृग = a deer, a fawn (from मृग् "to seek, to range")
अक्षी = eyed (अक्षि with the feminine)
"The fawn-eyed."

Vigraha: मृगस्य इव अक्षिणी यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: मृग + अक्षी → मृगाक्षी (आ by 6.1.101). index.html has no commentary.

अक्षि here after कमलाक्ष three namas back, where the lotus-eyed was Viṣṇu — the same word for eye, once his and once hers. And विशालाक्षी at 936 gives her wide eyes, where Bhāskararāya converted the epithet into a pīṭha seated in them.

562. मोहिनी → मोहिनी

मोहिनी = she who bewilders, enchants, infatuates (from मुह् "to be confused," in the causative)
"The Enchantress."

Vigraha: मोहयतीति मोहिनी।

The Laghu-Nāradīya Purāṇa derives the name from its effect: "because, O beautiful one, this whole universe is enchanted with thee, thy name shall be the enchanting one, which is derived from its own qualities."

Then the Mohinī of the churning. Viṣṇu assumed that form when the ocean was churned, and the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa makes it Her second appearance: the first was the Śakti called Prakṛti, who appeared to Brahmā as the fruit of his meditation; the second, "causing enchantment of all, transcending mind and speech, was during the churning for nectar, seeing which even the omniscient Śiva was enchanted." The deity resides on the bank of the river Pratara.

That Śiva was enchanted is the point the text returns to at 954 शंभुमोहिनी, where the same causative names Her as his bewilderer specifically. And मुह् had given मुग्धा at 868, where She was the bewildered one and the Viśva's two senses, "beautiful and ignorant," both came from this root. Bewildered, bewilderer, bewilderer of Śiva — the one root three ways.

563. मुख्या → मुख्या

मुख्या = chief, principal, first (from मुख "face" — that which is at the front)
"The First."

Vigraha: मुखे भवा मुख्या।

The citation is Taittirīya Upaniṣad 3.10.6 — "I am the first born of truth." That is the very verse cited at 975 पूर्वजा, and the two namas are therefore the same claim on the same authority, four hundred apart: primacy of birth there, primacy of rank here.

With 553 अग्रगण्या this makes three namas for being first in this stretch of the text, each on a different ground — first to be counted because first in causality, first by rank, first in time. And मुख्य had stood at 525 हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता, where Haṃsavatī was chief among two.

564. मृडानी → मृड-आनी

मृड = Mṛḍa, Śiva — the gracious, the giver of happiness (from मृड् "to be gracious")
आनी = the feminine ङीष् with its आनुक् augment (Pāṇini 4.1.49)
"Mṛḍānī — the consort of Mṛḍa."

Vigraha: मृडस्य पत्नी मृडानी।

Bhāskararāya glosses मृड as "the giver of happiness, that is Paramaśiva," and drops a counting marker: the twenty-second verse divides thirty-one names.

The formation is the one set out at 112 भवानी. Pāṇini 4.1.49 lists the words taking the आनुक् augment before the feminine ङीष् — इन्द्र, वरुण, भव, शर्व, रुद्र, मृड and the rest — and मृड is among them. So भवानी at 112, शर्वाणी at 121, and मृडानी here are three members of one Pāṇinian list standing as three namas, and the suffix is why none of them is *भवी or *मृडी.

565. मित्ररूपिणी → मित्र-रूपिणी

मित्र = a friend; and Mitra, the Vedic deity — Bhāskararāya adds the twelve suns
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is the friend."

Vigraha: मित्रं रूपं यस्याः सा।

The whole commentary is four words: "or Mitra, the twelve suns" — the Ādityas, of whom Mitra is one. So the nama is at once friendship and a solar identification, and the second is offered as the alternative to the first.

रूपिणी closes this verse as it closed the last, and the count in the text is considerable — 548 विमर्शरूपिणी opened verse 112 with it, and 833, 840, 850, 893, 897, 908, 981, 991 and 999 carry it later.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and the verse is the most physical in this stretch. Two of appearance — the betel-filled mouth, the pomegranate radiance — then fawn eyes; and the three belong together, since betel reddens the mouth and the flower supplies the colour.

Then four namas of relation and rank: enchantress, first, Śiva's consort, friend. The turn from body to relation happens at 562, and 562 is where the verse's weight lies, because the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa's account there makes Her enchantment of Śiva the point — a claim the text will make its own at 954.

564 is worth noting for grammar rather than doctrine. मृडानी, भवानी and शर्वाणी are three namas of this text drawn from one list in Pāṇini 4.1.49, and the आनुक् augment is what all three have in common.

---

## नित्यतृप्ता भक्तनिधिर्नियन्त्री निखिलेश्वरी । मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी

*nityatṛptā bhaktanidhir niyantrī nikhileśvarī । maitryādivāsanālabhyā mahāpralayasākṣiṇī*

Verse 115, namas 566–571.

566. नित्यतृप्ता → नित्य-तृप्ता

नित्य = eternal, perpetual; and as a noun per the commentary, happiness itself
तृप्ता = satisfied, content (past participle of तृप् "to be satisfied")
"She who is eternally content."

Vigraha: नित्यं तृप्ता।

Bhāskararāya's alternative is a single clause: "or नित्या, happiness itself" — taking the first member as a substantive rather than an adverb.

तृप् is the root of तर्पण at 974 बिन्दुतर्पणसंतुष्टा, where the libation at the Bindu satisfied Her, and that nama pairs तर्पण with तुष्टा — two roots for satisfaction. Here तृप् supplies the participle directly. And the sense is that of 921 सदातुष्टा, ever content: नित्य here, सदा there, the same claim with different words for always.

567. भक्तनिधिः → भक्त-निधिः

भक्त = a devotee, one devoted (from भज् "to share, to worship")
निधिः = a treasure, a store; a receptacle (नि + धा "to place down")
"She who is the treasure of her devotees."

Vigraha: भक्तानां निधिः।

Bhāskararāya's gloss defines the treasure by function: "निधि, which fulfils desire" — not a hoard but a wishing-store.

The dev field reads भक्तनिधि, the visarga lost. In the verse भक्तनिधिः + नियन्त्री gives भक्तनिधिर्नियन्त्री, the visarga becoming र् before the voiced न् — but here, unlike at 538 and 540, the following nama has not gained the र्. The letter has simply been dropped, so this is the same fault as 539 श्रुतिः rather than the mis-division of 537–538 and 540–541.

निधि is from नि + धा, the same धा that gives धात्री at 935 and स्वधा at 536 — placing, sustaining, and here a placed store.

568. नियन्त्री → नियन्त्री

नि = down, back
यन्त्री = she who restrains, controls, guides (from यम् "to hold, to restrain," with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्)
"She who guides."

Vigraha: नियमयतीति नियन्त्री।

The commentary is one clause: "because she is the guide of the universe."

यम् is the root of restraint, and नियम is its ordinary derivative — the observances. So नियन्त्री is the one who holds the reins, and the guidance is a checking rather than a leading. The तृ agent-noun again, as at 557 कालहन्त्री nine namas back.

The nama sits against 995 सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना, where Her command may not be transgressed by anyone, Brahmā included.

569. निखिलेश्वरी → निखिल-ईश्वरी

निखिल = entire, whole, all (नि + खिल "remainder" — leaving no remainder)
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady (from ईश् "to rule")
"Sovereign of all."

Vigraha: निखिलस्य ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: निखिल + ईश्वरी → निखिलेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87). index.html carries only the verse marker.

निखिल is worth its etymology: नि with खिल, a remainder or waste piece — so "all" here means all with nothing left over, which is a stronger word than सर्व.

ईश्वरी had stood at 831 प्राणेश्वरी over the breaths and at 945 वामकेश्वरी over the Vāma; ईशी at 932, 949 and 983. This is the widest of them, and the only one with no remainder.

570. मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या → मैत्री-आदि-वासना-लभ्या

मैत्री = friendliness, benevolence (vṛddhi derivative of मित्र, "friend")
आदि = beginning with, and the rest
वासना = a mental disposition, an abiding impression (from वास्, to perfume or to dwell — that which lingers)
लभ्या = to be obtained, attainable (लभ् with the gerundive यत्)
"She who is attained through the dispositions beginning with friendliness."

Vigraha: मैत्र्यादिवासनाभिः लभ्या।

Sandhi: मैत्री + आदि → मैत्र्यादि, the ई becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (6.1.77 इको यणचि); and वासना + लभ्या leaves the आ standing.

Bhāskararāya names the four and matches each to its object: friendship, compassion, complacency and indifference, applied respectively to the happy, the miserable, the virtuous and the sinful. He refers to the Viṣṇu Bhāgavata for the explanation and to Yoga Sūtra 1.33 for the source, where Rājamārtaṇḍa's commentary notes that "happiness and the rest" stand for the persons who are happy and the rest. Their function is stated plainly: "these purify the mind."

Māgha 4.55 is then quoted for what follows the purification: "they whose minds are purified by friendship and the rest, removing their sorrow, and who obtaining here the seed of Yoga and attaining glory by discriminating Puruṣa from Sattva, and remaining in Samādhi, desire to transcend even that state."

मैत्री is the vṛddhi abstract of मित्र, which stood as a nama five back at 565 मित्ररूपिणी. There She is the friend; here friendliness is the means of reaching Her.

And वासना had been used at 858 कल्पनारहिता, in the division reading कल्प + नर + हित, where at the universal dissolution She holds the souls in Her belly "in the form of vāsanās, latent tendencies." There they are what survives the world; here they are what reaches Her.

571. महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी → महा-प्रलय-साक्षिणी

महा = great
प्रलय = dissolution, the reabsorption of the universe (प्र + ली "to dissolve")
साक्षिणी = witness — literally she who is with the eye, an eye-witness (स + अक्षि, with the suffix इन् and feminine ङीप्)
"She who is witness of the great dissolution."

Vigraha: महाप्रलयस्य साक्षिणी।

साक्षिन् is स with अक्षि — the one who has the eye present, hence a witness in the forensic sense. It is the third अक्षि-nama in this stretch, after 558's lotus-eyed Viṣṇu and 561 मृगाक्षी, and here the eye is not an ornament but a function.

The reason She alone can witness is that no one else is left: "as Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest perish at the time of the dance of Śiva at the great dissolution, she alone is the witness of that dance." The five gods who were the couch at 947 and the chain of command at 995 are here the ones who do not survive.

And the verse Bhāskararāya quotes describes Her by her weapons: "bearing the noose, the elephant hook, the bow of sugarcane and the arrow of flowers, your form alone remains victorious, witnessing the dance of the divine Parabhairava, bearing the axe at the time of dissolution of the universe." That is the same equipment the verse at nama 1000 uses to explain Her name — "thy bow is made of sugarcane, thy arrows are flowers, and everything connected with thee is lovely" — so the sugarcane bow appears both at the end of the world and in the etymology of Lalitā.

Note on the verse. Six namas, four on न and two long compounds.

The न-group is a sequence of increasing scope: eternally content in herself, treasure to her devotees, guide of the universe, sovereign of all without remainder. Then 570 gives the means of attaining Her and 571 places Her where nothing else is.

570 is the most technical nama here and the most transferable. The four vāsanās — maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā — are the four dispositions of Yoga Sūtra 1.33, each matched to a class of person, and their stated function is to purify the mind. What the Māgha verse adds is that purification is not the end: those so purified obtain the seed of Yoga and then "desire to transcend even" samādhi.

And 571 closes the verse where several verses in this text close, on Her outlasting the gods. But the detail worth keeping is the sugarcane bow. It is named here at the dissolution and again at nama 1000 in the derivation of the name Lalitā — the same object at the two ends of the text, once among the ruins and once as evidence that everything about Her is lovely.

Textual note for these five verses. Three faults.

547's dev is the most corrupt field in the text: बर्ब बंधु रालका for बर्बरालका, with two intruded spaces and an interpolated बंधु evidently bled from बन्धमोचनी in the preceding nama, and the iast repeating all of it. Only the gloss preserves the reading, and there is no commentary body.

554's dev reads ऽचिन्त्यरूपा, carrying the avagraha of the अ elided from अग्रगण्या + अचिन्त्यरूपा — the eighth instance of that class, single form for a short vowel as the rule holds.

567's dev reads भक्तनिधि, the visarga lost. Unlike 537–538 and 540–541 the following nama has not gained the र्, so this is the simple loss seen at 539 rather than a mis-division.

Beyond those: 542's पुण्यकीर्त्तिः with doubled त्त is an orthographic variant, not an error. 544's body is a fragment. 559, 561 and 563 have no commentary bodies, and 569 only a verse marker.
