## पराशक्तिः परानिष्ठा प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी । माध्वीपानालसा मत्ता मातृकावर्णरूपिणी

*parāśaktiḥ parāniṣṭhā prajñānaghanarūpiṇī । mādhvīpānālasā mattā mātṛkāvarṇarūpiṇī*

Verse 116, namas 572–577.

572. पराशक्तिः → परा-शक्तिः

परा = supreme, highest, beyond
शक्तिः = power, energy (from शक् "to be able")
"The Supreme Energy."

Vigraha: परा शक्तिः।

Bhāskararāya's first gloss is anatomical and unexpected. The Kāmikāgama divides the body's constituents between Śiva and Devī: "skin, blood, flesh, fat and bone, these five are derived from Devī; marrow, semen, breath and vitality, these four are derived from Śiva. Thus this body consists of nine substances derived from nine origins. The tenth substance alone is called Parā Śakti."

That is a different scheme from the seven dhātus the yoginī-sets used at 509, 516, 524 and 531, where each constituent belonged to one yoginī in order. Here nine are parcelled between the two, and Parāśakti is what is left over — named by subtraction rather than by position.

The Liṅga Purāṇa then generalises it: "whatever energy is attributed to any substance, that is Devī, the ruler of all; the energised substance is the great Śiva. Those substances which possess energy are the manifestations of Śiva. The wise recognise the energies in substance to be Devī." So the division is not of parts but of aspects — substance is Śiva, and the power in it is She. Śvetāśvatara 6.8 is cited: "his supreme Śakti is known in different forms." And the Paramantra is also called Parāśakti.

573. परानिष्ठा → परा-निष्ठा

परा = supreme, highest
निष्ठा = firm standing, fixity, completion; hence the final end, the goal (नि + स्था "to stand")
"The Supreme End."

Vigraha: परा निष्ठा।

निष्ठा is नि + स्था with the retroflexion, so the word is literally a standing-down, a coming to rest — the same root that has run through the seat-namas and that gives प्रतिष्ठा at 829. There it was what all things stand on; here it is where they come to a stop.

Bhāskararāya makes it a kind of knowledge, "the goal of all desires and all worlds," on Gītā 4.33: "O Pārtha, all kinds of actions end in knowledge." The Sūta Saṃhitā (Sūta Gītā 5.50–54) then describes that knowledge in a sequence of four stages, and the last is the interesting one. Convinced by scripture, teachers and reasoning that he is the witness of all; knowing the whole that appears other than Self as his own Self; convinced by his own experience that he is the pure non-dual Brahman; merging that conviction in his own unchangeable consciousness — and then, "knowing that even that merging is of the nature of thought, he should remain as the absolute." The final move is to see that the merging too is only cit and to stop there. "This is the highest end of scriptural teachings and of experience."

574. प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी → प्र-ज्ञान-घन-रूपिणी

प्र = forth, superior — here "different from," per the commentary
ज्ञान = knowledge (from ज्ञा "to know")
घन = dense, compact, concentrated; a mass
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is concentrated knowledge."

Vigraha: प्रज्ञानघनं रूपं यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya glosses each member: प्र is superior, that is, different from the mental modifications; ज्ञान the eternal wisdom; घन concentrated, that is, not contaminated by avidyā. So the compound denies both that this knowledge is a mental state and that it is mixed with ignorance.

The citation is Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.5.13, and the simile is exact: "just as the taste of a quantity of salt is neither inside nor outside but everywhere, so, O wife, this Self is neither within nor without, but is full and concentrated knowledge." घन does the work — a lump of salt is salt through and through, with no part of it not salt.

575. माध्वीपानालसा → माध्वी-पान-अलसा

माध्वी = made of honey — mead, wine (from मधु "honey")
पान = drinking (from पा "to drink")
अलसा = languid, indolent, without stir (अ + लस् "to be lively")
"She who is languid with the drinking of wine."

Vigraha: माध्वीपानेन अलसा।

Sandhi: पान + अलसा → पानालसा (आ by 6.1.101). index.html's body is a single restatement of the gloss.

अलस is the privative of लस् "to be lively," so the word is not sleepiness but the absence of stir — stillness after drinking rather than stupor. माध्वी is from मधु, honey, and the ritual mead had stood behind वीर at 836 and 898, and behind the Rudrayāmala's line at 918 that wisdom is better than mead.

576. मत्ता → मत्ता

मत्ता = intoxicated, exhilarated (past participle of मद् "to be exhilarated")
"The Intoxicated."

Vigraha: मत्ता मदयुक्ता।

The plain sense continues 575, but Bhāskararāya's alternative pulls the nama in a quite different direction: मत्त is the state of egoism, "the Parāhantā of Parā Śiva" — supreme I-ness.

That is the term used at 854 गम्भीरा, where meditation on the Mahāhrada was said to yield पूर्णाहन्ता, complete I-ness, and at 856 गर्विता, where Her pride was located as "supreme egoism concerning the creation of the universe." So three namas in the text name the same thing — the creator's I-ness — once as a meditation's fruit, once as pride, and here as intoxication.

577. मातृकावर्णरूपिणी → मातृका-वर्ण-रूपिणी

मातृका = the mother-letters, the alphabet as a set of deities (from मातृ "mother")
वर्ण = a letter; and also a colour — both senses are used
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is the mātṛkā letters."

Vigraha: मातृकावर्णाः रूपं यस्याः सा।

This is the longest commentary in the verse and the most consequential nama in it, because वर्ण is taken in both senses at once and the two are made to agree.

As colour, Bhāskararāya gives the Sanatkumāra Saṃhitā's scheme letter by letter: the sixteen vowels from अ are smoke-coloured; क to ड (thirteen) red; ध to फ (nine) yellowish; the five from ब crimson; the five from स gold-coloured; ह and क्ष the colour of lightning. He then reports that some Tantras differ — vowels crystal, क to म coral, य to ह yellowish, क्ष crimson — and that some say all the letters are white, while the Mātṛkāviveka assigns a distinct colour to each, beginning "अ is all divinity, red, controlling all things."

As letters simply: the fifty-one from अ to क्ष are Her form. And the Sūta Saṃhitā (IV.4.21–22) divides them as the text divides Her: "just as the Supreme Śiva is twofold as Śakti and Śiva, so this Mātṛkā Devī herself shines in two. The vowels indicate one form of Śakti, the consonants that of Śiva." So the alphabet is itself the Śiva–Śakti pair, vowels and consonants — which is the same claim 999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी makes of Her outright.

Then अक्षमाला, the garland of letters: the Jñānārṇava — "अ is the first, O Devī, and क्ष is the last, thus she is called Akṣamālā. She is the Brahman-Word itself, but in reality she transcends the Word." The last clause is worth keeping beside 962 सर्वातीता, where Bhāskararāya narrowed "transcending all" to transcending all words.

Two further readings. रूप taken as "creates," so She creates the letters — for which he refers to the Saubhāgyasudhodaya on their origin through the Icchāśakti of Śiva in his Anuttara aspect. Or the letters as belonging to the Śrīcakra, on the Mātṛkāviveka's sixth chapter, with the Sanandana Saṃhitā: "meditation on the letters and on the Śrīcakra as one is called Kailāsa Prastāra."

Sastry's footnotes add two things worth having. There are three Prastāras — Meru, Kailāsa and Bhū — identifying the Śrīcakra respectively with the sixteen Nityās, the fifty-one mātṛkās, and the eight Vāsinīs. And the Varivasyārahasya derives मातृका syllabically: म limits or measures, त्रि crosses, क shines — "one who knows the Mātṛkā letters knows Brahman, crosses saṃsāra, and shines."

The letters have been Her form three times now on three counts: fifty-one as pīṭhas at 833, sixty-four as varṇas at 850, fifty-one as mātṛkās here — and at 529 सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता both senses of वर्ण were in play as they are here.

Note on the verse. Six namas in two triads. 572–574 are metaphysical and each is defined by exclusion: Parāśakti is the tenth substance, what the other nine are not; Parāniṣṭhā is where action stops; and प्रज्ञानघन is knowledge that is neither a mental modification nor mixed with ignorance.

575–577 turn to the body and then past it. Wine, intoxication, and the alphabet — and the turn happens inside 576, where the plain reading is drunkenness and the alternative is the I-ness of Parāśiva. The two readings are not reconciled, and the verse simply moves on to the letters.

577 is the verse's weight. वर्ण means letter and colour together, and the commentary refuses to choose: it gives the letters their colours letter by letter, notes that the schemes disagree, and then reads the alphabet as the Śiva–Śakti pair in the form of vowels and consonants. Held with the Jñānārṇava's line that She "is the Brahman-Word itself, but in reality transcends the Word," the nama says both that She is the alphabet and that no alphabet reaches Her.

---

## महाकैलासनिलया मृणालमृदुदोर्लता । महनीया दयामूर्तिः महासाम्राज्यशालिनी

*mahākailāsanilayā mṛṇālamṛdudorlatā । mahanīyā dayāmūrtiḥ mahāsāmrājyaśālinī*

Verse 117, namas 578–582.

578. महाकैलासनिलया → महा-कैलास-निलया

महा = great
कैलास = Kailāsa — Śiva's mountain; and here Mahākailāsa, a place beyond it
निलया = abode, dwelling (नि + ली "to settle")
"She whose abode is the great Kailāsa."

Vigraha: महाकैलासः निलयः यस्याः सा।

Mahākailāsa is "a place much beyond the present Kailāsa mountain, known in the Śiva and other Purāṇas as the abiding place of Paramaśiva." That is exactly where 960 लोकातीता placed Her — beyond the lokas from Indra's to Viṣṇu's, in Paraśiva's city Mahākailāsa, above which the Śivadharmottara set three supreme seats. The two namas name one place, once by transcendence and once by residence.

Two further readings. महाकैलास as the Kailāsa Prastāra of the Śrīcakra — the identification of cakra with the fifty-one mātṛkās, which the nama immediately preceding this verse had just described. Or कैलास as the sahasrāra in the brahmarandhra: the Tripurasāra — "this is called Kailāsa, the Kula, and the seat of Akula, where the lord of the lords in the form of bindu resides."

And महत् is given a reason: it is great "because Vāsinī and the Nityā deities, which belong to the other Prastāras, have no place in this one." Greatness by exclusion.

निलया for the third time in the text's six — 99, 521, and here, before 839, 873, 895 and 996.

579. मृणालमृदुदोर्लता → मृणाल-मृदु-दोः-लता

मृणाल = the lotus stalk, the fibrous stem
मृदु = soft, tender, yielding
दोः = arm (दोस्)
लता = a creeper, a slender vine
"She whose creeper-like arms are soft as the lotus stem."

Vigraha: मृणालमृदुः दोर्लता यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The two figures in the compound are both of slenderness — the lotus stalk and the creeper — and both have stood in the text before. मृणाल is what 111 बिसतन्तुतनीयसी measured Her against, where She was finer than a fibre drawn from that stalk; लता is what 107 तटिल्लतासमरुचिः used for the branching filament of a lightning-flash. There the two figures bracketed the kuṇḍalinī; here they describe an arm.

580. महनीया → महनीया

महनीया = to be honoured, worthy of reverence (from मह् "to magnify, to honour," with the gerundive अनीय)
"The Illustrious."

Vigraha: महनीया पूजनीया।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The form is a gerundive in अनीय — "to be honoured" rather than "honoured" — so the nama states a claim on the worshipper rather than a fact about Her. मह् is the root behind मह at 109 महासक्तिः, where मह was the festival, and behind महा- throughout.

581. दयामूर्तिः → दया-मूर्तिः

दया = compassion, pity (from दय् "to sympathise")
मूर्तिः = form, embodiment
"She who is compassion embodied."

Vigraha: दया मूर्तिः यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The nama is 992 अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः without its qualifier — करुणा there for दया here, and मूर्ति in both. There the compassion was अव्याज, needing no pretext; here it is stated bare. And मूर्ति had been भद्रमूर्तिः at 116, where what Her form embodied was the auspicious. Three namas built alike, on three abstractions.

582. महासाम्राज्यशालिनी → महा-साम्राज्य-शालिनी

महा = great
साम्राज्य = universal sovereignty, empire (vṛddhi derivative of सम्राज्, "emperor")
शालिनी = possessing, endowed with, resplendent with (from शाल्)
"She who is resplendent with great sovereignty."

Vigraha: महासाम्राज्येन शालिनी।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

साम्राज्य is built on सम्राज्, the emperor — सम् with राज्, one who rules wholly — so the word is not kingship but universal kingship, and महा doubles it.

Note on the verse. Five namas, four of them without commentary. That is unusual, and it makes the verse read as a plain sequence: Her abode, Her arms, Her worthiness, Her compassion, Her sovereignty.

578 carries all the weight. Mahākailāsa is where 960 लोकातीता had placed Her beyond the worlds, and the alternative readings collapse the geography into the body and into the diagram — the sahasrāra, and the Kailāsa Prastāra where letters and Śrīcakra are meditated as one. The place beyond all places is also a spot in the skull and a way of laying out a figure.

579 is the only physical nama, and its two images — lotus stalk and creeper — are the two that 111 and 107 had used for the kuṇḍalinī. Applied to an arm they are ornament; applied there they were doctrine.

---

## आत्मविद्या महाविद्या श्रीविद्या कामसेविता । श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या त्रिकूटा कामकोटिका

*ātmavidyā mahāvidyā śrīvidyā kāmasevitā । śrīṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā trikūṭā kāmakoṭikā*

Verse 118, namas 583–589.

583. आत्मविद्या → आत्म-विद्या

आत्म = self (आत्मन्)
विद्या = knowledge, science; a mantra of a female deity
"The knowledge of the Self."

Vigraha: आत्मनः विद्या।

Bhāskararāya's whole note is one clause, and it is technical rather than philosophical: "Ātmavidyā may mean the eight-syllabled Mantra." So the nama names a particular mantra, not the science of the Self in general — and that sets the pattern for the three vidyā-namas that open this verse, each of which he identifies with a specific formula.

विद्या had stood alone at 549, where it was knowledge that confers salvation, and also the third of the five kalās.

584. महाविद्या → महा-विद्या

महा = great
विद्या = knowledge, science; a mantra
"The Great Science."

Vigraha: महती विद्या।

Two glosses, both brief. "Because it removes all sorrows" — the greatness lying in the effect. And: "Mahāvidyā, the Vanadurgā Mantra." Again a named formula.

585. श्रीविद्या → श्री-विद्या

श्री = splendour, auspiciousness, prosperity
विद्या = knowledge, science; a mantra
"The Auspicious Science."

Vigraha: श्रीमती विद्या।

"Or, the Pañcadaśī Mantra" — the fifteen-syllabled vidyā that the whole text is built around, whose three kūṭas were mapped onto Her body at 85–87.

The Viṣṇu Purāṇa is then quoted for the set: "O fair one, the sacrificial science, exalted science, secret science, and spiritual science, O Devī, thou art all these, the bestower of salvation; also thou art Logic, Trayī, Vārtā, trade and justice." And the commentators gloss the first four as the science of action, devotion to deities, the science of mantras, and the science of Brahman; Vārtā as architecture, medicine and the like.

Trayī in that list is nama 872, where the three Vedas were derived by performing sandhi on their opening letters.

586. कामसेविता → काम-सेविता

काम = desire; Kāma the god of love; and per the commentary, Mahākāma, that is Paramaśiva
सेविता = served, attended, worshipped (from सेव् "to serve")
"She who is worshipped by Kāma."

Vigraha: कामेन सेविता।

Bhāskararāya's first gloss is that काम is Mahākāma. He also notes here, apparently in passing, that "the lower six cakras from Ājñā to Mūlādhāra are called Kula" — which bears on the seven namas at 90–96 and on 897 कुलरूपिणी.

Then the substantial reading, and the passage is the strangest in this stretch. काम is the bodiless one, the god of love without a body — and the Aruṇa Upaniṣad is quoted on him: "the bodiless son of Lakṣmī, though without mind, has animation. He knew that jewel. He, though without fingers, worshipped. Though without neck, he adorned himself. Though without tongue, he tasted it." Bhāskararāya unpacks every clause: without eyes he saw the jewel, which is Śrīvidyā; having seen it without eyes he touched it without fingers, wore the necklace without a neck, tasted without tongue — and by that he is the Ṛṣi, the seer of the mantra.

The application is ritual and precise. "Without knowing that Ṛṣi one should enter the city" — the external cakra can be entered only by knowledge of him; the internal cakra needs no ceremonial worship, so there the Ṛṣi need not be known. And "when one enters, he should enter after performing secret rites; this is the vow of Manmatha" — the secret rites being "the knowledge of the essential equality of Śiva with Devī." The conclusion is stated flatly: worship performed without that knowledge cannot be fully effective.

Kāma's bodilessness is what 84 हरनेत्राग्निसंदग्धकामसंजीवनौषधिः had accounted for — Kāma burnt to ash by the fire of Hara's eye, and She the herb that restores him. Here the burnt god, still without a body, is the mantra's seer.

587. श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या → श्री-षोडश-अक्षरी-विद्या

श्री = auspicious; and, per the second reading, the sixteenth syllable itself
षोडश = sixteen
अक्षरी = syllabled (अक्षर "syllable, imperishable")
विद्या = mantra, science
"The auspicious sixteen-syllabled Vidyā."

Vigraha: श्रीमती षोडशाक्षरी विद्या।

Sandhi: षोडश + अक्षरी → षोडशाक्षरी (आ by 6.1.101).

Bhāskararāya has an arithmetical difficulty to meet. The Gauḍapāda Sūtra (67) says "this Mantra consists of twenty-eight syllables," which does not agree with sixteen — and he resolves it by dividing the fifteen-syllabled mantra into three parts and adding syllables between the divisions. Or, more simply, षोडशाक्षरी means a vidyā in which the sixteenth syllable, श्री, is used: the Pañcadaśī with one syllable added, which is the ordinary account of the Ṣoḍaśī.

अक्षर is literally the imperishable, so a syllable is named by what cannot be worn away — apt for a mantra counted by them.

588. त्रिकूटा → त्रि-कूटा

त्रि = three
कूटा = peak, segment, cluster — a kūṭa of the mantra
"The Three-peaked."

Vigraha: त्रीणि कूटानि यस्याः सा।

Bhāskararāya lists what the three may be: Brahmā and the rest; the three states, waking and the others; the three seats, Jālandhara and the others; the three worlds; the three qualities. "Or Trikūṭa means Vāgbhava and the other kūṭas."

That last is the reading the verse wants, since 587 has just named the Ṣoḍaśī and 585 the Pañcadaśī. The three kūṭas — Vāgbhava, Kāmarāja, Śakti — were mapped onto Her body at 85–87, named as her frame at 89 मूलकूटत्रयकलेबरा, given as one reading of कूटस्था at 896, and made the object of Her rule at 983 त्रिखण्डेशी. Here they are simply Her.

589. कामकोटिका → काम-कोटिका

काम = desire; and per the commentary, Paramaśiva
कोटिका = a point, a tip, an edge; also a crore (कोटि with the diminutive क)
"Kāmakoṭikā."

Vigraha: कामस्य कोटिका।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is one sentence and it does two things: "Kāma is Paramaśiva, because the essential equality of Śiva with Devī is Brahman itself." So काम here is not the god but Śiva, and the reason given is the same doctrine the Aruṇa Upaniṣad passage at 586 called the secret rite — the essential equality of the two.

काम thus stands twice in this verse with two referents, at 586 as the bodiless god and at 589 as Paramaśiva, and Bhāskararāya moves between them without remark.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and four of them name mantras. आत्मविद्या is the eight-syllabled; महाविद्या the Vanadurgā; श्रीविद्या the Pañcadaśī; श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या the Ṣoḍaśī; and त्रिकूटा the three segments of the Pañcadaśī. The verse is a catalogue of formulae with Her name attached to each.

586 interrupts it, and the interruption is where the doctrine sits. The Aruṇa Upaniṣad's bodiless Kāma — who saw the jewel without eyes, touched it without fingers, tasted it without a tongue — is made the Ṛṣi of the vidyā, and the passage ends in a ritual rule: the external cakra requires knowing that seer, the internal does not, and no worship at all is effective without "the knowledge of the essential equality of Śiva with Devī." That last phrase is then reused four namas later as the reason for reading काम as Paramaśiva.

And the burnt Kāma of 84 is the same figure. There She was the herb reviving him; here he is still bodiless and has become the seer of Her mantra.

---

## कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता । शिरःस्थिता चन्द्रनिभा भालस्थेन्द्रधनुःप्रभा

*kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtakamalākoṭisevitā । śiraḥsthitā candranibhā bhālasthendradhanuḥprabhā*

Verse 119, namas 590–594.

590. कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता → कटाक्ष-किङ्करी-भूत-कमला-कोटि-सेविता

कटाक्ष = a side-glance, a look from the corner of the eye (कट "corner" + अक्ष "eye")
किङ्करी = a female servant, a handmaid (from किं करोमि, "what shall I do?" — the servant's question)
भूत = become (past participle of भू "to be")
कमला = Lakṣmī, the lotus-goddess
कोटि = a crore, ten million
सेविता = served, attended (from सेव् "to serve")
"She who is attended by crores of Lakṣmīs made her handmaids by a glance."

Vigraha: कटाक्षेण किङ्करीभूताभिः कमलाकोटिभिः सेविता।

किङ्करी is worth its etymology: the servant is named from the question "किं करोमि," what shall I do — so a किङ्करी is one who stands waiting to be told. And what makes crores of Lakṣmīs into such servants is a कटाक्ष, a look from the corner of the eye, not a command.

591. शिरःस्थिता → शिरः-स्थिता

शिरः = the head (शिरस्)
स्थिता = abiding, seated
"She who abides in the head."

Vigraha: शिरसि स्थिता।

Bhāskararāya's gloss is brief and technical: शिरस् means the brahmarandhra, "wherein she resides assuming the form of the Guru."

This nama opens a nyāsa — a sequence placing Her at points of the body — which runs to 597 and is the most systematic thing in these five verses. Head, forehead, heart, triangle: and at each station what is placed there is named.

592. चन्द्रनिभा → चन्द्र-निभा

चन्द्र = the moon
निभा = resembling, like (नि + भा "to shine" — shining like)
"She who is like the moon."

Vigraha: चन्द्रः इव निभा।

Bhāskararāya makes this an item of the nyāsa rather than a simile: "there is a moon in the lower part of the brahmarandhra, that is the third division of the Vidyā." So the moon in the head is the third kūṭa of the Pañcadaśī, the Śakti-kūṭa — and the sequence that follows will place the second kūṭa in the heart at 596.

The three kūṭas were mapped onto Her body once already, at 85–87 — Vāgbhava as the face, Kāmarāja from throat to waist, Śakti below. That was a mapping onto Her form; this is a mapping into the worshipper's body, and the order is reversed, third in the head and second in the heart.

593. भालस्था → भाल-स्था

भाल = the forehead, the brow
स्था = abiding, seated
"She who abides in the forehead."

Vigraha: भाले स्थिता।

"She resides in the forehead in the form of the Bindu of the syllable Hrīṃ." So the second station of the nyāsa holds not a luminary but a mark — the anusvāra-dot of the bīja.

594. इन्द्रधनुःप्रभा → इन्द्र-धनुः-प्रभा

इन्द्र = Indra; इन्द्रधनुः = Indra's bow, the rainbow
धनुः = a bow (धनुस्)
प्रभा = radiance, splendour (प्र + भा "to shine")
"She whose radiance is the rainbow."

Vigraha: इन्द्रधनुषः प्रभा इव प्रभा यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: भालस्था + इन्द्रधनुःप्रभा → भालस्थेन्द्रधनुःप्रभा (आ + इ → ए by guṇa, Pāṇini 6.1.87 आद्गुणः).

The Nityāhṛdaya — that is Yoginīhṛdaya I.28 — supplies the placement, and it is quantitative: "the Ardhamātra, the dot or bindu of Om or Hrīṃ, is in the forehead in the form of light; above that there is the Ardhacandra in the same form, and it is a quarter of that." Sastry's note gives the arithmetic: a mātrā is 256 lavas, an ardhamātrā 128, an ardhacandra 64. So above the bindu of 593 sits the half-moon, at a quarter of the measure, and the rainbow is its light.

Note on the verse. Five namas: one of attendance and four that are a nyāsa.

The nyāsa is the point. 591 places Her in the brahmarandhra as the Guru; 592 finds a moon there and identifies it with the third kūṭa of the Pañcadaśī; 593 places Her in the forehead as the bindu of Hrīṃ; 594 sets the half-moon above that bindu, at a quarter of its measure, and calls its light the rainbow. The next verse continues: heart, sun, second kūṭa, and then the triangle.

Read with 85–87 the design is clear. There the three kūṭas of the mantra were laid on Her body — face, torso, below the waist. Here they are laid into the body of the worshipper, and the sequence descends from the crown. The mantra is mapped twice, once onto Her and once into whoever recites it.

Textual note. This is the worst-divided verse in the text, and the fault runs through four of its five namas.

590's dev reads कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता शिरः — it has absorbed the शिरः belonging to the next nama, and carries 589's gloss and a duplicate of 589's body besides. 591's dev is therefore only स्थिता, its शिरः having gone forward into 590; its gloss is 590's, and its body holds its own heading, "Residing in the head."

Then the same thing happens again at the next joint. 593's dev reads भालस्थें, which is neither भालस्था nor भालस्थे — it has taken the ए produced by the sandhi with the following nama and added a stray anusvāra, while losing its own final आ. And 594's dev reads न्द्रधनुः प्रभा, having lost the initial इ of इन्द्र to that same guṇa, with a spurious space besides.

So both word-boundaries in this verse have been drawn inside a nama rather than between two. Elsewhere the text loses a visarga or gains a र्; here the division has been made in the middle of शिरःस्थिता and again in the middle of इन्द्रधनुःप्रभा. All four dev fields are recoverable, because each nama's own gloss survives — 590's under 591, 591's under its body, 593's and 594's in place.

---

## हृदयस्था रविप्रख्या त्रिकोणान्तरदीपिका । दाक्षायणी दैत्यहन्त्री दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी

*hṛdayasthā raviprakhyā trikoṇāntaradīpikā । dākṣāyaṇī daityahantrī dakṣayajñavināśinī*

Verse 120, namas 595–600.

595. हृदयस्था → हृदय-स्था

हृदय = the heart; and per the commentary, the Parābīja, an Upaniṣad, and the seed of the universe
स्था = abiding, seated
"She who abides in the heart."

Vigraha: हृदये स्थिता।

The plain reason first: "because she is to be contemplated as in the heart." This is the third station of the nyāsa begun at 591.

Then three technical senses of हृदय. It is the Parābīja — the Kalpa Sūtra, "he who knows the heart of the Lord finds happiness at every step," where heart means that bīja. Or it is an Upaniṣad, the Parameśvarahṛdaya. Or it is the seed of the universe, and the Anuttaratriṃśikāśāstra gives the figure: "just as a great banyan tree is contained potentially in a tiny seed, so the animate and inanimate universe resides as a seed in the heart."

Bhāskararāya drops a counting marker here: the twenty-third verse divides thirty-five names.

596. रविप्रख्या → रवि-प्रख्या

रवि = the sun
प्रख्या = resembling, having the appearance of; literally well-known (प्र + ख्या "to make known")
"She who resembles the sun."

Vigraha: रविः इव प्रख्या।

Another item of the nyāsa: "in the heart there is a solar disc, that is the second division of the Mantra." So the sun in the heart is the Kāmarāja kūṭa, the middle segment of the Pañcadaśī — where 592 found the moon in the head and made it the third.

प्रख्या is the word of 964 बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या, where the likeness was to a red blossom; and प्र + ख्या is the same formation as सङ्ख्या at 950.

597. त्रिकोणान्तरदीपिका → त्रि-कोण-अन्तर-दीपिका

त्रि = three
कोण = a corner, an angle — त्रिकोण, the downward triangle
अन्तर = within, the interior
दीपिका = a lamp, that which illumines (दीप् "to shine," in the causative)
"She who is the lamp within the triangle."

Vigraha: त्रिकोणस्य अन्तः दीपिका।

Sandhi: कोण + अन्तर → कोणान्तर (आ by 6.1.101).

This completes the nyāsa: head, forehead, heart, and now the triangle, where what is placed is a light. The commentary here is not a gloss but a deferral — Bhāskararāya quotes the opening and closing of a passage, "the Supreme Energy is called Tripurā" through to "hence she is called Tripurā," and says he will explain it in more detail in its own commentary.

The triangle is the one 895 योनिनिलया named, where She dwells in it as the Bindu; 982 made the योनि the veil covering that Bindu, and 986 त्रिकोणगा had Her going to it. And दीपिका is the word of 993 अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका, the lamp dispelling the darkness of ignorance — there a lamp against something, here a lamp within something.

598. दाक्षायणी → दाक्षायणी

दाक्षायणी = the daughter of Dakṣa — Satī (vṛddhi patronymic of दक्ष)
"Dākṣāyaṇī — Dakṣa's daughter."

Vigraha: दक्षस्य अपत्यं दाक्षायणी।

index.html carries 597's gloss and a duplicate of 597's body on this nama, so no commentary proper to it survives.

The patronymic is the same formation as कात्यायनी at 556, the daughter of Kātya. And दक्ष means "able, skilful," the word that stood in both halves of 923 दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या — so Her father's name is the adjective that nama turned on.

599. दैत्यहन्त्री → दैत्य-हन्त्री

दैत्य = a Daitya, a demon — son of Diti (vṛddhi derivative of दिति)
हन्त्री = she who slays (हन् "to strike" with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्)
"The Slayer of the Daityas."

Vigraha: दैत्यान् हन्तीति दैत्यहन्त्री।

index.html carries 597's gloss and body here too.

हन्त्री is the form of 557 कालहन्त्री, where what was slain was Time itself, and the root is the हन् behind घ्नी at 842 भवरोगघ्नी. Slayer of demons, of the disease of existence, and of time — three objects for one root.

600. दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी → दक्ष-यज्ञ-विनाशिनी

दक्ष = Dakṣa
यज्ञ = sacrifice
विनाशिनी = she who destroys utterly (वि + नश् "to perish," in the causative)
"The Destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice."

Vigraha: दक्षयज्ञं विनाशयतीति।

index.html carries 597's gloss and body here as well.

The nama refers to the sacrifice from which Satī was excluded and which was wrecked in consequence. What makes the placement pointed is 598: two namas apart, She is Dakṣa's daughter and the destroyer of Dakṣa's rite. The text sets the relation and its rupture side by side and says nothing about either.

विनाशिनी is the fuller form of नाशिनी at 555 कलिकल्मषनाशिनी, where the defilement of the Kali age was destroyed. And यज्ञ had been loved, performed and patronised by Her at 881–883, and loved again in its fivefold form at 946 — so this is the one sacrifice in the text that She destroys.

Note on the verse. Six namas: three completing the nyāsa, three on दक्ष and its demons.

595–597 finish what 591 began. The stations are head, forehead, heart, triangle; and what is set at each is a moon, a bindu, a sun, a lamp. Two of the four are identified with kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī — the third in the head at 592, the second in the heart at 596 — so the mantra is being laid into the body from the crown downward. Read against 85–87, where the same three kūṭas were laid on Her body, the design is a double mapping: the mantra onto Her, and the mantra into the worshipper.

598 and 600 make the sharpest pair in these five verses, and the text leaves it unremarked. She is the daughter of Dakṣa and the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, two namas apart, with 599 slaying demons between them.

Textual note. Four consecutive namas — 597, 598, 599 and 600 — carry one gloss and one body between them, all four holding 597's. That is worse than the three-way duplication at 997–999 and the worst instance in the text. The commentary proper to 598, 599 and 600 is not preserved anywhere, and only their glosses are lost too, since all four carry 597's; the namas themselves are sound and their sense is not in doubt.


---

> **Note on verses 121–125.** Namas 597–626 form a single block-duplication run in index.html: all thirty carry nama 597's gloss and body. No commentary proper to namas 601–626 survives anywhere in the file, so the entries below for those namas give the philology — split, sandhi, derivation, vigraha, sense — and cross-references within the Sahasranāma, but report no Bhāskararāya, because there is none to report. Commentary resumes at 627. For scale: this is a thirty-nama run, and the next longest anywhere in the text is three.

## दरान्दोलितदीर्घाक्षी दरहासोज्ज्वलन्मुखी । गुरुमूर्तिर्गुणनिधिर्गोमाता गुहजन्मभूः

*darāndolitadīrghākṣī darahāsojjvalanmukhī । gurumūrtir guṇanidhir gomātā guhajanmabhūḥ*

Verse 121, namas 601–606.

601. दरान्दोलितदीर्घाक्षी → दर-आन्दोलित-दीर्घ-अक्षी

दर = a little, slightly
आन्दोलित = swung, set gently rocking (आ + दुल् "to swing," causative)
दीर्घ = long
अक्षी = eyed (अक्षि with the feminine)
"She whose long eyes are faintly moving."

Vigraha: दरान्दोलिते दीर्घे अक्षिणी यस्याः सा।

Sandhi at two joints: दर + आन्दोलित → दरान्दोलित, and दीर्घ + अक्षी → दीर्घाक्षी (आ by 6.1.101 both times).

दर in the sense of "slightly" is the word of 924 दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा, where the smile was faint — and the two namas are built alike, दर qualifying a movement of the face. There Bhāskararāya turned दर to its other senses, conch and fear; here no commentary survives to say whether he did the same.

आन्दोलित is a causative participle: not eyes that move but eyes that have been set moving, which is a more exact observation than "restless." This is the fourth अक्षि-nama in a hundred, after 558, 561 and 571's साक्षिणी.

602. दरहासोज्ज्वलन्मुखी → दर-हास-उज्ज्वलत्-मुखी

दर = a little, slightly
हास = a smile, laughter (from हस् "to laugh")
उज्ज्वलत् = blazing up, shining out (present participle of उत् + ज्वल् "to blaze")
मुखी = faced (मुख with the feminine)
"She whose face is lit up by a faint smile."

Vigraha: दरहासेन उज्ज्वलत् मुखं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: हास + उज्ज्वलत् → हासोज्ज्वलत् (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, 6.1.87).

The pairing with 601 is deliberate — eyes then mouth, and दर governing both. And the tension inside this compound is the point: a faint smile and a blazing face, the smallest cause with the largest effect. उज्ज्वल् is the strong word, ज्वल् "to blaze" with उत्, so the face flares.

603. गुरुमूर्तिः → गुरु-मूर्तिः

गुरु = heavy, weighty; hence venerable, a teacher
मूर्तिः = form, embodiment
"She whose form is the Guru."

Vigraha: गुरुः मूर्तिः यस्याः सा।

The dev field reads गुरुमूर्ति, the visarga lost. In the verse गुरुमूर्तिः + गुणनिधिः gives गुरुमूर्तिर्गुणनिधिः, the visarga becoming र् before the voiced ग् — but 604 has not gained that र्, so the letter is simply dropped, as at 539 श्रुतिः and 567 भक्तनिधिः rather than mis-divided as at 537–538.

गुरु is literally the heavy — weight, and so gravity, and so authority. The identification is not new: at 591 शिरःस्थिता Bhāskararāya said She resides in the brahmarandhra "assuming the form of the Guru," which is this nama stated as a location twelve namas earlier.

मूर्ति for the fourth time — 116 भद्रमूर्तिः, 581 दयामूर्तिः, 992 अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः, and here. The auspicious, compassion, unmotivated compassion, and the teacher.

604. गुणनिधिः → गुण-निधिः

गुण = a quality, a virtue; and literally a strand
निधिः = a treasure, a store (नि + धा "to place down")
"She who is a treasure-house of virtues."

Vigraha: गुणानां निधिः।

The dev field reads गुणनिधि, the visarga lost in the same way as 603's.

गुण here is virtue, not the strand of Prakṛti's rope that 961 गुणातीता transcended and 984 त्रिगुणा was made of — the same word doing quite different work a few hundred namas apart. निधि is the word of 567 भक्तनिधिः, where She was Her devotees' treasure and Bhāskararāya glossed it "that which fulfils desire"; here what is stored is qualities.

The Paribhāṣā verse at nama 1000 lists गुणनिधि among the four namas that are masculine in gender — so the nominative is गुणनिधिः and not *गुणनिधी.

605. गोमाता → गो-माता

गो = a cow; also the earth; also speech, and a ray of light
माता = mother
"The Mother of cows."

Vigraha: गवां माता।

गो is one of the widest words in Sanskrit — cow, earth, speech, ray — so the compound can be read as mother of cattle, of the earth, of speech, or of light, and nothing in the surviving text chooses. With 640 वागधीश्वरी nineteen namas on, ruler of speech, the third of those is not idle.

The cow-sense makes this the Surabhi identification; the earth-sense would set it beside 955 धरा.

606. गुहजन्मभूः → गुह-जन्म-भूः

गुह = Guha, Skanda — literally the one in the cave (from गुह् "to hide")
जन्म = birth
भूः = ground, place of origin; that in which a thing comes to be (from भू "to be")
"She who is the birthplace of Guha."

Vigraha: गुहस्य जन्मभूः।

गुह is Skanda named for concealment, from गुह् "to hide" — the cave-born. And जन्मभू is not "mother" but "birth-ground," which keeps the compound spatial: not she who bore him but the place his birth happened.

Skanda has stood in the text already: at 535 स्वाहा he is Svāhā's son, "the divine six-faced one," where Svāhā is Śiva's wife in his fire-form; and at 960 लोकातीता the three supreme seats above Mahākailāsa were "resorted to by Skanda, Umā and Śiva."

Note on the verse. Six namas: two of the face, then four on ग.

601 and 602 are a matched pair, दर qualifying eyes and then mouth, and both compounds set something faint against something large — eyes long but barely moving, a slight smile that lights the whole face.

The ग-group is a run of quite unlike things: the Guru's form, a hoard of virtues, the mother of cows, the ground of Skanda's birth. What holds them is the letter, and this is one of the places where the text's alliteration is plainly doing the organising work.

No commentary survives for any nama in this verse.

---

## देवेशी दण्डनीतिस्था दहराकाशरूपिणी । प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता

*deveśī daṇḍanītisthā daharākāśarūpiṇī । pratipanmukhyarākāntatithimaṇḍalapūjitā*

Verse 122, namas 607–610.

607. देवेशी → देव-ईशी

देव = a god (from दिव् "to shine")
ईशी = mistress, ruler (from ईश् "to rule")
"Sovereign of the gods."

Vigraha: देवानाम् ईशी।

Sandhi: देव + ईशी → देवेशी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

ईशी for the fourth time — 932 महेशी absolute, 949 पञ्चभूतेशी over the elements, 983 त्रिखण्डेशी over the mantra's divisions, and here over the gods. With ईश्वरी at 569, 831 and 945 the root ईश् has seven turns in the text, and each specifies a different domain.

608. दण्डनीतिस्था → दण्ड-नीति-स्था

दण्ड = a staff, a rod; hence punishment, chastisement
नीति = guidance, policy, statecraft (from नी "to lead")
स्था = abiding, established
"She who abides in the science of chastisement."

Vigraha: दण्डनीतौ स्थिता।

दण्डनीति is the technical name for the science of government — the rod and the leading, punishment as policy — one of the four vidyās in the classical reckoning. So the nama places Her in political science, and it is the only nama in the text that does.

The two members have each stood before. दण्ड in दण्डनाथा at 70, the rod-bearing commander-in-chief Vārāhī; and नी, the root of नीति, gave नायिका at 56, the leader. And the sense answers 568 नियन्त्री, where She was the guide of the universe and the guidance was a checking — यम्, to restrain. Here the restraint has a discipline attached to it.

609. दहराकाशरूपिणी → दहर-आकाश-रूपिणी

दहर = small, minute — the technical term for the tiny space within the heart
आकाश = ether, space
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is the ether within the heart."

Vigraha: दहराकाशः रूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: दहर + आकाश → दहराकाश (आ by 6.1.101).

दहराकाश is a fixed Upaniṣadic term, from the dahara-vidyā of Chāndogya 8.1 — the small space inside the lotus of the heart, which the text there says contains everything that the great space outside contains. So the compound is not "small ether" descriptively but a named locus of meditation.

This is the fourth word for ether in the text, after वियत् at 837, गगन at 855 and व्योम at 942 — and the only one that is interior. And it stands beside 595 हृदयस्था, where She was to be contemplated as in the heart and where हृदय was also given as the seed of the universe on the banyan-simile: "just as a great banyan is contained potentially in a tiny seed, so the animate and inanimate universe resides as a seed in the heart." That is the dahara doctrine in another figure.

610. प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता → प्रतिपत्-मुख्य-राका-अन्त-तिथि-मण्डल-पूजिता

प्रतिपत् = the first day of a lunar fortnight (प्रति + पद्)
मुख्य = chief, beginning with (from मुख "face")
राका = the full moon; the day of the full moon
अन्त = end
तिथि = a lunar day
मण्डल = a circle, a set, a whole round
पूजिता = worshipped (from पूज् "to honour")
"She who is worshipped in the whole round of lunar days, from the first to the full moon."

Vigraha: प्रतिपन्मुख्येन राकान्तेन तिथिमण्डलेन पूजिता।

Sandhi: प्रतिपत् + मुख्य → प्रतिपन्मुख्य, the त् assimilating in nasality before म् (Pāṇini 8.4.45, यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा) — the same rule that gives श्रीमन्नगर- at 56. And राका + अन्त → राकान्त (आ by 6.1.101).

The compound is a calendar: the fifteen tithis from pratipad to the full moon, taken as a मण्डल, a closed round. Those fifteen are the fifteen Nityā deities of the Śrīvidyā system, one to each lunar day — and the fifteen syllables of the Pañcadaśī, which 585 श्रीविद्या named. Nama 73 नित्यापराक्रमाटोपनिरीक्षणसमुत्सुका had Her eager to watch the Nityās' valour in the war; and the Meru Prastāra, named in Sastry's footnote at 577, is the identification of the Śrīcakra with those same sixteen Nityās.

So the nama says She is worshipped through a complete lunar cycle, and the cycle is also a mantra and also a diagram.

Note on the verse. Four namas, and they are unusually heterogeneous: sovereign of the gods, established in the science of punishment, the ether within the heart, worshipped through the lunar month.

608 is the outlier worth marking. दण्डनीति is statecraft, and no other nama in the text places Her in a secular science. It sits oddly between a divine sovereignty and a meditative locus — though 568 नियन्त्री had already made Her guidance a restraining rather than a leading.

609 and 610 are the two technical namas here, and they pull in opposite directions: the smallest interior space, and the largest closed cycle of time. Both are named loci of worship.

No commentary survives for any nama in this verse.

## कलात्मिका कलानाथा काव्यालापविनोदिनी । सचामररमावाणीसव्यदक्षिणसेविता

*kalātmikā kalānāthā kāvyālāpavinodinī । sacāmararamāvāṇīsavyadakṣiṇasevitā*

Verse 123, namas 611–614.

611. कलात्मिका → कला-आत्मिका

कला = a part, a portion; a digit of the moon; one of the sixty-four arts; and in Śaiva doctrine one of the five kalās
आत्मिका = having the nature of, being the very self of (आत्मन् + क, feminine आ)
"She whose nature is the kalās."

Vigraha: कला आत्मा यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: कला + आत्मिका → कलात्मिका (आ by 6.1.101).

कला is doing several jobs at once and the text has used most of them. As one of the five Śaiva kalās it stood at 853 शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका — which is this nama with शान्त्यतीत prefixed, so 611 is 853 stripped to its base — and प्रतिष्ठा, the second of those five, was a nama at 829, विद्या the third at 549, and the lower four Her śaktis at 929. As a digit of the moon it looks to the nama following. As one of the sixty-four arts it looks to 613.

आत्मिका also returns from 853 and, in its plain form, from 963 शमात्मिका.

612. कलानाथा → कला-नाथा

कला = a digit of the moon
नाथा = mistress, protectress (from नाथ् "to be master"); the feminine of नाथ, and कलानाथ is a standing name for the moon
"Mistress of the moon's digits."

Vigraha: कलानां नाथा।

कलानाथ — lord of the digits — is an ordinary Sanskrit word for the moon, so कलानाथा in the feminine can be read either as the moon's mistress or as the moon herself. The text has both readings available: 592 चन्द्रनिभा made Her like the moon and put a moon in the brahmarandhra, and 879 सुधासृतिः located the nectar in the moon at the sahasrāra's pericarp.

नाथा had stood at 70 as दण्डनाथा, Vārāhī the rod-mistress — and दण्ड- was in the nama three back at 608.

613. काव्यालापविनोदिनी → काव्य-आलाप-विनोदिनी

काव्य = poetry, a poem (from कवि "poet")
आलाप = conversation, discourse, recitation (आ + लप् "to speak")
विनोदिनी = she who takes delight; and also she who removes (वि + नुद् "to push away")
"She who delights in the discourse of poetry."

Vigraha: काव्यालापेन विनोदते इति।

Sandhi: काव्य + आलाप → काव्यालाप (आ by 6.1.101).

विनोदिनी is the word of 966 लीलाविनोदिनी, where the delight was in play and where वि + नुद् made diversion literally a pushing-aside. Here what she is diverted by is talk about poetry — आलाप being conversation rather than recitation proper.

This is the third nama of the text to name an art She enjoys, after 857 गानलोलुपा, avid for song, and 909 सामगानप्रिया, delighting in the Sāman's chant. Song twice and now poetry, and 611's कला in the sense of the sixty-four arts stands two namas back.

614. सचामररमावाणीसव्यदक्षिणसेविता → स-चामर-रमा-वाणी-सव्य-दक्षिण-सेविता

स = together with, having (सह in composition)
चामर = a chowrie, a yak-tail fly-whisk — the emblem of attendance on royalty
रमा = Ramā, Lakṣmī
वाणी = Vāṇī, Sarasvatī — speech
सव्य = left
दक्षिण = right
सेविता = attended, served (from सेव् "to serve")
"She who is attended on left and right by Ramā and Vāṇī bearing chowries."

Vigraha: चामरसहिताभ्यां रमावाणीभ्यां सव्यदक्षिणे सेविता।

The dev field reads साचामर- with a long आ, where the word is स-चामर-, the प्रादि compound स "having." No rule lengthens it, and the sense requires the short form: bearing chowries.

सव्य and दक्षिण are the pair that 912 सव्यापसव्यमार्गस्था turned into four cosmologies — the sun's three courses, the two roads of the dead, the Vāma and Dakṣiṇa rites, and the three nāḍīs — on the strength of सव्य meaning both left and right. Here they are simply two sides of a throne, and the nama is the plainest use of the pair in the text.

Lakṣmī had appeared at 590 कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता, where crores of her were made handmaids by a glance; here one of her holds a fly-whisk. And सेविता is the participle of 558 कमलाक्षनिषेविता and 636.

Note on the verse. Four namas, and the first three are about arts and measures — the kalās, the moon's digits, poetry. कला carries two of them and 611 is 853 with its qualifier removed.

614 then closes the verse with a court scene, and it is worth noticing what it does not do. सव्य and दक्षिण, the words that 912 made carry astronomy, eschatology and ritual polemic, are here just left and right; and Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī, who elsewhere in the text are ranks of attendants or aspects of Her, are two women holding whisks.

No commentary survives for any nama in this verse. 614's dev also carries a spurious लambda vowel: साचामर for सचामर.

## आदिशक्तिरमेयात्मा परमा पावनाकृतिः । अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डजननी दिव्यविग्रहा

*ādiśaktir ameyātmā paramā pāvanākṛtiḥ । anekakoṭibrahmāṇḍajananī divyavigrahā*

Verse 124, namas 615–621.

615. आदिशक्तिः → आदि-शक्तिः

आदि = beginning, first, primal
शक्तिः = power, energy
"The Primal Energy."

Vigraha: आदिः शक्तिः।

The dev field reads आदिशक्तिर, with a र where the visarga belongs. It comes from the sandhi with the following nama: आदिशक्तिः + अमेया gives आदिशक्तिरमेया, the visarga becoming र् before the vowel, and the division was taken after that र्. Same fault as 848–849, 894–895, 992–993 and 540–541.

शक्ति had stood at 572 पराशक्तिः, the supreme energy; here it is the first. And आदि is the word of 550 वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः, where the world was named through its first term.

616. अमेया → अ-मेया

अ = not (नञ्)
मेया = measurable, to be measured (मा "to measure" with the gerundive यत्)
"The Immeasurable."

Vigraha: मेया न भवति इति अमेया।

The dev field reads मेया, the initial अ lost to the preceding sandhi — so the nama as recorded says the opposite of what it means, "measurable." This is the same class of damage as 993 अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका, where the lost अ made the darkness belong to knowledge; and here as there the gloss preserves the reading, "unlimited."

मा "to measure" is the root of मान, the word Bhāskararāya listed without choosing at 931 मानवती and spent completely at 943 विमानस्था — where one division took वि + मा as "without limitation" and made Her either the unconditioned or its limiter. This nama says the same thing with a gerundive.

617. आत्मा → आत्मा

आत्मा = the Self (आत्मन्)
"The Self."

Vigraha: आत्मा एव सा।

The dev field reads त्मा, having lost the आ — which was absorbed in अमेया + आत्मा → अमेयात्मा (आ + आ → आ, 6.1.101). So both 616 and 617 have lost their initial vowel at the same seam, and 615 has gained a र् at the seam before it: three consecutive namas damaged by two joints.

आत्मन् is one of the four namas the Paribhāṣā verse at 1000 lists as masculine in gender, which is why the nominative is आत्मा and not a feminine form — the text names Her by a masculine noun and does not adjust it. आत्मिका, the derived feminine, stood two verses back at 611 and at 853 and 963.

618. परमा → परमा

परमा = highest, supreme, furthest (superlative of पर)
"The Supreme."

Vigraha: परमा सर्वोत्कृष्टा।

परम is the first member of 939 परमोदारा and 940 परमोदा, and परा of 572 पराशक्तिः and 573 परानिष्ठा — the same stem in four namas, and here it stands alone with nothing qualified.

619. पावनाकृतिः → पावन-आकृतिः

पावन = purifying, cleansing (from पू "to purify")
आकृतिः = form, shape, outward configuration (आ + कृ "to make")
"She whose form purifies."

Vigraha: पावना आकृतिः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: पावन + आकृतिः → पावनाकृतिः (आ by 6.1.101).

पावन is a causative-sense adjective: not pure but purifying, so the nama makes Her shape an agent. आकृति is the word of 830 प्रकटाकृतिः, where the form was manifest, and 933 मङ्गलाकृतिः, where it was auspiciousness — three namas built alike, adjective with आकृति in a bahuvrīhi.

620. अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डजननी → अनेक-कोटि-ब्रह्माण्ड-जननी

अनेक = many — literally not-one (अ + एक)
कोटि = a crore, ten million
ब्रह्माण्ड = a cosmic egg, a universe (ब्रह्म + अण्ड "egg")
जननी = mother, she who gives birth (from जन्, causative जनय्)
"Mother of many crores of universes."

Vigraha: अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डानां जननी।

अनेक is built by negation — not-one — so the plurality is stated as a denial of singleness, which is apt for a nama about how many worlds there are.

जननी had stood alone at 823, where Bhāskararāya noted it might be compounded with the preceding ब्रह्म and read as ब्रह्मजननी, mother of Brahmā. Here it takes the brahmāṇḍas instead, and by crores. ब्रह्माण्ड is Bhāskararāya's own gloss of विश्व at 889 विश्वभ्रमणकारिणी — "all the brahmāṇḍas" — where She turns them.

621. दिव्यविग्रहा → दिव्य-विग्रहा

दिव्य = divine, celestial (from दिव् "to shine, the sky")
विग्रहा = body, bodily form — that which is held together (वि + ग्रह्)
"She whose body is divine."

Vigraha: दिव्यः विग्रहः यस्याः सा।

विग्रह for the fifth time in the text — 840 मूलविग्रहरूपिणी the root-body of all śaktis, 861 कान्तार्धविग्रहा half Her Beloved's, 865 लीलाविग्रहधारिणी the body taken in play, 644 ज्ञानविग्रहा whose body is knowledge, and here simply divine. And दिव्य opens the next verse's 631 दिव्यगन्धाढ्या.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and the first four are all negative or superlative abstractions: primal, immeasurable, the Self, the supreme. Then 619 gives Her form a function, 620 counts the worlds, 621 calls the body divine.

617 is the nama worth marking. आत्मा is a masculine noun and the text uses it unaltered — one of only four such namas by the Paribhāṣā's own count at 1000. Two verses back at 611 the derived feminine आत्मिका appeared, so the text has both forms available and chose the masculine here.

No commentary survives for any nama in this verse.

Textual note. Three consecutive namas damaged at two joints. 615's dev has gained the र् of its own visarga; 616 has lost its initial अ, which inverts its sense from immeasurable to measurable; 617 has lost its आ. The verse as recorded reads आदिशक्तिर | मेया | त्मा where it should read आदिशक्तिः | अमेया | आत्मा, and only the glosses show it.

## क्लींकारी केवला गुह्या कैवल्यपददायिनी । त्रिपुरा त्रिजगद्वन्द्या त्रिमूर्तिस्त्रिदशेश्वरी

*klīṃkārī kevalā guhyā kaivalyapadadāyinī । tripurā trijagadvandyā trimūrtis tridaśeśvarī*

Verse 125, namas 622–629.

622. क्लींकारी → क्लीं-कारी

क्लीं = the bīja klīṃ, the Kāma-bīja
कारी = she who makes, who utters (from कृ "to do")
"She who is the maker of the syllable klīṃ."

Vigraha: क्लीम् इति कारी।

क्लीं is the Kāmabīja, and the same formation — a bīja with कारी — is the standard way of naming a syllable's deity. The syllable belongs to Kāma, who has stood in the text at 84 (burnt and revived), 586 कामसेविता (bodiless, and the mantra's seer) and 589 कामकोटिका (where काम was read as Paramaśiva).

623. केवला → केवला

केवला = alone, sole, unmixed, absolute; devoid of attributes
"The Absolute."

Vigraha: केवला असहाया।

The word is the first member of 925 कौलिनीकेवला, where Bhāskararāya gave its range — the knowledge of Īśvara "as we often see it used in the Jaina Tantras," or devoid of all attributes, or freed from pleasure and pain, Śiva Sūtra 3.35 naming Śiva the Kevalin; and the Viśva's four senses, of which he took the first three. Here it stands alone, and 625 gives its abstract two namas on.

624. गुह्या → गुह्या

गुह्या = to be hidden, secret (गुह् "to hide" with the gerundive यत्)
"The Secret."

Vigraha: गुह्या गोपनीया।

गुह् is the root of गुह at 606 गुहजन्मभूः, Skanda the cave-born — eighteen namas back, the same root once as a name and here as a gerundive. And the gerundive is prescriptive: not hidden but to-be-hidden, so the nama is an instruction to the reciter as much as a description of Her.

625. कैवल्यपददायिनी → कैवल्य-पद-दायिनी

कैवल्य = absoluteness, isolation, final liberation (the abstract of केवल)
पद = place, station, state
दायिनी = she who gives (दा + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who bestows the state of Kaivalya."

Vigraha: कैवल्यपदं ददातीति।

This is 926 अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी without its अनर्घ्य — and the two namas stand three hundred apart with the same three final members. At 926 Bhāskararāya glossed कैवल्यपद as "the fifth state of salvation," placing it in the set of five he had declined to name at 839 मुक्तिनिलया. So the fifth and last liberation is named twice in the text, once bare and once as priceless.

And the pairing with 623 is the same as 925–926's: She is केवला, and what She gives is कैवल्य. The text repeats the pair.

दायिनी for the fifth time — 117, 851, 926, 989, and here.

626. त्रिपुरा → त्रिपुरा

त्रिपुरा = Tripurā — she of the three (त्रि "three" + पुर "city, fortress, state")
"Tripurā."

Vigraha: त्रयः पुराः यस्याः सन्ति सा।

The name stands here bare, and the text gives it four incompatible derivations elsewhere. At 875 त्रिपुरमालिनी she is the sixth enclosure's deity; at 905 बैन्दवासना the Jñānārṇava concludes "as Devī is joined to the three Bindus, she is named Tripurā"; at 976 त्रिपुराम्बिका the three are the states of the jīva, or cities, or Vāmā and the rest; at 997 श्रीमत्त्रिपुरसुन्दरी the three are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra as Śiva's three body-parts, which makes Tripura masculine. Four accounts, no two agreeing, and the bare name here commits to none.

627. त्रिजगद्वन्द्या → त्रि-जगत्-वन्द्या

त्रि = three
जगत् = world — literally "the moving" (from गम्)
वन्द्या = to be praised, to be saluted (वन्द् "to praise" with the gerundive यत्)
"She who is to be adored by the three worlds."

Vigraha: त्रिभिः जगद्भिः वन्द्या।

Sandhi: जगत् + वन्द्या → जगद्वन्द्या, the त् voicing before व्.

Commentary resumes at this nama after thirty without it, and it is a single restatement of the gloss.

But the nama has already done work elsewhere. At 927 स्तोत्रप्रिया Bhāskararāya listed the six marks of a stotra and assigned namas of this text as instances of each — and नाम 627, "worshipped by the three worlds," is the one he named for नमस्कार, salutation. So this is the text's own example of what a salutation looks like.

628. त्रिमूर्तिः → त्रि-मूर्तिः

त्रि = three
मूर्तिः = form, embodiment
"She of the three forms."

Vigraha: तिस्रः मूर्तयः यस्याः सन्ति सा।

The dev field reads त्रिमूर्ति, the visarga lost — and 629 has gained the स् that visarga became before त् (त्रिमूर्तिः + त्रिदशेश्वरी → त्रिमूर्तिस्त्रिदशेश्वरी). So this is the mis-division fault again, but with स् instead of र्, which is what a visarga becomes before a voiceless dental.

Bhāskararāya's first gloss is lexical and startling: "according to Dhaumya a girl three years old is called Trimūrti." Then the doctrinal reading — the three are Brahmā and the rest, or the three Śaktis Vāmā and the others, or Icchā and the rest.

And then the Varāha Purāṇa's story, which is the best passage in these ten verses. Brahmā looked at Śiva and called Nārāyaṇa to mind; Nārāyaṇa stood between them; the three regarded one another, "and from that sight sprang a young girl of divine form." Asked who she was, "that girl of three colours, black, white and red, replied: O best ones, do you not know me, your own Śakti, supreme dominion, of beautiful shape, born from the triad?" They granted her boons — "your name is the triple Devī, ever protect the world" — and told her to make her body threefold according to her three colours, which she did.

The three colours are the guṇas, and the same three stood in the Śvetāśvatara verse cited at 866 अजा, अजाम् एकां लोहितशुक्लकृष्णाम्, "the one unborn, red and white and black." There the colours were Prakṛti's; here they are hers by grant of the three gods who produced her by looking at one another.

मूर्ति for the fifth time, after 116, 581, 603 and 992.

629. त्रिदशेश्वरी → त्रिदश-ईश्वरी

त्रिदश = the gods — literally "three ten," that is thirty, or thrice ten (त्रि + दश)
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady
"Sovereign of the gods."

Vigraha: त्रिदशानाम् ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: त्रिदश + ईश्वरी → त्रिदशेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87). The dev field reads स्त्रिदशेश्वरी, carrying the स् that belongs to 628's visarga.

त्रिदश is an old word for the gods whose arithmetic is disputed, and Bhāskararāya reports the dispute rather than settling it: the Tridaśas are the devas; or त्रि three with दश states, or ten, giving thirteen; or the Tridaśas are the Viśvedevas; or triple ten, so that She rules the thirty-three gaṇas of gods — "of course three is understood."

The nama restates 607 देवेशी, twenty-two namas back, with a different word for the gods and ईश्वरी for ईशी.

Note on the verse. Eight namas in two quartets, क- then त्रि-.

The क-quartet is built on केवल. 622 names a bīja; 623 is केवला; 624 makes Her to-be-hidden; 625 gives कैवल्य. And 623 with 625 repeats exactly the pair 925–926 had made — She is alone, and what She gives is aloneness — so the text sets the same two words together twice, three hundred namas apart.

The त्रि-quartet is where the commentary resumes, and 628 carries its weight. The Varāha Purāṇa's account has the three gods produce her by looking at one another, and her three colours — black, white, red — granted to her as a boon and then made into three bodies. Those are the guṇas, and 866's Śvetāśvatara verse had given the same three colours to the unborn Prakṛti.

626 त्रिपुरा stands bare in the middle of it, and that is worth noting given how hard the text works elsewhere to derive the name. Four derivations at 875, 905, 976 and 997, no two agreeing, and here the name with nothing attached.

Textual note. 628's dev has lost its visarga and 629 has gained the resulting स् — the mis-division fault again, and the only instance in the text where the visarga's replacement is स् rather than र्, since the following sound is a voiceless dental.

## त्र्यक्षरी दिव्यगन्धाढ्या सिन्दूरतिलकाञ्चिता । उमा शैलेन्द्रतनया गौरी गन्धर्वसेविता

*tryakṣarī divyagandhāḍhyā sindūratilakāñcitā । umā śailendratanayā gaurī gandharvasevitā*

Verse 126, namas 630–636.

630. त्र्यक्षरी → त्रि-अक्षरी

त्रि = three
अक्षरी = syllabled (अक्षर "syllable" — literally the imperishable, from अ + क्षर् "to perish")
"The Three-syllabled."

Vigraha: त्रीणि अक्षराणि यस्याः सन्ति सा।

Sandhi: त्रि + अक्षरी → त्र्यक्षरी, the इ becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि).

The three syllables are the bījas of the three divisions of the Pañcadaśī — Vāgbhava, Kāmarāja and Śakti — and the Vāmakeśvara Tantra assigns a śakti to each, which is the substance of the entry: "Vāgīśvarī is the Jñāna Śakti, which is in the Vāgbhava division and confers salvation. Kāmarāja is the Kriyā Śakti, the ruler of desires, and fulfils desire. The Śakti division is the Icchā Śakti, the supreme energy, and is in the form of Śiva. Thus Devī, the great Tripurasundarī, is three-syllabled."

That triad — Icchā, Jñāna, Kriyā — is nama 658, four verses on, where the same three energies are made Her head, trunk and feet. So the three kūṭas and the three śaktis are one scheme, and the text names it twice.

Three further readings. त्र्यक्षरी as the Śuddhavidyā and Kumārī mantras, on Gauḍapāda Sūtra 69–70, "the Śuddhavidyā and Kumārī are three-syllabled." Or as हृदय and सत्य — heart and truth — on Bṛhadāraṇyaka 5.3.1 and 5.5.1, "the words heart and truth are each three-syllabled." Or as the three divisions of the alphabet called Yugākṣara, Māsākṣara and Nityākṣara.

Bhāskararāya drops a counting marker: the twenty-fourth verse divides thirty-five names.

अक्षर is the imperishable, so the three kūṭas of 85–87 and 588 त्रिकूटा are counted here by a word that means what cannot wear away.

631. दिव्यगन्धाढ्या → दिव्य-गन्ध-आढ्या

दिव्य = divine, celestial; and per the commentary, divine beings
गन्ध = smell, perfume
आढ्या = rich in, abounding in
"She who is rich in divine perfumes."

Vigraha: दिव्यगन्धेन आढ्या।

Sandhi: गन्ध + आढ्या → गन्धाढ्या (आ by 6.1.101).

Two readings. दिव्य as the divine beings: "She is surrounded by celestial things and not like the ordinary kings who surround themselves with terrestrial objects" — the comparison being to a court. Or दिव्यगन्ध as actual perfumes, harichandana and the like, with Taittirīya Āraṇyaka X.10: "Devī possesses perfumes and is not to be easily perceived."

Then Bhāskararāya makes it a siddhi. Yoga Sūtra 3.41 — "from concentration with reference to the relation between the organ of hearing and ether, a superperfect organ of hearing" — and similarly for the other senses; "it is by the favour of Devī one obtains the divine perfumes." So the divine smells are not Her ornament but a yogic attainment She grants.

आढ्या is the word of 969 सुवेषाढ्या, rich in fine dress, where the same governing construction made the claim one of abundance rather than of taste.

632. सिन्दूरतिलकाञ्चिता → सिन्दूर-तिलक-अञ्चिता

सिन्दूर = red lead, vermilion; and per the Viśva, an elephant
तिलक = a forehead mark; and per the Viśva, a she-elephant
अञ्चिता = honoured, distinguished; also bent, curved (from अञ्च्)
"She who is graced with a vermilion forehead-mark."

Vigraha: सिन्दूरतिलकेन अञ्चिता।

Sandhi: तिलक + अञ्चिता → तिलकाञ्चिता (आ by 6.1.101).

The Viśva's alternative senses turn the nama into something else entirely: सिन्दूर an elephant, तिलक a she-elephant, अञ्चिता worshipped — "worshipped by females whose gait resembles that of an elephant," the elephant-gait being a stock mark of beauty.

And on that reading Bhāskararāya supplies two stories of women who worshipped Her for husbands. The Viṣṇu Bhāgavata's gopīs: "the daughters of Nanda, whose love is intense and hard to resist — O Kātyāyanī, O Devī, O great Māyā, O great Yoginī, O ruler, give us the son of the cowherd for a husband." And Rukmiṇī at her marriage, when Kṛṣṇa was delayed: "Fortune is against me, Maheśvara is against me, Devī also, the wife of Śiva, the daughter of the mountain, is unfavourable" — after which she left the women's apartments on foot for Devī's temple, "and by worshipping Devī she obtained her desired objects."

Kātyāyanī, whom the gopīs address, is nama 556; and this is the third place the text records worship for a specific end, after 545 पुलोमजार्चिता, where Śacī worshipped to have Indra restored, and 546 बन्धमोचनी's two prisoners.

633. उमा → उमा

उमा = Umā; and per the lexica, the china rose, saffron, fame, brightness, and the daughter of Himavat
"Umā."

Vigraha: उमा गिरिजा।

This is the most heavily re-divided nama in the batch, and Bhāskararāya gives five readings.

उ Śiva with मा Lakṣmī; or उ Śiva with मा "limits." Or the lexical senses — the Viśva gives उमा for china rose, the daughter of Himavat, saffron, fame and brightness, and Devī "resides as brightness in all creatures."

Or उ as an interrogative and मा as negation, which yields a story: the Kālikā Purāṇa says that "because when she was forbidden to go to the forest to perform penance she was called Umā" — u mā, "do not." The same story is in the Brahmā Purāṇa and the Puṣkarakhaṇḍa of the Padma. So the name is her mother's prohibition, quoted.

Or उ superior with मा a certain mental modification, on the Sūta Saṃhitā 4.1.20: "I adore the supreme experience which destroys the noose of earthly existence, which purifies even Sadāśiva, called Umā."

Or उ, म and अ as the three letters of the praṇava, meaning Brahmā, Rudra and Viṣṇu — "and many other meanings of the Praṇava also are to be taken here." The three letters of ॐ had been one reading of त्रिवर्ग at 873.

634. शैलेन्द्रतनया → शैल-इन्द्र-तनया

शैल = a mountain (from शिला "rock")
इन्द्र = chief, lord — शैलेन्द्र, the king of mountains, Himavat
तनया = daughter (from तन् "to stretch, to extend" — the one who continues a line)
"Daughter of the king of mountains."

Vigraha: शैलेन्द्रस्य तनया।

Sandhi: शैल + इन्द्र → शैलेन्द्र (अ + इ → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

The Devī Purāṇa's gloss is a bare etymology: "being born in the abode of the king of mountains, she is called the daughter of the king of the mountains."

तनया is from तन्, to stretch — the daughter as the extension of a line, which is a different figure from सुता at 956 धरसुता, from सू "to bring forth." And 956 made her the mountain's daughter through धर, the bearer, without naming Himavat; here he is named by title. The text also gives her a different parentage at 932 महेशी, "born from Mahādeva."

635. गौरी → गौरी

गौरी = white, pale, yellowish, brilliant (feminine of गौर)
"The Fair One."

Vigraha: गौरवर्णा गौरी।

The colour is unsettled and Bhāskararāya reports it so. "Because her colour is yellowish"; the Mahā-Vasiṣṭha, "she is called Gaurī because her body is yellow"; but the Devī Purāṇa, "she who was burned by the fire of Yoga was again born of Himālaya, and as she has the colour of the conch, the jasmine and the moon, she is called Gaurī" — which is white, not yellow.

That second account also supplies a biography: burnt by yoga-fire and reborn of the mountain, which is the Satī–Pārvatī sequence, and it sits directly against 598 दाक्षायणी and 600 दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी, where she was Dakṣa's daughter and the destroyer of his sacrifice.

Further senses: a Kośa gives गौरी for a certain river and for a girl of ten; the Padma Purāṇa makes Gaurī the wife of Varuṇa, and also the deity at Kanyakubja.

Her colours in the text now number several and none agrees with another — coral at 891, the young sun's rose at 922, bandhūka red at 964, pomegranate at 560, and fair or yellow here. 922 supplied the principle that reconciles them: colour is a function of the meditation's purpose, not of Her.

636. गन्धर्वसेविता → गन्धर्व-सेविता

गन्धर्व = a Gandharva, a celestial musician; also a horse; also a certain deity
सेविता = attended, served (from सेव् "to serve")
"She who is attended by the Gandharvas."

Vigraha: गन्धर्वैः सेविता।

Bhāskararāya lists the senses without choosing: "Gandharva, Viśvāvasu and others; or horses; or a certain deity called Aśvāroḍha; or it may mean a celestial song."

The last is the one that connects. The Gandharvas are the heavenly musicians, and गान्धर्व was given at 857 गानलोलुपा as one of the kinds of music She is avid for — "śārīra, the voice, and gāndharva, the instrumental art." With 909's Sāman and 613's poetry, the text names her attendance by musicians four times in different words.

Note on the verse. Seven namas: one on the mantra, two on ornament, and four that are the Pārvatī biography.

630 belongs with the mantra-namas of verse 118 and it supplies what they lacked — the three kūṭas matched to the three śaktis, Jñāna to Vāgbhava, Kriyā to Kāmarāja, Icchā to Śakti. That is the same triad 658 will make her head, trunk and feet.

633–635 are the closest the text comes to a life. Umā named by her mother's prohibition; daughter of the mountain-king; burnt by yoga-fire and reborn fair. And the accounts do not agree with each other or with the rest of the text: 932 has her born from Mahādeva, 956 makes her the mountain's daughter without naming him, 598 makes her Dakṣa's.

632's elephant-reading is worth keeping for what it produces rather than for its plausibility. Once तिलक is a she-elephant and अञ्चिता is "worshipped," the nama becomes about women who worship Her for husbands, and Bhāskararāya supplies the gopīs and Rukmiṇī.
