## विश्वगर्भा स्वर्णगर्भा वरदा वागधीश्वरी । ध्यानगम्यापरिच्छेद्या ज्ञानदा ज्ञानविग्रहा

*viśvagarbhā svarṇagarbhā varadā vāgadhīśvarī । dhyānagamyā'paricchedyā jñānadā jñānavigrahā*

Verse 127, namas 637–644.

637. विश्वगर्भा → विश्व-गर्भा

विश्व = all, the whole, the universe
गर्भा = womb; and also the foetus, what is in the womb
"She whose womb holds the universe."

Vigraha: विश्वं गर्भे यस्याः सा।

गर्भ is ambiguous between the container and the contained — womb and embryo — so the compound reads either as "having the universe for her foetus" or "whose womb is the universe." index.html's body for this nama is a single stranded word.

विश्व for the fifth time — 889 the universe She turns, 890 the universe She eats, 934 the universe She mothers, and here the universe she carries.

638. स्वर्णगर्भा → स्वर्ण-गर्भा

स्वर्ण = gold (सु + वर्ण, "of good colour"); and by division, सु with अर्ण
गर्भा = womb, embryo
"She whose womb is golden."

Vigraha: स्वर्णं गर्भः यस्याः सा।

The Vāyu Purāṇa: "her womb is golden and born from gold, hence she is called Hiraṇyagarbhā" — which identifies her with the Hiraṇyagarbha of the cosmogonies, the golden germ.

Then two divisions on सु + अर्ण. सु "excellently" with अर्ण "letters" and गर्भ "shining" — she is explained by the mātṛkā letters. Or सु "superior" with अर्ण "mantras" — she has all the higher mantras in her womb. Both readings turn a colour into a container of language, which is what 577 मातृकावर्णरूपिणी and 529 सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता had done with वर्ण, the word स्वर्ण is built from.

639. वरदा → वर-दा

वर = a boon, a gift, a wish granted; and per the commentary's division, अवर, the unholy
दा = giving, she who gives (from दा "to give")
"The Giver of boons."

Vigraha: वरं ददातीति वरदा।

The gloss in index.html gives not this but the divided reading: "punisher of unholy persons" — अवर the unholy Asuras, or अव "shining" with रद "teeth." So the recorded gloss belongs to the alternative and the plain sense has to be supplied.

वरद is among the commonest of divine epithets, and the text has used it once already at 518 वरदादिनिषेविता, where Varadā was the first of four śaktis attending Her — so a name of hers is also the name of one of her attendants.

640. वागधीश्वरी → वाक्-अधि-ईश्वरी

वाक् = speech (from वच् "to speak")
अधि = over, above
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady
"Sovereign over speech."

Vigraha: वाचाम् अधीश्वरी।

Sandhi: वाक् + अधि → वागधि, the क् voicing before the vowel; then अधि + ईश्वरी → अधीश्वरी (इ + ई → ई, Pāṇini 6.1.101 अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, the long-vowel rule applying to like vowels).

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

अधीश्वरी stacks अधि on ईश्वरी, so the sovereignty is over-lordship rather than lordship — and this is the eighth turn of ईश् in the text, after 569, 607, 629, 831, 932, 945, 949 and 983. वाक् itself is Vāgdevī, and 630 named Vāgīśvarī as the Jñāna Śakti of the Vāgbhava kūṭa.

641. ध्यानगम्या → ध्यान-गम्या

ध्यान = meditation, contemplation (from ध्यै "to meditate")
गम्या = to be reached, attainable (गम् with the gerundive यत्)
"She who is to be attained by meditation."

Vigraha: ध्यानेन गम्या।

Śvetāśvatara 1.3 is cited: "they, the sages devoted to meditation, saw the Śakti of the divine Self hidden by its own qualities."

This is the third of the गम्या-namas, and the three differ only in their means: 113 भावनागम्या by भावना, 980 ज्ञानगम्या by knowledge, and here by ध्यान. At 113 Bhāskararāya offered the reading अगम्या, unattainable, and denied that the path of action reaches Her — and the very next nama here makes a related denial.

642. अपरिच्छेद्या → अ-परि-छेद्या

अ = not (नञ्)
परि = around, on all sides
छेद्या = to be cut, to be divided, to be delimited (छिद् "to cut" with the gerundive यत्)
"She who cannot be circumscribed."

Vigraha: परिच्छेत्तुं न शक्या इति अपरिच्छेद्या।

The dev field reads ऽपरिच्छेद्या. The avagraha marks the अ elided in ध्यानगम्या + अपरिच्छेद्या → ध्यानगम्यापरिच्छेद्या (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101) — the ninth instance of that class in the text, and the single form again correctly signals a short vowel.

Bhāskararāya's whole gloss is four words: "that is as to place and time." So the delimitation denied is spatial and temporal, which is what परिच्छेद means technically — a bounding-around.

छिद् "to cut" gives परिच्छेद its edge: to define is to cut a thing out of its surroundings, and the nama says no such cut can be made. That is 616 अमेया's claim in another root — immeasurable there, undelimitable here.

643. ज्ञानदा → ज्ञान-दा

ज्ञान = knowledge; and per the second reading, the knowledge that binds
दा = giving; and per that reading, the slayer, the remover
"The Giver of knowledge."

Vigraha: ज्ञानं ददातीति ज्ञानदा।

The Kena Upaniṣad (25) is quoted, and it is a good choice: "in that ether he met a very beautiful woman, Umā, the daughter of Himavat; to her he said — what is this Yakṣa? She replied: that is Brahman." Indra learns what he has seen from Umā, so the nama's giving of knowledge has a scriptural instance, and Umā is nama 633 ten namas back.

The Sūta Saṃhitā (4.47.58): "such is the supreme Vidyā Śaṃkarī, destroyer of saṃsāra, which arises in men by the grace of Śakti alone." And the Sūtagītā (8.80) makes her the speech through whose grace salvation comes.

Then the reversal, and it is sharp. ज्ञान is taken as the knowledge that leads to bondage and दा as the slayer — She who destroys that knowledge. The authority is Śiva Sūtra 1.2, "jñāna is bondage," which some commentators read as ajñāna; the Vārtika glosses it as the knowledge that turns outward from inward feeling. So the same compound gives giver of knowledge and destroyer of it, and the pivot is which knowledge is meant.

644. ज्ञानविग्रहा → ज्ञान-विग्रहा

ज्ञान = knowledge
विग्रहा = body, bodily form; and per the second reading, expansion
"She whose body is knowledge."

Vigraha: ज्ञानं विग्रहः यस्याः सा।

"Because the whole world is the form of knowledge." The Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Book II, is quoted and it holds both sides of 643's reversal at once: "Jñāna alone is the supreme Brahman; Jñāna is the cause of bondage. This universe consists of knowledge. There is nothing beyond knowledge. O Maitreya, know that Jñāna is both Vidyā and Avidyā."

So the resolution 643 needed is supplied here by the authority rather than by Bhāskararāya: knowledge is both the liberating and the binding thing, and there is nothing else for it to be.

A second reading takes विग्रह as expansion — through Her one's knowledge expands — which is a different sense of वि + ग्रह् from the holding-together the word has elsewhere. विग्रह for the sixth time, after 621, 640's neighbourhood, 840, 861 and 865.

Note on the verse. Eight namas in three groups: two on गर्भ, two on giving and speech, and four on how She is known.

637–638 pair as wombs, and 638's divisions turn the golden womb into a container of letters and mantras — the same move the text makes with वर्ण at 529 and 577.

641–642 are means and limit: attainable by meditation, and not to be circumscribed. And 643–644 are the verse's substance, because 643 reverses itself — giver of knowledge, or destroyer of the knowledge that binds — and 644's Viṣṇu Purāṇa citation resolves it by refusing the distinction: "Jñāna is both Vidyā and Avidyā."

---

## सर्ववेदान्तसंवेद्या सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी । लोपामुद्रार्चिता लीलाक्लृप्तब्रह्माण्डमण्डला

*sarvavedāntasaṃvedyā satyānandasvarūpiṇī । lopāmudrārcitā līlākḷptabrahmāṇḍamaṇḍalā*

Verse 128, namas 645–648.

645. सर्ववेदान्तसंवेद्या → सर्व-वेद-अन्त-सम्-वेद्या

सर्व = all
वेद = the Veda (from विद् "to know")
अन्त = end — वेदान्त, the end of the Veda
सम् = fully
वेद्या = to be known (विद् with the gerundive यत्)
"She who is to be fully known through all the Vedāntas."

Vigraha: सर्वैः वेदान्तैः संवेद्या।

Sandhi: वेद + अन्त → वेदान्त (आ by 6.1.101).

The compound puts विद् at both ends — the Veda is what is known and वेद्या is what is to be known — so the nama runs the root through subject and object. The Varāha Purāṇa: "this Devī is explained as the threefold energy and set forth as the end of logic. She is the energy of wisdom, set forth in all the Vedāntas."

The nama is 852 सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा restated with different words: there all the Upaniṣads proclaimed Her aloud, and Bhāskararāya made सर्व earn its place by Vedānta Sūtra 3.3.1, that the cognitions of all the Vedānta texts are identical. Here they are how She is known rather than what proclaims Her.

646. सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी → सत्य-आनन्द-स्व-रूपिणी

सत्य = truth, reality, being (from सत्, the present participle of अस् "to be")
आनन्द = bliss (आ + नन्द् "to rejoice")
स्व = own
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose very form is truth and bliss."

Vigraha: सत्यम् आनन्दः च स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: सत्य + आनन्द → सत्यानन्द (आ by 6.1.101). Some, Bhāskararāya notes, divide this into two namas, सत्य and आनन्दस्वरूपिणी.

He then takes सत्य apart on Taittirīya 2.6.1, "he became sat as well as tyat" — so सत्य is सत् with त्य, being and that-beyond-being. Or सत् is prāṇa and food, on the Śruti "sat, prāṇa and food," with य the sun. Or सत् means brightness.

For आनन्द he cites Vedānta Sūtra 3.3.11, "bliss and other qualities as belonging to the subject," where the point established is that bliss and the rest are qualities of Brahman itself and not attributed from outside.

The pair सत्य–आनन्द is two-thirds of सच्चिदानन्द, and the missing term, चित्, is what 918 चैतन्यार्घ्यसमाराध्या and 919 made the offering and the flower. The full triad had been given at 907 as the three tattvas Sat, Cit and Ānanda, with the thirty-six distributed among them.

647. लोपामुद्रार्चिता → लोपामुद्रा-अर्चिता

लोपामुद्रा = Lopāmudrā, the wife of Agastya; and also a name of the Pañcadaśī mantra in its Hādi form
अर्चिता = worshipped (from अर्च् "to worship")
"She who is worshipped by Lopāmudrā."

Vigraha: लोपामुद्रया अर्चिता।

Sandhi: लोपामुद्रा + अर्चिता → लोपामुद्रार्चिता (आ by 6.1.101).

The Triśatī (I.15) has Her say it in the first person: "his wife named Lopāmudrā worships me with much devotion." The Tripurā Siddhānta adds that "as the supreme ruler was pleased with the wife of Agastya, named Lopāmudrā, this Devī is invoked under the name of Lopāmudrā" — so a worshipper's name becomes the deity's.

And Bhāskararāya's second reading makes that literal: Lopāmudrā is the Pañcadaśī mantra itself, cross-referring to nama 238, and अर्चिता means She is to be worshipped through that mantra. The Kādimata is cited for the practice: "one should perform all the ceremonies by the third division of the mantra."

Sastry's footnote records a syllabic derivation from the Bhāgavata-Nārāyaṇa: लोप "by the absence of worship," मुद् bliss, र "taken away" — bliss removed where worship is wanting.

अर्चिता for the fourth time — 825 बुधार्चिता by the wise, 545 पुलोमजार्चिता by Śacī, 917 धीरसमर्चिता by the steady, and here by Agastya's wife. Two of the four name the worshipper.

648. लीलाक्लृप्तब्रह्माण्डमण्डला → लीला-क्लृप्त-ब्रह्माण्ड-मण्डला

लीला = play, sport, effortless action
क्लृप्त = arranged, formed, fashioned (from कृप्/क्लृप् "to be arranged")
ब्रह्माण्ड = a cosmic egg, a universe
मण्डला = a circle, a whole round, a set
"She who has fashioned the round of universes in play."

Vigraha: लीलया क्लृप्तं ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलं यस्याः सा।

"That is, without effort." And Bhāskararāya quotes his own Devīstava, which puts the claim comparatively: "even Śiva is powerless to create, preserve or destroy Brahmā, Viṣṇu and other gods, but, O mother, the regulation of the universe is but sport to you." The Śakti Sūtra: "she manifests the Universe at will in herself."

That is the strongest form in the text of a claim it makes repeatedly — Śiva unable where She is unexerted. Compare 947, where the five gods are her couch, and 995's Saundaryalaharī 24, where each of the five acts under the one above and Sadāśiva waits on her eyebrows.

लीला returns from 865 लीलाविग्रहधारिणी, where the effortlessness was of taking bodies, and 966 लीलाविनोदिनी, where it was delight. Here it is cosmogony. And ब्रह्माण्ड had been counted by crores at 620, eighteen namas back; मण्डल had been the lunar round at 610.

Note on the verse. Four namas, and each is long. Two of how She is known — through all the Vedāntas, as truth and bliss — then two named acts: worshipped by Lopāmudrā, and having made the universes in play.

647 is the interesting one structurally, because the worshipper's name becomes a name of the mantra and then of the practice. Lopāmudrā worships Her, so Devī is invoked as Lopāmudrā, so Lopāmudrā is the Pañcadaśī, so worship is performed "by the third division of the mantra." A person, a name, a formula, a rubric.

648 gives the sharpest version of the text's standing claim about Śiva. Bhāskararāya's own verse has him powerless over the four gods below him while the whole universe is Her sport.

## अदृश्या दृश्यरहिता विज्ञात्री वेद्यवर्जिता । योगिनी योगदा योग्या योगानन्दा युगन्धरा

*adṛśyā dṛśyarahitā vijñātrī vedyavarjitā । yoginī yogadā yogyā yogānandā yugandharā*

Verse 129, namas 649–657.

649. अदृश्या → अ-दृश्या

अ = not (नञ्)
दृश्या = to be seen, visible (दृश् "to see" with the gerundive यत्)
"The Invisible."

Vigraha: द्रष्टुं न शक्या इति अदृश्या।

"Not to be perceived by the eyes and other senses." Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.4.2 is cited, and it is the exact verse for a gerundive of seeing: "you do not see the seer of sight." What cannot be seen is what does the seeing.

The Devī Bhāgavata, Book III: "your unqualified form is not an object of visual perception; Śakti is without quality, difficult of approach; the supreme Person also is without qualities."

650. दृश्यरहिता → दृश्य-रहिता

दृश्य = the visible, what is to be seen
रहिता = devoid of, free from (from रह् "to abandon")
"She who is free of the visible."

Vigraha: दृश्येन रहिता।

The reason given is not epistemic but temporal: "she is freed from dṛśya, the worldly things, because they are not eternal." So the freedom is from impermanence rather than from being seen.

649 and 650 are subject and object of one root — not to be seen, and free of what is seen — and 651–652 do the same with knowing. Four namas, two roots, each denied from both ends.

रहिता is the word of 858 कल्पनारहिता, where what She was free of was mental construction, and where Bhāskararāya glossed कल्पना as "the waves of the objective world, because they are only imagined." The reasoning there and here is the same: what is not real is not hers.

651. विज्ञात्री → वि-ज्ञात्री

वि = fully, distinctly
ज्ञात्री = she who knows, the knower (ज्ञा "to know" with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्)
"The Knower."

Vigraha: विजानातीति विज्ञात्री।

The computed pada in index.html reads विज्ञा-अत्री, which invents a stem विज्ञा and a suffix अत्री; the split is वि + ज्ञात्री, and ज्ञात्री is the तृ agent-noun that stood as ज्ञातृ in 981 ज्ञातृज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी.

Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.4.14 is quoted, and again it is the precise verse: "O, how is the knower to be known?" The nama asserts the knower; the citation asks how such a thing could be an object; and the next nama answers by removing the object.

The formation is that of सवित्री at 826, दात्री at 832, कर्त्री at 882, धात्री at 935 and हन्त्री at 557 — the तृ agent-noun with ङीप्, which this text uses more than any other device.

652. वेद्यवर्जिता → वेद्य-वर्जिता

वेद्य = the knowable, what is to be known (विद् with the gerundive यत्)
वर्जिता = devoid of, excluding (from वृज् "to avoid, to exclude")
"She who is without an object of knowledge."

Vigraha: वेद्येन वर्जिता।

"Because they are not eternal" — the same four words as at 650, and the same argument.

The pair 651–652 is exactly 981 ज्ञातृज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी taken apart and negated on one side. There She was the form of both knower and known; here She is the knower and has no known. And वेद्य is the gerundive whose positive stood at 645 संवेद्या four namas back, where She was what the Vedāntas know — so the text affirms and denies the same form within a verse of each other.

653. योगिनी → योगिनी

योगिनी = a female adept in yoga; she who is joined, or who joins (from युज् "to yoke" — योग + इन्, feminine ङीप्)
"The Yoginī."

Vigraha: योगः अस्याः अस्तीति योगिनी।

"Yoga is the idea of union. As she has this and bestows it on others she is so called." So the nama already contains the next one, and Bhāskararāya says so.

The five yoga-namas beginning here are the longest single-root run in this stretch. And योगिनी had been the word for the seven cakra-deities at 519–534 and for the eight planetary Yoginīs — Bhāskararāya gives both under 655.

654. योगदा → योग-दा

योग = union, yoga
दा = giving (from दा "to give")
"The Giver of Yoga."

Vigraha: योगं ददातीति योगदा।

The commentary is a restatement of the gloss. The bare दा is the form of 953 शर्मदा and 639 वरदा — the shortest of the giving-suffixes the text uses, against दायिनी at 117, 851, 926, 989 and 625, and दात्री at 832.

655. योग्या → योग्या

योग्या = fit, suitable, capable of being joined (from युज् with the gerundive यत्)
"The Fit."

Vigraha: योक्तुं योग्या।

Bhāskararāya uses this nama to define yoga itself, and gathers four definitions. The Viṣṇu Purāṇa: "having controlled all the senses with the mind, the idea of the unity of the soul with the supreme Self is Yoga." Gītā 6.23: "one should know that Yoga which frees from the attachment of pain." Yoga Sūtra 1.2: "Yoga means the restraint of mental modifications."

Then the classification: yoga is of four kinds — Mantra, Laya, Haṭha and Rāja — and Rājayoga of three, Sāṃkhya, Tāraka and Amanaska. "The characteristics of these are omitted here for want of space," which is a rare admission.

Two further readings of योगिनी are given here rather than at 653. The eight Yoginīs from Maṅgalā to Saṅkaṭā, planets, which "according to the Jyotiṣ Śāstra make a round in thirty-six years" — Sastry's footnote records that the Bombay edition reads twenty-six. Or the seven yoginīs Ḍākinī and the rest of the Mantra Śāstra, with a cross-reference to nama 475 — which is the run this text worked through at 519–534.

And a division of labour across the three namas: "Yoga means enjoyment of objects, hence of these three names the first is enjoyer, the second the bestower" — the third being the fit.

656. योगानन्दा → योग-आनन्दा

योग = union; and per the commentary, the common essence of Śiva and Śakti
आनन्दा = bliss (आ + नन्द्)
"The Bliss of Yoga."

Vigraha: योगस्य आनन्दः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: योग + आनन्दा → योगानन्दा (आ by 6.1.101).

"Yoga, the common essence of Śiva and Śakti; that alone is her bliss." That is 999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी's ऐक्य named as bliss instead of as form.

Then a striking second reading: योगानन्द is yoga-sleep, "because bliss chiefly pervades in sleep, and that state belongs to Devī." The Harivaṃśa is quoted for it — "she who is a mass of bliss and is known in the world as sleep. Even among the gods none supported her except Nārāyaṇa. She is the companion of Sadāśiva, Māyā, the mother of Viṣṇu, unborn; she is ever in the presence of Nārāyaṇa, thus causing him to sleep." Yoganidrā, the sleep of Viṣṇu between world-ages, is thus one of Her names.

Or Yogānanda is the Nṛsiṃha of that name. Or the nama divides as अयोग + नन्द, the unattached — on Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.9.26, "the unattached is never attached." Or अय "mountain," so immovable as a mountain; or अय "good actions" with उ Śiva and ग "to go."

657. युगन्धरा → युग-न्धरा

युग = a yoke; also a measure of four cubits; a pair; and one of the four world-ages
धरा = bearing, holding (from धृ "to hold")
"She who bears the yoke."

Vigraha: युगं धरतीति युगन्धरा।

The Viśvaprakāśa's senses are given in full — "yuga means a measure consisting of four cubits, a chariot yoke, a plough, also the cycles Kṛta and the rest, a pair, and a species of medicinal plant" — and Bhāskararāya applies three of them. As yoke: "as the horse and bull bear the yoke, she supports the whole universe." As pair: Śiva and Śakti. As the cycles: she directs them.

धरा is the participle of 530 सर्वायुधधरा, bearing all weapons, and the word that stands alone at 955 धरा as the earth, she who bears. The support-thread — 829, 877, 884, 935, 955 — takes another turn here, and the yoke-figure is its most concrete.

Note on the verse. Nine namas: four of negation, five on योग.

649–652 are the tightest construction in these ten verses. Two roots, दृश् and विद्, each denied from both ends — not to be seen and free of the visible; the knower, and without a knowable. And the reason given twice, in the same four words, is that the objects are not eternal.

That also puts 652 four namas from 645, where संवेद्या made Her what all the Vedāntas know. The text affirms the knowable of Her and denies it inside a single verse-pair, and does not remark on it.

653–656 then run one root through four namas — yoginī, giver of yoga, fit for it, its bliss — and Bhāskararāya distributes the roles explicitly: enjoyer, bestower, fit. 655 is where he defines yoga and classifies it; 656 is where yoga becomes sleep, and Yoganidrā is identified with Her.

## इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपिणी । सर्वाधारा सुप्रतिष्ठा सदसद्रूपधारिणी

*icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktisvarūpiṇī । sarvādhārā supratiṣṭhā sadasadrūpadhāriṇī*

Verse 130, namas 658–661.

658. इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपिणी → इच्छा-शक्ति-ज्ञान-शक्ति-क्रिया-शक्ति-स्व-रूपिणी

इच्छा = desire, will (from इष् "to wish")
ज्ञान = knowledge
क्रिया = action (from कृ "to do")
शक्ति = power, energy
स्व = own
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose very form is the energies of will, knowledge and action."

Vigraha: इच्छाशक्तिः ज्ञानशक्तिः क्रियाशक्तिः च स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

The dev field breaks this seven-member compound with a space before क्रियाशक्ति-; it is one nama.

The three correspond to the three guṇas. The Saṅketapaddhati makes them a body: "desire is her head, wisdom her trunk, action her feet, thus her body consists of three energies." And the Vāmakeśvara Tantra pairs them with the trimūrti — "Tripurā is threefold, viz. Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Īśa, and she is the energies of desire, wisdom and action."

The ordering is causal, and Bhāskararāya states it: "of these energies the preceding one is the cause of the succeeding." The Mālinīvijaya Tantra gives the sequence as a narrative — "that supreme divine energy becomes the energy of desire when Brahman wishes to create; she becomes the energy of knowledge when she reminds him, saying let this be thus; when thus knowing he acts, she becomes the energy of action." Will, then the specification of the will, then the doing.

The Kriyāśakti is then subdivided fivefold on the Sūta Saṃhitā (4.14.28): Spanda, Parispanda, Prakrama, Pariśīlatā and Paracāra.

This triad has stood in the text three times before. At 110 कुण्डलिनी the Devī Purāṇa derived the name from the śṛṅgāṭaka's three angles, "icchā, jñāna and kriyā." At 630 त्र्यक्षरी the Vāmakeśvara assigned each to a kūṭa of the Pañcadaśī — Jñāna to Vāgbhava, Kriyā to Kāmarāja, Icchā to Śakti. At 628 त्रिमूर्तिः they were one reading of the three forms. And 927 स्तोत्रप्रिया cited this nama, 658, as the text's own instance of पराक्रम, the praising of exploits, among the six marks of a stotra.

659. सर्वाधारा → सर्व-आधारा

सर्व = all
आधारा = support, foundation, that which bears up (आ + धृ "to hold")
"The Support of all."

Vigraha: सर्वस्य आधारा।

Sandhi: सर्व + आधारा → सर्वाधारा (आ by 6.1.101).

Two readings, and they differ in whether She is in things or under them. Taking धारा as gradation: "she is one with created things." Taking आधार as support: "she is in all." The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is quoted for the first — "in reality it is Devī herself who is perceived in all things, permanent or impermanent, gross or subtle or more subtle, embodied or disembodied, one or many, in earth, in heaven or elsewhere."

आधारा is the word of 884 धर्माधारा, where the compound stacked धृ twice — dharma being what upholds and आधार what upholds it. Here the object is not the law but everything.

660. सुप्रतिष्ठा → सु-प्रतिष्ठा

सु = well, firmly
प्रतिष्ठा = firm standing, foundation, established position (प्रति + स्था)
"The firmly Established."

Vigraha: सुष्ठु प्रतिष्ठा।

Bhāskararāya's only note is metrical: "Supratiṣṭhā is a metre of twenty syllables."

That is characteristic — he did the same at 829 प्रतिष्ठा, where after the doctrinal readings he added that प्रतिष्ठा "is also the name of the sixteen-syllabled Vedic metre." So both the bare word and its intensified form are metres, and he records the metre in both places.

प्रतिष्ठा at 829 was "that on which all things stand," and 877 निरालम्बा then argued that what supports all can have no support. This nama, with 659 immediately before it, restates the first half of that pair — support of all, firmly established — without the second.

661. सदसद्रूपधारिणी → सत्-असत्-रूप-धारिणी

सत् = being, the existent; Brahman
असत् = non-being, the non-existent; and per the commentary, the universe
रूप = form
धारिणी = she who bears, assumes (धृ "to hold" + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who bears the form of being and non-being."

Vigraha: सत् असत् च रूपं धारयतीति।

Sandhi: सत् + असत् → सदसत्, the त् voicing before the vowel; then सदसत् + रूप → सदसद्रूप, voicing again before र्.

Bhāskararāya notes first that She is different from both, and then that असत् here stands for the universe — with two Śrutis: Taittirīya 2.7.1, "in the beginning this was indeed asat," and Chāndogya 6.2.2, "how did sat come to exist from asat?" In both, he says, असत् means the universe rather than nothing.

A second reading makes them two kinds of knowledge. सत् is the last mental modification before the realisation of unity; असत् the remaining modifications, called vikalpa, fanciful — on Yoga Sūtra 1.9, "fancy is a notion founded on a knowledge conveyed by words, but of that there is no object corresponding in reality," and Gautama's sūtra, "whatever is perceived by the mind is asat."

A third takes them as existence and non-existence simply, existence being what is permanent and unchangeable.

धारिणी is the word of 527 हाकिनीरूपधारिणी and 865 लीलाविग्रहधारिणी — bearing a form rather than being one, which the text distinguishes from स्वरूपिणी. And this nama's pairing of two contraries with रूपधारिणी is the same shape as 908 तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी and 981 ज्ञातृज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी, where She was the two poles of a relation. Here the poles are being and its opposite.

Note on the verse. Four namas: one very long, then two of support, then one of contraries.

658 is the most doctrinally central nama in these ten verses. The triad Icchā–Jñāna–Kriyā is given a body (head, trunk, feet), a correspondence with the trimūrti, a causal ordering in which each energy produces the next, and a narrative of creation in which desire precedes specification and specification precedes act. And the same triad has been used at 110 for the kuṇḍalinī's triangle and at 630 for the three kūṭas of the mantra, so this is the third scheme it organises.

659–660 restate the support-claim of 829 and 884 without the counter-claim of 877, and 660's only gloss is that the word names a twenty-syllable metre — which is exactly the kind of note Bhāskararāya added to 829.

661 then closes on being and non-being, read three ways, of which the second is the most interesting: सत् as the last mental modification before unity is realised, and असत् as all the fanciful ones before it.

---

Textual note for verses 121–130.

The dominant fact is the block-duplication. Namas 597–626 share one gloss and one body, thirty namas in a single run, so no commentary proper to 601–626 survives — twenty-six of the sixty-one namas in these verses. The run is an outlier and not a pattern: the next longest anywhere in the text is three namas, at 184–186, 460–462, 480–482 and 997–999.

Sandhi mis-divisions, four of them, all the same fault of taking the word-boundary one letter late across a visarga:

603 गुरुमूर्तिः and 604 गुणनिधिः have each lost a visarga without the following nama gaining anything, as at 539 and 567.

615 आदिशक्तिः has gained the र् of its own visarga; 616 अमेया has lost its initial अ, which inverts its sense from immeasurable to measurable, as the same loss did at 993; and 617 आत्मा has lost its आ. Three consecutive namas damaged at two joints, and the verse as recorded reads आदिशक्तिर | मेया | त्मा.

628 त्रिमूर्तिः has lost its visarga and 629 त्रिदशेश्वरी has gained the resulting स् — the only place in the text where the visarga's replacement is स् rather than र्, the following sound being a voiceless dental.

Other faults: 614's dev reads साचामर- for सचामर-, a spurious long आ where the प्रादि compound स is wanted. 642's dev reads ऽपरिच्छेद्या, carrying the avagraha of the elided अ from ध्यानगम्या — ninth instance of that class, single mark for a short vowel as the rule holds. 658's dev breaks its seven-member compound with a space before क्रियाशक्ति-. 651's computed pada reads विज्ञा-अत्री, inventing both members where the split is वि + ज्ञात्री. 637's body is a single stranded word, and 640 has no body at all.


---

> **Note on verses 138–140.** The verse table has no row for verse 138: verses 138 and 139 are merged into a single row labelled 139, whose text carries a ॥ in the middle where the boundary falls. Its range, 708–721, is also off by one, because 722 गुरुप्रिया carries the verse number ॥१३९॥ in its dev field — the same fault as 830 प्रकटाकृतिः ॥१५५॥, which displaced verse 156's range in the same way. Read correctly: verse 138 is namas 708–713, verse 139 is 714–722, and verse 140 is 723–727.
