## अष्टमूर्तिरजाजैत्री लोकयात्राविधायिनी । एकाकिनी भूमरूपा निर्द्वैता द्वैतवर्जिता

*aṣṭamūrtir ajājaitrī lokayātrāvidhāyinī । ekākinī bhūmarūpā nirdvaitā dvaitavarjitā*

Verse 131, namas 662–668.

662. अष्टमूर्तिः → अष्ट-मूर्तिः

अष्ट = eight
मूर्तिः = form, embodiment
"She of the eight forms."

Vigraha: अष्टौ मूर्तयः यस्याः सन्ति सा।

The dev field reads अष्टमूर्तिर, having gained the र् of its own visarga at the joint with the following nama.

Bhāskararāya gives four eightfold sets. The Matsya Purāṇa's is a list of goddesses: "wealth, intelligence, earth, nourishment, Gaurī, contentment, radiance, stability — protect me, O Sarasvatī, by these eight forms." The Yoga Śāstra's is a list of Selves: embodied, inner, supreme, unstained, pure, wisdom, great and elemental — "thus there are eight Selves." Then two versions of Śiva's eight forms: the five elements with sun, moon and jīva; and the Viṣṇu Purāṇa's sun, water, earth, fire, air, ether, the sacrificing Brāhmaṇa, and the moon.

That last set is the one 883 यजमानस्वरूपिणी turned on, where the eighth of Śiva's forms was "sometimes the sacrificer and sometimes Ātman," and the nama took both at once. मूर्ति for the sixth time — 116, 581, 603, 628, 992, and here.

663. अजाजैत्री → अजा-जैत्री

अजा = the unborn; also the she-goat; and here, per the commentary, ignorance
जैत्री = conquering, victorious (vṛddhi derivative of जेतृ, from जि "to conquer")
"The Conqueror of the Unborn."

Vigraha: अजायाः जैत्री।

The dev field reads जाजैली — two faults. The initial अ went with the preceding sandhi (अष्टमूर्तिः + अजाजैत्री → अष्टमूर्तिरजाजैत्री, the visarga becoming र् before the vowel), and जैत्री has become जैली, a त्र read as ल. The gloss preserves the reading in transliteration, "(Ajājaitrī)."

Bhāskararāya's gloss is compressed but exact. He cites Śvetāśvatara 4.5 — "Ajā, the one, red, white and black" — and then says "the meaning is, as she is wisdom she destroys ignorance." So अजा here is not She but what She conquers: the unborn Prakṛti of that verse, taken as avidyā.

That verse has stood twice before. At 866 अजा it made Her the unborn, and Bhāskararāya noted there that it turns on the double sense, unborn and she-goat, reading Prakṛti as both; at 961 गुणातीता its three colours were the guṇas she transcends. Here the same अजा is the enemy. So the text uses one word of one Śruti verse three ways: as Her name, as what she transcends, and as what she defeats.

664. लोकयात्राविधायिनी → लोक-यात्रा-विधायिनी

लोक = a world — per the commentary, the fourteen worlds
यात्रा = a going, a course, a journey; and per the commentary, destruction or protection
विधायिनी = she who ordains, arranges, brings about (वि + धा "to place")
"She who ordains the course of the worlds."

Vigraha: लोकयात्रां विधातीति।

The gloss on यात्रा is odd and worth recording as given: "Lokas, the fourteen worlds; Yātrā, destruction or protection." So the word for a journey is read as covering both the maintaining and the ending of the worlds' course.

विधायिनी is वि + धा, the same धा behind धात्री at 935 and निधि at 567 — placing, and here arranging.

665. एकाकिनी → एकाकिनी

एकाकिनी = alone, solitary (एक "one" with the suffix आकिन्, feminine ङीप्)
"The Solitary One."

Vigraha: एका एव एकाकिनी।

"Because she is without a second." Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.2 is cited, and the choice is pointed: "he feared; therefore any one who is lonely fears. He thought, why should I fear, since there is none beside me — thence his fear passed away." So the verse used to establish Her solitude is one about solitude producing fear and then curing it.

The Devī Purāṇa supplies the positive form: "alone she consumes the worlds, alone she established them, alone she creates the universe, hence she is called the one."

That Bṛhadāraṇyaka passage is the neighbour of 1.4.3, which 878 स्वात्मारामा quoted for the opposite point — "he was not happy; therefore the lonely one is never happy. He desired a second." So the text uses two consecutive verses of one Upaniṣad for solitude sufficient and solitude insufficient.

Bhāskararāya drops a counting marker: the twenty-fifth verse divides thirty-four names.

666. भूमरूपा → भूम-रूपा

भूम = plenitude, fullness, the infinite (from भू "to be" — भूमन्)
रूपा = form
"She whose form is the plenum."

Vigraha: भूम रूपं यस्याः सा।

Vedānta Sūtra 1.3.8 establishes that भूमा means Brahman, and the passage behind it is Chāndogya VII.23: "where one does not see anything else, nor hears anything else — that which is infinite is bliss."

Then Bhāskararāya sets this nama against the last as a deliberate contrast: "the previous name means she is one; this, she is many." And the Devī Purāṇa's illustration is a chain of four similes, all of one thing taking many appearances without changing: "as the crystal is coloured by the transmission of different colours, so by the qualities Devī is described as Bhūmā. Just as one cloud becomes many retaining the same nature and colours, so Umā. Just as the rain from the sky assumes various tastes according to the soil, so Umā. Just as the wind which is one takes on different odours, fragrant and otherwise, so Umā."

So 665–666 are one and many, and the resolution is the crystal: the multiplicity is in what passes through.

667. निर्द्वैता → निर्-द्वैता

निर् = without, free from (निः)
द्वैता = duality (vṛddhi abstract of द्वि "two")
"She who is without duality."

Vigraha: द्वैतं यस्याः नास्ति सा।

Chāndogya VII.23 again, and now for the other half of it: "when he sees nothing else which is small, that is perishable" — by which, Bhāskararāya says, "the Śruti sets forth the impermanence of duality." So the same passage that gave भूमा its plenitude at 666 gives duality its impermanence here.

668. द्वैतवर्जिता → द्वैत-वर्जिता

द्वैत = duality
वर्जिता = devoid of, excluding (from वृज् "to avoid")
"She who excludes duality."

Vigraha: द्वैतेन वर्जिता।

The gloss is one clause and it explains why the previous nama was not enough: "this refutes the theory that at any time duality is permanent."

So 667 and 668 are not a repetition. 667 says She is without duality; 668 denies that duality is ever permanent — the first about Her, the second about duality. This is the tightest pair of the verse, and वर्जिता is the word of 652 वेद्यवर्जिता, where what was excluded was the knowable "because they are not eternal," the same argument.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and four of them are about one and many.

665 and 666 are set as a contrast by the commentary itself — she is one, she is many — and the Devī Purāṇa's four similes resolve it by putting the multiplicity in the medium: crystal, cloud, rain, wind. Then 667 and 668 deny duality twice over, of Her and then of itself.

The Upaniṣadic handling is worth marking. Chāndogya VII.23 supplies both 666 and 667, once for the plenum and once for duality's impermanence. And 665's Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.2 stands immediately before the 1.4.3 that 878 स्वात्मारामा used to argue that the lonely one is never happy — so two adjacent verses of one text serve opposite conclusions in this Sahasranāma.

Textual note. 662 has gained the र् of its own visarga and 663 has lost its initial अ to the same joint — the familiar mis-division. 663 also reads जैली for जैत्री, a त्र misread as ल, so this nama carries two independent faults; only its transliterated gloss preserves the word.

---

## अन्नदा वसुदा वृद्धा ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी । बृहती ब्राह्मणी ब्राह्मी ब्रह्मानन्दा बलिप्रिया

*annadā vasudā vṛddhā brahmātmaikyasvarūpiṇī । bṛhatī brāhmaṇī brāhmī brahmānandā balipriyā*

Verse 132, namas 669–677.

669. अन्नदा → अन्न-दा

अन्न = food (from अद् "to eat")
दा = giving (from दा "to give")
"The Giver of food."

Vigraha: अन्नं ददातीति अन्नदा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama; the citation stands under 670, where the two are taken together.

670. वसुदा → वसु-दा

वसु = wealth, goods; also a class of gods
दा = giving
"The Giver of wealth."

Vigraha: वसु ददातीति वसुदा।

Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.24 is quoted for the pair, and it supplies both namas in one clause: "this indeed is the great unborn Self, the giver of food and the giver of wealth. He who knows this obtains food and wealth."

So 669 and 670 are one Upaniṣadic phrase divided into two namas — the same procedure as 992–993, where Gītā 10.11's compassion and lamp became two namas, and 669–670's source likewise calls that Self अज, unborn, which is 866 अजा and 663's conquered अजा.

The bare दा twice running, as at 639 वरदा, 654 योगदा and 953 शर्मदा.

671. वृद्धा → वृद्धा

वृद्धा = grown, aged, old; also increased, expanded (past participle of वृध् "to grow")
"The Ancient."

Vigraha: वृद्धा पुराणी।

Śvetāśvatara 4.3 is cited: "thou, as an old man, totterest along on thy staff." Then three glosses of वृद्ध, and they pull in different directions: "the oldest of all; or expanded in the form of the Universe; or she nourishes the world."

The root वृध् is "to grow," so वृद्ध is what has grown — and the three glosses are its three ends: grown old, grown large, and causing growth. The same root gave वर्धिनी at 886 and 959, where at 959 Bhāskararāya reversed it into a cutting.

672. ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी → ब्रह्म-आत्म-ऐक्य-स्व-रूपिणी

ब्रह्म = Brahman; and per the second reading, Śiva
आत्म = the Self; and per that reading, the jīva
ऐक्य = oneness, identity (vṛddhi abstract of एक)
स्व = own; and per that reading, the Haṃsa mantra
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is the oneness of Brahman and the Self."

Vigraha: ब्रह्मात्मनोः ऐक्यं स्वरूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi at both joints: ब्रह्म + आत्म → ब्रह्मात्म (आ by 6.1.101), then आत्म + ऐक्य → आत्मैक्य by vṛddhi (अ + ऐ → ऐ, Pāṇini 6.1.88 वृद्धिरेचि).

The nama is 999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी's construction exactly — two terms with ऐक्य and रूपिणी — and Bhāskararāya's second reading makes the parallel explicit. ब्रह्म is Śiva, आत्म the jīva, and स्व is the Haṃsa mantra "which unites the souls with Śiva."

The Sūta Saṃhitā (IV.7.9–12) is then quoted, and it derives the union from the mantra's two syllables: the जीव-mantra is "I," meaning the embodied soul; the Śakti-mantra is स and indicates the supreme Lord, "for Parameśvara is known to be in every object. From the greatest to the smallest the whole universe animate and inanimate is born, lives and dies in the supreme Lord. The Jīva who manifests through earthly existence is also the supreme Lord."

That is the same Haṃsa derivation 999 gives, where the Sūta Saṃhitā (4.7.2) took स and ह as Śakti and Bīja and concluded that "this supreme mantra signifies Śiva as well as Śakti." So the two ऐक्य-namas rest on one mantra, three hundred namas apart, and Bhāskararāya cross-refers here to the Triśatī (173).

673. बृहती → बृहती

बृहती = great, large (feminine of बृहत्, from बृह् "to grow, to swell"); also a metre of thirty-six syllables
"The Great."

Vigraha: बृहती महती।

बृह् is the root behind ब्रह्म — 822 ब्रह्म was glossed "that which expands, grows vast" — so this nama and the ब्रह्म-namas around it share a root, which is presumably why they stand together.

Bhāskararāya's note is metrical and then dialectical. बृहती is a metre of thirty-six syllables; and this does not contradict the Kūrma Purāṇa's "thou art the Gāyatrī among the metres," because "Devī is both the metres." He then extends the same resolution to a second conflict: Gītā 10.35 has "I am Bṛhatsāman among the Sāmans," the Kūrma Purāṇa "I am Jyeṣṭhā Sāman among the Sāmans" — and both stand, with the Bṛhatsāman identified as what is praised in the Ṛk beginning सत्वन्नः and the Jyeṣṭhasāman in the two Ṛks उदित्यम् and चित्रम्.

Metres as namas have appeared twice already — प्रतिष्ठा the sixteen-syllabled at 829, सुप्रतिष्ठा the twenty-syllabled at 660 — and both times the note was Bhāskararāya's afterthought. Here it is the substance.

674. ब्राह्मणी → ब्राह्मणी

ब्राह्मणी = a Brāhmaṇa's wife; a Brāhmaṇa woman; and per the Viśva, also a harlot and a medicinal plant
"The Brāhmaṇī."

Vigraha: ब्राह्मणस्य पत्नी ब्राह्मणी।

The reading Bhāskararāya develops is that She is Śiva's wife "because Śiva belongs to the Brāhmaṇa caste" — and he assembles authority for the claim, which is not a common one. Chāndogya 8.14.1: "thou art Brāhmaṇa among the Devas, I am the Brāhmaṇa among men; he who thinks thus attains Brahman." The Parāśara, Āditya, Kūrma, Vasiṣṭha and Liṅga Purāṇas together: "the divine Śambhu, the consort of Devī, is Brāhmaṇa and is the deity of Brāhmaṇas. A Brāhmaṇa especially should take refuge in Rudra, the Lord." And the Śivatattvaviveka quoting the Viṣṇu Bhāgavata for the conclusion, "Śiva is proved to be a Brāhmaṇa."

The Vipras had been dear to Her at 887 and Her form at 888, where "whether he is ignorant or learned, the Brāhmaṇa is my body." Here the caste is Her husband's.

675. ब्राह्मी → ब्राह्मी

ब्राह्मी = belonging to Brahman or Brahmā; the female counterpart of Brahmā; also speech
"Brāhmī."

Vigraha: ब्रह्मणः शक्तिः ब्राह्मी।

The whole commentary is seven words: "the female counterpart of Brahman, or speech."

The text has now named Her by three feminines of the same stem within a few namas — ब्राह्मणी at 674, ब्राह्मी here — and ब्रह्माणी at 821, where the आणी suffix took its ण by ṇatva. At 907 Bhāskararāya listed Brāhmī as one of the three kinds of भावना (Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Akṣara), and at 948 She was "the fifth in the order of Brāhmī and the rest."

676. ब्रह्मानन्दा → ब्रह्म-आनन्दा

ब्रह्म = Brahman
आनन्दा = bliss (आ + नन्द् "to rejoice")
"The Bliss of Brahman."

Vigraha: ब्रह्मणः आनन्दः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: ब्रह्म + आनन्दा → ब्रह्मानन्दा (आ by 6.1.101).

Two readings, and the first is careful about who the bliss is for: "the unconditioned Brahman is itself bliss to the conditioned one" — so the bliss is Brahman as experienced from below. Or, more simply, "she is the possessor of the bliss of Brahman."

आनन्द had been half of 646 सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी and the whole of 656 योगानन्दा, where yoga's bliss was "the common essence of Śiva and Śakti" and then became sleep.

677. बलिप्रिया → बलि-प्रिया

बलि = strong, mighty; an offering, an oblation; and Bali, the demon-king
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in the mighty."

Vigraha: बलिनः प्रियाः यस्याः सा।

Three readings, and they are quite unlike each other. बलि as the strong: "those who are able to overcome nescience and conquer the enemies, viz., desire and the rest" — so strength is moral, and such men are "fit objects of grace." Or बलि as the king Bali, which brings in the Vāmana incarnation. Or बलि as the accessories of ceremonial worship, the oblation — so She delights in the offering.

प्रिया for the ninth time in the text, and the range of its objects is now wide: the auspicious at 115, sacrifice at 881, the learned at 887, the heroes' assembly at 898, the Sāman at 909, the flower of consciousness at 919, hymns at 927, and here the strong or the oblation.

Note on the verse. Nine namas, and the middle five are a ब्रह्म-cluster held together by the root बृह्, to swell — ब्रह्म, बृहती, ब्राह्मणी, ब्राह्मी, ब्रह्मानन्दा. That is why बृहती stands among them.

669–670 open the verse with an Upaniṣadic phrase split in two: Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.24's "giver of food and giver of wealth" becomes two namas, and its subject is the "great unborn Self."

672 is the doctrinal centre, and it is 999's construction three hundred namas early — two terms joined by ऐक्य and predicated with रूपिणी. Both namas are then grounded in the same Haṃsa mantra by the same Sūta Saṃhitā, so the text's penultimate nama and this one are one claim in two vocabularies: Brahman with Ātman here, Śiva with Śakti there.

673's metrical note is the fullest of the three in the text, and its method is worth marking: two apparent conflicts of authority — Bṛhatī against Gāyatrī, Bṛhatsāman against Jyeṣṭhasāman — resolved the same way, by saying She is both.

---

## भाषारूपा बृहत्सेना भावाभावविवर्जिता । सुखाराध्या शुभकरी शोभनासुलभागतिः

*bhāṣārūpā bṛhatsenā bhāvābhāvavivarjitā । sukhārādhyā śubhakarī śobhanāsulabhāgatiḥ*

Verse 133, namas 678–683.

678. भाषारूपा → भाषा-रूपा

भाषा = speech, a spoken language (from भाष् "to speak")
रूपा = form
"She whose form is language."

Vigraha: भाषा रूपं यस्याः सा।

"That is Sanskrit, Prakrit and other languages. Or she is adored in different languages" — and the verse Bhāskararāya quotes for it is generous about which: "some praise you in Sanskrit, some in foreign (Mleccha) languages, others in the vulgar tongue, and some others in Prākṛta."

Sastry's footnote lists the bhāṣās: Laukika, Vaidika, Prākṛta, Māgadha, Śaurasenī, Paiśāca, Drāviḍa, Gauḍa and others.

The nama is worth setting beside the letter-namas — 577 मातृकावर्णरूपिणी, 850 वर्णरूपिणी, 529 सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता — where Her form is the alphabet. Those are all Sanskrit varṇas; this one admits the vernaculars and the Mleccha tongues, and says worship in them reaches Her.

679. बृहत्सेना → बृहत्-सेना

बृहत् = great, vast (from बृह् "to swell")
सेना = an army, a host
"She of the mighty army."

Vigraha: बृहती सेना यस्याः सा।

The commentary is one clause: "Bṛhatsenā is also the name of a certain king."

सेना is the word of 65 भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्तशक्तिसेनासमन्विता, where the army of Śaktis was girded to slay Bhaṇḍāsura — so the mighty host has a referent in the text's own narrative. And बृहत् returns from बृहती six namas back.

680. भावाभावविवर्जिता → भाव-अभाव-विवर्जिता

भाव = existence, being; substance, quality
अभाव = non-existence, absence
विवर्जिता = wholly devoid of, excluding (वि + वृज् "to avoid")
"She who is devoid of both being and non-being."

Vigraha: भावेन अभावेन च विवर्जिता।

Sandhi: भाव + अभाव → भावाभाव (आ by 6.1.101).

Bhāskararāya raises the obvious objection himself and answers it, which is the interest of the entry. भाव is substance and quality; अभाव is antecedent non-existence and the rest, one of the four kinds of non-existence recognised in the schools. "As abhāva is non-existence, it may be said that Devī cannot be said to be devoid of it" — you cannot be free of nothing.

The answer is Vyāsa's, from the Sūta Saṃhitā (4.2.8–9), and it turns on the substratum: "destruction of imagined things means their substratum alone remains. For destruction is the non-existence of the existent, and the existence of the non-existent. The substratum is different from these two, viz., existence and non-existence. The substratum is not destroyed, because it is ever real."

So both terms are denied of Her by making Her the substratum of which they are predicated. This is 661 सदसद्रूपधारिणी from the other side — there She bore the form of सत् and असत्, here She is devoid of both — and the two namas are eighteen apart.

681. सुखाराध्या → सुख-आराध्या

सुख = happiness, ease (traditionally सु + ख, the good axle-hole)
आराध्या = to be worshipped, propitiated (आ + राध्, gerundive यत्)
"She who is easily worshipped."

Vigraha: सुखेन आराध्या।

Sandhi: सुख + आराध्या → सुखाराध्या (आ by 6.1.101). The computed pada reads सुखा-राध्या, dividing one letter late.

सुख is glossed practically: "without bodily pain by fasting and the rest, and without restrictions on the mode of meditation." So the ease is the absence of austerity and of rubric both. And the authority is a scene rather than a rule — in the Kūrma Purāṇa the Lord says to Himavat, "if you are unable to meditate on my eternal supreme form," and then describes an easy mode of worship.

आराध्या for the fourth time — 870, 918, 923, 977 — and the qualifications there were inwardness, consciousness as oblation, competence-or-incompetence, and the ten mudrās. Here the qualification is that none is needed.

682. शुभकरी → शुभ-करी

शुभ = auspicious, good, bright (from शुभ् "to shine")
करी = she who makes (from कृ "to do")
"She who does good."

Vigraha: शुभं करोतीति शुभकरी।

The gloss extends 681's leniency: "that is, even to him who but imperfectly worships her."

शुभ् is the root of शोभना in the next nama and of 972 आशोभना, and करी of 968 सुखकरी — which pairs सुख with कृ as this nama pairs शुभ with it, and 681 has just used सुख. The three namas 681–683 are built out of two roots.

683. शोभनासुलभागतिः → शोभना-सुलभा-गतिः

शोभना = auspicious, splendid; and per the commentary, salvation
सुलभा = easily obtained (सु + लभ्)
गतिः = a going, a way, a path; a state; a means (from गम् "to go")
"She who is the auspicious and easily attained path."

Vigraha: शोभना सुलभा गतिः यस्याः सा।

The members are glossed: "Śobhana, salvation and the rest; Sulabha, easy modes of worship; Gati, result or means" — with the Viśva giving गति as road, state, knowledge, journey and means. The Kūrma Purāṇa: "she alone is the highest goal of the movements of all creatures."

Then three divisions, and they disagree about the sense. Some divide the nama into two — शोभनगति and सुलभगति — to avoid repeating शोभन, which had already stood at 462. Some read the second as असुलभागति, "not easily attainable," on the ground that "there is no return from that state which puts an end to birth"; and the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa is quoted through the Triśatī (112) for how hard it is — "the fifteen-syllabled Mantra is to be attained by him alone whose present birth is his last, or by Śaṃkara himself." Or असुलभागति means the attainment of human birth and the like, hard to get, which worship of Devī makes auspicious.

So the same string gives easily attained and not easily attained, and the verse holds both against 681's claim that She is easy to worship. गति is also the sense of 859 काष्ठा, where She was the goal, "the finishing-post."

Note on the verse. Six namas: form, army, a metaphysical denial, and then three on ease.

681–683 make the run, and they are the text's clearest statement that access is cheap: worship needs no fasting and no rubric, She does good even to those who worship imperfectly, and the path is auspicious and easily found. Then 683's own alternatives take it back — some read the path as not easily attained, and the Triśatī says the mantra comes only to one in his last birth, or to Śaṃkara.

That is the same unresolved tension the text carries elsewhere between 869 क्षिप्रप्रसादिनी, quickly pleased, and 990 अभ्यासातिशयज्ञाता, known only by unremitting practice. Here it happens inside one nama.

680 is the philosophically careful entry. Bhāskararāya states the objection — you cannot be devoid of non-existence — and answers with the substratum, which is what remains when imagined things are destroyed and is "different from these two."

---

## राजराजेश्वरी राज्यदायिनी राज्यवल्लभा । राजत्कृपा राजपीठनिवेशितनिजाश्रिता

*rājarājeśvarī rājyadāyinī rājyavallabhā । rājatkṛpā rājapīṭhaniveśitanijāśritā*

Verse 134, namas 684–688.

684. राजराजेश्वरी → राज-राज-ईश्वरी

राज = a king (राजन्, from राज् "to shine, to rule")
राजराज = king of kings — per the commentary, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, or Kubera
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady
"Sovereign of the king of kings."

Vigraha: राजराजस्य ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: राज + ईश्वरी → राजेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

Two identifications of the राजराज: "Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the rest, who are the king of the Devas"; or Kubera. Both have standing in the text — the first is the group that becomes Her couch at 947 and Her chain of command at 995; the second is Kubera, of whom 885 धनाध्यक्षा said that "there is no difference between the worshipper and the worshipped," so his office is hers.

Rājarājeśvarī is also the name under which She is most commonly worshipped in Śrīvidyā, and the text has used it once already: at 840 मूलविग्रहरूपिणी, मूलविग्रह was glossed as "the Rājarājeśvarī Śakti, root of all the other śaktis." So a name of hers there defined a technical term; here it is the nama.

ईश्वरी for the ninth turn of ईश् in the text.

685. राज्यदायिनी → राज्य-दायिनी

राज्य = kingdom, dominion, sovereignty (from राजन्)
दायिनी = she who gives (दा + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"The Bestower of dominion."

Vigraha: राज्यं ददातीति राज्यदायिनी।

The gloss specifies what dominion: "Rājya, dominion over Vaikuṇṭha, Kailāsa and the rest." So the kingdoms in her gift are the gods' own heavens, not earthly ones — which is consistent with 684 making her sovereign over their sovereigns.

दायिनी for the sixth time — 117, 625, 851, 926, 989, and here.

686. राज्यवल्लभा → राज्य-वल्लभा

राज्य = dominion; and per the commentary, the rulers of those dominions
वल्लभा = beloved, dear; a favourite (from वल्ल्)
"She who delights in dominion."

Vigraha: राज्यं वल्लभं यस्याः सा।

The second reading takes राज्य as the rulers rather than the realms, "because their abode is said to be in the Śrīcakra" — and the Lalitāstavaratna (49) locates them: "between the thirteenth and fourteenth walls there are lakes of sapphire. We adore the protectors of that region with their wives."

So Brahmā and the rest are placed inside the diagram, between two of its enclosures, with their wives. That is the same move 947 made with the couch and 995 with the hierarchy — the gods given a position relative to Her — but here the position is architectural.

वल्लभा is the word of 54 स्वाधीनवल्लभा, where Her beloved was wholly won to her.

687. राजत्कृपा → राजत्-कृपा

राजत् = shining, radiant (present participle of राज् "to shine")
कृपा = compassion, pity (from कृप् "to lament, to pity")
"She whose compassion shines forth."

Vigraha: राजती कृपा यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

राज् means both to shine and to rule, and this verse uses both: राज- in 684–686 is the king, राजत् here is the shining. The compound puts compassion in the visible register — not felt but radiating.

कृपा is the word of 992 अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः only by sense, not by root; करुणा there, दया at 581, कृपा here — three words for compassion in three namas of the text, each in a different compound-shape.

688. राजपीठनिवेशितनिजाश्रिता → राज-पीठ-निवेशित-निज-आश्रिता

राज = king, royal
पीठ = a seat, a throne
निवेशित = caused to sit, installed, established (नि + विश् "to enter," causative)
निज = one's own
आश्रिता = those who have taken refuge, dependants (आ + श्रि "to lean on")
"She who installs her own dependants upon royal thrones."

Vigraha: राजपीठे निवेशिताः निजाश्रिताः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: निज + आश्रिता → निजाश्रिता (आ by 6.1.101).

The gloss names the thrones: "that is, Indra's and other thrones." So what She gives her refugees is the seats of the gods — which is 685's dominion over Vaikuṇṭha and Kailāsa, now with the recipients specified as her own dependants.

आश्रित is from आ + श्रि, to lean upon — so an आश्रित is one who leans, and the nama's claim is that leaning on Her ends in a throne. पीठ is the word of 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी, where the fifty-one pīṭhas were Her form and were set in the places of the mātṛkās; here it is furniture.

Note on the verse. Five namas, four of them on राज- and all five on sovereignty. It is the most sustained treatment of kingship in the text.

The sequence is a graded transfer of power. 684 makes Her sovereign over the king of kings; 685 has her give away dominion over Vaikuṇṭha and Kailāsa; 686 places the gods who hold those dominions inside the Śrīcakra, between the thirteenth and fourteenth walls, with their wives; 688 seats her own dependants on Indra's throne. What begins as her rank ends as her patronage.

687 interrupts with compassion, and the interruption is done by the same root: राज् is both to rule and to shine, and the verse uses the ruling sense four times and the shining sense once.

---

## राज्यलक्ष्मीः कोशनाथा चतुरङ्गबलेश्वरी । साम्राज्यदायिनी सत्यसन्धा सागरमेखला

*rājyalakṣmīḥ kośanāthā caturaṅgabaleśvarī । sāmrājyadāyinī satyasandhā sāgaramekhalā*

Verse 135, namas 689–694.

689. राज्यलक्ष्मीः → राज्य-लक्ष्मीः

राज्य = kingdom, dominion
लक्ष्मीः = fortune, prosperity; Lakṣmī
"The Fortune of kingdoms."

Vigraha: राज्यस्य लक्ष्मीः।

The whole commentary is a cross-reference: "the Mantra of Rājyalakṣmī is described in the Tantrarāja." So the nama names a deity with a mantra of her own, as आत्मविद्या, महाविद्या and श्रीविद्या did at 583–585.

Lakṣmī has stood at 590, where crores of her were made handmaids by a glance, and at 614, where one of her held a fly-whisk on Her left.

690. कोशनाथा → कोश-नाथा

कोश = a treasury, a store; a sheath, a covering; also a dictionary
नाथा = mistress, protectress (from नाथ्)
"Mistress of the treasury."

Vigraha: कोशस्य नाथा।

index.html carries the same single sentence in this nama's gloss and body, and it is cut off mid-list: "Kośa may mean the five sheaths, viz. Annamaya—". The five kośas are the sheaths of the Taittirīya — annamaya, prāṇamaya, manomaya, vijñānamaya, ānandamaya — so She is mistress of those as well as of a treasury.

That set has appeared before: at 821 ब्रह्माणी, Bhāskararāya's first reading was ब्रह्मा + अणि, "tail of a bird," making Her "the Brahman which forms the tail of the ānandamaya sheath" on the Vedānta Sūtra's ānandamaya section. And at 948 पञ्चमी She was "the last in the deities of the five sheaths."

कोश in its lexicographical sense is what the text quotes constantly — the Viśva and the Amara are कोशs — so a nama meaning "mistress of dictionaries" is available and nobody takes it.

नाथा returns from 612 कलानाथा and, as दण्डनाथा, from 70.

691. चतुरङ्गबलेश्वरी → चतुर्-अङ्ग-बल-ईश्वरी

चतुर् = four
अङ्ग = a limb, a division — चतुरङ्ग, having four divisions
बल = force, an army
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady
"Sovereign of the fourfold army."

Vigraha: चतुरङ्गबलस्य ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: बल + ईश्वरी → बलेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

चतुरङ्गबल is the standard term for a complete army: "cavalry, elephants, chariots and infantry" — the four arms, which are also the four kinds of piece in caturaṅga, the game. Bhāskararāya gives the military sense and then two others: the four kinds of military array; or the four Vyūhas, "according to the Vaiṣṇavas, Vāsudeva and the rest; to the Śaivas and Śāktas their respective four Vyūhas."

And a fourth, from the Bahvṛca Upaniṣad: the Person in the body, the Person in the metre, the Person in the Veda, and the Great Person. That is the same fourfold set 929 श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा gave when it read श्रुति as the numeral four — "her glory is experienced in four ways, the Person in the body, the Person in the metres, the Person in the scriptures, and the great Person as described in the Bahvṛca Upaniṣad." So the army of four divisions and the four Persons are one word.

Her elephants and cavalry were named in the war-verses at 66 and 67, under Sampatkarī and Aśvārūḍhā.

692. साम्राज्यदायिनी → साम्राज्य-दायिनी

साम्राज्य = universal sovereignty, empire (vṛddhi derivative of सम्राज्)
दायिनी = she who gives
"The Bestower of empire."

Vigraha: साम्राज्यं ददातीति।

Bhāskararāya defines the term by the rite that establishes it: "Sāmrājya, the state of a king who performs the Rājasūya sacrifice, or a king of the earth, or the king of kings." The Agni Purāṇa and the Kośas: "he who has performed the Rājasūya sacrifice, one who is the lord of the earth and who rules over kings, is called Samrāṭ."

So empire is not extent but a consecration — and this nama is the one 927 स्तोत्रप्रिया cited as the text's own instance of विभूति, the rehearsing of glory, among the six marks of a stotra.

साम्राज्य had stood at 582 महासाम्राज्यशालिनी, where She was resplendent with it; here she gives it away. दायिनी for the seventh time.

693. सत्यसन्धा → सत्य-सन्धा

सत्य = truth, reality (from सत्, present participle of अस् "to be")
सन्धा = an agreement, a compact, a promise (सम् + धा "to place together")
"She whose compact is truth."

Vigraha: सत्या सन्धा यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

सन्धा is सम् + धा, a placing-together — the same धा that gives निधि at 567 and 604, धात्री at 935, and विधायिनी at 664. A compact is literally what is put together between parties, so सत्यसन्धा is one whose agreements hold.

The word is a standing epithet of Rāma and of kings generally, which suits its position: this verse and the last are about sovereignty, and truthfulness of promise is the royal virtue.

694. सागरमेखला → सागर-मेखला

सागर = the ocean (said to be named from Sagara, whose sons dug it)
मेखला = a girdle, a belt, a waistband
"She who is girdled by the ocean."

Vigraha: सागरः मेखला यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The compound is an earth-epithet: the ocean is the girdle of the land, so सागरमेखला is a standing description of the earth, and applying it to Her identifies Her with it. That identification is made outright at 955 धरा, the earth as she who bears, and at 718 मही in the verse after next.

And the figure belongs to this verse's theme. A girdle of ocean is what a universal sovereign's realm has, so the nama closes a run about empire by giving her the emperor's boundary.

Note on the verse. Six namas, continuing the sovereignty of verse 134 and then turning.

689–692 are all of rule: the fortune of kingdoms, the treasury, the fourfold army, the bestowal of empire. And two of them are lexically double in a way that matters — कोश is both treasury and the five sheaths of the self, and चतुरङ्गबल is both a complete army and the four Persons of the Bahvṛca Upaniṣad. So the martial vocabulary is being read twice over, once as statecraft and once as doctrine.

693 and 694 then close differently. Truth of compact is the royal virtue rather than a royal possession; and the ocean-girdle is the emperor's boundary, but it is also the standing epithet of the earth, which the text identifies with Her at 955 and 718.

692 is also the text's own example of विभूति, the rehearsing of glory, by Bhāskararāya's reckoning at 927.

---

## दीक्षिता दैत्यशमनी सर्वलोकवशंकरी । सर्वार्थदात्री सावित्री सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी

*dīkṣitā daityaśamanī sarvalokavaśaṃkarī । sarvārthadātrī sāvitrī saccidānandarūpiṇī*

Verse 136, namas 695–700.

695. दीक्षिता → दीक्षिता

दीक्षिता = initiated, consecrated (from दीक्ष् "to consecrate")
"The Initiated."

Vigraha: दीक्षां प्राप्ता दीक्षिता।

Bhāskararāya gives two derivations, and both make दीक्षा a compound of giving and destroying. The Atharva Brāhmaṇa is cited for the word's standing — "next, therefore Dīkṣā, from which root Dīkṣita is derived; they call the man who is initiated Dīkṣita." Then the syllabic reading: दी wisdom, क्षि to give.

And the Parānanda Tantra makes it double: "out of compassion she imparts (दीयते) to her disciples, and consequently she destroys (क्षीयते) their sins; hence she is called Dīkṣita." So दीक्षा is giving-and-destroying in one word — what is given is the mantra, what is destroyed is sin.

That makes the nama active rather than passive despite the participle: not she who has been initiated but she who initiates. दीक्षा had appeared at 883 यजमानस्वरूपिणी, where Śiva's seventh form was the sacrificer "and his wife is called Dīkṣā."

696. दैत्यशमनी → दैत्य-शमनी

दैत्य = a Daitya, a demon — son of Diti
शमनी = she who quiets, subdues, extinguishes (from शम् "to be quiet," causative)
"The Subduer of the Daityas."

Vigraha: दैत्यान् शमयतीति दैत्यशमनी।

The gloss is three words: "Daityas, Bhaṇḍa and the rest." So the demons are the ones the text's own war-narrative named at 65–82, and this nama is that campaign in summary.

शमनी is the word of 551 सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी, where what was quieted was disease, and the root of 963 शमात्मिका, where शम was tranquillity itself and Bhāskararāya defined it as "tranquillising the activity of the world." Here the tranquillising is military — and that is the same range as 599 दैत्यहन्त्री, where the demons were slain rather than quieted.

697. सर्वलोकवशंकरी → सर्व-लोक-वशम्-करी

सर्व = all
लोक = a world
वशम् = under control, into subjection
करी = she who makes
"She who brings all the worlds under her sway."

Vigraha: सर्वलोकान् वशं करोतीति।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

वशंकरी is the formation of 978 त्रिपुराश्रीवशंकरी, where what She subdued was the deity of the Śrīcakra's fifth enclosure — and वशंकरी is also the name of one of the ten mudrās invoked at 977. Here the object is everything.

698. सर्वार्थदात्री → सर्व-अर्थ-दात्री

सर्व = all — per the commentary, the four objects of human desire
अर्थ = an object, a purpose, a thing sought; also wealth
दात्री = the giver (दा with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्)
"The Giver of all objects."

Vigraha: सर्वान् अर्थान् ददातीति।

Sandhi: सर्व + अर्थ → सर्वार्थ (आ by 6.1.101).

सर्व is specified as "the four objects of human desire" — dharma, artha, kāma, mokṣa. And the Devī Purāṇa is quoted with a different form of the name: "in all the works she gives righteousness and the other desired objects, hence she is called by all by the word Sarvārthasādhinī, fulfiller of all objects."

दात्री is the तृ agent-noun, as at 832 प्राणदात्री — the text's commonest formation. And the four objects had stood at 873 त्रिवर्गनिलया as three, dharma, artha and kāma, where the fourth was not counted.

699. सावित्री → सावित्री

सावित्री = the begetter, she who brings forth (feminine of सवितृ, the Sun, from सू "to generate"); also the Sāvitrī verse
"Sāvitrī."

Vigraha: सवितुः पत्नी सावित्री। or प्रसवित्री सावित्री।

The derivations are all of generation, and Bhāskararāya gives four. She is the wife of the creator of the universe, the supreme Śiva — the Viṣṇudharmottara, "he is called Savitā because he creates beings." The Bharadvāja Smṛti, "as she gives light to the sun, or because she creates the Universe, she is called Sāvitrī," which makes her prior to the sun rather than its consort. The Devī Purāṇa, "Devī is worshipped by Devas, and worshipped by Yoga and in the Scriptures, and she is naturally pure, hence she is called Sāvitrī." And the Devī Bhāgavata's root-play: "the root सृ means flowing; from the flow arises brightness, hence she is called Sāvitrī."

The Padma Purāṇa makes her the deity worshipped at Puṣkaratīrtha — the fourth pīṭha-identification in the text, after Viśālākṣī at Benares (936), Mīnākṣī at Madhurā (915), Kātyāyanī at Oḍḍiyāna (556), Gaurī at Kanyakubja (635) and Lalitā at Prayāga (1000).

The nama is 826 प्रसवित्री without its प्र — there "the Progenitrix," here the same feminine of सवितृ standing alone, and Bhāskararāya's gloss there was likewise that She is the begetting power of which the Sun is the masculine figure.

A counting marker: the twenty-sixth verse divides thirty-six names.

700. सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी → सत्-चित्-आनन्द-रूपिणी

सत् = being, existence
चित् = consciousness
आनन्द = bliss
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is Being, Consciousness and Bliss."

Vigraha: सत् चित् आनन्दः च रूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: सत् + चित् → सच्चित्, the त् assimilating to च् before च् (Pāṇini 8.4.40, स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः); then चित् + आनन्द → चिदानन्द, the त् voicing before the vowel.

index.html's body for this nama is not commentary but a colophon, and it is worth having: "thus ends the eighth Kalā, called Bhogadā, with the seventh hundred in the Saubhāgyabhāskara composed by Bhāsurānanda," followed by the heading "Eighth Hundred."

So this nama closes the seventh hundred. The text preserves two other such colophons — at 900 नैष्कर्म्या, closing the ninth hundred with the Bodhinī Kalā, and at 1000 ललिताम्बिका, closing the tenth with the eleventh Kalā called Dhāriṇī. Three of the ten division-points survive, and the kalā-numbering runs ahead of the hundred-numbering in each: the eighth kalā closes the seventh hundred here, the eleventh closes the tenth at the end.

The triad itself has been assembled piecemeal across the text. At 907 तत्त्वमयी Sat, Cit and Ānanda were the three tattvas from which the thirty-six descend, with Śiva and Śakti belonging to Ānanda, Sadāśiva and Īśvara and Śuddhavidyā to Cit, and everything from Māyā to earth to Sat. At 646 सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी two of the three stood without Cit; and Cit had been the whole of 918–919's चैतन्य. Here the three are named together and complete.

Note on the verse. Six namas, and the verse is organised as a descent from act to essence.

695–698 are all things She does: initiates, subdues demons, brings the worlds under sway, gives every object of desire. Then 699 names her as the begetting power, and 700 as Being, Consciousness and Bliss.

695 is the best entry. दीक्षा is derived as giving-and-destroying in a single word — दी wisdom with क्षि to give, and the Parānanda Tantra's "she imparts to her disciples and consequently destroys their sins." Initiation is one act with two faces, and the participle दीक्षिता, which should be passive, is read as active.

700 also carries a structural marker rather than a gloss: the colophon closing the seventh hundred, one of three that survive in this text.

---

## देशकालापरिच्छिन्ना सर्वगा सर्वमोहिनी । सरस्वती शास्त्रमयी गुहाम्बा गुह्यरूपिणी

*deśakālāparicchinnā sarvagā sarvamohinī । sarasvatī śāstramayī guhāmbā guhyarūpiṇī*

Verse 137, namas 701–707.

> From 703 to 713 the commentary is continuous: Bhāskararāya runs a single philosophical dialogue about non-duality across eleven namas, each nama being the next move in the argument, with the questions and answers marked as such. That is unlike anything else in the text and the entries below follow it step by step.

701. देशकालापरिच्छिन्ना → देश-काल-अ-परिच्छिन्ना

देश = place, region
काल = time
अ = not (नञ्)
परिच्छिन्ना = cut around, delimited, defined (परि + छिद् "to cut")
"She who is not delimited by place or time."

Vigraha: देशेन कालेन च अपरिच्छिन्ना।

Sandhi: काल + अपरिच्छिन्ना → कालापरिच्छिन्ना (आ by 6.1.101).

Yoga Sūtra 1.26 is cited — "he is the Guru even of the ancients, because he is not defined by time" — with the ancients glossed as Brahmā and the rest, and गुरु as father.

Bhāskararāya then defines the two limitations with precision, and the definitions are logical rather than descriptive. Limitation by place "means the absolute non-existence of a thing in a certain place, saying: this is not here." Limitation by time is "this was not before and it will not exist in future" — a thing having neither antecedence nor succession. And he adds a third, limitation as to things: "relative difference, or mutual non-existence, between things, such as this is here and that is not there." The Saura Saṃhitā: "the Person is omnipresent like ether; as everything except himself is illusory, he is said to be unlimited as to space, time and things."

This is 642 अपरिच्छेद्या in the participle rather than the gerundive — there "not to be circumscribed," and Bhāskararāya's gloss there was four words, "that is as to place and time." Here he spends a paragraph on the same two.

702. सर्वगा → सर्व-गा

सर्व = all
गा = going, pervading (from गम् "to go")
"The All-pervading."

Vigraha: सर्वं गच्छतीति सर्वगा।

"She is inseparably present in all substances." And then a story from the Varāha Purāṇa that makes omnipresence a boon She asked for: while performing penance on the Śveta Mountain in the form of the creative Śakti, Brahmā offered her a boon, and "Devī replies: O holy one, I cannot bear to remain in one place, hence I beg of you to grant me the boon of omnipresence." He grants it — "O thou of all forms, thou shalt become omnipresent" — which Bhāskararāya unpacks: of all forms means nothing is separate from her; omnipresent means her qualified forms will be in all bodies, or she will become the soul of all.

The Devī Purāṇa is then quoted for the doctrine: "she is certainly the Vedas, sacrifices, heaven; all this Universe, animate and inanimate, is pervaded by Devī. She is sacrificed to and she is worshipped."

गा is the bare root-noun of गम्, as at 986 त्रिकोणगा where She went to the triangle. There the going had a destination; here it has none, which is what pervasion is.

703. सर्वमोहिनी → सर्व-मोहिनी

सर्व = all — per the commentary, all ordinary people
मोहिनी = she who bewilders (from मुह् "to be confused," causative)
"The All-bewildering."

Vigraha: सर्वान् मोहयतीति सर्वमोहिनी।

Here the dialogue begins, and Bhāskararāya states the question first: "How can this Devī be said to possess contradictory attributes, such as permanence and impermanence, animation and non-animation? This name answers the above question."

The answer is that the contradiction is in the observer. "She bewilders all the ordinary people, who believe in the reality of the apparent duality — that is, she makes them devoid of the knowledge of Unity. The meaning is that the apparent difference between Brahman and the Universe is illusory."

So the attributes conflict only for those already bewildered, and the bewildering is Hers. The Kūrma Purāṇa has Śiva say it in the first person: "this supreme Śakti is in me and is Brahman itself. This Māyā is dear to me, infinite, by which this world is bewildered. I bewilder the whole Universe with the Devas, Daityas and men; and I create them and I cause them to exist."

मुह् for the fourth time — 868 मुग्धा where She was bewildered, 562 मोहिनी the enchantress, 954 शंभुमोहिनी where the object was Śiva, and here where it is everyone.

704. सरस्वती → सरस्-वती

सरस् = a lake, a pool; also fluid, essence
वती = possessing (मतुप्, feminine ङीप्)
"Sarasvatī — she who possesses the lake."

Vigraha: सरः अस्याः अस्तीति सरस्वती।

The dialogue continues, and the next objection is sharper: "Why should we make a difference between a pot and a cloth, as their apparent difference is simply illusory according to the previous rule? The foregoing name answers the question."

That is a real difficulty. If all difference is illusory because She bewilders, then ordinary distinctions collapse too — and nobody is in fact confused about pots and cloths. The answer distinguishes the two kinds of knowledge: "Sarasvatī is the deity which presides over knowledge, that is, she is in the form of the ocean of knowledge. That means non-sensuous knowledge." Bewilderment does not arise in the understanding of pots, because Gītā 5.15 locates it elsewhere — "knowledge is covered by nescience, hence people are bewildered." And the concealment is purposive: "it is necessary to confuse sinful men, because they are devoid of divine grace, to conceal from them the knowledge of non-duality."

So the bewildering of 703 is specific to non-dual knowledge, not general. Bhāskararāya adds Dhaumya's lexical note: Sarasvatī is a girl of two years — as Trimūrti was a girl of three at 628.

705. शास्त्रमयी → शास्त्र-मयी

शास्त्र = scripture, authoritative teaching (शास् "to teach" + त्र)
मयी = made of, consisting of (मय with the feminine)
"She who consists of the scriptures."

Vigraha: शास्त्रैः निर्मिता शास्त्रमयी।

The third move. If duality is illusory but nobody is deceived about pots, how is the illusion established at all? "This bewilderment is not like the bewilderment as to locality, because the duality is to be inferred by a thousand arguments consisting of different contradictory qualities. Hence this name."

The answer is an appeal to authority over inference. Chāndogya 3.14.1's "all is Brahman" "rests on the authority of scriptures alone. The meaning is, the Scriptures alone are the convincing proof, and not inference, because in the light of the Śāstras, inference is weak." Vedānta Sūtra 1.1.3 is cited for it — "śāstra is the original authority" — with Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.9's "I ask you that Person spoken of in the Upaniṣads."

So non-duality is known from scripture, not argued to. मयी is the suffix of 907 तत्त्वमयी and 941 मनोमयी, and शास्त्र the word of 845 शास्त्रसारा, where the Bhāmatī defined it widest: "that by which men are instructed to act or to refrain."

706. गुहाम्बा → गुहा-अम्बा

गुहा = a cave, a hiding-place — here the cavity of the heart (from गुह् "to hide")
अम्बा = mother
"The Mother within the cave."

Vigraha: गुहायाम् अम्बा।

Sandhi: गुहा + अम्बा → गुहाम्बा (आ by 6.1.101).

The fourth move, and it is an objection that uses scripture against the last answer: "Duality is not only commonly accepted, like the idea that the moon is measured by a span, but is also Scriptural."

And the nama supplies the scripture. गुह is the cavity, अम्बा the mother — She remains in the heart's cave "in the form of shadow." Kaṭha Upaniṣad III.1: "there are the two, drinking their reward in the world of their own works, entered into the cave of the heart, dwelling on the highest summit. Those who know Brahman call them shade and light." Bhāskararāya draws the conclusion against himself: "as both, shadow and light, enter the cavity of the heart, and both differ from one another, so duality is sanctioned by the Scriptures."

A second reading takes गुह as Subrahmanya, so the nama is the mother of Guha — which is 606 गुहजन्मभूः, a hundred namas back, where She was his birth-ground rather than his mother.

707. गुह्यरूपिणी → गुह्य-रूपिणी

गुह्य = secret, to be hidden (गुह् with the gerundive यत्)
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is the secret."

Vigraha: गुह्यं रूपं यस्याः सा।

The answer to 706, and it resolves the scriptural conflict by ranking the two kinds of truth: "all the ordinary ideas of duality are only true for a time, but non-duality is ever true. This non-duality is most secret, not perceivable by ordinary vision."

The Sūta Saṃhitā (4.47.69) is quoted, and it is built entirely of the word: "we adore Devī, who assumes the form of the Guru, secret, in the form of secret knowledge, beloved by her secret devotees, residing in the secret place." Then the conclusion: "thus by attributing two forms to the one Brahman, the two kinds of scriptures are reconciled."

Or गुह्य is the Guhya Upaniṣad, which is Her form — the Kūrma Purāṇa, "among the Upaniṣads, O Devī, you are the Guhyopaniṣad."

गुह्या had stood alone at 624, and गुह् has now given four namas in this text: 606, 624, 706, 707.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and from 703 they stop being descriptions and become moves in an argument.

The sequence is: She is unlimited by space and time (701); She pervades everything (702); how then can she have contradictory attributes — because she bewilders those who believe in duality (703); but then why are we not confused about pots — because the bewilderment concerns non-sensuous knowledge only (704); how is non-duality established at all — by scripture, not inference (705); but scripture also sanctions duality, shadow and light both in the heart's cave (706); and the resolution — duality is true for a time, non-duality always, and the second is secret (707).

Each nama is the next step, and Bhāskararāya marks the questions and answers explicitly. The argument does not end here: it runs on through 713.

701 also restates 642 अपरिच्छेद्या in the participle, and where 642 got four words this gets a full analysis of the three limitations — place, time, and mutual difference between things.

---

## सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता सदाशिवपतिव्रता । संप्रदायेश्वरी साधु ई गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी

*sarvopādhivinirmuktā sadāśivapativratā । sampradāyeśvarī sādhu ī gurumaṇḍalarūpiṇī*

Verse 138, namas 708–713. The verse table has no row for this verse; see the note at the head of these ten.

708. सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता → सर्व-उपाधि-विनिर्मुक्ता

सर्व = all
उपाधि = a limitation, an attribute, a conditioning adjunct (उप + आ + धा "to place upon")
विनिर्मुक्ता = wholly freed, released (वि + निः + मुक्ता, from मुच्)
"She who is free from all limitations."

Vigraha: सर्वेभ्यः उपाधिभ्यः विनिर्मुक्ता।

Sandhi: सर्व + उपाधि → सर्वोपाधि (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, 6.1.87).

The fifth move of the argument, and the objection is the sharpest yet: "But if both scriptures are authoritative, non-duality is not established."

The answer turns on उपाधि, which is the technical word for a conditioning attribute — literally something placed upon. "Sarvopādhi: all limitations or attributes, such as the Mother of Skanda, shadow and light, whether conditioned or unconditioned. The relation between the qualities and the thing which is qualified is illusory, like the relation of the silver in the mother-of-pearl."

Note that the examples are the previous two namas' own material — mother of Skanda from 706's second reading, shadow and light from its Kaṭha citation. So the attributes being dissolved are the ones just used to establish duality.

Then the rule for reading scripture: "all the Vedāntas mean directly or indirectly one and the same supreme Brahman, which is non-duality. The other scriptures which advocate duality are to be taken as explaining the ordinary vision" — and the analogy is astronomical: "as we find the same in the science of eclipses, where it is indicated by the words five or six fingers with regard to the consumption of the sun and moon." Eclipse-tables speak in finger-widths because that is how the thing looks; dualist scripture speaks in duality for the same reason.

विनिर्मुक्ता is the word of 867 क्षयविनिर्मुक्ता, and निर्मुक्ता of 862 — freed from decay and from causality; here from attribution itself.

709. सदाशिवपतिव्रता → सदाशिव-पति-व्रता

सदाशिव = Sadāśiva, the ever-auspicious
पति = husband, lord
व्रता = vowed, devoted (व्रत "a vow")
"She who is vowed to Sadāśiva as her lord."

Vigraha: सदाशिवः पतिः, तत्र व्रतम् यस्याः सा।

The sixth move, and the question is now about Her: "If the above is true, as Tripurasundarī is in the form of energy, and as she is in the form of supreme egoism (Parāhantā) and other qualities, these attributes become illusory."

That is the difficulty the last nama created. If all upādhis are illusory, then Her own being-śakti and being-Parāhantā are illusory too, and there is nothing left to worship.

The answer distinguishes the power from its qualities: "'devoted to Śiva' means ever remaining with him in all the three times. The other attributes are imaginary and their qualities are also imaginary. But in this Śakti only the qualities are attributed, not the energy itself — hence she belongs to Brahman, or she is the same as Brahman."

So the śakti is not an upādhi; only its describable qualities are. And पतिव्रता — the vow to one husband through past, present and future — is the word chosen to say that the relation itself does not vary.

Sadāśiva had been Her husband at 911 सदाशिवकुटुम्बिनी, where कुटुम्बिनी made it a household; her mattress at 947; and the fifth of the five at 948, where the Sūta Saṃhitā ranked him above Śiva "because Sadāśiva is with the Mother."

710. संप्रदायेश्वरी → सम्-प्रदाय-ईश्वरी

सम् = fully, regularly
प्रदाय = handing over, transmission (प्र + दा "to give")
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady
"Mistress of the tradition."

Vigraha: संप्रदायस्य ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: प्रदाय + ईश्वरी → प्रदायेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

The seventh move, and the objection presses the last answer: "How, in the absence of special authority, can all qualities except the Parāhantā be said to be imaginary? Rather all the qualities must be unreal and false."

The answer names the authority, and it is transmission itself: "Sampradāya, the wisdom regularly (सम्) imparted (प्रदाय) to the disciples by the teachers; Īśvarī, ruling. This knowledge is arrived at by reason and by tradition."

He then gives the regress the objection depends on: "just as ether and other qualities are attributed to Brahman which is without attributes; again, of the ether, when predicated of Brahman, sound and substance are attributed; again, when these are predicated of Brahman, other qualities are attributed to them — similarly, in Brahman, which is without attributes, both the visible qualities and the things which are qualified are attributed, and one thing becomes both quality and possessor of quality." The point is that attribution has no natural stopping-place, so something outside the series must fix it, and that is the tradition.

संप्रदाय is one of the six interpretations of the mantra listed at 841 भावज्ञा — bhāvārtha, sampradāyārtha, nigarbha, kaulika, sarvarahasya, mahātattvārtha — so the word names both a mode of reading and, here, the lineage that authorises it.

711. साधु → साधु

साधु = good, right, well; a good man; and as an interjection, "well done"
"Well."

Vigraha: साधु सम्यक्।

Two things need saying about this nama and the next, and they are connected.

The Paribhāṣā verses at nama 1000 prescribe that "साध्वी is to be split as साधु + ई" — so what is written in the verse as one word, साध्वी, is counted as two namas. This text's data applies the split but slips one place: nama 711's dev reads साध्वी, the undivided word, and 712's reads साधु. The correct reading is 711 = साधु and 712 = ई, and 712's own commentary proves it, since it discusses a one-syllabled nama. Both namas also share a single body between them.

The commentary at this point closes the argument that began at 703, and it does so with an analogy from ordinary predication: "as we see burning to be the inherent quality of fire only, so Parāhantā is rightly said to be the inherent quality of Devī."

That is the answer 710 was owed. Attribution has no stopping-place in general, but some qualities are proper to their subject and not attributed from outside — burning to fire, and supreme I-ness to Her. So the eight-nama regress ends on a distinction between inherent and imputed quality.

Parāhantā has been the text's word for that I-ness at 854 पूर्णाहन्ता, 856 गर्विता and 576 मत्ता.

712. ई → ई

ई = the syllable ī — the one-lettered nama, belonging to the Turīya and known as Kāmakalā
"Ī."

Vigraha: ईकारः कामकला।

The dev field reads साधु, carrying the previous nama's second half; the nama is the single letter ई, and the commentary is unambiguous: "this name is one-syllabled, belonging to the Turīya known as Kāmakalā."

So the text contains a nama consisting of one vowel. Its derivation is given: "the derivation of the ई is from आ, with an addition — that is, आ is Viṣṇu and ई his sister. The meaning is she partakes the nature of Viṣṇu (आ) and that of his sister (ई)."

And then the doctrine, which is the ninth and last move of the argument: "the Brahman becomes twofold by becoming both the quality and the thing qualified. Again the quality is divided into two, masculine and feminine. The feminine became the wife of Paramaśiva; the masculine became Viṣṇu as the material cause of the Universe. These three together, according to Śaiva doctrine, form the partless Brahman."

Three, not two: the qualified, and the quality divided into masculine and feminine. That is what Kāmakalā names, and it answers the question 703 opened — how one Brahman can bear contradictory attributes — by making the division internal to it and countable.

The nama is also the reason the Paribhāṣā at 1000 has to legislate a division: a one-letter nama cannot be recognised in the written verse without a rule, since साध्वी looks like one word.

713. गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी → गुरु-मण्डल-रूपिणी

गुरु = a teacher, a preceptor — literally the heavy
मण्डल = a circle, a round; a regular succession
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is the circle of Gurus."

Vigraha: गुरुमण्डलं रूपं यस्याः सा।

The argument closes here, and it closes by refusing to go further: "this name indicates that the determination of the nature of that ई must be ascertained from the teacher alone, because it is most secret."

गुरुमण्डल is defined: "Gurus, from Paramaśiva to one's own teacher; maṇḍala, the regular succession of them" — and the reason it must be oral is stated as a historical claim. "This secret was handed down uninterruptedly from teacher to pupil and was not written in books. Hence it is said in the Yoginīhṛdaya (1.3): into this world this secret was handed down from ear to ear."

This is the fourth place the text stops and refers the reader to a teacher, after the light of the two samādhis at 907, the five M's at 948, and the mudrā's use in correcting mantra-errors at 982. And it is the only one where the refusal is itself the content of a nama.

गुरु had been Her form at 603 गुरुमूर्तिः and her seat at 591 शिरःस्थिता, "wherein she resides assuming the form of the Guru"; the guru-lineage meditation had been interpolated into 950's body; and 722 गुरुप्रिया closes the next verse.

Note on the verse. Six namas, and they complete the dialogue.

The moves are: if both scriptures hold, non-duality fails — answered by making all attributes upādhis, illusory as the silver in mother-of-pearl (708). Then: but Her own śakti and Parāhantā would be illusory too — answered by distinguishing the energy from its qualities, with पतिव्रता for the invariant relation (709). Then: what authorises that exception — the tradition, since attribution otherwise regresses without end (710). Then the analogy that closes it: burning is fire's own quality, and Parāhantā is Hers (711). Then Kāmakalā, the one-letter nama, which makes the division internal to Brahman and threefold (712). And finally the referral to the guru, because the rest cannot be written (713).

Eleven namas, from 703 to 713, reading as a continuous argument with its objections marked. Nothing else in this text does that.

712 is also the text's oddest nama on any measure: a single vowel, requiring a rule at 1000 to be counted at all, and carrying the doctrine the whole argument was for.

---

## कुलोत्तीर्णा भगाराध्या माया मधुमती मही । गणाम्बा गुह्यकाराध्या कोमलाङ्गी गुरुप्रिया

*kulottīrṇā bhagārādhyā māyā madhumatī mahī । gaṇāmbā guhyakārādhyā komalāṅgī gurupriyā*

Verse 139, namas 714–722.

714. कुलोत्तीर्णा → कुल-उत्तीर्णा

कुल = family, lineage; the Kula; and per the commentary, the group of senses
उत्तीर्णा = crossed over, gone beyond (उत् + तृ "to cross")
"She who has crossed beyond the Kula."

Vigraha: कुलात् उत्तीर्णा।

Sandhi: कुल + उत्तीर्णा → कुलोत्तीर्णा (अ + उ → ओ by guṇa, 6.1.87).

Two glosses, both brief. "This and the next three names express the secrecy of the doctrine" — so the run continues 713's point about oral transmission. And "Kula, the group of senses," which makes the crossing a transcendence of sense rather than of a lineage.

That reading is unusual. कुल has meant the Kaula path at 90–96 and 897 कुलरूपिणी, the mūlādhāra at 93, and at 586 कामसेविता "the lower six cakras from Ājñā to Mūlādhāra are called Kula." The senses are a fifth sense of the word, and उत्तीर्णा makes Her past them — where 96 अकुला had made Her past kula in the Kaula sense, "one with Śiva."

715. भगाराध्या → भग-आराध्या

भग = the sun's disc; good fortune, dignity; and per the second reading, the letter ए
आराध्या = to be worshipped (आ + राध्, gerundive यत्)
"She who is to be worshipped in the sun's disc."

Vigraha: भगे आराध्या।

Sandhi: भग + आराध्या → भगाराध्या (आ by 6.1.101). The computed pada reads भगा-राध्या, dividing one letter late.

"Bhaga, the sun's disc, because the sun's disc is the object of secret adoration" — so the secrecy-run of 714 continues.

The second reading is phonetic: भग is the letter ए, "and she is to be worshipped through the letter ए." The Setubandha (I.6) is cited — "the eleventh letter of her Mantra is the support and the seed and is in the triangle form" — with a cross-reference to the commentary on nama 17.

भग had been given seven senses at 117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी, from the Agni Purāṇa: "fortune, desire, magnanimity, strength, effort, sun, and fame." The sun is one of the seven, and it is the one taken here.

आराध्या for the fifth time — 870, 918, 923, 977, 681, and here.

716. माया → माया

माया = illusion, the power of appearance; and per the Devī Purāṇa, the instrument of marvellous action
"Māyā."

Vigraha: मीयते अनया इति माया।

Two definitions, and they differ in temper. Bhāskararāya's own is privative: "the energy which obscures what is plain is Māyā." The Devī Purāṇa's is productive: "it is called Māyā because it is the instrument of marvellous actions, producing unheard-of results, like dreams or jugglery."

The Varāha Purāṇa is then quoted at length — Viṣṇu to the Earth — and the examples are all of ordinary appearance and disappearance rather than deception: "the cloud sends forth rain and water is collected; next the quarters become clear. This is my Māyā, O beloved one. Even the moon wanes, again waxes, and on the new-moon day it is invisible. This is my power of illusion; by it I remain in the water. I create Prajāpatis as well as I destroy them." Thirty-six verses of it, Bhāskararāya notes. And the Śāṇḍilya Sūtra (86): "his energy is Māyā."

Māyā had been one reading of योनि at 895, where निलय was taken as limit and She limited Māyā; and at 703 सर्वमोहिनी the Kūrma Purāṇa had Śiva call Māyā "dear to me, infinite, by which this world is bewildered." Here it is Her name.

717. मधुमती → मधु-मती

मधु = honey, mead; sweetness
मती = possessing (मतुप्, feminine ङीप्)
"She who possesses honey."

Vigraha: मधु अस्याः अस्तीति मधुमती।

Three readings, ascending in technicality. The Śruti's, "the nature of the great deity is honey-like." The Madhuvidyā of Chāndogya 3.1.1, "the Sun is the honey of the Devas."

And then the yogic one, which is the substance. The Yoga Śāstras give four kinds of yogin, of whom the fourth and highest is the अतिक्रान्तभावन, "who transcends even the state of meditation"; and he must pass seven भूमिकas, of which the last is called Madhumatī — "hence her name. That wisdom alone which arises from this foundation causes one to cross over the ocean of saṃsāra." Yoga Sūtra III.54's commentaries are cited for it: "the knowledge resulting from discrimination is emancipating, omni-objective, super-objective, instantaneous."

So the nama names the seventh and last stage of the highest kind of yogin. मधु had stood at 915 स्वभावमधुरा, where the sweetness needed no vehicle, and the mead of 836 and 918 is the same word.

718. मही → मही

मही = the earth, the great one (feminine of मह्, "great"); also the name of a river
"The Earth."

Vigraha: महती मही।

"Mahī is the name of a river." And the Devī Purāṇa's etymology: "it is great because it pervades all, hence Prakṛti is called Mahī."

So मही is derived from मह् "great" and identified with Prakṛti rather than with soil. The text's other earth-namas are 955 धरा, the bearer, and 694 सागरमेखला, girdled by ocean — three words, and this is the only one that makes the earth great rather than supporting or bounded.

719. गणाम्बा → गण-अम्बा

गण = a troop, a host — the Gaṇas of Śiva; and per the commentary, Gaṇeśa
अम्बा = mother
"Mother of the hosts."

Vigraha: गणानाम् अम्बा।

Sandhi: गण + अम्बा → गणाम्बा (आ by 6.1.101).

The gloss is six words: "Gaṇa, the hosts of Pramatha and the rest, or Gaṇeśa." So either the Gaṇas collectively or their lord singly.

Gaṇeśa's birth is nama 77 कामेश्वरमुखालोककल्पितश्रीगणेश्वरा, where She brought him forth by a glance at Kāmeśvara's face, and 78 has him shatter Viśukra's obstruction-yantra. अम्बा for the third time — 706 गुहाम्बा the mother in the cave, 985 अम्बा alone, and here.

720. गुह्यकाराध्या → गुह्यक-आराध्या

गुह्यक = a Guhyaka, a class of demigod — literally a concealed one (from गुह् "to hide")
आराध्या = to be worshipped
"She who is worshipped by the Guhyakas."

Vigraha: गुह्यकैः आराध्या।

Sandhi: गुह्यक + आराध्या → गुह्यकाराध्या (आ by 6.1.101).

"Guhyakas may mean a kind of Deva, or an unknown secret place" — and the second gloss identifies that place: the mūlādhāra. So the nama is either worshipped-by-demigods or worshipped-in-the-root-cakra.

This is the third आराध्या in six namas, after 715 and back to 681. And गुह् gives its fifth nama here, after 606, 624, 706 and 707 — the secrecy-run of 714 is still running.

721. कोमलाङ्गी → कोमल-अङ्गी

कोमल = soft, tender, delicate
अङ्गी = limbed, having limbs (अङ्ग with the feminine)
"The tender-limbed."

Vigraha: कोमलानि अङ्गानि यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: कोमल + अङ्गी → कोमलाङ्गी (आ by 6.1.101). index.html has no commentary for this nama.

अङ्गी is the word of nama 50 अनवद्याङ्गी, whose limbs were flawless, and 579 मृणालमृदुदोर्लता had made her arms soft as the lotus-stem — मृदु there, कोमल here, the same claim in a different word.

722. गुरुप्रिया → गुरु-प्रिया

गुरु = a teacher, a preceptor; and per the commentary, Śiva as the world's teacher
प्रिया = dear to, fond of; also a wife
"She who is dear to the Guru."

Vigraha: गुरुः प्रियः यस्याः सा। or गुरोः प्रिया।

The dev field reads गुरुप्रिया १३९॥, carrying the verse number into the nama — the same fault as 830 प्रकटाकृतिः ॥१५५॥, and with the same consequence: it displaced the next verse's range in the table by one.

Two readings, and प्रिया carries both. She delights in the Guru; or she is the Guru's wife — "Guru, Śiva, the guru of the world; she is his wife."

गुरु closes this verse as it opened 713, and the two together frame the verse: the circle of Gurus is Her form, and the Guru is Her husband. प्रिया for the tenth time in the text.

Note on the verse. Nine namas, and the first three continue 713's secrecy: crossed beyond the senses, worshipped in the sun's disc which is "the object of secret adoration," and Māyā. Bhāskararāya says so at 714 — "this and the next three names express the secrecy of the doctrine."

717 is the most technical entry. Madhumatī is the seventh and last of the bhūmikās that the highest of the four kinds of yogin must pass, and "that wisdom alone which arises from this foundation causes one to cross over the ocean of saṃsāra." So a nama names a stage of attainment rather than an attribute.

716's two definitions of Māyā are worth holding apart. Bhāskararāya's own makes it what obscures; the Devī Purāṇa's makes it what produces marvels; and the Varāha Purāṇa's examples — rain gathering, the moon waning and waxing, the new moon's invisibility — are of ordinary appearance rather than deceit.

And the verse is framed by गुरु, at 713 immediately before it and 722 at its close.

---

## स्वतन्त्रा सर्वतन्त्रेशी दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी । सनकादिसमाराध्या शिवज्ञानप्रदायिनी

*svatantrā sarvatantreśī dakṣiṇāmūrtirūpiṇī । sanakādisamārādhyā śivajñānapradāyinī*

Verse 140, namas 723–727.

723. स्वतन्त्रा → स्व-तन्त्रा

स्व = own, self
तन्त्रा = dependence, subordination; a doctrine, a system; a Tantra (from तन् "to stretch, to weave")
"The Independent."

Vigraha: स्वस्मिन् तन्त्रा स्वतन्त्रा।

Three readings, and they use three senses of तन्त्र.

As dependence: "as she creates without depending on instruments she is called Svatantrā." Bhāskararāya adds that Svatantra is also the name of a book.

As the Tantras: "all the Tantras belong to her; even in the Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava, Gāṇapatya and other Tantras her glory only is described, hence all Tantras are Hers." That reading makes स्व possessive rather than reflexive, and the next nama states it outright.

As mutual dependence: स्व the Self, that is Paramaśiva, and तन्त्र depending — "the meaning is that each depends on the other." The Kālikā Purāṇa is quoted for the shared dwelling: "Śiva ever lives in that place sporting with Devī. In the centre is the abode of Devī, Śaṃkara ever remains there."

So the same nama gives independent, owner of all Tantras, and interdependent with Śiva. तन् is the root of तनया at 634 and of तन्तु at 111.

724. सर्वतन्त्रेशी → सर्व-तन्त्र-ईशी

सर्व = all
तन्त्र = a Tantra
ईशी = mistress, ruler
"Mistress of all the Tantras."

Vigraha: सर्वेषां तन्त्राणाम् ईशी।

Sandhi: तन्त्र + ईशी → तन्त्रेशी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

"The Tantras are sixty-four in number; Īśī, the promulgator." So ईशी is glossed not as ruler but as the one who promulgates — she does not govern the Tantras, she issues them.

Sixty-four is the count that also stood at 850 वर्णरूपिणी for the letters and at 846 मन्त्रसारा for "the sixty-four books on mantra" — which are presumably these. ईशी for the fifth time, and ईश् for its tenth turn.

725. दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी → दक्षिणामूर्ति-रूपिणी

दक्षिणामूर्ति = Dakṣiṇāmūrti — Śiva as the south-facing teacher (दक्षिणा "south" + मूर्ति "form")
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is Dakṣiṇāmūrti."

Vigraha: दक्षिणामूर्तिः रूपं यस्याः सा।

The gloss identifies him: "Dakṣiṇāmūrti is Śiva sitting faced southwards, well known as the instructor of Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa and the rest, whose mantras are found described in the Tantras."

So this is the teaching-Śiva, and the nama makes Her his form — which continues 713's guru-circle and 722's Guru-husband. The Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā had been cited at 948 पञ्चमी for the conventional use of पञ्चमी to mean Vārāhī.

दक्षिणा here is the compass-point, where at 923 दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या it was the adept and the offering, and at 912 one of the two paths. The word has served three quite different purposes in the text.

726. सनकादिसमाराध्या → सनक-आदि-सम्-आराध्या

सनक = Sanaka, first of the four mind-born sons of Brahmā
आदि = beginning with, and the rest
सम् = fully
आराध्या = to be worshipped
"She who is fully worshipped by Sanaka and the rest."

Vigraha: सनकादिभिः समाराध्या।

Sandhi: सनक + आदि → सनकादि (आ by 6.1.101).

"Hence they are included in the succession of gurus" — so the Kumāras' worship of Her earns them a place in the guru-maṇḍala of 713. The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa is quoted: "thou art the beginningless, the whole, in the form of cause and effect; the Yogins, Sanaka and the rest, are searching after you alone."

समाराध्या for the fourth time — 870, 918, 977, and here — and the qualification each time is different: inward attention, consciousness as oblation, the ten gestures, and now a named lineage.

727. शिवज्ञानप्रदायिनी → शिव-ज्ञान-प्र-दायिनी

शिव = Śiva
ज्ञान = knowledge
प्र = forth, fully
दायिनी = she who gives
"She who bestows the knowledge of Śiva."

Vigraha: शिवज्ञानं प्रददातीति।

The compound is ambiguous as to whose knowledge, and Bhāskararāya takes it both ways.

She gives knowledge of Śiva — and the Vasiṣṭha Rāmāyaṇa supplies the epistemology: "wind is recognised by motion, fire by heat; Śiva, who is consciousness, purity and tranquillity, is known by his vibratory energy. There is no other way to know him." So Śiva is known only through his śakti, which makes Her the sole access to him.

Or Śiva gives knowledge of Devī — with the Varāha Purāṇa, "these three, the Trimūrtis, are attained by one who really knows Rudra."

प्रदायिनी is the form of 989 वाञ्छितार्थप्रदायिनी, दायिनी with प्र, and this is the eighth दायिनी in the text. And the nama closes the verse where it began: 723 made Śiva and Her mutually dependent, and 727 makes each the way to the other.

Note on the verse. Five namas, and the verse is about the Tantras and the teacher.

723–724 pair on तन्त्र, and 723 gets three senses out of it — independent, owner of all Tantras, and mutually dependent with Śiva. The third is the interesting one, because it undercuts the first: स्वतन्त्रा means both "depending on herself" and "each depends on the other."

725–727 then turn to teaching. Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the south-facing instructor of Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa, and She is his form; Sanaka and the Kumāras worship Her and are thereby "included in the succession of gurus"; and 727 makes the access mutual, since Śiva "is known by his vibratory energy — there is no other way," while Śiva in turn gives knowledge of Her.

With 713's guru-maṇḍala and 722's Guru-husband, the last three verses of this batch are largely about transmission.

---

Textual note for verses 131–140.

The verse table has no row for verse 138. Verses 138 and 139 are merged into one row labelled 139, whose text carries a ॥ where the boundary falls, and whose range 708–721 is off by one at the end because 722 गुरुप्रिया carries ॥१३९॥ in its dev field. That is the same fault as 830 प्रकटाकृतिः ॥१५५॥, and it displaces verse 140's range in the table to 722–727 where it should be 723–727 — exactly as verse 156's was displaced to 830–837.

Sandhi mis-division, one instance: 662 अष्टमूर्तिः has gained the र् of its own visarga and 663 अजाजैत्री has lost its initial अ at that joint. 663 carries a second, independent fault as well — जैली for जैत्री, a त्र read as ल — so only the transliterated gloss preserves the word.

Nama 712 is the oddest case in the text. The Paribhāṣā at nama 1000 prescribes splitting साध्वी into साधु + ई, and this data applies the split one place late: 711's dev reads साध्वी and 712's reads साधु, where they should read साधु and ई. The commentary under 712 settles it, since it expounds a one-syllabled nama, "belonging to the Turīya known as Kāmakalā." So the text contains a nama consisting of a single vowel, and the rule at 1000 exists in order to make it countable.

Shared bodies: 711 and 712 share one, and 689–690 carry the same truncated sentence in gloss and body. 669, 687, 693, 694, 697 and 721 have no commentary body at all.

Computed pada faults: 681 सुखा-राध्या for सुख-आराध्या, and 715 भगा-राध्या for भग-आराध्या — both dividing one letter late at the same kind of joint.
