## चित्कलानन्दकलिका प्रेमरूपा प्रियंकरी । नामपारायणप्रीता नन्दिविद्या नटेश्वरी

*citkalānandakalikā premarūpā priyaṃkarī । nāmapārāyaṇaprītā nandividyā naṭeśvarī*

Verse 141, namas 728–734.

728. चित्कला → चित्-कला

चित् = consciousness (from चित् "to perceive")
कला = a part, a portion, a fraction
"The portion of consciousness."

Vigraha: चितः कला।

Bhāskararāya glosses चित् as "Brahman which is existence, knowledge and bliss" and कला as part — so the compound is a fraction of the whole.

The second reading makes it the individual soul: "Citkalā, the consciousness encased in the mind, because it is a small part of that consciousness which has no vehicle." Gītā 15.7 is cited for it — "my part alone in the world are the eternal Jīvas" — and the Padma Purāṇa: "in the mind of all embodied souls resides the energy called Citkalā."

So a nama of Hers names the jīva. कला had been the five Śaiva kalās at 611 and 853, the moon's digits at 612, and one of the sixty-four arts; here it is a fraction of consciousness.

729. आनन्दकलिका → आनन्द-कलिका

आनन्द = bliss (आ + नन्द् "to rejoice")
कलिका = a bud, an unopened flower (कलि with the diminutive क)
"The Bud of bliss."

Vigraha: आनन्दस्य कलिका।

The dev field reads ऽऽनन्दकलिका with a double avagraha, marking the आ elided in चित्कला + आनन्दकलिका → चित्कलानन्दकलिका (आ + आ → आ, 6.1.101). Tenth instance of that class in the text, and the doubled form again correctly signals a long vowel, as at 828 and 972.

"She is one portion of the bliss enjoyed by Jīvas," with Taittirīya 2.7.1 — "other beings live by a part of this bliss." So 728 and 729 are the same claim twice: a part of consciousness, a part of bliss, both being what the individual soul has of Her.

Or कलिका is "the bud of the Ānandamaya sheath" — the last of the five kośas, which had stood at 690 कोशनाथा and at 821, where Her being the sheath's "tail" was the Vedānta Sūtra's ānandamaya section.

कलिका rather than कला: a bud is a part that will open, so the diminutive carries a promise the fraction at 728 did not.

730. प्रेमरूपा → प्रेम-रूपा

प्रेम = love, affection (from प्री "to please" — प्रेमन्)
रूपा = form
"She whose form is love."

Vigraha: प्रेम रूपं यस्याः सा।

The gloss is four words: "Prema, affection or devotion." प्री is the root of प्रिया, which has stood ten times in the text, and of प्रीता at 971 and 732.

731. प्रियंकरी → प्रियम्-करी

प्रियम् = dear, beloved (accusative of प्रिय)
करी = she who makes (from कृ "to do")
"She who makes love."

Vigraha: प्रियं करोतीति प्रियंकरी।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The formation is the accusative with करी, as in वशंकरी at 697 and 978 — bringing into a state. So प्रियंकरी is she who causes affection, and with 730 the pair is love as her form and love as her effect.

732. नामपारायणप्रीता → नाम-पारायण-प्रीता

नाम = a name (नामन्)
पारायण = complete recitation, going through to the end (पार "far shore" + अयन "going")
प्रीता = pleased, delighted (past participle of प्री)
"She who delights in the full recitation of her names."

Vigraha: नामपारायणेन प्रीता।

पारायण is literally a going to the far shore — a recitation carried through to its end, not a sampling.

The commentary is an arithmetic of names, and it is worth setting out. The letters from अ to क्ष are Her names: अ is one and क and the rest are thirty-five, thirty-six in all, "and these thirty-six represent thirty-six years." Adding the sixteen vowels to each gives 576, which are the first letters; adding a second letter in order to each brings the total to 20,737 names. The Laghustuti (19) is cited in support, and the Devī Bhāgavata: "when from अ to क्ष the vowels are joined to the consonants, countless names, O son of Raghu, are obtained."

And then the practice: the Kādimata prescribes reciting them "in five ways — by day, week, fortnight, month and year." Bhāskararāya adds "so also the repetition of this Sahasranāma," which makes the nama self-referential: a name in the thousand names asserting the merit of reciting the thousand names.

That is the same move as 544 पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना, where hearing and reciting Her were holy.

733. नन्दिविद्या → नन्दि-विद्या

नन्दि = Nandi, Śiva's bull and attendant (from नन्द् "to rejoice")
विद्या = knowledge; a mantra of a female deity
"The Vidyā of Nandi."

Vigraha: नन्देः विद्या।

The whole commentary is five words: "the Vidyā worshipped by Nandi."

So this is the fifth nama that names a particular mantra by its holder or user, after आत्मविद्या, महाविद्या and श्रीविद्या at 583–585, and राज्यलक्ष्मी at 689 whose "mantra is described in the Tantrarāja." And Nandi-vidyā is a recognised Śrīvidyā variant, one of the named recensions of the Pañcadaśī.

नन्द् is the root of आनन्द at 729 and 676 — the same root gives bliss and the bull's name.

734. नटेश्वरी → नट-ईश्वरी

नट = a dancer, an actor (from नट् "to dance")
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady; and here, wife
"Wife of the Dancer."

Vigraha: नटस्य ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: नट + ईश्वरी → नटेश्वरी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

The gloss identifies him precisely: "she is the wife of the Dancer, the Naṭarāja of Cidambaram." So the nama is geographically specific, and it belongs with the other located identifications — Viśālākṣī at Benares (936), Mīnākṣī at Madhurā (915), Kātyāyanī at Oḍḍiyāna (556), Gaurī at Kanyakubja (635), Sāvitrī at Puṣkara (699), Virajā at Utkala (779), Lalitā at Prayāga (1000).

Dancing is about to return: 738 लास्यप्रिया four namas on has Her fond of it, and 739 लयकरी glosses लय as both mental absorption and "a pause in the music." ईश्वरी for the eleventh turn of ईश्.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and the verse divides after three.

728–729 are a pair about what the individual soul has of Her — a fraction of consciousness, a bud of bliss — and both are supported by texts about parts: Gītā 15.7's "my part alone are the eternal Jīvas," and Taittirīya's "other beings live by a part of this bliss." So two namas of Hers name what is not Her but derived from Her.

730–732 then move through love to recitation, and 732 is the entry worth keeping. Its arithmetic runs the alphabet up to 20,737 names and then prescribes reciting them by day, week, fortnight, month and year — with Bhāskararāya adding "so also the repetition of this Sahasranāma." A nama recommending the recitation it belongs to.

733–734 close with two specifics: a named recension of the mantra, and the wife of the Naṭarāja at Cidambaram.

---

## मिथ्याजगदधिष्ठाना मुक्तिदा मुक्तिरूपिणी । लास्यप्रिया लयकरी लज्जा रम्भादिवन्दिता

*mithyājagadadhiṣṭhānā muktidā muktirūpiṇī । lāsyapriyā layakarī lajjā rambhādivanditā*

Verse 142, namas 735–741.

735. मिथ्याजगदधिष्ठाना → मिथ्या-जगत्-अधिष्ठाना

मिथ्या = falsely, illusorily; false
जगत् = the world — "the moving" (from गम्)
अधिष्ठाना = substratum, basis, that on which a thing rests (अधि + स्था "to stand")
"She who is the substratum of the illusory world."

Vigraha: मिथ्याजगतः अधिष्ठाना।

Sandhi: जगत् + अधिष्ठान → जगदधिष्ठान, the त् voicing before the vowel.

The simile is the standard one for a substratum and Bhāskararāya uses it: "she is the basis of the illusory universe as the mother-of-pearl is the basis of the silver illusorily perceived." That figure had done the same work at 708 सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता, where the relation of quality to qualified was "illusory, like the relation of the silver in the mother-of-pearl."

The Śrutis: Gauḍapāda Kārikā 1.17, "this duality is mere Māyā, non-duality is the reality"; Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.19, "here there is no manifoldness whatever"; and the Devī Bhāgavata, "indeed I am alone all this, there is never any other."

Then two divisions — अधिष्ठ basis with अन life, "her life is the Brahman who is the basis of the universe"; or अधिष्ठान as supported, "in Her all are sustained."

And then Bhāskararāya records a dissent, which is unusual: "really, according to the doctrine of the Tāntrikas, who hold that the universe is the manifestation of Brahman, the universe is real, because like the pot and clay..." So the school he belongs to does not accept मिथ्या in the Advaitin's sense, and he says so under a nama that asserts it.

अधिष्ठान is the same स्था that gave प्रतिष्ठा at 829 and 660, and the substratum-argument had been made at 680 भावाभावविवर्जिता, where "the substratum is different from these two, existence and non-existence."

736. मुक्तिदा → मुक्ति-दा

मुक्ति = release, liberation (from मुच् "to loose")
दा = giving
"The Giver of liberation."

Vigraha: मुक्तिं ददातीति मुक्तिदा।

All three citations are about liberation granted on very little. The Kūrma Purāṇa: "one desirous of salvation should take refuge in Pārvatī, Parameśvarī, the Soul of all beings and also of Śiva." The Śiva Purāṇa: "if one recites the names of the supreme Lord even unconsciously, Śiva gives him salvation. Why say more?" The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa: "those who worship the supreme Śakti, whether regularly or irregularly, are not entangled in saṃsāra."

That is the same leniency as 681–682, where worship needed no fasting and She did good "even to him who but imperfectly worships her," and as 913's Kūrma passage which waived its own list of qualifications.

737. मुक्तिरूपिणी → मुक्ति-रूपिणी

मुक्ति = liberation
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is liberation."

Vigraha: मुक्तिः रूपं यस्याः सा।

The commentary is a piece of technical philosophy about what liberation is not. "By destruction of avidyā, or by recovering the fifth state, one does not obtain the supreme object of human desire; it should be said only when one remains in his own bliss."

The Saura Saṃhitā (ch. 14) is then quoted through a chain of refutations: knowledge is the means — no, "knowledge is not the means, but is merely calling to remembrance"; knowledge is neither effect nor substance; salvation is neither substance, quality, action, nor sāmānya, samavāya or abhāva — the six Vaiśeṣika categories, denied one by one. "Hence the supreme salvation is becoming the absolute Self."

So the nama is defined by exclusion from the categories, and knowledge is demoted from cause to reminder.

The five kinds of liberation were left unnamed at 839 मुक्तिनिलया and the fifth, कैवल्यपद, named at 926 and 625. "Recovering the fifth state" here refers to that set.

738. लास्यप्रिया → लास्य-प्रिया

लास्य = dancing (from लस् "to play, to dance")
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in dancing."

Vigraha: लास्यं प्रियं यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The nama follows 734, where She was the Naṭarāja's wife, and precedes 739, where लय is glossed as including "a pause in the music." So three namas within six touch on dance.

739. लयकरी → लय-करी

लय = dissolution, absorption; a mental state; and a musical pause (from ली "to dissolve, to cling")
करी = she who makes
"She who causes absorption."

Vigraha: लयं करोतीति लयकरी।

Two glosses, and the pairing is the interest. "Laya, a peculiar state of mind, for it is said: laya, mental absorption, is equal to ten meditations." And then: "Laya also means a pause in the music."

So the same word gives the highest of the meditative states — worth ten dhyānas — and a rest in a rhythmic cycle. With 738's dancing immediately before, the musical sense is not idle.

ली is the root of निलया, which has stood six times in the text, and of प्रलय at 571 महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी. लय is one of the four kinds of yoga listed at 655 — "Mantra, Laya, Haṭha and Rāja."

740. लज्जा → लज्जा

लज्जा = shame, modesty, bashfulness (from लज्ज् "to be ashamed")
"Shame."

Vigraha: लज्जा एव सा।

The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is quoted, and it is one of a formulaic series: "Devī who resides in all beings in the form of shame." That formula has appeared at 538 मेधा — "Devī who resides in all beings in the form of intelligence" — and at 633 उमा, "Devī who resides as brightness in all creatures." The Devīmāhātmya's litany of "yā devī sarvabhūteṣu" is being drawn on repeatedly, and each nama takes one of its terms.

741. रम्भादिवन्दिता → रम्भा-आदि-वन्दिता

रम्भा = Rambhā, the apsaras; and per the commentary, the Hrīllekhā-bīja
आदि = beginning with, and the rest
वन्दिता = praised, saluted (from वन्द् "to praise")
"She who is praised by Rambhā and the rest."

Vigraha: रम्भादिभिः वन्दिता।

Sandhi: रम्भा + आदि → रम्भादि (आ by 6.1.101).

The gloss is two clauses: "Others: Urvaśī and the rest. Rambhā: Hrīllekhā-bīja." So the apsarases are the plain reading, and the second makes रम्भा a name of the bīja ह्रीं — which the text has already located at 593 भालस्था, "she resides in the forehead in the form of the Bindu of the syllable ह्रीं."

वन्दिता is the participle of 627 त्रिजगद्वन्द्या, where the gerundive made Her to-be-adored by the three worlds, and where Bhāskararāya cited that nama as the text's own instance of नमस्कार among the six marks of a stotra.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and it turns on मुक्ति in the middle.

735 is the philosophically loaded entry, and its interest is that Bhāskararāya dissents from it. The nama calls the world मिथ्या and he gives the Advaitin's authorities for that — Gauḍapāda, Bṛhadāraṇyaka, the mother-of-pearl — and then records that "according to the doctrine of the Tāntrikas, who hold that the universe is the manifestation of Brahman, the universe is real." He is a Tāntrika, and the nama is glossed against his own school.

736–737 then pair as gift and essence, and their tempers differ sharply. 736 gives liberation to those who recite "even unconsciously" and worship "whether regularly or irregularly"; 737 defines it by refuting six categories in turn and demoting knowledge from cause to "merely calling to remembrance."

738–740 are a ल-run, and 739's two senses of लय — the meditative state worth ten dhyānas, and a musical pause — sit together because 738 has just named dancing.

---

## भवदावसुधावृष्टिः पापारण्यदवानला । दौर्भाग्यतूलवातूला जराध्वान्तरविप्रभा

*bhavadāvasudhāvṛṣṭiḥ pāpāraṇyadavānalā । daurbhāgyatūlavātūlā jarādhvāntaraviprabhā*

Verse 143, namas 742–745.

> **Namas 742–749 are a single figure repeated eight times.** The commentary says so at 749: "the eight names from 742 to 749 are described by similes (rūpakālaṅkāra)." Each is a compound of the form *affliction-as-X* plus *the-thing-that-destroys-X*, and the eight destroyers are rain, fire, gale, sunbeam, moonbeam, cloud, thunderbolt and axe. It is the longest sustained figure in the text.

742. भवदावसुधावृष्टिः → भव-दाव-सुधा-वृष्टिः

भव = worldly existence, saṃsāra; and per the second reading, Śiva
दाव = a forest fire; a forest (from दु "to burn")
सुधा = nectar, ambrosia
वृष्टिः = rain, a downpour (from वृष् "to rain")
"She who is the rain of nectar upon the forest-fire of worldly existence."

Vigraha: भवदावे सुधावृष्टिः।

The figure sets a fire against a rain, and both terms are already in the text: भव as saṃsāra at 114, 842 and 843; सुधा as the nectar at 106 and 879; and वृष् as the raining at 106 सुधासाराभिवर्षिणी, where She showered "the very essence of nectar," and at 79, where what she rained was counter-missiles.

Bhāskararāya then divides the compound into three separate namas — भवदा, वसुधा, वृष्टिः — reading भव as Śiva with दा gift, वसु wealth or jewel with दा gift, and वृष्टि as a shower of both. On that reading She bestows worldly enjoyment and salvation together, and the Rudrayāmala and Maṅgalarājastava are quoted for how rare that is: "where there is worldly enjoyment there is no salvation, where there is salvation there is no worldly enjoyment. To the best devotees of Śrīsundarī, salvation and enjoyment are both in their hands."

743. पापारण्यदवानला → पाप-अरण्य-दव-अनला

पाप = sin, evil
अरण्य = a forest, a wilderness
दव = a forest fire
अनला = fire (अनल)
"She who is the wildfire consuming the forest of sin."

Vigraha: पापारण्यस्य दवानला।

Sandhi at two joints: पाप + अरण्य → पापारण्य, and दव + अनला → दवानला (आ by 6.1.101 both times). The dev field reads पापारष्य- with ष् where ण् belongs — a letter confusion, and the gloss preserves the reading, "the forest-fire consuming the forest of sin."

Note that दाव was the fire to be quenched in 742 and दवानल is the fire that consumes in 743 — the same thing destructive and then salutary, one nama apart.

The forest-of-existence figure is 114 भवारण्यकुठारिका, where She was the axe to it; here the forest is sin and the instrument is fire. And 749 will bring the axe back for the tree of death.

The Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa is quoted for a rival holder of the epithet: "the supreme name of Gaṅgā is the fire that consumes the forest of sin, because Gaṅgā is the remover of the disease of saṃsāra." Then a syllabic division — दव as devotion and the other means of destroying sin, अन life-energy, ल receive. And the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa's expiation: "the supreme expiation of all sin, whether committed knowingly or unknowingly, is the remembrance of the feet of the supreme Śakti" — with a practical rubric, standing in water after bathing and repeating the Pañcadaśī 1,008 times.

744. दौर्भाग्यतूलवातूला → दौर्भाग्य-तूल-वातूला

दौर्भाग्य = misfortune, ill luck (vṛddhi derivative of दुर्भग)
तूल = cotton, the tufted seed-down of a reed
वातूला = a whirlwind, a gale (from वात "wind")
"She who is the gale that scatters the cotton-down of misfortune."

Vigraha: दौर्भाग्यतूलस्य वातूला।

The figure is exact: misfortune is not a weight to be lifted but seed-down, and what disposes of down is wind. दौर्भाग्य is the negative of the सौभाग्य that stood at 117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी, where Bhāskararāya identified सुभगा with Lalitā herself — and सुभगा is a nama at 761, seventeen on.

The alternative takes वातुल as "certain good actions which make misfortune become as light as the thistle-down; the meaning is such actions originate from her alone." So the gale becomes the deeds, and what they do is not to blow the misfortune away but to make it light enough to blow.

745. जराध्वान्तरविप्रभा → जरा-ध्वान्त-रवि-प्रभा

जरा = old age, decay (from जृ "to grow old")
ध्वान्त = darkness
रवि = the sun
प्रभा = radiance, a ray (प्र + भा "to shine")
"She who is the sunbeam dispelling the darkness of old age."

Vigraha: जराध्वान्तस्य रविप्रभा।

Sandhi: जरा + ध्वान्त → जराध्वान्त (आ by 6.1.101). index.html carries only the verse marker.

The compound is the shape of 993 अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका, where the darkness was ignorance and the light a lamp — ध्वान्त in both, and there the loss of an initial अ inverted the sense. Here the darkness is age, and the light is the sun rather than a lamp.

जरा is the third member of the triad at 851 जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी, and मृत्यु the second will close this figure at 749.

Note on the verse. Four namas, and all four are the same construction: an affliction figured as something, and Her as the thing that destroys it.

The elements are drawn from the text's own stock. भव as the forest was 114's figure; सुधा and वृष् were 106's nectar-shower; ध्वान्त was 993's darkness; जरा and मृत्यु are two members of 851's triad. So the eight-nama figure that begins here is built largely out of images the Sahasranāma has used elsewhere as claims, now recast as similes.

742 also gets divided into three namas by Bhāskararāya, and the division changes the register entirely: instead of a rain on a fire, she becomes the giver of enjoyment and salvation both — which the Rudrayāmala says are ordinarily exclusive.

---

## भाग्याब्धिचन्द्रिका भक्तचित्तकेकिघनाघना । रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिर्मृत्युदारुकुठारिका

*bhāgyābdhicandrikā bhaktacittakekighanāghanā । rogaparvatadambholir mṛtyudārukuṭhārikā*

Verse 144, namas 746–749.

746. भाग्याब्धिचन्द्रिका → भाग्य-अब्धि-चन्द्रिका

भाग्य = good fortune, destiny (from भग "portion")
अब्धि = the ocean — literally the water-holder (अप् "water" + धि "holding")
चन्द्रिका = moonlight, a moonbeam (चन्द्र with the diminutive क)
"She who is the moonlight upon the ocean of good fortune."

Vigraha: भाग्याब्धेः चन्द्रिका।

Sandhi: भाग्य + अब्धि → भाग्याब्धि (आ by 6.1.101). index.html has no commentary for this nama.

This is the one member of the eight that inverts the figure. In the other seven the first term is an affliction and She destroys it; here the first term is good fortune and what She does is make it swell, as the moon raises a tide. So the same construction serves both destruction and increase, and only this nama takes the second.

अब्धि is a good word for the position: the ocean named as what holds water, and moonlight named by a diminutive.

747. भक्तचित्तकेकिघनाघना → भक्त-चित्त-केकि-घन-अघना

भक्त = a devotee (from भज् "to worship")
चित्त = mind, thought
केकि = a peacock — named from its cry, केका
घन = a cloud; dense, massed
अघना = unceasing, continuous (अ + घन, per the commentary)
"She who is the unfailing raincloud to the peacocks that are her devotees' minds."

Vigraha: भक्तचित्तकेकिनां घनाघना।

Sandhi: घन + अघना → घनाघना (आ by 6.1.101).

The figure needs the convention to work: the peacock cries for the rains and dances when the clouds come, so a mind figured as a peacock is a mind waiting. And the compound's second half is read by Bhāskararāya as "Ghana, cloud, the deeds of Devī; Aghana, continual — her life-work is the spiritual nourishment for her devotees."

केकिन् is a peacock named from its call, which makes the bird in this compound already a voice. And the cloud returns as an image of Her from 824 बहुरूपा, where the Devī Purāṇa's simile was "just as one cloud becomes many retaining the same nature."

748. रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः → रोग-पर्वत-दम्भोलिः

रोग = disease (from रुज् "to break, to afflict")
पर्वत = a mountain
दम्भोलिः = Indra's thunderbolt, the vajra
"She who is the thunderbolt shattering the mountain of disease."

Vigraha: रोगपर्वतस्य दम्भोलिः।

The dev field reads रोगपर्वतदम्भोलि, the visarga lost — and 749 has gained the र् it became before म् (रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः + मृत्यु- → दम्भोलिर्मृत्यु-). Mis-division again, the same fault as 848–849, 894–895, 992–993, 540–541 and 662–663.

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

दम्भोलि is a name of the vajra, which the text made a nama at 944 वज्रिणी — and there Bhāskararāya's developed reading took वज्र as Brahman, "the great terrible thunderbolt," making Her its limitator. Here it is simply a weapon against a mountain. रोग had been saṃsāra itself at 842 भवरोगघ्नी, and disease was allayed at 551.

749. मृत्युदारुकुठारिका → मृत्यु-दारु-कुठारिका

मृत्यु = death (from मृ "to die"); and per the commentary, pains
दारु = wood, a tree; a block of timber
कुठारिका = a small axe, a hatchet (कुठार with the diminutive क and feminine आ)
"She who is the axe to the tree of death."

Vigraha: मृत्युदारोः कुठारिका।

कुठारिका is 114 भवारण्यकुठारिका's word exactly — there the axe was to the forest of worldly existence, here to the timber of death — and the diminutive matters in both: a hand-axe, which is what actually fells wood.

Bhāskararāya reads दारु by Vararuci's numeral system: "Dāru means 28 — र 2 and द 8." So the compound encodes a number, and the twenty-eight are "the twenty-eight kinds of pains described before, as differentiated by energy, success and elation," with a cross-reference to nama 354. That is the second place the text uses that numeral system, after 529 सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता, where उप was read as ten by the same rule and gave the arithmetic that turns fifty letters into a thousand petals.

Kaṭha Upaniṣad 2.25 is cited: "to Him death is like pickle" — the same verse quoted at 890 विश्वग्रासा and 752 for Her devouring, where "the Brāhmaṇa and Kṣatriya are both his food, death is his condiment."

And then the structural note: "the eight names from 742 to 749 are described by similes."

Note on the verse. Four namas closing the eight-fold figure, and the commentary marks the set at its end.

The eight destroyers are rain, fire, gale, sunbeam, moonbeam, cloud, thunderbolt, axe — four of water and light, four of force. And the eight afflictions are existence, sin, misfortune, age, good fortune, the waiting mind, disease, death. Two of the eight are not afflictions at all: 746's good fortune, which the moonlight raises rather than removes, and 747's devotee-mind, which the cloud feeds.

749 is the entry to keep. It carries the numeral reading of दारु as 28, which links it to 529's उप as 10 — the only two places Vararuci's system is used — and it recycles 114's हatchet after six hundred namas, for death instead of for the forest of birth.

Textual note. 748 has lost its visarga and 749 has gained the resulting र्. 743's dev reads ष् for ण् in पापारण्य-. 749 and 750 share a single body, and 750's gloss is 749's.

---

## महेश्वरी महाकाली महाग्रासा महाशना । अपर्णा चण्डिका चण्डमुण्डासुरनिषूदिनी

*maheśvarī mahākālī mahāgrāsā mahāśanā । aparṇā caṇḍikā caṇḍamuṇḍāsuraniṣūdinī*

Verse 145, namas 750–756.

750. महेश्वरी → महा-ईश्वरी

महा = great
ईश्वरी = mistress, sovereign lady
"The Great Sovereign."

Vigraha: महती ईश्वरी।

Sandhi: महा + ईश्वरी → महेश्वरी (आ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

index.html carries 749's gloss and body on this nama, so no commentary of its own survives; 751's gloss holds its stranded heading, "Maheśvarī."

The nama is 932 महेशी with the fuller feminine — ईश्वरी rather than ईशी — and that makes twelve turns of ईश् in the text. Māheśvarī had also been one of the three kinds of भावना at 907 (Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Akṣara), and 918's Sūta Saṃhitā had "one should worship with devotion the Maheśvarī who becomes oneself by one's own spiritual experience."

751. महाकाली → महा-काली

महा = great
काली = the black one; and per the commentary, fate, time (feminine of काल)
"The Great Kālī."

Vigraha: महती काली।

Two glosses. "She is called great because she rules over even death" — काली taken from काल, time and death, so Mahākālī outranks what she is named for. And the geographical identification: "Mahākālī is the deity worshipped at Ujjayinī, or she is the wife of Mahākāla."

काल had been slain at 557 कालहन्त्री — "she who slays Time," where Bhāskararāya glossed काल as death and cited Śvetāśvatara 6.2's "time of time." So the text names Her the slayer of time and then names Her by time's own feminine.

Ujjayinī joins the located identifications; Mahākāla is its Jyotirliṅga.

752. महाग्रासा → महा-ग्रासा

महा = great
ग्रासा = a mouthful, a morsel (from ग्रस् "to swallow")
"She whose mouthful is great."

Vigraha: महान् ग्रासः यस्याः सा।

Kaṭha Upaniṣad 2.25 again: "of whom both Brāhmaṇa and Kṣatriya are food."

This is 890 विश्वग्रासा with महा for विश्व — there the mouthful was the universe, and ग्रास being specifically the morsel taken at one swallow made the compound stronger than "devourer." The same verse was cited there, and again three namas back at 749 for death as condiment.

753. महाशना → महा-अशना

महा = great
अशना = eating, devouring; food (from अश् "to eat")
"The great Devourer."

Vigraha: महत् अशनं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: महा + अशना → महाशना (आ by 6.1.101).

"Mahat, because consuming both the animate and the inanimate Universe." So 752 and 753 are the same claim in two roots — ग्रस् and अश् — and the pairing is deliberate: the mouthful and the eating, what is swallowed and the act.

Vedānta Sūtra 1.2.9's अत्तृ or eater passage, cited at 890, is the proof-text behind both.

754. अपर्णा → अ-पर्णा

अ = not (नञ्)
पर्णा = a leaf (पर्ण); and per the commentaries, from पर्ण "falling," or ऋण "debt"
"She who is without a leaf."

Vigraha: पर्णम् अपि न अस्ति यस्याः सा।

Three derivations, and they disagree about which word is inside the name.

Reading अप + ऋण: अप removing, ऋण debt — she who discharges debt. And Bhāskararāya quotes his own Devīstava, which turns the etymology into a complaint against Śiva: "when you have not discharged your debt to me, though I repeat your name, O Śiva, why are you not ashamed to bear the name of Aparṇa, the discharger of debt?"

Reading with the Nirukta: पर्ण falling, so अपर्णा is free from falling.

Or the plain sense, leafless, which the Kālikā Purāṇa turns into biography: "she renounced even leaves as food when she was making tapas, hence the daughter of Himavat is called by Devas Aparṇā." The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa repeats it.

That last belongs with the Pārvatī material at 633–635, where Umā was named from her mother's prohibition and Gaurī was "burned by the fire of Yoga and again born of Himālaya."

755. चण्डिका → चण्डिका

चण्डिका = the fierce one, the wrathful (चण्ड with the diminutive क and feminine आ)
"Caṇḍikā."

Vigraha: चण्डा एव चण्डिका।

"The root चण्डि means anger. She becomes angry with those who are not devotees." And "according to the Devī Bhāgavata, a girl of seven years of age is called Caṇḍikā."

That last is one of a series of girl-ages the commentary supplies for namas, and they are worth collecting: Sarasvatī is a girl of two (704), Trimūrti of three (628), Subhagā of five (761), Caṇḍikā of seven here, Gaurī of ten (635). Five namas of the thousand double as ages in the kumārī-pūjā reckoning.

चण्ड had been intensified at 827 प्रचण्डा, where Bhāskararāya grounded the wrath in scripture — "for fear of Him the wind blows" — and gave the Viśva's other senses, a perfume and the śaṅkha flower.

756. चण्डमुण्डासुरनिषूदिनी → चण्ड-मुण्ड-असुर-निषूदिनी

चण्ड = Caṇḍa, a demon
मुण्ड = Muṇḍa, a demon; and also a head, a shaven head
असुर = a demon
निषूदिनी = she who destroys, slays (नि + सूद् "to destroy")
"The Slayer of the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa."

Vigraha: चण्डमुण्डासुरान् निषूदयतीति।

Sandhi: मुण्ड + असुर → मुण्डासुर (आ by 6.1.101); and the स् of सूदिनी retroflexes to ष् after नि.

"Hence she alone is to be called Cāmuṇḍā," and the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is quoted for the naming: "because you captured the Daityas Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, you shall be called Cāmuṇḍā."

Bhāskararāya then reports a competing etymology. The Varāha Purāṇa: "Devī struck the Daitya Ruru with her trident and cut off his head, and because she carried off the head (मुण्ड) and trunk (चर्म) she is called Cāmuṇḍā." So the name is either from two demons or from two body parts of a third. The Kośa (44) is added for the synonyms: "Karṇamoṭī is called Cāmuṇḍā, and Carcikā, Carmamuṇḍā."

The demon-slaying namas of this text are 599 दैत्यहन्त्री, 696 दैत्यशमनी, and the war-narrative at 65–82; Cāmuṇḍā herself was counted at 824 बहुरूपा, where the Varāha Purāṇa gave "nine crore Cāmuṇḍās."

Note on the verse. Seven namas: four on महा, then three of fierceness.

752 and 753 are the tightest pair, two roots for one act — ग्रस् the mouthful and अश् the eating — both resting on the same Kaṭha verse and the same Vedānta Sūtra as 890.

751 sets up a contradiction the text does not mark. She slays Time at 557 कालहन्त्री and is named Mahākālī here, "great because she rules over even death" — so the name she bears is the name of what she kills.

754 is the entry with the most disagreement in it: three derivations placing three different words inside अपर्णा — leaf, falling, and debt — and Bhāskararāya's own verse uses the debt-reading to reproach Śiva.

756 leaves its own etymology open, two demons or one demon's head and trunk, which is characteristic: the text prefers to record rival derivations rather than settle them.

---

## क्षराक्षरात्मिका सर्वलोकेशी विश्वधारिणी । त्रिवर्गदात्री सुभगा त्र्यम्बका त्रिगुणात्मिका

*kṣarākṣarātmikā sarvalokeśī viśvadhāriṇī । trivargadātrī subhagā tryambakā triguṇātmikā*

Verse 146, namas 757–763.

757. क्षराक्षरात्मिका → क्षर-अक्षर-आत्मिका

क्षर = perishable, flowing away (from क्षर् "to flow, to perish")
अक्षर = imperishable; and also a syllable
आत्मिका = having the nature of, being the very self of
"She whose nature is the perishable and the imperishable."

Vigraha: क्षरम् अक्षरं च आत्मा यस्याः सा।

Sandhi at two joints: क्षर + अक्षर → क्षराक्षर, and अक्षर + आत्मिका → अक्षरात्मिका (आ by 6.1.101 both times). The dev field reads क्षारा- with a long आ in the first member, where the word is क्षर; no rule lengthens it.

अक्षर means imperishable and also syllable, and Bhāskararāya takes the second first: "Kṣara, multiform; akṣara, syllables; ātma, her body — that is, she is one-syllabled and also many-syllabled." The Varāha Purāṇa: "though Devī is all-syllabled, yet she is called one-syllabled; she is the ruler of the Universe, she alone is all-syllabled."

The one-syllabled nama is 712 ई, the Kāmakalā vowel — so this nama's claim has a concrete referent in the text.

Then the metaphysical reading, on Gītā 15.16: "Kṣara is applied to all beings and Akṣara to the Kūṭastha Lord; she is both." The Mahābhārata: "being and non-being, sat and asat, are called kṣara and akṣara" — which makes this nama 661 सदसद्रूपधारिणी in different words, and 680 भावाभावविवर्जिता its negation.

Kūṭastha is nama 896 कूटस्था, where Bhāskararāya got seven readings out of कूट and the anvil was the best of them.

758. सर्वलोकेशी → सर्व-लोक-ईशी

सर्व = all
लोक = a world
ईशी = mistress, ruler
"Sovereign of all the worlds."

Vigraha: सर्वेषां लोकानाम् ईशी।

Sandhi: लोक + ईशी → लोकेशी (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87). index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The nama restates 607 देवेशी and 629 त्रिदशेश्वरी with लोक for the gods, and 697 सर्वलोकवशंकरी with ईशी for वशंकरी — ruling all the worlds rather than subduing them. Thirteenth turn of ईश्.

759. विश्वधारिणी → विश्व-धारिणी

विश्व = all, the whole, the universe
धारिणी = she who bears, upholds (धृ "to hold" + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"The Upholder of the universe."

Vigraha: विश्वं धारयतीति विश्वधारिणी।

index.html has no commentary, and the computed pada reads विश्वधा-अरिणी, which invents a stem विश्वधा and a suffix अरिणी; the split is विश्व + धारिणी.

धारिणी had been the milder of the two closing formulas in the yoginī-sets — 527 हाकिनीरूपधारिणी, bearing a form rather than being one — and had stood at 865 and 661. Here what is borne is everything, which puts the nama in the support-thread with 829 प्रतिष्ठा, 884 धर्माधारा, 935 जगद्धात्री, 955 धरा, 659 सर्वाधारा and 657 युगन्धरा.

760. त्रिवर्गदात्री → त्रिवर्ग-दात्री

त्रिवर्ग = a set of three; the three ends of life — dharma, artha, kāma
दात्री = the giver (दा with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्)
"The Giver of the three ends."

Vigraha: त्रिवर्गं ददातीति।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

त्रिवर्ग had been Her abode at 873 त्रिवर्गनिलया, where Bhāskararāya listed what the three might be — "dharma, artha and kāma; or the three times; or अ, उ and म, the three letters of the praṇava." And 698 सर्वार्थदात्री gave "the four objects of human desire," which is this three plus mokṣa; 764 स्वर्गापवर्गदा two namas on gives heaven and salvation.

दात्री for the fourth time — 832, 698, 760, and 792 ahead.

761. सुभगा → सु-भगा

सु = well, excellently
भगा = fortune, prosperity, dignity; and per the commentary, the sun
"The Fortunate."

Vigraha: शोभनं भगं यस्याः सा।

"According to Dhaumya, a girl of five years of age is called Subhagā" — the fourth of the five girl-ages, with Sarasvatī at two (704), Trimūrti at three (628), Caṇḍikā at seven (755) and Gaurī at ten (635).

The senses of भग are then given twice over, and the two lists do not match. Bhāskararāya's: "wealth, desire, magnanimity, strength, effort, fame." The Viśva's, longer: "dominion, wisdom, dispassion, womb, fame, strength, effort, desire, wealth, virtue, sun, and salvation." And the Agni Purāṇa had given seven at 117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी — "fortune, desire, magnanimity, strength, effort, sun, and fame."

Then the solar reading, which is developed: भग is the sun, "by her the sun is illuminated, because she resides in the sun and causes all its works," with the Viṣṇu Purāṇa (II.11) — "the whole and supreme energy of Viṣṇu, which is called the three Vedas, Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman, lightens the whole universe and destroys its iniquity."

सुभगा is also what Bhāskararāya identified with Lalitā herself at 117, where सौभाग्य was built on it: "so the saubhāgyas She bestows are Her own qualities extended to the devotee." And भग was the sun's disc at 715 भगाराध्या.

762. त्र्यम्बका → त्रि-अम्बका

त्रि = three
अम्बका = eyed (from अम्बक "an eye"); or, per the second reading, from अम्बा, mother
"The Three-eyed."

Vigraha: त्रीणि अम्बकानि यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: त्रि + अम्बका → त्र्यम्बका, the इ becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि).

The Devī Purāṇa names the three: "the moon, the sun and the fire are the three eyes of Devī, hence she is called by sages three-eyed." So the eyes are luminaries, which fits the nyāsa at 591–597 where a moon was set in the head and a sun in the heart.

The second reading takes अम्बा rather than अम्बक: "Tri, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra; ambā, mother" — mother of the three. That is 976 त्रिपुराम्बिका's construction and one of the four accounts of Tripurā's name.

Tryambaka is of course Śiva's own epithet, and the feminine here takes it over as शिवा did at 998 and ब्रह्माणी did at 821.

763. त्रिगुणात्मिका → त्रि-गुण-आत्मिका

त्रि = three
गुण = a quality, a strand
आत्मिका = having the nature of
"She whose nature is the three qualities."

Vigraha: त्रयः गुणाः आत्मा यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: गुण + आत्मिका → गुणात्मिका (आ by 6.1.101).

The dev field reads त्रिगुणात्मिका १४६॥, carrying the verse number into the nama. That is the third instance of this fault — after 830 प्रकटाकृतिः ॥१५५॥ and 722 गुरुप्रिया ॥१३९॥ — and it has the same consequence each time: the verse table's range is displaced by one, so this verse shows as 757–762 and the next as 763–770 where they should be 757–763 and 764–770.

"Her body is the equilibrium of the three qualities, Sattva, Rajas and Tamas." साम्य, equilibrium, is the technical term for Prakṛti's unmanifest state, so the nama places Her at the point before the guṇas differentiate.

That is a third position on the guṇas. 961 गुणातीता put Her beyond them; 984 त्रिगुणा made Her endowed with them, resolved by the Vāyu Purāṇa's "by function and by her sport she is threefold"; and here she is their equilibrium. आत्मिका for the fourth time — 611, 853, 963, and here.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and the verse is a run of pairs and triads: perishable and imperishable, all worlds, the universe, the three ends, fortune, three eyes, three qualities.

757 is the substantial entry, and its interest is that अक्षर means both imperishable and syllable, so the nama says at once that She is both the transient and the eternal, and that she is both one-syllabled and many-syllabled. The first has referents at 661 and 680; the second has one at 712, the single-vowel nama.

763's equilibrium is the third distinct position the text takes on the three guṇas, and none of the three is reconciled with the others.

Textual note. 757's dev reads क्षारा- for क्षर-, a spurious long आ. 763's dev carries ॥१४६॥, the third instance of a verse number inside a nama, displacing this verse's range and the next's by one. 759's computed pada reads विश्वधा-अरिणी for विश्व-धारिणी. 758, 759 and 760 have no commentary bodies.

---

## स्वर्गापवर्गदा शुद्धा जपापुष्पनिभाकृतिः । ओजोवती द्युतिधरा यज्ञरूपा प्रियव्रता

*svargāpavargadā śuddhā japāpuṣpanibhākṛtiḥ । ojovatī dyutidharā yajñarūpā priyavratā*

Verse 147, namas 764–770.

764. स्वर्गापवर्गदा → स्वर्ग-अपवर्ग-दा

स्वर्ग = heaven (स्वः + ग, "going to the bright realm")
अपवर्ग = completion, cessation; final emancipation (अप + वृज् "to turn away")
दा = giving
"The Giver of heaven and of release."

Vigraha: स्वर्गम् अपवर्गं च ददातीति।

Sandhi: स्वर्ग + अपवर्ग → स्वर्गापवर्ग (आ by 6.1.101).

Bhāskararāya's gloss distinguishes the two gifts by duration. The Śruti's definition of heaven is quoted — "that happiness which is not interrupted by pain now or in future, attained through desire, is called Svarga" — and then: "this happiness is temporary. The happiness in salvation is an eternal one."

अपवर्ग is अप + वृज्, a turning-away, so release is named by aversion where स्वर्ग is named by destination. And the pairing repeats 742's divided reading, where She gave "worldly enjoyment and salvation both" against the Rudrayāmala's rule that the two exclude each other.

765. शुद्धा → शुद्धा

शुद्धा = pure, cleansed (past participle of शुध् "to purify")
"The Pure."

Vigraha: शुद्धा निर्मला।

The gloss is five words: "free from the stains of avidyā."

शुद्ध had been the first member of 973 शुद्धमानसा, where the purity was of mind; here it stands alone. And Śuddhavidyā, built on it, was one of the three into which the Gauḍapāda Sūtra divided the one Vidyā at 840, and one of the three corresponding to Cit at 907.

766. जपापुष्पनिभाकृतिः → जपा-पुष्प-निभ-आकृतिः

जपा = the china rose, hibiscus
पुष्प = a flower
निभ = resembling, like
आकृतिः = form, shape (आ + कृ "to make")
"She whose form is like the china-rose flower."

Vigraha: जपापुष्पनिभा आकृतिः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: निभ + आकृतिः → निभाकृतिः (आ by 6.1.101).

This is Her fifth red, and again a particular one — after coral at 891, the young sun's rose at 922, bandhūka at 964 and pomegranate at 560. The china rose had also been one of the Viśva's senses of उमा at 633.

The commentary here is displaced. Its gloss trails off with "this name may be taken as two, adding the syllable—", and the body does not continue that thought but expounds अजपा, which belongs to the division just mooted: "O Deveśī, that which brings to the practitioners of Mantra the attainment of the repetition is called Ajapā, which breaks asunder the noose of saṃsāra." Ajapā is the unrepeated repetition, the haṃsa-mantra told by the breath — which 672 and 999 both rested on.

Then the Hema Kośa on पुष्प: "the flowering season, the chariot of Kubera, a flower, and the beauty of the eyes."

आकृति for the fourth time — 830 प्रकटाकृतिः, 619 पावनाकृतिः, 933 मङ्गलाकृतिः, and here.

767. ओजोवती → ओजस्-वती

ओजस् = vital power, vigour, splendour; and per the Vedic commentaries, the eighth dhātu
वती = possessing (मतुप्, feminine ङीप्)
"She who possesses vital power."

Vigraha: ओजः अस्याः अस्तीति ओजोवती।

Sandhi: ओजस् + वती → ओजोवती, the अस् becoming ओ before a voiced consonant, as with मनस् at 941 मनोमयी.

"Ojas is explained as the eighth substance in the Vedic Commentaries. Some explain it as the vitality of the senses." The Viśva: "Ojas means light, the vitality of substances, splendour, strength and radiance."

The eighth dhātu is worth marking. The text's yoginī-sets at 509–534 ran through seven — rasa, rakta, māṃsa, medas, asthi, majjā, śukra — one to each yoginī, and 572 पराशक्तिः gave a different reckoning in which nine substances were divided between Śiva and Devī and "the tenth substance alone is called Parā Śakti." So this text carries three incompatible countings of the bodily constituents: seven, nine-plus-one, and here an eighth.

768. द्युतिधरा → द्युति-धरा

द्युति = light, splendour, brilliance (from द्युत् "to shine")
धरा = bearing, holding (from धृ "to hold")
"The Bearer of light."

Vigraha: द्युतिं धरतीति द्युतिधरा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

द्युत् is the root behind दिव् and द्यु, the bright sky — and द्युति is one of the senses the Viśva gave ओजस् in the previous nama, so 767 and 768 overlap by a word. धरा is the participle of 530 सर्वायुधधरा and the noun of 955 धरा.

769. यज्ञरूपा → यज्ञ-रूपा

यज्ञ = sacrifice; and per the Śruti, Viṣṇu
रूपा = form
"She whose form is the sacrifice."

Vigraha: यज्ञः रूपं यस्याः सा।

The Taittirīya Saṃhitā is cited for the identification — "Yajña means Viṣṇu" — which is the same authority 881 यज्ञप्रिया used: "yajña, on the authority of the Śruti, means Viṣṇu."

Then the sacrificial anatomy, from the Harivaṃśa and Padma Purāṇas, and it is the longest single figure in this verse: "Vedas are his feet, the sacrificial post his teeth, the oblation his hand, the pile of sacrificial fuel his face, the fire his tongue, the rules his hair, the Brāhmaṇa his head, day and night his eyes, the Vedāntas his ear-ornaments, the sacrificial ladle his mouth, the ghee his nose, the great sound of the Sāman his voice; he is virtue and truth, good actions his moving to and fro, penance his finger-nails, the sacrificial animals his knees, the Audgātra his bowels, the homa his organ of generation, the fruits his organs, Vāyu his inner breath."

So the rite is mapped limb by limb, which is the procedure the text uses on Her own body at 85–87 for the mantra's three kūṭas and at 847, 936 and 942 for the Virāṭ form.

The यज्ञ-namas of this text are 881–883, where She was the sacrifice's lover, performer and patron, and 946 पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया with its six competing sets of five.

770. प्रियव्रता → प्रिय-व्रता

प्रिय = dear, beloved
व्रता = vowed, observing a vow (व्रत)
"She to whom vows are dear."

Vigraha: प्रियं व्रतं यस्याः सा।

The gloss is generous in a way that matters: "she is fond of all vows, even those which are made to other deities." And the Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa is quoted for the principle: "he who makes a vow to any god or to any goddess, all is for the delight of Śiva and Devī, who are the creators of the world. There is no difference here, because the whole world is Śiva and Śakti."

So a vow to any deity reaches Her, and the reason given is not tolerance but identity. That is the same argument the text made of Kubera at 885 ("no difference between the worshipper and the worshipped"), of the Vipras at 888, of Viṣṇu at 893, and of Śiva at 910.

"Priyavrata also means the name of a king" — and व्रता had stood at 709 सदाशिवपतिव्रता, where the vow was to one husband "in all the three times."

Note on the verse. Seven namas, and no single theme: two gifts, purity, a red flower, vigour, light, the sacrifice, and vows.

764 and 770 make the frame worth noticing. The first gives heaven and release together, which the Rudrayāmala at 742 said were mutually exclusive; the last accepts vows made to other gods, on the ground that "the whole world is Śiva and Śakti." Both namas widen what counts.

767's eighth dhātu is the third counting of the bodily constituents in this text, against the seven of the yoginī-sets and the nine-plus-one of 572, and none of the three is reconciled with the others.

769's sacrificial anatomy is the fullest limb-by-limb mapping in the text apart from the mantra-body of 85–87.

Textual note. 766's commentary is displaced: its gloss breaks off mid-clause proposing a division of the nama, and its body expounds अजपा, which belongs to that division rather than to the nama as it stands. 768 has no commentary body.

---

## दुराराध्या दुराधर्षा पाटलीकुसुमप्रिया । महती मेरुनिलया मन्दारकुसुमप्रिया

*durārādhyā durādharṣā pāṭalīkusumapriyā । mahatī merunilayā mandārakusumapriyā*

Verse 148, namas 771–776.

771. दुराराध्या → दुर्-आराध्या

दुर् = hard, difficult (दुस्)
आराध्या = to be worshipped, propitiated (आ + राध्, gerundive यत्)
"She who is hard to worship."

Vigraha: दुःखेन आराध्या।

Sandhi: दुर् + आराध्या → दुराराध्या.

The gloss is six words and it names who finds it hard: "impossible to be worshipped by the fickle-minded."

That is a needed qualification, because 681 सुखाराध्या said the opposite — easily worshipped, "without bodily pain by fasting and without restrictions on the mode of meditation." The two namas are ninety apart and Bhāskararāya reconciles them by the worshipper: easy in method, impossible for the unsteady. The same distinction, differently drawn, governs 869's quick grace against 990's long practice.

आराध्या for the sixth time — 870, 918, 923, 977, 681, 715, and here, making seven.

772. दुराधर्षा → दुर्-आधर्षा

दुर् = hard, difficult
आधर्षा = to be assailed, overcome, approached violently (आ + धृष् "to dare, to assail")
"She who cannot be assailed."

Vigraha: दुःखेन आधर्षा।

Two readings. "She is not to be attained by the fickle-minded men" — repeating 771's qualification. Or "Dur, difficult; ādharṣa, controlling — that is, it is very difficult to perceive her."

धृष् is "to dare," so आधर्ष is an assault, and the nama is a claim about invulnerability rather than about difficulty of access. Read so it belongs with 871 बहिर्मुखसुदुर्लभा, where सु stacked on दुर् made the difficulty emphatic for the outward-faced.

773. पाटलीकुसुमप्रिया → पाटली-कुसुम-प्रिया

पाटली = the trumpet-flower tree
कुसुम = a flower
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in the pāṭalī flower."

Vigraha: पाटलीकुसुमं प्रियं यस्याः सा।

"Pāṭalī, a red and white flower." And the Padma Purāṇa gives the pairing: "Śiva is fond of the Bilva tree and Devī of the Pāṭala."

पाटल had been the colour at 922 तरुणादित्यपाटला, where Bhāskararāya made it the rose of the young sun and the whole entry turned on colour being a function of the meditation's purpose. The word is the flower's name used for its colour there; here it is the flower.

This verse has two कुसुमप्रिया-namas, at 773 and 776, and the text has three more कुसुम-compounds — 919 चैतन्यकुसुमप्रिया, 964 बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या, 560 दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा.

774. महती → महती

महती = great (feminine of महत्); also the Vīṇā of Nārada
"The Great."

Vigraha: महती महाभागा।

Three glosses, and the third is a lexical surprise. "As she manifests in the form of the things she is called Mahat." Śākapūrṇi explains it as "the Mahat by which all things are measured"; Yāska explains it as "to be worshipped." And then: "Mahatī means also the Vīṇā of Nārada."

महती had stood at 673 in this text as a nama in its own right, glossed as a metre of thirty-six syllables — so the word appears twice among the thousand names, once as a metre and once as Nārada's lute. And महत् is the first tattva, the कार्य of 862 कार्यकारणनिर्मुक्ता, "the tattva-series beginning with Mahat."

775. मेरुनिलया → मेरु-निलया

मेरु = Mount Meru, the axial mountain
निलया = abode, dwelling (नि + ली "to settle")
"She whose abode is Meru."

Vigraha: मेरुः निलयः यस्याः सा।

The Tantrarāja's twenty-eighth chapter is quoted, and it makes Meru a cosmology of Nityās: "now I shall describe to you the sixteen Nityā deities which are the Lokas" — and after their worlds with their oceans and islands, "in the midst of Meru the great shining Lalitā ever remains," with fourteen continents around it up to the ocean where the other deities remain, and beyond them, "in the last supreme ether, is the abode of Citrā and the other deities."

Then Bhāskararāya stops: "these are to be known from a guru alone." That is the fifth such referral in the text, after 907, 948, 982 and 713.

And the second reading names the three Prastāras: "the Śrīcakra has three aspects — Bhūmi, Kailāsa and Meru." Sastry's footnote at 577 gave the same three with their identifications: Meru with the sixteen Nityās, Kailāsa with the fifty-one mātṛkās, Bhū with the eight Vāsinīs. So this nama's Meru is the first of them, and 578 महाकैलासनिलया was the second.

Meru had opened the text's topography at 55 सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था, where She dwelt on its central peak, and 56 श्रीमन्नगरनायिका gave her the city upon it. निलया for the seventh time.

776. मन्दारकुसुमप्रिया → मन्दार-कुसुम-प्रिया

मन्दार = the coral tree, one of the five trees of Indra's heaven; and per the commentary, the Devataru or Śvetārka
कुसुम = a flower
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in the mandāra flower."

Vigraha: मन्दारकुसुमं प्रियं यस्याः सा।

The gloss is four words: "Mandāra: Devataru, or the Śvetārka tree."

मन्दार is one of the pañcavṛkṣa of Indra's heaven, so this flower is celestial where 773's pāṭalī was terrestrial, and the verse pairs them at its two ends. प्रिया for the twelfth time in the text.

Note on the verse. Six namas in three pairs, and the pairs are of difficulty, greatness and flowers — with the flowers split to the two ends.

771–772 are the correction the text needed. 681 सुखाराध्या had said She is easily worshipped, "without bodily pain by fasting"; here she is hard to worship and cannot be assailed, and the reconciliation is in the worshipper — "impossible to be worshipped by the fickle-minded." Easy in method, impossible in temperament.

775 is the substantial entry, and it does two things. It gives Meru as a cosmology of the sixteen Nityās with Lalitā at the centre, and it names the three Prastāras of the Śrīcakra — Bhūmi, Kailāsa, Meru — of which 578 was the second and this the first. Then it stops and refers the reader to a teacher, the fifth time the text does that.

774 also puts महती into the thousand names twice, at 673 as a thirty-six-syllable metre and here as Nārada's lute.

---

## वीराराध्या विराड्रूपा विरजा विश्वतोमुखी । प्रत्यग्रूपा पराकाशा प्राणदा प्राणरूपिणी

*vīrārādhyā virāḍrūpā virajā viśvatomukhī । pratyagrūpā parākāśā prāṇadā prāṇarūpiṇī*

Verse 149, namas 777–784.

777. वीराराध्या → वीर-आराध्या

वीर = a hero; in Kaula usage, the foremost among devotees
आराध्या = to be worshipped
"She who is worshipped by the heroes."

Vigraha: वीरैः आराध्या।

Sandhi: वीर + आराध्या → वीराराध्या (आ by 6.1.101). The computed pada reads वीरा-राध्या, dividing one letter late.

The commentary defines the वीर, and the definition is entirely interior: "one who enjoys or realises the Self, the remover of pain, brings about the dissolution of egoism and of what is opposed to the Self — that is, duality — devoted to bravery."

So heroism here is the dissolution of egoism, not its assertion. That fits the Kaula sense the text gave वीर at 836 वीरमाता, "the chief among devotees," and at 898 वीरगोष्ठीप्रिया, the assembly of adepts — while 899 वीरा took the word domestically, the Nāmamālā's "she who has a husband and sons."

आराध्या for the eighth time, and this verse follows two namas of difficulty with one of who succeeds.

778. विराड्रूपा → विराट्-रूपा

विराट् = the Vast — the cosmic form, the universe considered as a body (वि + राज् "to shine, to rule")
रूपा = form
"She whose form is the Vast."

Vigraha: विराट् रूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: विराट् + रूपा → विराड्रूपा, the ट् voicing to ड् before र्. The dev field reads विराड्पा, having lost the रू of रूपा — so the compound's second member is reduced to a syllable, and only the gloss preserves it.

index.html carries no commentary beyond a counting marker: the twenty-eighth verse divides forty-eight names.

The Virāṭ form is the one the text has been assembling feature by feature — Atala-loka as Her waist at 847 तलोदरी, a pīṭha in Her eyes at 936 विशालाक्षी, the ether as Her hair at 942 व्योमकेशी. This nama names the whole of which those were parts.

779. विरजा → वि-रजा

वि = without
रजा = dust, impurity; passion; and per the commentary, sin, light, water, worlds (रजस्)
"She who is without impurity."

Vigraha: विगतं रजः यस्याः सा।

"Vi, without; rajas, sin." Then the geography: "Virajā is the presiding deity at Utkalakṣetra," and the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa — "at Virajā the goddess is Virajā, established by Brahmā. By seeing her a mortal purifies as far as seven generations." Bhāskararāya adds that रजस् "also means light, water and worlds."

रजस् is one of the three guṇas, whose equilibrium She was at 763 त्रिगुणात्मिका sixteen namas back, and which she transcended at 961 and consisted of at 984. Here one of the three is denied of her by name.

Virajā at Utkala — Jājpur in Orissa — joins the located identifications, the eighth in the text.

780. विश्वतोमुखी → विश्वतस्-मुखी

विश्वतस् = from all sides, in every direction (विश्व with the adverbial तस्)
मुखी = faced (मुख with the feminine)
"She who faces in every direction."

Vigraha: विश्वतः मुखानि यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: the visarga of विश्वतः becomes ओ before म्, as at 532 सर्वतोमुखी — which is this nama with सर्व for विश्व, and there the citation was Gītā 13.13, "everywhere eyes, heads and mouths."

Here the citation is Śvetāśvatara 3.3, "having eyes and mouths on all sides," and Bhāskararāya uses it to raise a problem and solve it. The scriptures also say "he has no hand or feet" — so which is true? His answer: "when a form is created by devotees through meditation, then alone does she become manifest" as having hands and feet everywhere; "the other passages speak in the real sense. Hence there is no contradiction."

That is 922's principle applied to limbs instead of colour — the descriptions are of what is meditated upon, not of what is the case — and it is the same reconciliation-by-purpose the text uses throughout.

781. प्रत्यग्रूपा → प्रत्यक्-रूपा

प्रत्यक् = turned inward, backward (प्रति + अञ्च् "to bend")
रूपा = form
"She whose form is inward."

Vigraha: प्रत्यक् रूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: प्रत्यक् + रूपा → प्रत्यग्रूपा, the क् voicing before र्.

The gloss is a piece of terminology, set out symmetrically: "Pratyak, tending inwards. The direction of the senses towards objects is called Bahirmukhatva and Parāṅmukhatva; their inward direction towards the Self is called Antarmukhatva and Pratyaṅmukhatva."

Kaṭha Upaniṣad 4.1 is cited: "the Self-existent made the senses outward-going; hence one sees externally but not internally." So the inwardness is against the grain of how the senses were made, and "the meaning is that Her nature is to be seen internally."

The pair अन्तर्मुख and बहिर्मुख is namas 870 and 871, where She was fully worshipped by the one and exceedingly hard for the other to attain — and 901's Nāda was "experienced by the mind turned inwards." This nama gives that vocabulary its technical statement.

782. पराकाशा → परा-आकाशा

परा = supreme, highest
आकाशा = ether, space
"The supreme Ether."

Vigraha: परा आकाशा।

Sandhi: परा + आकाशा → पराकाशा (आ by 6.1.101).

"Because she is without quality, that is, she is Parabrahman." And the identification of ether with Brahman is argued from scripture: Chāndogya I.9.1 — "he said, that is ether; ether is the greatest of all these things; this ether is the supreme rest" — with Vedānta Sūtra 1.1.22, "the ether is Brahman on account of characteristic marks," which Bhāskararāya glosses as meaning "it does not mean the elemental ether."

The Kūrma Purāṇa: "whose supreme divine energy is called ether. Thus she is the origin of the Universe — one, all, all-controlling, Maheśvarī, energy, without beginning, called ether, as if shining in the heaven."

This is the fifth word for ether in the text, after वियत् (837, 550), गगन (855), व्योम (942) and दहराकाश (609) — and the second, after दहराकाश, that is not the element. The distinction Bhāskararāya insists on here is exactly the one 609's dahara-vidyā depended on.

783. प्राणदा → प्राण-दा

प्राण = breath, vital air; the five vital breaths; the eleven senses (प्र + अन् "to breathe")
दा = giving; and per the commentary, controlling
"The Giver of life."

Vigraha: प्राणं ददातीति प्राणदा।

The gloss takes दा against its obvious sense: "Prāṇa, the five kinds of vital breath or the eleven senses; dā, literally to destroy, to control." So the nama may be giver or controller of the breaths.

Then the scriptural identification, and it is the point of the entry: Vedānta Sūtra 1.1.23, "for the same reason breath is Brahman," establishes that the word breath in the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad denotes Brahman — "I am Prāṇa, I am consciousness; worship me as age and immortality."

प्राण had been ruled at 831 प्राणेश्वरी and bestowed at 832 प्राणदात्री, where दात्री was the तृ agent-noun; this is the same claim with the bare दा.

784. प्राणरूपिणी → प्राण-रूपिणी

प्राण = breath, life; and per the Nityā Tantra, the sixteen Nityā deities
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying
"She whose form is breath."

Vigraha: प्राणः रूपं यस्याः सा।

The computed pada reads प्राण्-अरूपिणी, which makes the nama mean the opposite by inventing a privative; the split is प्राण + रूपिणी.

"Hence Prāṇa means Brahman," continuing 783's argument, with Chāndogya 4.10.5 — "Prāṇa is Brahman, Ka is Brahman, ether is Brahman" — and Manu 12.123: "the same Brahman some call fire, others Manu, others Prajāpati, others Indra, others breath, and others Maheśvarī."

Then the Nityā Tantra's reading, which is chronometric. The sixteen Nityā deities are called Prāṇas "because from the time of one respiration the day, month and the rest are determined; again, twenty-two and a half respirations make orderly the twelve zodiacal signs." So breath measures time, the Nityās are the measures, and "according to this method it is clear enough that Lalitā also becomes breath."

The sixteen Nityās are the lunar days of 610 प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता and the Meru Prastāra of 775, nine namas back. Here they are respirations.

Note on the verse. Eight namas, and the verse runs from the outermost form to the innermost.

778 names the Virāṭ, the cosmic body the text had been assembling piecemeal at 847, 936 and 942. 780 gives that body faces on every side — and Bhāskararāya immediately reconciles it with the scriptures that deny Her hands and feet, by the rule that meditative descriptions are not literal. Then 781 turns the direction inward and supplies the technical vocabulary for it, प्रत्यङ्मुखत्व against बहिर्मुखत्व, which 870–871 had used without defining. 782 makes Her the supreme ether, insisting it is not the element. And 783–784 end in breath, which the Vedānta Sūtra is cited to prove means Brahman.

So the sequence is: the vast body, its faces, the inward turn, the non-elemental ether, and the breath. It is the tightest progression in this batch.

Textual note. 778's dev reads विराड्पा, having lost the रू of रूपा; only the gloss preserves the word. 784's computed pada reads प्राण्-अरूपिणी, which inverts the sense, and 777's reads वीरा-राध्या for वीर-आराध्या.

---

## मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या मन्त्रिणीन्यस्तराज्यधूः । त्रिपुरेशी जयत्सेना निस्त्रैगुण्या परापरा

*mārtāṇḍabhairavārādhyā mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ । tripureśī jayatsenā nistraiguṇyā parāparā*

Verse 150, namas 785–790.

785. मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या → मार्ताण्ड-भैरव-आराध्या

मार्ताण्ड = the sun (said to be from मृत-अण्ड, "born of a dead egg")
भैरव = Bhairava, the terrible — a form of Śiva
आराध्या = to be worshipped
"She who is worshipped by Mārtāṇḍabhairava."

Vigraha: मार्ताण्डभैरवेण आराध्या।

Sandhi: भैरव + आराध्या → भैरवाराध्या (आ by 6.1.101). The dev field breaks the compound with a space after मार्ताण्ड, and the computed pada divides it as मार्ताण्ड-भैरवा-राध्या, one letter late at the second joint.

Three identifications. First, a position in the diagram: "in the Śrīcakra, between the twenty-second and twenty-third walls, there is the devotee of Devī named Mārtāṇḍabhairava" — and Durvāsa's Lalitāstavaratna (100) is quoted, "in my heart I adore Mārtāṇḍabhairava, decked with the jewelled crown, sporting with his wife Chāyā, who is the energy which supplies light to the eye." That is the same kind of placement as 686 राज्यवल्लभा, where the gods were located "between the thirteenth and fourteenth walls."

Second, a regional identity: "Śiva, in order to kill the Daitya called Maṇimalla, mounted a horse and descended to Earth, and is called in the Mahārāṣṭra country by the name Mallāri and also Mārtāṇḍabhairava," with the Tantracintāmaṇi confirming and the Mallārimāhātmya describing his worship of Devī. Third, simply the Sun.

आराध्या for the ninth time in the text, and the third in this batch alone after 771 and 777.

786. मन्त्रिणीन्यस्तराज्यधूः → मन्त्रिणी-न्यस्त-राज्य-धूः

मन्त्रिणी = the Minister — Śyāmalā, Rājamātaṅgī
न्यस्त = laid down, entrusted, deposited (नि + अस् "to throw")
राज्य = dominion, kingdom
धूः = a burden, a yoke; the pole of a chariot (धुर्)
"She who has entrusted the burden of dominion to Mantriṇī."

Vigraha: मन्त्रिण्यां न्यस्ता राज्यधूः यस्याः सा।

धूर् is the chariot-pole, the point where the load bears — so राज्यधूः is government as a weight rather than a right, and न्यस्त is a setting-down.

The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa is quoted for the delegation: "the care of the dominion and of the Śaktis of Lalitā, the supreme ruler — all are in the power of Mantriṇī." Mantriṇī is Śyāmalā, who rode the Geyacakra at 69 गेयचक्ररथारूढमन्त्रिणीपरिसेविता and killed Viṣaṅga at 75; and 911 सदाशिवकुटुम्बिनी made Śyāmalā one of the household.

Then two further readings. मन्त्रिणी as those who worship by mantras — "Mantra is a pure thought, because it has the quality of protecting the man during meditation," which is the मननात् त्रायते derivation used at 846. Or मन्त्रिणी as "a certain effort which leads to union with Bhagavatī, and in that effort depends the power of attaining universal dominion." Śiva Sūtras II.1–3 are cited: "thought is Mantra; effort is the means; knowledge is the body."

And धुर् is the word of 915's second division, where स्व + भा + अवम + धुर made Her bear "the yoke of the wise," and of 657 युगन्धरा, where the yoke was the universe.

787. त्रिपुरेशी → त्रिपुरा-ईशी

त्रिपुरा = Tripurā
ईशी = mistress, ruler
"Tripureśī."

Vigraha: त्रिपुरायाः ईशी।

Sandhi: त्रिपुरा + ईशी → त्रिपुरेशी (आ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

The whole commentary is one sentence, and it is an office: "the deity of the Sarvāśāparipūraka cakra is called Tripureśī."

That is the second enclosure of the Śrīcakra, and it completes a set the text builds across four namas. Tripuramālinī is given the Antardaśāra, the sixth, at 875; Tripurāmbā the eighth at 976; Tripurāśrī the fifth at 978; and Tripureśī the second here. Four of the nine āvaraṇa-deities named, and Bhāskararāya's numbering is correct in each case — Tripureśī is indeed second in the standard list.

Fourteenth turn of ईश्.

788. जयत्सेना → जयत्-सेना

जयत् = conquering, victorious (present participle of जि "to conquer")
सेना = an army, a host
"She whose army conquers."

Vigraha: जयन्ती सेना यस्याः सा।

"Jayat refers to the conquest of Bhaṇḍāsura and others. Senā, her attendant Śaktis; or Jayatsenā is the name of a king."

So the nama points back to the war-narrative at 65–82, and सेना is the word of 65 भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्तशक्तिसेनासमन्विता and 679 बृहत्सेना.

789. निस्त्रैगुण्या → निः-त्रैगुण्या

निः = without, free from
त्रैगुण्या = the state of having three guṇas (vṛddhi abstract of त्रिगुण)
"She who is free of the three-guṇa state."

Vigraha: त्रैगुण्यं यस्याः नास्ति सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The form is worth noting: त्रैगुण्य is not "the three guṇas" but the abstract of being three-guṇa'd — so what is denied is the condition rather than the qualities.

This is the fourth position the text takes on the guṇas, and it stands twenty-six namas after the third. 961 गुणातीता put Her beyond them; 984 त्रिगुणा made her endowed with them; 763 त्रिगुणात्मिका made her their equilibrium; and here the whole condition is negated. Only 984's Vāyu Purāṇa line — threefold "by function and by her sport" — offers any reconciliation, and it is not repeated at any of the other three.

790. परापरा → परा-अपरा

परा = far, superior, higher; also an enemy, another
अपरा = near, inferior, lower; also the Self, a friend
"The Higher and the Lower."

Vigraha: परा च अपरा च परापरा।

Sandhi: परा + अपरा → परापरा (आ by 6.1.101).

The commentary is a run of paired opposites, and the pairs are not consistent with one another — which is the point.

The Śruti's levelling: "Brahman is the servant, Brahman is the ferryman, and Brahman is these gamblers." Then परा as others and अपरा as the Self; or परा foe and अपरा friend, with Gītā 9.29, "I have neither foe nor friend"; or परा the far and अपरा the near, with Gītā 13.15, "I am far and near." The Viśva: "parā means superior, enemy, distance."

Then a technical use: in logic, सामान्य, generality, "is threefold — parā, aparā, and parāparā," which are the higher, lower and intermediate universals.

And finally the theological pair that matters: "parā and aparā, the two forms of Brahman, the unconditioned and the conditioned," with Praśna Upaniṣad 5.2 — "this indeed, O Satyakāma, is Parā and Aparā" — and the Smṛti, "two Brahmans are to be known, one is..."

That last is the distinction the whole dialogue at 703–713 was about, and 707 गुह्यरूपिणी had resolved the scriptural conflict by "attributing two forms to the one Brahman." Here the two forms are the nama.

Note on the verse. Six namas, and the verse divides into two threes: two named devotees and delegates, then three of Her nature.

785–786 are both about someone else acting for Her — Mārtāṇḍabhairava worshipping from between the twenty-second and twenty-third walls, and Mantriṇī carrying the burden of government. And 786's धूः is worth the attention: government named as a chariot-pole, the point where a load bears, and न्यस्त as setting it down.

787 completes a quiet set. With 875, 976 and 978, the text names four of the nine Śrīcakra enclosure-deities, and the commentary's numbering is right every time — sixth, eighth, fifth, and second here.

789 is the fourth incompatible position on the guṇas, and 790 closes the verse on परा and अपरा, the conditioned and unconditioned Brahman, which is the pair the eleven-nama dialogue at 703–713 was constructed to reconcile.

---

Textual note for verses 141–150.

Verse-number contamination, third instance: 763 त्रिगुणात्मिका carries ॥१४६॥ in its dev field, which displaces the table's ranges for this verse and the next by one — 757–762 and 763–770 where they should be 757–763 and 764–770. The earlier instances are 830 प्रकटाकृतिः ॥१५५॥ and 722 गुरुप्रिया ॥१३९॥, both with the same effect.

Sandhi mis-division, one instance: 748 रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः has lost its visarga and 749 मृत्युदारुकुठारिका has gained the resulting र्.

Avagraha, one instance: 729's dev reads ऽऽनन्दकलिका, carrying the आ elided from चित्कला. Tenth instance in the text, and the doubled mark again correctly signals a long vowel — the rule established at 985 still holds without exception.

Letter faults: 743's dev reads पापारष्य- for पापारण्य-, ष् for ण्. 757's reads क्षारा- for क्षर-, a spurious long आ. 778's reads विराड्पा for विराड्रूपा, the रू lost — the most damaging of the three, since the compound's second member disappears and only the gloss preserves it.

Spacing: 785's dev breaks मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या after मार्ताण्ड.

Shared bodies: 749 and 750, with 750's gloss also being 749's and its own heading stranded in 751's gloss. Displaced commentary: 766's gloss breaks off mid-clause proposing a division of the nama, and its body expounds अजपा, which belongs to that division and not to the nama.

Computed pada faults: 759 विश्वधा-अरिणी for विश्व-धारिणी; 777 वीरा-राध्या for वीर-आराध्या; 784 प्राण्-अरूपिणी for प्राण-रूपिणी, which inverts the sense; 785 मार्ताण्ड-भैरवा-राध्या for मार्ताण्ड-भैरव-आराध्या.

No commentary body: 731, 738, 745, 746, 748, 758, 759, 760, 768, 789.
