## अनाकलितसादृश्यचुबुकश्रीविराजिता । कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभितकन्धरा

*anākalitasādṛśyacubukaśrīvirājitā । kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtraśobhitakandharā*

Verse 12, namas 29–30.

29. अनाकलितसादृश्यचुबुकश्रीविराजिता → अन्-आकलित-सादृश्य-चुबुक-श्री-विराजिता

अन् = not (नञ् before a vowel)
आकलित = ascertained, found, reckoned (आ + कल् "to reckon")
सादृश्य = likeness, resemblance (vṛddhi abstract of सदृश)
चुबुक = the chin
श्री = beauty, splendour
विराजिता = made resplendent (वि + राज् "to shine")
"She resplendent with the beauty of a chin for which no likeness can be found."

Vigraha: अनाकलितसादृश्या चुबुकश्रीः यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The construction is the aṅga-series' fifth way of saying *unsurpassed*, and it is the only one that gives up on comparison rather than winning one. The cheeks outdo a ruby mirror at 23 by परिभावि, the lips shame coral at 24 by न्यक्कारि, the nose-jewel eclipses stars at 20 by तिरस्कारि, the feet outdo lotuses at 45 by पराकृत — and here nothing is outdone, because no simile could be reckoned in the first place. सादृश्य is the word for the resemblance a comparison needs, and अनाकलित says none was found.

आकलित is from कल्, to reckon — the root of कला, which the text works at 611 कलात्मिका and 612 कलानाथा, and of 902 विज्ञानकलना, where कलना is the making-one's-own of direct knowledge.

30. कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभितकन्धरा → कामेश-बद्ध-माङ्गल्य-सूत्र-शोभित-कन्धरा

कामेश = Kāmeśa, Kāmeśvara
बद्ध = bound, tied (past participle of बन्ध् "to bind")
माङ्गल्य = auspicious, nuptial (vṛddhi derivative of मङ्गल)
सूत्र = a thread, a cord (from सिव् "to sew")
शोभित = adorned, made beautiful (from शुभ्)
कन्धरा = the neck, the throat
"She whose throat is adorned with the nuptial thread tied by Kāmeśa."

Vigraha: कामेशेन बद्धेन माङ्गल्यसूत्रेण शोभिता कन्धरा यस्याः सा।

index.html's body is only the verse-division marker (12) and a stray footnote numeral.

The nama's own footnote has been displaced into nama 32's body, two namas on, and it is worth recovering because it is a historical remark rather than a gloss: "the marriage emblem tied round the neck was not the Āryan custom and was not found referred to in any Vedic literature. Earring was the emblem." So Sastry notes that the maṅgalya-sūtra of this nama is post-Vedic, and that the older emblem of marriage was the ear-ornament — which is nama 22, where Her two ear-pendants are the sun and the moon.

This is the neck, so it is where the Kāmarāja kūṭa begins on the reckoning of 13 and 86. कन्धरा is not used again; the throat is कण्ठ at 86 कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्तमध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी, which draws the same boundary technically — "from below the throat down to the waist is the middle kūṭa."

माङ्गल्य had stood at 17, where the brows were the festal arches of Kāma's nuptial house. The wedding-imagery of that nama is here made literal, and the same husband ties the thread.

Note on the verse. Two namas, chin and throat, and the second is a boundary.

29 completes the description of the face by declining to compare it, which after four namas of eclipsed rubies, corals and stars is a change of tactic rather than a repetition.

30 marks the seam. Everything from 13 to 29 has been the head, which is the Vāgbhava kūṭa; from the neck onward is the Kāmarāja. And its displaced footnote is the only place in these verses where Sastry steps outside the commentary to date a custom.

Textual note. 29 has no body; 30's is a verse marker and a bare footnote numeral, its own footnote having been carried down into 32.

---

## कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजान्विता । रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता

*kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyabhujānvitā । ratnagraiveyacintākalolamuktāphalānvitā*

Verse 13, namas 31–32.

31. कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजान्विता → कनक-अङ्गद-केयूर-कमनीय-भुजा-अन्विता

कनक = gold
अङ्गद = an armlet worn on the upper arm (अङ्ग + द)
केयूर = a bracelet, an arm-ring
कमनीय = lovely, desirable (from कम् "to desire," gerundive अनीय)
भुजा = an arm (from भुज् "to bend")
अन्विता = endowed with, accompanied by (अनु + इ)
"She endowed with lovely arms bearing golden armlets and bracelets."

Vigraha: कनकाङ्गदकेयूराभ्यां कमनीयाभ्यां भुजाभ्याम् अन्विता।

Sandhi: कनक + अङ्गद → कनकाङ्गद and भुजा + अन्विता → भुजान्विता (आ by 6.1.101 both).

index.html's body for this nama is the fragment "necklace of" — two words that belong to nama 32's gloss, which as recorded reads "having a pearl dangling from a gems and gold" and is missing exactly that phrase. So 32's gloss and 31's body together give "having a pearl dangling from a necklace of gems and gold," and neither field is complete on its own.

अङ्गद and केयूर are both upper-arm ornaments and the pair is conventional. भुजा is from भुज्, to bend — the arm named by its joint, where बाहु at 7 is the arm as a limb. Those four arms at 7 held the noose, goad, bow and arrows; these two are simply ornamented, which is the aṅga-series describing what 7–11 had already itemised.

कनक is the metal of 864 कनत्कनकताटङ्का, where the earrings are glittering gold — and there the dev field has lost the कनत् to a misreading as फनत्.

32. रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता → रत्न-ग्रैवेय-चिन्ताक-लोल-मुक्ता-फल-अन्विता

रत्न = a gem, a jewel
ग्रैवेय = worn on the neck, a necklace (vṛddhi derivative of ग्रीवा, "neck"); and per the second reading, one who meditates on the throat
चिन्ताक = a pendant, a locket; and per the second reading, a meditator (from चिन्त् "to think")
लोल = swinging, dangling; also fickle, restless, greedy
मुक्ता = a pearl; and per the second reading, the liberated
फल = a fruit; and per the second reading, the fruit obtained
अन्विता = endowed with
"She endowed with a pearl swinging from a jewelled neck-pendant."

Vigraha: रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताके लोलेन मुक्ताफलेन अन्विता।

Sandhi: फल + अन्विता → फलान्विता (आ by 6.1.101).

The plain reading is an ornament. Bhāskararāya's alternative turns the whole compound into a taxonomy of worshippers, and it is the most sustained allegory in the aṅga-series.

ग्रैवेयचिन्ताक is read not as a neck-pendant but as ग्रीवा with चिन्तक: "those who meditate on the throat alone are called Graiveyacintākas — that is, they who cannot fix the deity in the cavity of the heart, but worship her externally, are the middle class of worshippers." लोल is then taken in its other sense: "the pearl dangling means those who are bound by earthly desires," with the Agni Purāṇa cited — "lola means change and desire" — and "these are the lowest class of worshippers." And मुक्ता, which as a noun is a pearl and as a participle is *released*, gives the third: "Muktas are the highest class of worshippers."

Then फल does the work of tying it together: "she is in each case the fruit to be obtained by these three classes according to their deserts."

So one ornament-compound yields three grades of devotee — the desire-bound, those who can only worship externally at the throat, and the liberated — and She is what each attains in proportion. The throat-detail is precise rather than decorative: the heart's cavity is where She is properly meditated, which is nama 595 हृदयस्था and the दहराकाश of 609, so failing to reach it and stopping at the neck is a specific deficiency and not a general one.

The text grades worshippers elsewhere and always by the same method — holding the act single and varying the fitness of the doer. The three speeds of grace at 869 क्षिप्रप्रसादिनी are this birth, the third, or the next; the four last-stage meditations at 957 धन्या have four different fruits; the tarpaṇa at 974 is one rite with four substances by class; and 923 दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या makes the adept and the inept both reach Her.

The body also carries the verse marker (13) and two intruded footnotes: nama 30's remark on the maṅgalya-sūtra being un-Vedic, and a note identifying the Kāmakalāvilāsa cited at 28 as "one of the Devī Tantras written by Puṇyānandanātha, with a commentary upon it by Naṭanānandanātha."

Note on the verse. Two namas of arm and neck ornament, and the second is where the description briefly stops describing.

32's allegory is worth the attention because of what it does to the genre. The aṅga-namas have so far been comparisons — a flower, a gem, a fish, a bud — and Bhāskararāya has glossed them thinly or not at all. Here he takes an ornament apart into ग्रीवा-cintaka, lola and mukta and gets the three classes of worshipper out of it, with फल as what each receives. Nothing in the compound has to be strained: every member has the second sense he needs.

Textual note. 31's body holds two words of 32's gloss, and 32's gloss is missing exactly those two words. 32's body carries two footnotes belonging elsewhere, one of them nama 30's.

## कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणस्तनी । नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलकुचद्वयी

*kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇipratipaṇastanī । nābhyālavālaromālilatāphalakucadvayī*

Verse 14, namas 33–34.

33. कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणस्तनी → कामेश्वर-प्रेम-रत्न-मणि-प्रतिपण-स्तनी

कामेश्वर = Kāmeśvara
प्रेम = love, affection (from प्री "to please")
रत्न = a jewel
मणि = a gem — रत्नमणि, a jewel among gems, the priceless one
प्रतिपण = the price given in exchange, a counter-stake (प्रति + पण "a wager, a stake")
स्तनी = breasted (स्तन with the feminine)
"She whose breasts are the price paid for the priceless jewel of Kāmeśvara's love."

Vigraha: कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणेः प्रतिपणः स्तनौ यस्याः सा।

The verse text reads पतिपण for प्रतिपण, having lost the र्, where the nama's dev field is correct — the fifth verse-text fault in the opening verses.

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

पण is the word for a stake in a game or a wager, so प्रतिपण is what is put up against something — the counter-stake. The compound is therefore a transaction and not a comparison: the love is the jewel, the breasts are what was laid down for it, and the exchange is stated as though it had been priced. That is a different figure from anything else in the series, which works by resemblance or by outdoing.

प्रेम is nama 730 प्रेमरूपा, where Her form is love and Bhāskararāya's whole gloss is four words. And Kāmeśvara has now stood four times in six namas — 28, 30, 33, and 39 ahead — so the section from the throat down is described throughout by reference to Him, which the kūṭa-scheme would predict, this being the Kāmarāja portion.

34. नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलकुचद्वयी → नाभि-आलवाल-रोम-आलि-लता-फल-कुच-द्वयी

नाभि = the navel
आलवाल = the basin or trench dug round the root of a tree to hold water
रोम = hair, down
आलि = a line, a row
लता = a creeper, a vine
फल = fruit
कुच = a breast
द्वयी = a pair (द्वय with the feminine)
"She whose two breasts are the fruit of the hair-creeper rooted in the basin of her navel."

Vigraha: नाभिः आलवालम्, रोमालिः लता, तस्याः फलं कुचद्वयी यस्याः सा।

Sandhi at both joints: नाभि + आलवाल → नाभ्यालवाल, the इ becoming य् before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 इको यणचि); and रोम + आलि → रोमालि (आ by 6.1.101).

index.html carries only the verse marker (14).

आलवाल is the precise word and the whole figure rests on it: not a hollow but the ring-shaped trench a gardener digs round a sapling so that water collects at the root. So the navel is where the creeper is watered, the line of hair is the vine, and the breasts are its fruit — a single horticultural image carried through four members, and read upward from the navel rather than downward, against the direction of the description.

The same creeper does structural work in the next nama, where the waist has to be inferred from it, so 34 and 35 are one figure across two namas — the vine established here and used as evidence there.

लता is the word of 107 तटिल्लतासमरुचिः, where the lightning-creeper is the kuṇḍalinī's own figure, and of 579 मृणालमृदुदोर्लता, where her arms are creepers. And फल is what 32 has just made the fruit obtained by three classes of worshipper.

Note on the verse. Two namas, and they change the description's method twice over.

33 prices a part of the body instead of comparing it — the breasts as the counter-stake laid down for the jewel of Kāmeśvara's love. 34 then builds a horticultural figure in which the navel is a watering-basin, the line of hair a vine and the breasts its fruit, and hands that vine to 35 as the only evidence for a waist.

Textual note. The verse text reads पतिपण for प्रतिपण at 33, the dev being correct. 33 has no body; 34's is the verse marker alone.

---

## लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयमध्यमा । स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धवलित्रया

*lakṣyaromalatādhāratāsamunneyamadhyamā । stanabhāradalanmadhyapaṭṭabandhavalitrayā*

Verse 15, namas 35–36.

35. लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयमध्यमा → लक्ष्य-रोम-लता-आधारता-सम्-उन्नेय-मध्यमा

लक्ष्य = to be seen, perceptible (लक्ष् "to observe," gerundive यत्)
रोम = hair
लता = a creeper
आधारता = the state of being a support (आधार + ता)
सम् = fully
उन्नेय = to be inferred, to be led up to (उत् + नी "to lead," gerundive)
मध्यमा = the waist, the middle
"She whose waist is to be inferred only from its supporting the visible hair-creeper."

Vigraha: लक्ष्यरोमलतायाः आधारतया समुन्नेया मध्यमा यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The nama is an inference and it is set out with the vocabulary of one. लक्ष्य is what is perceptible, उन्नेय is what must be inferred, and आधारता — the abstract, *being-the-support-of* — is the middle term. The creeper of 34 is seen; a creeper requires something to grow on; therefore a waist, though not itself seen. So the waist's slenderness is established by argument rather than asserted, and the figure of the previous nama supplies the premise.

That is a deliberate joke about a body too slender to observe, and the text makes it again at 111 बिसतन्तुतनीयसी, where She is "finer than the fibre of a lotus stalk" — तनीयसी being a comparative, so not thin as a fibre but thinner than one.

आधार is the word of 659 सर्वाधारा and 884 धर्माधारा, where what She supports is everything and the law; here what is supported is a line of hair.

36. स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धवलित्रया → स्तन-भार-दलत्-मध्य-पट्ट-बन्ध-वलि-त्रया

स्तन = a breast
भार = a weight, a burden (from भृ "to bear")
दलत् = splitting, breaking, giving way (present participle of दल् "to burst")
मध्य = the middle, the waist
पट्ट = a band, a strip of cloth
बन्ध = a binding, a tie (from बन्ध्)
वलि = a fold, a wrinkle of the skin
त्रया = a triad, three (त्रय with the feminine)
"She whose waist, giving way under the burden of her breasts, is bound with a cloth band and shows three folds."

Vigraha: स्तनभारेण दलन् मध्यः, तस्य पट्टबन्धः, वलित्रयं च यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: दलत् + मध्य → दलन्मध्य, the त् assimilating in nasality before म् (Pāṇini 8.4.45) — the same change as चलन्मीन at 18 and प्रतिपन्मुख्य at 610. The computed pada records दलन्, the sandhi-form, where the stem is दलत्.

index.html carries only the verse marker (15).

दलत् is a strong word — दल् is to burst or split, the root behind दल a petal, which is a leaf that has split open — so the waist is not merely bending but failing, and the band is what holds it. The three folds are the standard त्रिवली of description, and here they are a consequence: the waist gives way, so the skin gathers.

35 and 36 are therefore a pair with opposite tactics. The first says the waist cannot be seen at all and must be inferred; the second says it is buckling under a weight and has had to be bandaged. The series does not reconcile them, and the joke in 35 depends on not needing to.

Note on the verse. Two namas of the waist, and between them the description reaches its most artificial point.

The waist is invisible at 35 and structurally overloaded at 36, and both namas are stated in technical language — the first with the vocabulary of inference, the second with a participle of bursting. Neither is glossed.

Textual note. 35 has no body; 36's is the verse marker alone, and its computed pada gives दलन् for the stem दलत्.

---

## अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी । रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादामभूषिता

*aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastrabhāsvatkaṭītaṭī । ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyaraśanādāmabhūṣitā*

Verse 16, namas 37–38.

37. अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी → अरुण-अरुण-कौसुम्भ-वस्त्र-भास्वत्-कटी-तटी

अरुण = red, rosy, the colour of dawn — doubled for intensity
कौसुम्भ = dyed with safflower, kusumbha-red (vṛddhi derivative of कुसुम्भ)
वस्त्र = a garment, cloth
भास्वत् = shining, radiant (from भास् "to shine")
कटी = the hip, the waist
तटी = a slope, a bank, a declivity
"She whose hip-slope shines with a garment of deepest safflower red."

Vigraha: अरुणारुणेन कौसुम्भवस्त्रेण भास्वती कटीतटी यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: अरुण + अरुण → अरुणारुण (आ by 6.1.101). The verse text reads मास्वत् for भास्वत्, a म् where भ् belongs, the nama's dev field being correct — the sixth verse-text fault in the opening verses.

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The reduplication is the point: अरुणारुण is not "red" but red-red, an intensive formed by repeating the word, and the compound then names the actual dye — कुसुम्भ, safflower, which gives a strong orange-red. So the redness of 6 and 12, which was Her Vimarśa aspect and the dawn meditation's colour, is here a fabric with a named dyestuff.

तटी for the curve of a hip is a landscape word — a river-bank or the slope of a hill — and the description uses it once only. कटी returns at 86 कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्तमध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी and 87 शक्तिकूटैकतापन्नकट्यधोभागधारिणी, where the waist is precisely the boundary between the second and third kūṭas of the mantra. So this nama and the next close the Kāmarāja section, and 39 opens the Śakti section with the thighs.

38. रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादामभूषिता → रत्न-किङ्किणिका-रम्य-रशना-दाम-भूषिता

रत्न = a gem
किङ्किणिका = a small bell, a tinkling bell (an onomatopoeic diminutive)
रम्य = delightful, pleasing (from रम् "to delight," gerundive)
रशना = a girdle, a woman's waist-belt
दाम = a string, a cord, a garland (from दा "to bind")
भूषिता = adorned (from भूष् "to adorn")
"She adorned with a lovely girdle-string of jewelled bells."

Vigraha: रत्नकिङ्किणिकाभिः रम्येण रशनादाम्ना भूषिता।

index.html carries only the verse marker (16).

किङ्किणिका is named from its sound, and दाम is the word of 849 उद्दामवैभवा, where Bhāskararāya's entire gloss is the etymology — "दाम, rope, that which limits; उद्, beyond" — and the image is a tethered animal whose glory has slipped the rope. Here the cord is a belt of bells, and it is doing the tying rather than being escaped.

भूषिता is the participle of 51 सर्वाभरणभूषिता, adorned with every ornament, which stands thirteen namas on and summarises what the whole ornament-series has been itemising.

Note on the verse. Two namas, garment and girdle, closing the middle section of the body.

37's reduplicated अरुणारुण is the strongest statement of Her redness in the text, and the only one that names the dye. Her reds elsewhere are all comparisons — a thousand rising suns at 6, coral at 891, the young sun's rose at 922, bandhūka at 964, pomegranate at 560 — and 922 makes colour a function of the meditation's purpose. Here it is safflower on cloth.

And with 38 the waist is reached, which on the reckoning of 13 and 86–87 is where the Kāmarāja kūṭa ends.

Textual note. The verse text reads मास्वत् for भास्वत् at 37, the dev being correct. 37 has no body; 38's is the verse marker alone.

---

## कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता । माणिक्यमकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता

*kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavorudvayānvitā । māṇikyamakuṭākārajānudvayavirājitā*

Verse 17, namas 39–40.

39. कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता → कामेश-ज्ञात-सौभाग्य-मार्दव-ऊरु-द्वय-अन्विता

कामेश = Kāmeśa
ज्ञात = known (past participle of ज्ञा "to know")
सौभाग्य = good fortune, beauty, excellence (vṛddhi derivative of सुभग)
मार्दव = softness, smoothness (vṛddhi abstract of मृदु)
ऊरु = the thigh
द्वय = a pair
अन्विता = endowed with
"She endowed with a pair of thighs whose excellence and softness are known to Kāmeśa alone."

Vigraha: कामेशेन ज्ञातं सौभाग्यं मार्दवं च ऊरुद्वयस्य, तेन अन्विता।

Sandhi at two joints: मार्दव + ऊरु → मार्दवोरु (अ + ऊ → ओ by guṇa, 6.1.87), and द्वय + अन्विता → द्वयान्विता (आ by 6.1.101).

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The nama's device is to name a limit on who can know, and it is the only one in the series that does so. Everything above the waist has been described by comparison to something the reader can also see; from here the description withdraws, and ज्ञात with the instrumental कामेशेन makes the knowledge exclusive.

सौभाग्य is the word Bhāskararāya works at 117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी, where he identifies सुभगा with Lalitā herself, so "the saubhāgyas she bestows are her own qualities extended to the devotee" — and सुभगा is nama 761, where Dhaumya makes it a girl of five and the Viśva gives भग twelve senses. Here the word is simply excellence of form.

This is the first nama below the waist, so on the reckoning of 13 and 87 the Śakti kūṭa begins here. And it is the fourth nama in twelve to name Kāmeśvara — 28, 30, 33, 39 — which is the density one would expect of the Kāmarāja section just ended.

40. माणिक्यमकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता → माणिक्य-मकुट-आकार-जानु-द्वय-विराजिता

माणिक्य = a ruby
मकुट = a crown, a diadem (मुकुट)
आकार = form, shape
जानु = the knee
द्वय = a pair
विराजिता = made resplendent
"She resplendent with a pair of knees shaped like ruby crowns."

Vigraha: माणिक्यमकुटाकारेण जानुद्वयेन विराजिता।

Sandhi: मकुट + आकार → मकुटाकार (आ by 6.1.101). The verse text breaks the compound with a space before विराजिता.

index.html carries only the verse marker (17).

माणिक्य is the ruby again, and the text is now on its fourth appearance of the stone: padmarāga on the crown at 14, where the Garuḍa Purāṇa recommends the kuruvinda variety because it "confers love, prosperity, and devotion to Hari"; a ruby mirror outdone by the cheeks at 23; māṇikya as one of the two stones in the nose-jewel at 20; and here the knees shaped like ruby diadems. It is also the second of the five gems the Viṣṇu Rahasya assigns to the elements at 949 पञ्चभूतेशी.

The comparison is of shape rather than colour — a kneecap as a small domed crown — and मकुट is the word for a crown at 14's कोटीर too. So Her crown is on her head at 14 and her knees resemble crowns at 40.

Note on the verse. Two namas, thighs and knees, opening the lowest section.

39 changes the description's terms. Above the waist everything has been compared to something visible; here what is named is a restriction on the knower, and Kāmeśa alone has it. That the change coincides with the boundary between the Kāmarāja and Śakti kūṭas is presumably not accidental, given that 13 said the sections correspond.

Textual note. The verse text breaks 40's compound with a space before विराजिता. 39 has no body; 40's is the verse marker alone.

---

## इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजङ्घिका । गूढगुल्फा कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदान्विता

*indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇābhajaṅghikā । gūḍhagulphā kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇuprapadānvitā*

Verse 18, namas 41–43.

41. इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजङ्घिका → इन्द्रगोप-परिक्षिप्त-स्मर-तूण-आभ-जङ्घिका

इन्द्रगोप = the cochineal insect, the scarlet velvet-mite — literally "Indra's cowherd"
परिक्षिप्त = strewn over, studded, scattered about (परि + क्षिप् "to throw")
स्मर = Smara, Kāma
तूण = a quiver
आभ = resembling
जङ्घिका = the calf, the lower leg (जङ्घा with the diminutive)
"She whose calves are like Kāma's quiver studded with cochineal."

Vigraha: इन्द्रगोपैः परिक्षिप्तः स्मरतूणः, तदाभे जङ्घिके यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: तूण + आभ → तूणाभ (आ by 6.1.101). The computed pada takes तूणाभ as a single member; it is two.

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

इन्द्रगोप is the interesting word, and Sastry's gloss — "the sapphire studded quiver" — is wrong about the colour. The इन्द्रगोप is a small brilliant scarlet insect, the rain-insect that appears with the first showers, and it is a standing simile for deep red. Bhāskararāya himself uses it so at 922 तरुणादित्यपाटला, where Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.3.6 is quoted for the principle of such comparison: the Self is likened to silver, to white cloth, to white wool, "or like the colour of the indragopa stone." So the insect of this nama is the Upaniṣad's own colour-standard, and the calves are red-flecked and not blue.

That makes the nama continuous with 37's safflower and with the redness of 6 and 12 rather than a departure from it. A quiver strewn with scarlet is a quiver flecked with the same colour as the rest of Her.

तूण is Kāma's quiver, and its arrows are namas 11's five tanmātras, whose gross form the Kādimata gives as five flowers. So the calves resemble the container of the weapon she holds in her upper right hand.

42. गूढगुल्फा → गूढ-गुल्फा

गूढ = hidden, concealed, covered (past participle of गुह् "to hide")
गुल्फा = the ankle (गुल्फ)
"She whose ankles are hidden."

Vigraha: गूढौ गुल्फौ यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

Two words, and it is the shortest nama in the whole aṅga-description — the surrounding compounds run to six and seven members. Sastry renders it "with rounded ankles," which is the sense: a well-formed ankle is one whose bone does not protrude, so गूढ, hidden, is praise. The bone is concealed by flesh rather than by clothing.

गुह् is the root that gives the text five namas — 606 गुहजन्मभूः, 624 गुह्या, 706 गुहाम्बा, 707 गुह्यरूपिणी, and 720 गुह्यकाराध्या — where what is hidden is Skanda's cave, the doctrine, the heart's cavity, non-duality, and the mūlādhāra. Here it is an anklebone, which is the root's most modest employment in the text.

43. कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदान्विता → कूर्म-पृष्ठ-जयिष्णु-प्रपद-अन्विता

कूर्म = a tortoise
पृष्ठ = the back, the shell
जयिष्णु = victorious over, surpassing (desiderative-adjectival of जि "to conquer")
प्रपद = the fore-part of the foot, the instep (प्र + पद)
अन्विता = endowed with
"She endowed with insteps that surpass the tortoise's shell."

Vigraha: कूर्मपृष्ठं जयिष्णु प्रपदं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: प्रपद + अन्विता → प्रपदान्विता (आ by 6.1.101).

index.html carries only the verse marker (18).

जयिष्णु is the sixth of the eclipsing-words the description uses, after तिरस्कारि at 20, परिभावि at 23, न्यक्कारि at 24, अनाकलितसादृश्य at 29 and विनिर्भर्त्सित at 27, with पराकृत still to come at 45. Six namas, six distinct words for outdoing, and no two repeated — which is the series' most consistent formal habit.

The tortoise-shell for an arched instep is the standard comparison and it works on curvature. जि is the root of 663 अजाजैत्री, where what She conquers is the unborn Prakṛti taken as ignorance, and of 788 जयत्सेना, whose army conquers.

Note on the verse. Three namas — the only three-nama verse in the aṅga-description — running calf, ankle, instep.

The scale-change at 42 is the thing to notice. It sits between two six-member compounds and consists of two words, and what it says is that a bone does not show. The description can spend seven members on a waist and two on an ankle.

41's इन्द्रगोप is also worth recovering from Sastry's mistranslation. The insect is scarlet, and Bhāskararāya cites it himself at 922 as the Bṛhadāraṇyaka's own standard of red — so the nama belongs with 37's safflower and 6's rising suns and not with the gem-namas.

Textual note. 41's computed pada takes तूणाभ as one member. 41 and 42 have no bodies; 43's is the verse marker alone.

## नखदीधितिसंछन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा । पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा

*nakhadīdhitisaṃchannanamajjanatamoguṇā । padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtasaroruhā*

Verse 19, namas 44–45.

44. नखदीधितिसंछन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा → नख-दीधिति-सम्-छन्न-नमत्-जन-तमस्-गुणा

नख = a nail
दीधिति = a ray, a beam, splendour (from दीधी "to shine")
सम् = fully
छन्न = covered, concealed, obscured (past participle of छद् "to cover")
नमत् = bowing, prostrating (present participle of नम् "to bow")
जन = people, persons
तमस् = darkness; the guṇa of inertia
गुणा = a quality, a strand
"She by the rays of whose nails the tamas-quality of prostrating people is wholly obscured."

Vigraha: नखदीधितिभिः संछन्नः नमज्जनानां तमोगुणः यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: नमत् + जन → नमज्जन, the त् assimilating to the palatal before ज् (Pāṇini 8.4.40, स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः); and तमस् + गुण → तमोगुण, the अस् becoming ओ. The computed pada takes नमज्जन and तमोगुणा each as single members, so both compounds' internal seams are lost.

The gloss is brief — "darkness, that is ignorance; the worshippers, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest. The meaning is that meditation on her feet dispels ignorance" — and then Bhāskararāya tells a story, and it is the best narrative in these ten verses.

It is from the Matsya and Padma Purāṇas: Nārada reading Pārvatī's bodily marks to her mother Menā, and finding three that appear disastrous. "A husband is not yet born for her, O lady. She will be devoid of good bodily marks, and she will always have her hand raised. And her feet will err by their own shadow. What more should be said?" Himavat, hearing these, "addressed him with sorrow" — at which Nārada answers: "when you have an occasion for great joy, why should you manifest sorrow? O great mountain, you are bewildered because you did not understand my speech."

The three are then turned round one by one. *No husband born for her* — because Śiva does not belong to the group of created beings. *Devoid of good bodily marks* — because she is unconditioned, and marks are conditions. *Her hand always raised* — because "a great giver herself, hers must necessarily be above that of the one who receives."

And the third is this nama: "I will explain what I meant by saying her feet will err by their own shadow. O best of mountains, her feet are like lotuses, shining with bright nails. When the Devas and Asuras prostrate before her, the various colours of their jewelled crowns, reflected, will drive away the rays of her nails — which, entering their hearts, dispel their tamas quality."

So the inauspicious reading was that the feet are shadowed, and the true reading is that what shadows them is the reflected light of crowns bowed before them. The nail-rays are not extinguished but redirected into the hearts of those bowing. That is a genuine reading of the compound: संछन्न, obscured, is predicated of the tamas and not of the rays, and the Purāṇa's story explains why the word for covering is there at all.

The three-marks passage also belongs with 5's Kūrma citation, where Devī tells Himavat her four reasons for being born of Menā and says she chose him as her father. Nārada is here explaining the same birth to the same parents from the other side.

तमस् is one of the three guṇas, on which the text takes four incompatible positions — beyond them at 961 गुणातीता, made of them at 984 त्रिगुणा, their equilibrium at 763 त्रिगुणात्मिका, and the whole condition negated at 789 निस्त्रैगुण्या. Here one of the three is dispelled in the worshipper.

45. पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा → पद-द्वय-प्रभा-जाल-पराकृत-सरोरुहा

पद = a foot
द्वय = a pair
प्रभा = radiance
जाल = a net, a web; a multitude
पराकृत = repelled, driven off, surpassed (परा + कृ)
सरोरुहा = a lotus — "pond-grown" (सरस् + रुह्)
"She by the net of whose two feet's radiance the lotus is put down."

Vigraha: पदद्वयप्रभाजालेन पराकृतं सरोरुहं यस्याः सा।

index.html carries only the verse marker (19).

जाल is a net or mesh, so the radiance is imagined as woven rather than poured — a different figure from the प्रभापूर, the flood of radiance, at 12 and 28. And सरोरुह is the lotus named by where it grows, सरस् a pond with रुह् to sprout.

पराकृत is the last of the eclipsing-words, and the lotus is the last thing outdone. The comparison is conventional in the extreme — feet like lotuses — and the nama's move is to defeat the comparison rather than make it, which is what the series has been doing since 20.

Her feet are lotuses at 46 श्रीपदाम्बुजा in the next verse, and the lotus is Her seat at 105 सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा, Her face at 85 मुखपङ्कजा, and Her grove at 59 महापद्माटवीसंस्था.

Note on the verse. Two namas of the feet, and 44 carries the whole verse.

The Nārada story is the only place in the aṅga-description where the commentary supplies a narrative, and it works by reinterpretation: three marks read as calamitous — no husband, no auspicious marks, a hand always raised, feet shadowed — are each turned into a distinction. Śiva is uncreated, so no husband could be born for her; she is unconditioned, so she has no marks; she gives, so her hand is above the receiver's; and her feet are shadowed by the reflected crowns of gods bowing to them.

The last of these is a real reading of the compound, and it explains why संछन्न is in the nama at all: what is obscured is the tamas of those bowing, and the rays that would have shone from the nails go into their hearts instead.

Textual note. 44's computed pada merges नमत् with जन and तमस् with गुण, so both internal seams are lost. 45's body is the verse marker alone.

---

## शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा । मरालीमन्दगमना महालावण्यशेवधिः

*śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍitaśrīpadāmbujā । marālīmandagamanā mahālāvaṇyaśevadhiḥ*

Verse 20, namas 46–48.

46. शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा → शिञ्जान-मणि-मञ्जीर-मण्डित-श्री-पद-अम्बुजा

शिञ्जान = tinkling, jingling (present participle of शिञ्ज् "to tinkle")
मणि = a gem
मञ्जीर = an anklet (नूपुर)
मण्डित = adorned (from मण्ड्)
श्री = auspicious, glorious — honorific
पद = a foot
अम्बुजा = a lotus (अम्बु "water" + ज "born")
"She whose glorious lotus-feet are adorned with tinkling jewelled anklets."

Vigraha: शिञ्जानैः मणिमञ्जीरैः मण्डितं श्रीपदाम्बुजं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: पद + अम्बुजा → पदाम्बुजा (आ by 6.1.101). The verse text breaks the compound with a space before श्रीपदाम्बुजा — the second such spacing fault in four verses, after 40.

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

शिञ्जान is onomatopoeic, like किङ्किणिका at 38, and this is the second ornament in the series named for its sound. The feet are lotuses here immediately after 45 defeated the comparison, so the series makes the claim and then makes it again in the next nama without acknowledging the contradiction.

श्री as an honorific prefix is what Bhāskararāya establishes at nama 1, where he argues from usage that "the names of great men and things should have the honorific word Śrī prefixed to them — hence we find Śrīcakra, Śrīśaila, Śrīvidyā, Śrīphala," and that its absence from Īśvara and Īśāna shows it belongs to Her names. Here it prefixes a body part.

47. मरालीमन्दगमना → मराली-मन्द-गमना

मराली = a female swan or flamingo (मराल)
मन्द = slow, gentle, unhurried
गमना = gait, going (from गम् "to go")
"She whose gait is the slow gait of a swan."

Vigraha: मराल्याः इव मन्दं गमनं यस्याः सा।

index.html has no commentary for this nama.

The description has finished with the parts and now names the whole in motion, so 47 is the first nama since 13 that is not about a limb. And मन्द is the word of 28, where the smile was faint — the same adjective for a smile and a walk.

The swan is also the haṃsa, and the text makes considerable use of that elsewhere: 525 हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता names Haṃsavatī, the śakti of the letter ह, as one of the two attendants at the two-petalled ājñā; and the Haṃsa mantra स-ह is what unites the jīva with Śiva at 672 ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी and again at 999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी. Here the bird is only a bird, and मराली rather than हंसी at that.

48. महालावण्यशेवधिः → महा-लावण्य-शेवधिः

महा = great
लावण्य = beauty, loveliness — literally saltiness, hence savour (vṛddhi derivative of लवण, "salt")
शेवधिः = a treasure, a hoard, a store
"The treasure-house of great beauty."

Vigraha: महालावण्यस्य शेवधिः।

index.html has no commentary; the body carries only the verse-division marker (20) and a fragment of the gloss.

**This nama is one of the four in the thousand that are masculine.** The Paribhāṣā verse at nama 1000 records the gender anomalies of the text — "four namas are masculine, Guṇanidhi, Ātman, Rogaparvata, Mahālāvaṇya; two neuter, Tat and Brahman; and two indeclinable, Svāhā and Svadhā" — and this is the fourth of the masculine four. The reason is शेवधि, which is a masculine noun, so the nominative is शेवधिः and no feminine form is substituted. The other three are 604 गुणनिधिः, 617 आत्मा, and 748 रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः.

That is a useful check on the list, because two of the four are निधि-words: गुणनिधि a treasure of virtues at 604, and शेवधि a treasure of beauty here. And 567 भक्तनिधिः, the devotees' treasure, has the same masculine ending without being counted — presumably because निधि there is not the last member of a masculine-gendered compound in the same way, or because the Paribhāṣā's list is of the namas whose gender is *anomalous* rather than of every masculine word.

लावण्य is worth its etymology. It is built on लवण, salt, so beauty is named as savour — the quality that makes a thing tasteful. The same figure underlies the Bṛhadāraṇyaka simile Bhāskararāya quotes at 574 प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी: "just as the taste of a quantity of salt is neither inside nor outside but everywhere, so this Self is full and concentrated knowledge."

Note on the verse. Three namas, and they close the body-description.

46 finishes the feet with anklets; 47 leaves the parts and gives the whole in motion; 48 stops describing and names the sum — a treasure-house of beauty. So the sequence begun at 13 with the hair ends thirty-six namas later with a summary, and 51 सर्वाभरणभूषिता will shortly restate the ornaments the same way.

48 is also one of the four masculine namas the Paribhāṣā counts at 1000, and the reason is grammatical: शेवधि is masculine and the text does not adjust it.

Textual note. The verse text breaks 46's compound with a space before श्रीपदाम्बुजा. 46 and 47 have no bodies; 48's holds the verse marker and a fragment of its own gloss.
