## सर्वारुणा ऽनवद्याङ्गी सर्वाभरणभूषिता । शिवकामेश्वराङ्कस्था शिवा स्वाधीनवल्लभा

*sarvāruṇā'navadyāṅgī sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā । śivakāmeśvarāṅkasthā śivā svādhīnavallabhā*

Verse 21, nama 49. Namas 50–54 stand earlier in this file, in the older format.

49. सर्वारुणा → सर्व-अरुणा

सर्व = all
अरुणा = red, rosy, the colour of dawn
"She who is entirely rosy."

Vigraha: सर्वं अरुणं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: सर्व + अरुणा → सर्वारुणा (आ by 6.1.101).

The whole commentary is one clause and it says what सर्व covers: "her garments, ornaments, flowers, colour and the rest are all rosy tinted."

So the nama gathers the redness the description has been distributing for forty-three namas. It began at 6 उद्यद्भानुसहस्राभा, where the red was identified as Her Vimarśa aspect and the Svacchandatantra was quoted — "Lalitā the universal form is said to be her own self, that is Prakāśa; the red colour is her Vimarśa"; it was the dawn-meditation's colour at 12; the ruby on the crown at 14; the padmarāga outdone at 23 and the coral at 24; the safflower dye at 37; the scarlet cochineal at 41. Now every one of those is subsumed under one word, and the enumeration in the gloss — garments, ornaments, flowers, colour — names the categories the description used.

That makes 49 the counterpart of 48. Where 48 summed the beauty, 49 sums the colour, and 51 सर्वाभरणभूषिता sums the ornaments. Three consecutive summary-namas closing the section.

The nama is also the site of the text's **first avagraha**. Its dev field is clean, but 50's reads ऽनवद्याङ्गी, carrying the अ elided in सर्वारुणा + अनवद्याङ्गी → सर्वारुणानवद्याङ्गी (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101). That is the earliest of the ten instances of the class — 50, 537, 554, 642, 729, 828, 926, 972, 985, 988 — and the single mark correctly signals a short vowel, as the rule holds throughout: a single ऽ where a short अ was swallowed, a double ऽऽ where a long आ was.

Note on the entry. Nama 49 closes the aṅga-description's colour and opens the verse whose remaining five namas were the first thing recorded in this file. With it, namas 1–111 are continuous.

---

Textual note for verses 11–21.

**The verse-text corruption of the opening is systematic.** Three more namas here have a correct `dev` field and a corrupt verse line: 27 विनिर्भर्त्सित appears as विनिर्भत्सिंत, 33 प्रतिपण as पतिपण, and 37 भास्वत् as मास्वत्. With 6 सहस्नाभा, 19 पुप्पाभ and 24 नवबिद्रुम from the previous batch, that is **six letter-faults in the verse texts of verses 1–21, every one of them with a sound `dev`**. Two spacing faults belong to the same set: verse 17 breaks 40's compound before विराजिता and verse 20 breaks 46's before श्रीपदाम्बुजा. Nowhere else in the text does the verse line fail this often against a correct nama field — the usual pattern is the reverse, as at 864 फनत्, 872 यी, 964 बन्धक and 778 विराड्पा. In this opening stretch the verse array and the nama array are independently corrupt, and neither checks the other.

**Computed pada faults, five, all of them merges or sandhi-forms rather than sense-inversions.** 36 records दलन् for the stem दलत्; 41 takes तूणाभ as one member where it is तूण + आभ; 44 takes both नमज्जन and तमोगुणा as single members, losing the नमत् + जन and तमस् + गुण seams that the commentary's own gloss depends on. None of these damages the meaning the way 9 क्रोधा | कारा or 23 शिला | दर्श did in the previous batch.

**Displaced fields.** 31's body holds the two words "necklace of," which belong to 32's gloss — and 32's gloss, "having a pearl dangling from a gems and gold," is missing exactly that phrase. 32's body carries two intruded footnotes, one of them nama 30's remark that the maṅgalya-sūtra "was not the Āryan custom and was not found referred to in any Vedic literature; earring was the emblem." 48's body holds a fragment of its own gloss.

**Empty and marker-only bodies, seventeen of the twenty-three.** No commentary at all at 29, 33, 35, 37, 39, 41, 42, 46, 47. Verse markers only at 30, 34, 36, 38, 40, 43, 45, 48. Commentary of substance survives at just four namas — 27, 28, 32 and 44 — and 31's body is a stray fragment. Across the whole aṅga-description, 13 to 48, Bhāskararāya comments at eight namas and passes twenty-eight. Where he does comment there is a reason: a kūṭa-identification at 13, a gem's efficacy at 14, the luminaries at 22, the four stages of speech at 25, the four lutes and the argument from articulation at 27, the Kāmakalā and the Mīmāṃsā inference at 28, the three classes of worshipper at 32, and Nārada's reading of the bodily marks at 44.

**The eclipsing-words.** Seven namas of the description defeat a comparison, and no two use the same word for it: विनिर्भर्त्सित at 27, अनाकलितसादृश्य at 29 (which declines the comparison instead), तिरस्कारि at 20, परिभावि at 23, न्यक्कारि at 24, जयिष्णु at 43, पराकृत at 45. It is the series' most consistent formal habit and the one thing that holds the ornamental namas together.


---

## सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा सामरस्यपरायणा । कपर्दिनी कलामाला कामधुक् कामरूपिणी

*satyajñānānandarūpā sāmarasyaparāyaṇā । kapardinī kalāmālā kāmadhuk kāmarūpiṇī*

Verse 151, namas 791–796.

791. सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा → सत्य-ज्ञान-आनन्द-रूपा

सत्य = truth, reality (from सत्, present participle of अस् "to be")
ज्ञान = knowledge (from ज्ञा "to know")
आनन्द = bliss (आ + नन्द् "to rejoice")
रूपा = form; and per the second reading, giving
"She whose form is truth, knowledge and bliss."

Vigraha: सत्यं ज्ञानम् आनन्दः च रूपं यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: ज्ञान + आनन्द → ज्ञानानन्द (आ by 6.1.101).

Taittirīya 2.1.1 is the primary citation, and it supplies the first two members exactly: *satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma* — "Brahman is truth, wisdom, infinity." Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.9.28 supplies the third: "Brahman is eternal, wisdom, bliss."

Then Bhāskararāya gives two divisions which invert the nama entirely, and they are the sharpest thing in the verse.

The first: सती true wisdom, अज्ञान those ignorant of it, अनानन्द such persons are without bliss, and रूप taken as "gives" — "she causes pain to those ignorant of the true wisdom." The authorities are the standard condemnations: Īśa 9 and Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.10, "those who worship ignorance enter into deep darkness"; and the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, "the Āraṇya Śruti condemns those who follow any but true knowledge."

The second is a pun on the word ānanda itself. सती Devī, अज्ञान ignorant of Her, and रूप "she assigns" — she assigns to such persons "worlds called Ānanda," meaning *joyless*, on Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.11: "those worlds are called Ānanda, which are covered with deep darkness; the ignorant and unwise men go to those worlds after death." The Upaniṣad's word is अनन्दा, joyless, and it is read here as the आनन्द of the nama.

So a nama whose plain sense is truth-knowledge-bliss is twice re-divided into a statement about what the ignorant get, and the second reading turns bliss into its own negation. The device — a compound made to say its opposite — is the one the text uses at 643 ज्ञानदा, where giver-of-knowledge becomes destroyer of the knowledge that binds, and at 979 ज्ञानमुद्रा, where द्र makes Her the concealer of the bliss she gives.

The triad itself is 700 सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी with सत्य for सत् and ज्ञान for चित् — the same three in different words, ninety-one namas apart. And 646 सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी had two of the three without the middle.

792. सामरस्यपरायणा → सामरस्य-परायणा

सामरस्य = identity of essence, coequality (vṛddhi abstract of समरस, "of one flavour")
परायणा = the final resort, the supreme abode; and as an adjective, devoted to, intent upon (परा + अयन "going")
"She whose supreme resort is the coequality of Śiva and Śakti."

Vigraha: सामरस्यं परायणं यस्याः सा।

सामरस्य is literally sameness-of-flavour — समरस with the vṛddhi abstract — so the word says the two have one taste, which is a stronger claim than that they are equal in rank.

The Candrāloka's opening verse is quoted, and it is the finest reciprocal formula in the text: "we praise the ancient pair, the parents of the Universe. Each is the end attained by the penance of the other." Neither is the other's means; each is the other's goal.

Kālidāsa is then cited for the condition under which the coequality is tasted: "Śiva milks out the essence of the coequal nature when the waves of the enjoyer, enjoyment, and the means are calm." The three — भोक्तृ, भोग्य, and the instrument — are the triad whose stilling 981 ज्ञातृज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी and 908 तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी both address by identifying Her with the poles rather than by calming them. And the Śruti: "equally pre-eminent, equally fundamental, both are equal."

Two further readings. समरस्य as the worlds of the Devas, with परायण their abode or refuge. Or रस्य songs with साम the Sāmaveda's, and परायण fond of — the Viśva giving परायण for "fond of, devoted to, dependent." That last makes the nama 909 सामगानप्रिया in other words.

सामरस्य is the doctrine of 999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी, where ऐक्य is glossed as "the supreme equality, the being absolutely without difference," and of 109 महासक्तिः, where the "festival" is the union of the two in the sahasrāra. This nama names it with the word for shared flavour.

793. कपर्दिनी → कपर्द-इनी

कपर्द = matted or braided hair, especially Śiva's jaṭā; also a cowrie; also, per the Viśva, cowdung cakes; and per the Sāra Saṃhitā's commentator, earth, mockery and praise
इनी = the possessive suffix इन् with the feminine ङीप्
"She who possesses the matted hair."

Vigraha: कपर्दः अस्याः अस्तीति कपर्दिनी।

index.html splits this entry mid-sentence: the gloss ends "...da, sanctifies. His" and the body opens "matted hair sanctifies even the water of the Gaṅgā," so the clause runs across the field boundary and neither half stands alone.

The syllabic reading comes first — क water, that is Gaṅgā's, with the flow and द sanctifies — and its point is a reversal: Śiva's matted hair "sanctifies even the water of the Gaṅgā." The river that purifies is itself purified by the hair it falls into.

Then three quite different senses of कपर्द. The Sāra Saṃhitā's commentator gives earth, mockery and praise, whence कपर्दिनी is "greatly praised." The Viśva gives "the matted hair of Śiva, and cowdung cakes" — and the second yields a regional identification: "when Śiva incarnated as Mailāra, his wife called Mahālasā was decked with a garland of cowdung cakes." Mailāra is the Mallāri of 785 मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या, where Śiva "is called in the Mahārāṣṭra country by the name Mallāri and also Mārtāṇḍabhairava" — so the same regional form of Śiva stands eight namas apart, once as Her worshipper and once as her husband.

And the Devī Purāṇa's placement: "Kapardinī is the wife of Kaparda, that is Śiva, a deity worshipped at Chagalaṇḍa, one of the sixty-eight sacred places."

That count is worth marking. At 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी Bhāskararāya argued at length that the pīṭhas number fifty-one and not fifty, rejecting the Sundarīmahodaya's fifty because it left क्ष out of the reckoning. Here the sacred places are sixty-eight. The two enumerations are not the same set — the fifty-one are the pīṭhas set in the places of the mātṛkās, the sixty-eight a separate Śaiva list — but the text uses both without remarking on the difference.

794. कलामाला → कला-माला

कला = a part; one of the sixty-four arts; a digit of the moon; and per the syllabic reading, beauty
माला = a garland, a string, a row
"The Garland of the Arts."

Vigraha: कलानां माला।

The whole commentary is a syllabic division: "Kalā, beauty; ma, brilliance; la, possessed of."

कला is the word the text has now used in five senses — the five Śaiva kalās at 611 कलात्मिका and 853, the moon's digits at 612 कलानाथा, the jīvas at 797 three namas on, and here the sixty-four arts. And माला is the word of 875 त्रिपुरमालिनी, where Bhāskararāya took its second sense, a ring or row, to fit her placement in the Antardaśāra; and of the अक्षमाला of 577 मातृकावर्णरूपिणी, the garland of letters running अ to क्ष.

Sixty-four is also the count of the Tantras at 724 सर्वतन्त्रेशी, of the letters at 850 वर्णरूपिणी, and of the books on mantra at 846 मन्त्रसारा.

795. कामधुक् → काम-धुक्

काम = desire, a wish
धुक् = yielding, milking (from दुह् "to milk"; the compound-final form is धुक्)
"The Wish-yielding Cow."

Vigraha: कामं दुग्धे इति कामधुक्।

**This is the only nama in the thousand that ends in a plain consonant.** The others end in -आ, in a visarga, or — at 712 — in a single vowel; here the form is कामधुक्, the nominative of a दुह्-final compound, whose final aspirate devoices to क् in pausa. So the recitation has to stop on a stop, which is worth knowing if one is reciting the thousand aloud.

The gloss is brief: "she fulfils all desires. Or she is the celestial cow, Kāmadhenu." And the Śruti — "may we be attended by that cow and by speech which confer strength" — pairs the cow with speech, which is the pairing गो makes possible at 605 गोमाता, where गो is cow, earth, speech and ray at once.

796. कामरूपिणी → काम-रूपिणी

काम = desire; and per the commentary, the supreme Śiva as Kāmeśvara
रूपिणी = having the form of, embodying; and per the second reading, taking form
"She whose form is desire."

Vigraha: कामः रूपं यस्याः सा।

काम is identified as Paramaśiva, and specifically as Śiva-desiring-to-create: "Kāmeśvara is he who desires to create the Universe," on Taittirīya 2.6.1 — "he desired, let me become many, let me create beings."

Then Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.9.11 is quoted, and it is a startling choice: "He is the Person consisting of desire. It is He, go on, Śākalya — who is His deity? He replied: woman is His deity." So the Person made of desire has woman for his deity, which makes the nama's compound reversible — She is the form of his desire, and she is what that desire worships.

A second reading takes काम adverbially: "at will; rūpa, forms — she assumes any form at will," or her forms are agreeable.

काम has now carried four referents in this text: the god burnt and revived at 84, the bodiless Ṛṣi of the vidyā at 586, Paramaśiva at 589 कामकोटिका, and the Bindu of the Kāmakalā at 28. Here it is the creative desire itself.

Note on the verse. Six namas, and the first two are the doctrinal pair.

791 is remarkable for how far its divisions travel from its surface. The plain reading is the Upaniṣadic सत्यं ज्ञानम् formula; the second makes it an account of what the ignorant receive; and the third turns आनन्द into अनन्दा, the joyless worlds of Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.11. A nama of bliss made to say the opposite.

792 then names the Śiva–Śakti coequality by the word for shared flavour, and the Candrāloka verse quoted there — "each is the end attained by the penance of the other" — is the text's most exact statement of the relation, better than 999's own gloss.

793 supplies a second count of the sacred places, sixty-eight, against the fifty-one of 833, and the text does not reconcile them. It also brings Mailāra-Mallāri back eight namas after 785.

And 795 is the thousand's one consonant-final nama.

Textual note. 791's body carries a footnote belonging to nama 790 परापरा: "here the commentator does not show the reason how the Parāparā is to be taken as four." So Sastry noted a gap in the commentary on the previous nama and the note has drifted forward one place. 793's gloss and body are split in the middle of a sentence.

---

## कलानिधिः काव्यकला रसज्ञा रसशेवधिः । पुष्टा पुरातना पूज्या पुष्करा पुष्करेक्षणा

*kalānidhiḥ kāvyakalā rasajñā rasaśevadhiḥ । puṣṭā purātanā pūjyā puṣkarā puṣkarekṣaṇā*

Verse 152, namas 797–805.

797. कलानिधिः → कला-निधिः

कला = a part, a portion; the jīvas; a digit of the moon; and per one reading, action
निधिः = a treasure, a store; a receptacle (नि + धा "to place down")
"The Treasury of the Kalās."

Vigraha: कलानां निधिः।

Three readings, and each takes कला differently.

As the jīvas: "kalās are jīvas," with Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.5.15 — "Ātman is the sixteenth kalā of him." So the store holds the individual souls, which is what 728 चित्कला said of one of them, "the consciousness encased in the mind, because it is a small part of that consciousness which has no vehicle."

Or कलानिधि in its ordinary sense, the moon — literally the treasury of digits, which is how Sanskrit names the moon by what it holds.

Or, on Śiva Sūtra 1.3, "kalā means body," which the commentator glosses as action, karma — "hence all actions end in her," निधि being where they are deposited. Gītā 4.33 is cited: "all actions, O Pārtha, end in wisdom." That reading makes the nama 573 परानिष्ठा in other words, where निष्ठा was where action comes to rest and the same Gītā verse was quoted.

निधि is the word of 567 भक्तनिधिः, the devotees' treasure "which fulfils desire," and of 604 गुणनिधिः, a hoard of virtues — and both of those are masculine-ending. So is this one.

798. काव्यकला → काव्य-कला

काव्य = poetry, a poem (from कवि "a poet"); and per the second reading, Śukrācārya
कला = an art; and per the second reading, one of his kalās
"The Art of Poetry."

Vigraha: काव्यस्य कला।

The dramatic genres are listed first — "Nāṭaka, Sāṭaka, Bhāṇa, Ḍima, Prahasana and the rest, described in the Agni and other Purāṇas" — so काव्य here covers the stage as well as the page.

Then the Viṣṇu Purāṇa, and the line is generous in the same way 678 भाषारूपा was about languages: "whether they praise him by means of poems or by means of songs, all the words form part of the body of the great Viṣṇu, who assumed the form of sound." Any praise in any form reaches him, because words are his body.

Two further readings. कला as "the inspiration which produces poetry, because as described in the Tantras variously, a certain kind of meditation confers the power of poetical composition" — so the nama names a siddhi, as 631 दिव्यगन्धाढ्या did with the divine perfumes. Or काव्य is Śukrācārya, whose patronymic it is, and कला the one called Amṛtasañjīvinī, the power of conferring immortality.

That last connects to 84 हरनेत्राग्निसंदग्धकामसंजीवनौषधिः, where She is the संजीवन herb reviving the burnt Kāma — the same reviving power, once a herb and once a kalā.

The poetry-namas of this text are 613 काव्यालापविनोदिनी, delighting in the discourse of poetry, and 817's Satyavrata, made king of poets by uttering one syllable.

799. रसज्ञा → रस-ज्ञा

रस = flavour, taste; the aesthetic modes of drama; also the nectar, the essence
ज्ञा = knowing, she who knows (from ज्ञा "to know")
"She who knows the Rasas."

Vigraha: रसान् जानातीति रसज्ञा।

The commentary is two clauses: "Rasa, the ten modes of dramatic composition, viz. Śṛṅgāra and the rest. Rasajñā means also the sense of taste."

The second is not an afterthought but the word's ordinary meaning — रसज्ञा is a standard Sanskrit term for the tongue, the organ that knows flavours. So the nama says at once that She is versed in the aesthetic modes and that she is the faculty of taste, and the pun is the whole point: रस is what both know.

Ten rather than the usual eight or nine rasas is the fuller reckoning, with śānta and vātsalya added. And श‍ृङ्गार, named first here, is the aspect whose colour 922 तरुणादित्यपाटला made the rose of the young sun — "rosy in the śṛṅgāra."

ज्ञा as the bare root-noun has stood at 828 आज्ञा's second reading, 841 भावज्ञा and 902 विज्ञानकलना.

800. रसशेवधिः → रस-शेवधिः

रस = flavour, essence; here the nectar of Brahman
शेवधिः = a treasure, a hoard, a store
"The Treasury of Rasa."

Vigraha: रसस्य शेवधिः।

रस is here taken at its highest: "the nectar of Brahman," on Taittirīya 2.7.1 — *raso vai saḥ*, "He is the Rasa; when this essence is obtained one becomes blessed."

The Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa then works the word through a chain, and the last turn is the interesting one: "Rasa is the supreme Brahman, Rasa is the supreme way, Rasa is the giver of light to man, Rasa is said to be the seed. He is the Rasa; one having obtained the Rasa becomes blessed. Thus, on the authority of the Scriptures, Rasa represents the vital breath — who can live or who can breathe without Him? Hence, O Agastya, Rasa is said to be both the vital breath and the giver of vital breath."

So रस ends as प्राण, which is what 783 प्राणदा and 784 प्राणरूपिणी made Brahman on the Vedānta Sūtra's authority. The same identification by a different route.

शेवधि is the word of 48 महालावण्यशेवधिः, which the Paribhāṣā at 1000 counts among the four masculine namas — and this nama has the same masculine ending without being counted, exactly as 567 भक्तनिधिः and 797 कलानिधिः do beside 604 गुणनिधिः. So the Paribhāṣā's list is of the namas whose gender a reciter might mistake, not of every non-feminine form in the text.

**This nama closes the eighth hundred, and the colophon survives in its body**: "thus ends in the Saubhāgyabhāskara composed by Bhāsurānanda the ninth Kalā called Viśva, with the eighth hundred," followed by the heading "The Ninth Hundred."

That is the fourth of the text's colophons, and with it the kalā-scheme is fully determined for the last four hundreds. 700 सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी closes the seventh hundred with the eighth Kalā, Bhogadā; 800 here closes the eighth with the ninth, Viśva; 900 नैष्कर्म्या closes the ninth with the Bodhinī, which must therefore be the tenth; and 1000 ललिताम्बिका closes the tenth with the eleventh, Dhāriṇī. So the kalā-numbering runs exactly one ahead of the hundred it closes, throughout — which was a guess when only three colophons were in hand and is now a rule with no exception in the surviving four.

801. पुष्टा → पुष्टा

पुष्टा = nourished, well-fed, full-grown (past participle of पुष् "to thrive, to nourish")
"The Nourished."

Vigraha: पुष्टा वर्धिता।

Four reasons are given for the participle, and they run from the cosmic to the social: "because she is the possessor of the body consisting of thirty-six tattvas; or possessed of many qualities; or by Brahmarasa; or by Brāhmaṇas."

The last is developed with two citations that make the nourishment mutual. The Smṛti: "Brahman is nourished by Brāhmaṇas." And the Śruti: "old Brahman becomes old through Brāhmaṇas."

That is 888 विप्ररूपा's second reading turned round. There She nourished the Brāhmaṇas "by the repetition of mantras and by homa," and the Āpastamba Smṛti's simile was of a cow exhausted by milking; here they nourish Her. The relation runs both ways within fifty namas and neither statement is qualified.

The thirty-six tattvas are the set of 906 तत्त्वाधिका, where Bhāskararāya gave the criterion for counting them — what lasts till the pralaya — and 907 तत्त्वमयी, where She consists of them.

Bhāskararāya also drops a counting marker in this stretch: the Paribhāṣā at 1000 gives पुष्ट as the opening word of the ninth hundred, and this is that nama.

802. पुरातना → पुरातना

पुरातना = ancient, of former times (from पुरा "formerly")
"The Ancient."

Vigraha: पुरा भवा पुरातना।

The whole commentary is five words: "because she is the first of all."

That is 553 अग्रगण्या's claim — first to be counted because first in causality — and 975 पूर्वजा's, first-born; and at 975 Bhāskararāya undercut the honour by allowing that पूर्वजा might name the first creation, "which was without intelligence." Here nothing undercuts it.

पुरा is the adverb behind पुराण, so पुरातना and the Purāṇas the text quotes constantly share a word.

803. पूज्या → पूज्या

पूज्या = to be worshipped, worthy of worship (पूज् "to honour" with the gerundive यत्)
"The Adorable."

Vigraha: पूजनीया।

The commentary is one clause: "she is to be worshipped by all, or to be attended."

The gerundive puts this with 580 महनीया, to be honoured, and 627 त्रिजगद्वन्द्या, to be adored by the three worlds — which 927 स्तोत्रप्रिया cited as the text's own instance of नमस्कार among the six marks of a stotra. Three gerundives of worship, and this the plainest.

804. पुष्करा → पुष्करा

पुष्करा = a lotus; and per the syllabic reading, पुष्क nourishment with र recover
"The Lotus."

Vigraha: पुष्करम् एव सा।

Three short readings. The syllabic one: "Puṣka, nourishment; ra, recover." The geographical: "Puṣkarā is the deity of Puṣkara Tīrtha." And an orthographic one — "as there is no difference between र and ल, Puṣkalā means complete."

Puṣkara-tīrtha is where 699 सावित्री is the presiding deity, per the Padma Purāṇa, so the same place supplies two namas five namas apart. And the र/ल interchange Bhāskararāya invokes is a real feature of the older language, which he uses again nowhere else in the text.

805. पुष्करेक्षणा → पुष्कर-ईक्षणा

पुष्कर = a lotus; and per the Viśva, some fifteen other things; per the Padma Purāṇa, the earth, and a planetary conjunction; per the Matsya Purāṇa, the banyan
ईक्षणा = an eye, a look, a glance (from ईक्ष् "to see")
"The Lotus-eyed."

Vigraha: पुष्करे इव ईक्षणे यस्याः सा।

Sandhi: पुष्कर + ईक्षणा → पुष्करेक्षणा (अ + ई → ए by guṇa, 6.1.87).

This is the longest entry in the verse and it is almost entirely lexical. The Viśva's list of पुष्कर is given whole, and it is the widest single list in the text: "lotus, ether, water, an elephant's trunk, end, herb, island, bird, place of pilgrimage, a certain musical note, a kind of serpent, the drum, head, sword, and a fruit called khaḍgaphala."

Then three of those senses are developed.

As a conjunction, from the Padma Purāṇa, and it is astronomically specific: "when the sun is in the asterism called Viśākhā and the moon is in the Kṛttikā, the conjunction is called Puṣkara, and it is very rare at the place of Puṣkara." So the nama's first member names a moment as well as a flower.

As the earth, with the Padma Purāṇa's lotus-cosmology mapped part by part: "the Devas call the pericarp of the lotus earth; the [stamens] in the lotus they call divine mountains. The upper petals of the lotus became the Mleccha country. The lower petals are the worlds of the serpents and the Daityas. Thus by the wish of Nārāyaṇa the earth came out from the lotus; earth is called Puṣkara." A flower read as a world-map, with the barbarian lands above and the nāga-worlds below.

And as the banyan, on the Matsya Purāṇa — "because there is a banyan tree in the Puṣkara island, hence it is called Puṣkara" — with the Viṣṇu Purāṇa's "the banyan tree is in the Puṣkara country, that is the supreme abode of Brahman," and Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpinī 1.1: "that one Prajāpati was in the banyan-leaf."

On that last reading the compound turns round completely. Viṣṇu, asleep on the banyan leaf, is himself called Puṣkara; ईक्षण is then a compassionate look; and the nama means "she beholds him with compassion." The Devī Bhāgavata is quoted for the image — "adoration to Viṣṇu in the form of a boy asleep on a banyan leaf" — with the note that "in a half verse it is said that Devī is the giver of all things."

So an epithet for the shape of an eye becomes an account of who She is looking at. And a last reading takes पुष्कर as water with ईक्षण as "she looked," with the Śruti's four waters — "Devas, manes and Asuras" — which is the passage 927 स्तोत्रप्रिया used for its third division.

क्षण is also glossed separately, from the Amara: "leisure, a division of time, festivity."

Note on the verse. Nine namas, the longest in this batch, in two groups of four and five with the colophon between them.

797–800 are all about arts and essences, and they narrow: the kalās, poetry, the rasas, and then रस at its highest as the nectar of Brahman. 799's pun holds the group together — रसज्ञा is both the connoisseur of dramatic modes and the tongue.

800 then closes the eighth hundred, and the colophon it carries completes the kalā-scheme: with 700, 900 and 1000 in hand, the kalā-number is now known to run one ahead of the hundred at every surviving division-point.

801–805 are the प-run, and 805 is the entry to keep. Its Viśva-list of fifteen senses for पुष्कर is the widest in the text, and three of them are developed: a rare conjunction of sun in Viśākhā with moon in Kṛttikā; the earth as a lotus with the Mleccha lands for upper petals and the nāga-worlds for lower; and Viṣṇu asleep on a banyan leaf, at whom She is looking with compassion. The last inverts the compound — an eye-shape becomes an object of Her gaze.

---

## परंज्योतिः परंधाम परमाणुः परात्परा । पाशहस्ता पाशहन्त्री परमन्त्रविभेदिनी

*paraṃjyotiḥ paraṃdhāma paramāṇuḥ parātparā । pāśahastā pāśahantrī paramantravibhedinī*

Verse 153, namas 806–812.

806. परंज्योतिः → परम्-ज्योतिः

परम् = highest, supreme (परम, with the anusvāra in composition)
ज्योतिः = light, radiance; and per the commentary, illuminator (ज्योतिस्)
"The supreme Light."

Vigraha: परमं ज्योतिः यस्याः सा।

Three Upaniṣads are cited and all three deny light to the luminaries. Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.4.16: "that is the light of light." Kaṭha 5.15: "there no sun shines, nor moon, nor stars, nor these lightnings, nor the fire. The sun shines only when he is illumined by Him." Chāndogya 8.3.4: "the supreme light one attains."

Then a grammatical point: "Jyotis here means illuminator, for we see the same meaning given in such places as *the illuminator of the mind*," Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.9.10. So the nama names an agent and not a quality — which is the same reading पावन got at 619 पावनाकृतिः, purifying rather than pure, and दीपिका at 993, a lamp that makes things shine.

And a mantra: "Paraṃjyotis is the eight-syllabled mantra described in the fifth chapter of the Dakṣiṇāmūrti Saṃhitā." That is the same formula 583 आत्मविद्या names — "Ātmavidyā may mean the eight-syllabled Mantra" — so two namas of the thousand designate one mantra, and both do it in a single clause.

807. परंधाम → परम्-धाम

परम् = highest, supreme
धाम = an abode, a dwelling; also light, splendour; and per one reading, a state of consciousness (धामन्)
"The supreme Abode."

Vigraha: परमं धाम यस्याः सा।

Gītā 15.6 is the primary citation and it is the verse the nama is built from: "the sun never illumines That, nor moon, nor fire. After reaching it, when one does not return — that is my supreme abode." So 806 and 807 rest on the same claim, that the luminaries do not reach Her, and take from it the light and the place respectively.

Then धाम is taken as the states of consciousness, with परा as beyond — she is beyond the three states. Gauḍapāda 1.5: "the man who knows both the object of enjoyment as well as the enjoyer is never stained though he enjoys in the three states." And the Sūta Saṃhitā 4.11.32–33 at length: "he who knows the three states, namely waking, dreaming and sleeping — he is the Self; that is not the object, the object is superimposed upon that. I take refuge in the supreme abode which is the evidence of the three abodes, characterised by reality, wisdom, bliss, and is the meaning of the word 'I'."

That last clause is worth keeping: the supreme abode is what the word "I" means. It is the ahaṃtā of 854 पूर्णाहन्ता, 856 गर्विता and 576 मत्ता stated as a definition.

Kaṭha 3.9 supplies the plain sense — "that is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu" — and the Kūrma Purāṇa the identification: "my energy is Maheśvarī, Gaurī, spotless, tranquil, reality, knowledge, bliss, the supreme abode."

The three states return at 976 त्रिपुराम्बिका, where one reading makes the three पुर the अवस्थाः — waking, dream and deep sleep — of which She is mother. Beyond them here, their mother there.

**A grammatical note.** धाम is the neuter nominative of धामन्, and a feminine bahuvrīhi would give परंधामा. So the nama as it stands is not formally feminine — and the Paribhāṣā at 1000 counts only two neuter namas in the thousand, तत् and ब्रह्म. Either this is a third that the Paribhāṣā did not flag, or धाम is being treated as fixed in composition. The same question arises for 806 परंज्योतिः and 808 परमाणुः, though those two are less clear: a bahuvrīhi in -इस् or -उ can stand unchanged in the feminine, so both may be regular. परंधाम cannot be got at the same way, and the text offers no remark.

808. परमाणुः → परम-अणुः

परम = highest, supreme, ultimate
अणुः = an atom, a minute particle; and per the second reading, a mantra
"The ultimate Atom."

Vigraha: परमः अणुः।

Sandhi: परम + अणुः → परमाणुः (आ by 6.1.101).

Kaṭha 2.20 is cited — "more subtle than the atom" — and glossed with an inference rather than a measurement: "that is, difficult to know." So subtlety is read as inaccessibility, which is 554 अचिन्त्यरूपा's claim by another route.

Then the technical sense: "the Paramāṇus of the Logicians are her forms." परमाणु is the Vaiśeṣika ultimate particle, the indivisible from which dyads and triads are built — so the nama takes a term from a rival school's physics and makes the particles Hers. The text does the same at 958 धर्मिणी, where धर्म is taken in the logicians' sense as attribute rather than duty, and at 931 मानवती, where मान is a means of valid knowledge.

Or परम supreme with अणु a mantra — "aṇu, mantra" — which is the third nama in this verse to be read as designating a formula, after 806.

809. परात्परा → परात्-परा

परात् = than the higher (ablative of पर)
परा = higher, supreme
"Higher than the high."

Vigraha: परस्मात् अपि परा।

The compound keeps its case-ending, which is unusual: परात् is a live ablative inside the word, so the form is a frozen phrase rather than a compound proper — "higher than the higher."

The gloss identifies whom she exceeds: "she is supreme over Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra." Three of the five who are her couch at 947, her chain of command at 995, and her husband's three body-parts at 997.

Then a temporal reading, and it is the more interesting. परा is taken as the age of Brahmā, and she is beyond that — with the Kālī Purāṇa: "the day and night of Brahmā is called Parā; the half of that is called Parārdha. Such is the day to the Lord, so also the night. He who is grosser than the gross and subtler than the subtle has neither day nor night, nor years."

So परात्परा becomes a statement about time rather than rank, and the last clause pairs with 808's atom: grosser than the gross and subtler than the subtle, which is the two directions this verse has been travelling.

790 परापरा stood nineteen namas back with the same two words differently joined — परा and अपरा, the higher and the lower, the conditioned and unconditioned Brahman. Here it is the higher and the higher-still.

810. पाशहस्ता → पाश-हस्ता

पाश = a noose, a snare (from पश् "to bind")
हस्ता = handed, having in the hand (हस्त)
"She who holds the noose in her hand."

Vigraha: पाशः हस्ते यस्याः सा।

The gloss gives the position and then a second reading: "the noose is in her left lower hand; or she removes the bonds with her hand."

The position is exactly nama 8's. There, at रागस्वरूपपाशाढ्या, Bhāskararāya said the noose "she has in her lower left hand" and identified it as desire in its supreme form, with the Yoginīhṛdaya making it the Icchāśakti. So the same weapon is placed in the same hand eight hundred namas apart, and the placement agrees.

And the second reading turns the noose from a weapon into an instrument of release, which the next nama states outright.

811. पाशहन्त्री → पाश-हन्त्री

पाश = a noose, a bond
हन्त्री = she who slays, destroys (हन् "to strike" with the agent-suffix तृ and feminine ङीप्)
"The Destroyer of the noose."

Vigraha: पाशं हन्तीति पाशहन्त्री।

The Harivaṃśa is quoted, and it is the Aniruddha episode: "when she had burst the bonds of Aniruddha, who was bound by the serpent-noose which was like a thunderbolt, and who was distressed in mind, she addressed him, offering to confer boons on him."

That is the same story as 546 बन्धमोचनी, where Aniruddha in Bāṇa's town prays "by thy grace let me be soon freed from prison" and "Durgā, the powerful one, thus praised, set free the brave Aniruddha." So one episode supplies two namas two hundred and sixty apart, and both are about literal imprisonment.

810 and 811 make a pair of the kind the text likes: she holds the noose, and she destroys the noose. The device is 894–895's, where योनि was first denied of Her and then made her dwelling, and 870–871's with मुख.

हन्त्री is the तृ agent-noun of 557 कालहन्त्री, where what was slain was Time, and 599 दैत्यहन्त्री, where it was the demons.

812. परमन्त्रविभेदिनी → पर-मन्त्र-विभेदिनी

पर = another, hostile, an enemy; and per other readings, superior, and those who hate her devotees
मन्त्र = a mantra, a charm; also counsel, one of the royal powers
विभेदिनी = she who splits apart, shatters, divides (वि + भिद् "to cleave")
"She who shatters hostile charms."

Vigraha: परमन्त्रान् विभिनत्तीति।

index.html splits this entry mid-list, the gloss breaking off after "the council (Mantraśakti)" and the body resuming with "and armed force (Utsāhaśakti). Energy of lordship (Prabhuśakti)" — so the three royal powers are divided across the two fields.

The first reading is political. पर are "those who hate her devotees, that is, kings," and मन्त्र the royal energies: मन्त्रशक्ति the power of counsel, उत्साहशक्ति of armed force, प्रभुशक्ति of lordship. So the nama breaks the counsels of hostile kings, which puts it with 608 दण्डनीतिस्था, the science of chastisement, as the second nama in the text with a political reference.

The second is magical: "Parā, by enemies; mantra, the magical charms, or the mantras of the magical weapons" — with the Harivaṃśa, where Indra sends word about Pradyumna: "to destroy that weapon you must now remember Devī."

And the third is the substantial one. पर superior, मन्त्र the fifteen-syllabled mantra, विभेदिनी "she divides into twelve kinds" — and the Tantras are quoted for the twelve: **"Manu, Candra, Kubera, Lopāmudrā, Manmatha, Agastya, Agni, Sūrya, Nandi, Skanda, Śiva and Krodhabhaṭṭāraka" — Krodhabhaṭṭāraka being Durvāsa — "these twelve are the devotees of Devī."**

That list is the key to a set of namas the text otherwise leaves unexplained. Each of the twelve holds his own recension of the Pañcadaśī, and two of them are namas in their own right: 733 नन्दिविद्या, "the Vidyā worshipped by Nandi," whose whole commentary is five words; and 647 लोपामुद्रार्चिता, worshipped by Lopāmudrā, where Bhāskararāya's second reading made Lopāmudrā the mantra itself and prescribed performing all ceremonies "by the third division." So those two namas name two of the twelve recensions, and this nama names the scheme they belong to. Manmatha in the list is the Kāma of 586 कामसेविता, made the Ṛṣi of the vidyā by the Aruṇa Upaniṣad; Agastya is Lopāmudrā's husband; and Durvāsa is the author of the Lalitāstavaratna quoted at 686 and 785.

A fourth reading divides differently again: परा superior, मन्त्रि those who meditate on Her, अवि their sins, भेदिनी destroys — with the Liṅga Purāṇa on the word: "the word avi in the scriptures means sins, say the Brāhmaṇas. It is called Avimukta, freed from sins, because it is freed from that and freed also from illusion." So the name of Avimukta, the Kāśī precinct, is derived here in passing.

Note on the verse. Seven namas, five on पर- and two on पाश.

806–809 are a graded ascent of the superlative, and the interesting thing is how the four differ in what they exceed. 806 exceeds the luminaries; 807 exceeds the three states of consciousness; 808 exceeds the atom in the direction of smallness; 809 exceeds Brahmā's own day and night. Three Upaniṣads, one Gītā verse and one Purāṇa, and the last clause quoted — "grosser than the gross and subtler than the subtle" — names the two directions the verse has run in.

810–811 pair on पाश and reverse it: she holds the noose, she destroys the noose. And 810's placement of it in the lower left hand agrees exactly with nama 8, eight hundred namas earlier.

812 is the batch's most useful entry. Its third reading gives the twelve devotees who hold the twelve recensions of the Pañcadaśī — Manu, Candra, Kubera, Lopāmudrā, Manmatha, Agastya, Agni, Sūrya, Nandi, Skanda, Śiva, Durvāsa — and two of the twelve, Nandi and Lopāmudrā, are namas of this text whose commentaries do not explain themselves. This one does.

Textual note. 812's gloss and body split in the middle of the list of royal powers. 807's form परंधाम is the neuter nominative of धामन् where a feminine bahuvrīhi would give परंधामा, and the Paribhāṣā at 1000 counts only two neuter namas; the text does not remark on it.

---

## मूर्तामूर्तानित्यतृप्ता मुनिमानसहंसिका । सत्यव्रता सत्यरूपा सर्वान्तर्यामिणी सती

*mūrtāmūrtānityatṛptā munimānasahaṃsikā । satyavratā satyarūpā sarvāntaryāmiṇī satī*

Verse 154, namas 813–820.

813. मूर्ता → मूर्ता

मूर्ता = having form, embodied, material (past participle of मूर्छ् "to solidify")
"The Formed."

Vigraha: मूर्तिः अस्याः अस्तीति मूर्ता।

index.html has no commentary for this nama; the material stands under 814, where the pair is treated together.

814. अमूर्ता → अ-मूर्ता

अ = not (नञ्)
मूर्ता = having form, embodied
"The Formless."

Vigraha: मूर्ता न भवति इति अमूर्ता।

The dev field reads मूर्ता, identical with 813 — the initial अ has been lost to the sandhi मूर्ता + अमूर्ता → मूर्तामूर्ता (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101), and unlike the ten avagraha-namas the elision has left no mark at all. The gloss preserves the reading: "shapeless."

That is worth setting against the very next nama. 815's dev reads ऽनित्यतृप्ता, carrying an avagraha for exactly the same kind of elision at exactly the same kind of joint. So within one verse the text marks one swallowed अ and silently drops another — the avagraha convention that holds without exception across 50, 537, 554, 642, 729, 828, 926, 972, 985 and 988 is applied to one of these two joints and not the other. Where the mark is present it is reliable; its absence proves nothing.

Bhāskararāya gives three divisions of the pair, and all three are Upaniṣadic.

The elemental: "that which has form is called mūrta — earth, water and fire; amūrta means air and ether, which are formless." The physical: "mūrta, the five gross elements mingled with each other; amūrta, the subtle elements which are not mingled." Both are said to be the commentator's readings of Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.3.1, "Brahman has two forms, mūrta and amūrta." And the metaphysical, from the Viṣṇu Purāṇa: "that Brahman has two forms, mūrta and amūrta, these two respectively perishable and imperishable, and both are in all beings. The imperishable is the ever-remaining Brahman, the perishable is the whole Universe."

Then a flat rejection, which the commentary almost never makes: "the Logicians explain the word mūrta as that which has motion, but we should not adopt their theory, as it has no foundation."

That is the more striking four namas after 808 परमाणुः, where the Vaiśeṣika atoms were accepted as Her forms without demur. So the same school is borrowed from and dismissed within one verse-pair, and only the dismissal is argued.

The pair itself is the text's standing device — a term affirmed and denied across two adjacent namas, as at 651–652 with the knowable, 810–811 with the noose, 894–895 with the योनि, and 870–871 with the face. And 824 बहुरूपा had reconciled exactly this contradiction in advance: "she is formless because she is supreme, she is many-formed because of her activity."

815. अनित्यतृप्ता → अ-नित्य-तृप्ता

अ = not; and per one reading, part of अनिति, breath
नित्य = eternal, perpetual; and here, the imperishable — so अनित्य, the perishable
तृप्ता = satisfied, content (past participle of तृप् "to be satisfied")
"She who is satisfied with perishable offerings."

Vigraha: अनित्येन तृप्ता।

The dev field reads ऽनित्यतृप्ता, the avagraha marking the अ elided in अमूर्ता + अनित्यतृप्ता → अमूर्तानित्यतृप्ता (आ + अ → आ, 6.1.101). Eleventh instance of that class in the text, and the single mark again correctly signals a short vowel.

The primary reading is a doctrine of cheap worship: "because she is pleased only by devotion," with Gītā 9.26 — "he who offers with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water, I accept from the striving Self." So अनित्य, the perishable, means the humblest and most transient offerings, and the point is that they suffice. "Whatever is given with devotion gives her satisfaction."

That is the same leniency as 681–682, where worship needed no fasting and She did good "even to him who but imperfectly worships her," and 736 मुक्तिदा, where liberation came to those who recite "even unconsciously."

Then two re-divisions, and the first inverts the nama. अनिति taken as breath, hence the jīvas, with अतृप्ता not satisfied — she is not satisfied with the souls, on Kaṭha 2.25: "both Brāhmaṇa and Kṣatriya are Its food." So the nama of easy satisfaction becomes a nama of insatiable eating, which is 890 विश्वग्रासा and 752–753's pair on ग्रस् and अश्.

The second is grammatical and elegant: न + अतृप्ता, "here two negatives make the ordinary meaning forcible" — so she is pleased with everything, the double negation strengthening rather than cancelling.

तृप् is the root of तर्पण at 974 बिन्दुतर्पणसंतुष्टा, where the libation satisfied Her and the substance was graded by class, and of 566 नित्यतृप्ता — which is this nama without its privative, "eternally content." The two stand 249 apart and the negation is the only difference.

816. मुनिमानसहंसिका → मुनि-मानस-हंसिका

मुनि = a sage, an ascetic (from मन् "to think"; or from मौन, silence)
मानस = the mind (vṛddhi derivative of मनस्); and Lake Mānasa, the swans' summer home
हंसिका = a female swan or goose (हंस with the diminutive)
"The swan on the Mānasa lake of the sages' minds."

Vigraha: मुनीनां मानसे हंसिका।

The compound is built on a pun that works only in Sanskrit: मानस is the mind and also Lake Mānasa, to which the haṃsas migrate. So the sages' minds are the lake, and She is the bird that comes to it — one word doing both halves of the figure, which is why the compound needs no comparative particle.

A second reading divides differently: "Muni, of Munis; mana, to please; sahaṃsikā" — glossed as a dancer with bangles on the ankles — "that is, she takes delight in pleasing the Munis." So the swan becomes a dancer and the direction of pleasure reverses.

The swan has stood at 47 मरालीमन्दगमना, where her gait was a swan's and the word was मराली; and the haṃsa proper is the mantra स-ह at 672 ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी and 999, and the śakti Haṃsavatī at 525. Here it is a bird on a lake, and the lake is a mind.

817. सत्यव्रता → सत्य-व्रता

सत्य = truth; Brahman; and per one reading, giving results quickly
व्रता = vowed, observing a vow (व्रत)
"She whose vow is truth."

Vigraha: सत्यं व्रतं यस्याः सा।

Both the dev field and the verse text read सत्यत्रता, with त् where व् belongs — a letter fault in both places, and the commentary spells व्रत throughout, so the reading is not in doubt.

Four readings, and they range from the theological to the medical.

"Satya, Brahman alone; vrata, dear" — or truth alone is her vow, "attained by the vow of observing the utterances of truth." Or सत्य as "giving result quickly," so वows to Her are of that kind, with the Viṣṇu Bhāgavata Book 10: "to attain Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd girls made a vow to Devī and quickly obtained their desired objects." That is the gopīs' vow of 632 सिन्दूरतिलकाञ्चिता, where they address Kātyāyanī for a husband.

Or सत्यव्रत is what Rāma says in the Rāmāyaṇa Book VI, and the line is quoted as a definition of the word: "one who once approaches me with a request, *I am yours* — on him I confer fearlessness from all beings. This is my vow."

And then a reading nothing else in the text prepares for. On Śiva Sūtra 2.27, "the cure of the body is a vow," the commentator says: "to take care of the body, which is filled with the nectar of devotion to Śiva, is a vow that should be performed; hence the care of the body should not be neglected." Bhaṭṭotpala's prayer is quoted for it — "may this body, nourished by the nectar derived from the pure Śakti manifested in me, remain long to enjoy thy worship." So bodily health is a religious obligation, because the body is the instrument of worship. It is the only place the text says so.

Last, Satyavrata as a proper name, from the Devī Bhāgavata Book III, and the story is a good one: "there was a Brāhmaṇa named Satyavrata, illiterate, very foolish; hearing the syllable from the mouth of the boar, and repeating from that time this syllable without the final म्, in course of time became the best of the wise. By his merely uttering the word *ai*, Devī became pleased and made him the king of poets."

The syllable is ऐं, the Vāgbhava bīja — the boar's grunt *aiṃ* heard by a frightened illiterate, repeated without its anusvāra as ऐ, and it makes him a poet. That bīja is what 872 त्रयी derives by performing sandhi on the opening letters of the three Vedas, and what 110's third reading identifies with the kuṇḍalinī. Here it is got by accident.

818. सत्यरूपा → सत्य-रूपा

सत्य = truth, reality
रूपा = form; and per the second reading, protecting
"She whose form is truth."

Vigraha: सत्यं रूपं यस्याः सा।

सत्य is defined by duration: "that which persists throughout the three times." So truth here is what does not vary with time, which is the criterion 906 तत्त्वाधिका used for the tattvas — what lasts till the pralaya — raised one degree.

Then a second division takes रूप as "protects," and the Bahvṛcas are quoted for a pair: "Satya and Asatya are two opposites; of these two, Satya is that which is direct, that Soma cherishes, and he destroys the other." Soma is glossed as Śiva with Umā — which is the स + उमा reading of 910 सौम्या, where सोम was made "the one who has Umā with him" and the derivative सौम्या then meant that Śiva is a part of Her.

So the nama's second reading makes Her the protector of truth by way of a compound in which Her own presence is what makes Śiva Soma. And सत् and असत् were the poles She bore at 661 सदसद्रूपधारिणी and was devoid of at 680 भावाभावविवर्जिता.

819. सर्वान्तर्यामिणी → सर्व-अन्तर्-यामिणी

सर्व = all; all beings
अन्तर् = within, inside; and per the syllabic reading, अन्त the senses
यामिणी = she who controls, restrains, directs (from यम् "to hold, to restrain")
"She who governs from within all things."

Vigraha: सर्वेषाम् अन्तर्यामिणी।

Sandhi: सर्व + अन्तर् → सर्वान्तर् (आ by 6.1.101). The computed pada takes अन्तर्यामिणी as one member; the compound has three.

अन्तर्यामिन् is a fixed Vedāntic term — the inner controller — and Bhāskararāya's own division is slightly different: "Sarva, all beings; anta, the senses; yāminī, directs." So on his reading what she governs is the senses rather than the beings.

Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.7.3 is the antaryāmin passage: "this is thy Self which is within all and is immortal." Māṇḍūkya 6: "this is within all and is the origin of all." And Taittirīya 2.6.1 for the second reading, which makes अन्तर्यामिणी "entered in all": "having created that, he entered into it; after entering it, he became animate and inanimate."

Then the Smṛti's etymology of सर्व, which is a real derivation and not a gloss: "because She always knows the beginning and the end of everything, and as she creates being and non-being, She is called Sarva."

यम् is the root of 568 नियन्त्री, where the guidance was a checking and She was "the guide of the universe" — and 995 सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना, where Her command may not be overstepped. Here the government is interior.

820. सती → सती

सती = existing, real; a virtuous woman, a faithful wife (feminine present participle of अस् "to be")
"The Faithful — and the Real."

Vigraha: सती साध्वी। or सती सत्यरूपा।

The word is the feminine participle of अस्, to be — so "a good wife" and "one who is" are the same form, and the nama holds both. Bhāskararāya says so in three words: "or Satī, reality."

Then the proper name: "this is the name of the daughter of Dakṣa." And the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa on the identity of the two births: "she who was before, Devī, the faithful spouse Satī, became Umā; she ever dwells with Śiva, and he is never deserted by her."

That closes the Satī–Pārvatī thread the text carries in pieces. 5 देवकार्यसमुद्यता has Her own account of the second birth, "disregarding my father Dakṣa who insulted Maheśvara my husband... I was born from the body of Menā, having chosen you as my father"; 598 दाक्षायणी names her Dakṣa's daughter and 600 दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी the destroyer of his sacrifice; 635 गौरी has her "burned by the fire of Yoga and again born of Himālaya"; and 754 अपर्णा has her renouncing even leaves in tapas. This nama names the first of the two lives and asserts that they are one person.

सत् closes the verse as it opened its second half — सत्यव्रता, सत्यरूपा, सर्वान्तर्यामिणी, सती, four namas of which three are built on अस्.

Note on the verse. Eight namas in two halves of four, म- then स-.

813–814 are the affirm-and-deny pair, and 824 बहुरूपा had already supplied the resolution: formless because supreme, many-formed because active. What this entry adds is the outright rejection of the Naiyāyika definition of मूर्त — "we should not adopt their theory, as it has no foundation" — four namas after 808 accepted the same school's atoms as Her forms.

815 is the leniency-nama of the batch, and its Gītā citation is the standard authority for cheap worship: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water. Then its own second reading turns it into insatiability by reading अनिति as breath and अतृप्ता as unsatisfied.

816's pun is the neatest compound in the batch — मानस being both mind and the swans' lake, so the figure needs no comparative.

And 817 carries two things worth keeping: the Śiva Sūtra's vow that the body must be cared for, which no other nama in the text supports; and Satyavrata the illiterate, who heard a boar grunt *aiṃ*, repeated it without the anusvāra, and became king of poets — the Vāgbhava bīja got by accident where 872 gets it by sandhi.

Textual note. Both the dev field and the verse text of 817 read सत्यत्रता for सत्यव्रता. 814's dev reads मूर्ता, its initial अ lost with no avagraha, while 815's carries one for the same kind of elision at the adjacent joint — so the marking convention is applied unevenly within a single verse. 819's computed pada merges अन्तर् with यामिणी. 813 has no commentary body.

The verse text also carries a stray numeral, "२१", immediately after the daṇḍa. It is not a verse number — verse 154 is not twenty-one — and it belongs to none of the namas; it looks like a page or section figure absorbed from the printed page. That is a different fault from the verse-number contamination at 722, 763 and 830, where a genuine verse number entered a nama's dev field.

---

Textual note for verses 151–154.

**A fourth colophon, and the kalā-scheme is now complete.** Nama 800 रसशेवधिः carries in its body: "thus ends in the Saubhāgyabhāskara composed by Bhāsurānanda the ninth Kalā called Viśva, with the eighth hundred," followed by "The Ninth Hundred." With the three already known — 700 (eighth Kalā, Bhogadā, seventh hundred), 900 (Bodhinī, ninth hundred), 1000 (eleventh Kalā, Dhāriṇī, tenth hundred) — the pattern is fixed: the kalā-number runs exactly one ahead of the hundred it closes, so Bodhinī at 900 is the tenth. Four of the ten division-points survive, all in the last four hundreds.

**The avagraha convention is applied unevenly inside one verse.** 814 अमूर्ता has lost its initial अ with no mark at all; 815 अनित्यतृप्ता carries an avagraha for the same elision at the adjacent joint. So the rule established across 50, 537, 554, 642, 729, 828, 926, 972, 985 and 988 — single ऽ for a short अ, double for a long आ — holds wherever the mark appears, but the mark's absence is not evidence that no vowel was swallowed. 815 is the eleventh instance of the marked class.

**Letter fault:** 817's dev and verse text both read सत्यत्रता for सत्यव्रता, त् for व्. Unusually, the fault is in both fields at once; the commentary's own spelling corrects it.

**A stray numeral in the verse text:** verse 154 carries "२१" after the daṇḍa, belonging to no nama and matching no verse number — a printed page or section figure absorbed into the line. Distinct from the verse-number-in-dev fault at 722, 763 and 830.

**Split fields:** 793's gloss and body divide in the middle of a sentence ("...sanctifies. His | matted hair sanctifies even the water of the Gaṅgā"). 812's divide in the middle of the list of royal powers. 791's body carries a footnote belonging to nama 790, noting that Bhāskararāya "does not show the reason how the Parāparā is to be taken as four."

**Computed pada:** most fields in this range are empty, the namas being short. 819 merges अन्तर् with यामिणी; 807's परम् is the anusvāra form rather than the stem.

**Empty bodies:** only 813, which is covered by 814. This is the best-preserved stretch of thirty namas in the text — every other nama here has commentary, several of it substantial, and there is not a single instance of the visarga mis-division that runs through 537–541, 848–849, 894–895, 992–993, 615–617, 628–629, 662–663 and 748–749.

**A grammatical query.** Three namas in verse 153 are formally non-feminine: 806 परंज्योतिः (ज्योतिस्, neuter), 807 परंधाम (धामन्, neuter), 808 परमाणुः (परमाणु, masculine). Bahuvrīhis in -इस् and -उ can stand unchanged in the feminine, so 806 and 808 may be regular; परंधाम cannot be got that way, since a feminine bahuvrīhi of धामन् would give परंधामा. The Paribhāṣā at 1000 counts only two neuter namas in the thousand, तत् and ब्रह्म, and this is not among them. Either the list is of namas whose gender a reciter might otherwise mistake rather than of every non-feminine form, or 807 is an unflagged third. The same question was raised at 48 महालावण्यशेवधिः, where शेवधि is masculine and *is* counted, while 567 भक्तनिधिः, 604 गुणनिधिः and 800 रसशेवधिः have the same ending and only 604 is listed.

## भवानी भावनागम्या भवारण्यकुठारिका । भद्रप्रिया भद्रमूर्तिः भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी

*bhavānī bhāvanāgamyā bhavāraṇyakuṭhārikā । bhadrapriyā bhadramūrtiḥ bhaktasaubhāgyadāyinī*

Verse 41, namas 112–117.

> **This is where the text turns from what She is to how She is reached, and Bhāskararāya says so at 113**: "having described the five forms, he describes by a few names the means of reaching them." The five forms are namas 1–5, the five functions his closing note at 1000 identifies as belonging to no other deity. So the thousand has a five-nama head, and the body opens at 112 with the means.
>
> **And the seventy-odd namas that follow are the most systematic philosophy in the text.** At 133 he announces a second programme — the nature of pure intellect determined "by assertion, by negation, by positive definition, and by elimination of attributes; then the means of obtaining it, and the real nature of the results thereby produced" — and at 156 a third, "to reject the theory that the differences in the mind belong to the Self, and to teach that renunciation is the means of overcoming the six impediments." The great नि-run of verses 43–49 executes both, and along the way it names and refutes eight rival schools. Nothing else in the Sahasranāma is built this deliberately.

112. भवानी → भव-आनी

भव = Śiva as Bhava; also worldly existence, saṃsāra; also Manmatha; and per the Liṅga and Vāyu Purāṇas, Śiva's water-form
आनी = the feminine formant of consorts' names — आनुक् with ङीष् (Pāṇini 4.1.49)
"Bhavānī — the consort of Bhava."

Vigraha: भवस्य पत्नी भवानी। or भवाय अनं ददातीति।

The formation is the one Pāṇini 4.1.49 provides for: a closed list of words — इन्द्र, वरुण, भव, शर्व, रुद्र, मृड and the rest — takes the आनुक् augment before the feminine ङीष्. So भवानी here, शर्वाणी at 124 twelve namas on, and मृडानी at 564 are three members of one Pāṇinian list standing as three namas of the text, and the augment is why none of them is *भवी.

Bhāskararāya's readings turn on how many things भव means. The Devī Purāṇa gives three at once — "Bhava means Rudra, Kāma, the ocean of saṃsāra; Devī is called Bhavānī because she gives life to the above" — taking आनी from अन्, to breathe, so that She animates all three.

Then the water-reading, from the Liṅga and Vāyu Purāṇas: "the water form of Śiva, one of his eight forms, is called Bhava; his wife is Uṣā and his son Śukra." And the Vāyu Purāṇa's etymology — "because all beings came from him and subsist in water, as he is the origin and supporter of all beings, he is called Bhava" — makes Her "the giver of life to Bhava, water."

Those eight forms of Śiva are the set 662 अष्टमूर्तिः lists and 883 यजमानस्वरूपिणी turns on, where the eighth is "sometimes the sacrificer and sometimes Ātman." Here the first is named and given a wife and a son.

And the Padma Purāṇa places her: "in the chapter enumerating the hundred and eight places of pilgrimage, she is said to be the presiding deity of the place called Sthāneśvara."

**A third count of the sacred places.** 833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी argued for fifty-one pīṭhas; 793 कपर्दिनी gave Chagalaṇḍa as one of sixty-eight; here the Padma Purāṇa enumerates a hundred and eight. Three enumerations in the text and no attempt anywhere to reconcile them.

भव is the word the text uses for saṃsāra at 114 two namas on, at 842 भवरोगघ्नी, 843 भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी, 742 भवदावसुधावृष्टिः and 174–175; and Bhavānī herself is one quarter of Her at 893 विष्णुरूपिणी, where the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa divides the ancient Śakti into four — "that Śakti becomes Bhavānī in her ordinary form, in battle she takes the form of Durgā, in anger that of Kālī, and she is also my male form."

113. भावनागम्या → भावना-गम्या

भावना = meditation, contemplation, the act of forming in the mind (from भू "to be," causative भावय्)
गम्या = to be reached, attainable (गम् with the gerundive यत्); and per the second reading, अगम्या, unattainable
"She who is to be attained by meditation."

Vigraha: भावनया गम्या।

This is the longest commentary in the verse and it is a taxonomy of meditation, given four ways.

**Two kinds by object.** "There are two kinds of meditation, one on the words themselves (śabda) and the other on the meanings (artha)" — words meaning "sacred words which are to be meditated upon according to the will of the Guru," and meanings being "tending towards action," the relations of cause and effect. Bhāskararāya refers to his own Mīmāṃsākavādakautūhala for both.

**The negative reading.** "The word gamya may be taken as agamya, unattainable. Or, She is unattainable by the path of action" — so the nama's gerundive is reversed, and what is denied is the karmamārga specifically. That distinction between works and meditation is the one 960 लोकातीता draws topographically, where the city of Śiva is reached by works and does not hold while the three seats above it are reached by meditation and do; and 980 ज्ञानगम्या's Kūrma Purāṇa says the supreme abode "is to be attained through much difficulty."

**Three kinds by name**, from the Kūrma Purāṇa: "there are three forms of meditation, Brāhmī, Māheśvarī and Akṣara; these three always reside in Rudra." And the same Purāṇa again, in the tortoise incarnation speaking to Indradyumna: "one is concerning me, akṣara; the second is upon the unmanifested, Māheśvara; the last is on Brahman with the three attributes." Bhāskararāya sends the reader to Appayya Dīkṣita's Ratnatrayaparīkṣā for the characteristics.

That triad returns at 907 तत्त्वमयी, where the three kinds of bhāvanā — Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Akṣara — are one of the four resolutions offered for the contradiction between 906 and 907.

**Three states by station**, on Yoginīhṛdaya 1.27, and this is the one that has consequences: "meditation from Mūlādhāra to Ājñā is Sakala; from Indu to Unmanī is Sakalaniṣkala; in the supreme abode, Mahābindu, is Niṣkala."

Those three stations are exactly the three grades of soul that 133–135 will use. Bhāskararāya's own Setubandha, quoted at 134, says: "Sakala is he who worships Devī from Mūlādhāra to Ājñā; Pralayākala, who worships from Ājñā to Unmanī; and Niṣkala or Vijñānakevala worships Devī in the supreme abode, Mahābindu." So the three meditations here and the three bound souls twenty namas on are one scheme seen from two ends — the practice and the practitioner.

114. भवारण्यकुठारिका → भव-अरण्य-कुठारिका

भव = worldly existence, saṃsāra
अरण्य = a forest, a wilderness
कुठारिका = a small axe, a hatchet (कुठार with the diminutive क and feminine आ)
"She who is the axe to the forest of worldly existence."

Vigraha: भवारण्यस्य कुठारिका।

Sandhi: भव + अरण्य → भवारण्य (आ by 6.1.101).

index.html has no commentary for this nama, which is remarkable given how much work the compound does elsewhere.

It is the text's founding metaphor for saṃsāra and it is recycled twice. At 743 पापारण्यदवानला the forest is sin and the instrument is a wildfire; at 749 मृत्युदारुकुठारिका this same कुठारिका — the same diminutive, a hand-axe — is applied to the timber of death, and there Bhāskararāya reads दारु by Vararuci's numeral system as twenty-eight. Both of those belong to the eight-nama simile-set at 742–749 which the commentary marks as rūpakālaṅkāra; so this nama, stated flatly and without comment, is the model those eight are built on.

The other metaphors for saṃsāra are a disease at 842, a wheel She herself turns at 843, and a bog requiring skill at 880 संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणपण्डिता.

115. भद्रप्रिया → भद्र-प्रिया

भद्र = auspicious, good, blessed; and per the commentary, a kind of elephant
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in the auspicious."

Vigraha: भद्रं प्रियं यस्याः सा।

The whole commentary is one clause: "or Bhadra may mean a kind of elephant."

This is the first of the text's twelve प्रिया-namas, and the range its objects cover is worth having in one place: the auspicious here, sacrifice at 881, the learned at 887, the heroes' assembly at 898, the Sāman at 909, the flower of consciousness at 919, hymns at 927, the strong or the oblation at 677, the pāṭalī at 773, the mandāra at 776, vows at 770, and the Guru at 722.

116. भद्रमूर्तिः → भद्र-मूर्तिः

भद्र = auspicious
मूर्तिः = form, embodiment
"She whose form is the auspicious."

Vigraha: भद्रा मूर्तिः यस्याः सा।

Both the dev field and the verse text read भद्रमूर्ति, the visarga lost. index.html also carries the whole of nama 117's commentary in this nama's body, opening "117. Conferring prosperity on the devotees" — so the two entries are displaced by one and 117's own fields hold only a division-marker.

The nama is 933 मङ्गलाकृतिः in different words — भद्र with मूर्ति here, मङ्गल with आकृति there, both saying that Her very form is auspiciousness, and stated twice eight hundred namas apart. मूर्ति for the first of six times; and 967 सुमङ्गली, 972 आशोभना and 682 शुभकरी carry the same claim on three further stems.

117. भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी → भक्त-सौभाग्य-दायिनी

भक्त = a devotee (from भज् "to worship")
सौभाग्य = good fortune, prosperity, marital happiness (vṛddhi derivative of सुभग)
दायिनी = she who gives, bestower (दा + णिनि, feminine ङीप्)
"She who confers prosperity on her devotees."

Vigraha: भक्तानां सौभाग्यं ददातीति।

The commentary stands in 116's body. Its substance is the range of भग and the identification that follows from it.

The Agni Purāṇa gives seven senses: "fortune, desire, magnanimity, strength, effort, sun, and fame." And then the identification, which is the point: "सुभग — Lalitā herself. Saubhāgyas are her qualities; she unites them with herself." So what She bestows is not something she has but something she is, extended to the devotee. सुभगा is a nama in its own right at 761, where Dhaumya makes it a girl of five and the Viśva gives भग twelve senses; and भग is the sun's disc at 715 भगाराध्या.

The Padma Purāṇa then supplies a quite different reading — a list of eight substances: "sugarcane, pārijāta, niṣpā and vājīra seeds, cow's milk with its changes, the saffron-coloured things, flower, and salt: thus the eight things are called Saubhāgyāṣṭaka," because these are used on auspicious occasions. So the abstract noun becomes a shopping-list of ritual materials.

Or simply सु much with भाग्य luck.

दायिनी for the first of eight times, and what She gives escalates across them: good fortune here, rest to the scorched at 851, the priceless state of kaivalya at 926, whatever is wished for at 989.

Bhāskararāya also drops a division-marker: "nine names are divided according to the Chchalākṣara Sūtras," and "from 109 to..." — the sentence broken where the field ends.

Note on the verse. Six namas, five on भ, and the verse is the hinge of the whole text.

113 is where the description of the five forms ends and the means begin, and Bhāskararāya marks it in one clause. What follows in that nama is the fullest taxonomy of meditation in the text — two kinds by object, three by name, three by station — and the three stations, Sakala / Sakalaniṣkala / Niṣkala, are the scheme that 133–135 will use for the three grades of bound soul.

114 states the saṃsāra-as-forest metaphor without a word of comment, and it is the model for the eight-nama simile-set at 742–749.

And 112 gives the text's third count of sacred places, a hundred and eight, against 793's sixty-eight and 833's fifty-one.

Textual note. 116's dev and verse text both lack the visarga of भद्रमूर्तिः, and 116's body carries the whole of 117's commentary, leaving 117 with only a division-marker. 112's gloss and body are duplicates. 114 has no commentary body.

---

## भक्तिप्रिया भक्तिगम्या भक्तिवश्या भयापहा । शांभवी शारदाराध्या शर्वाणी शर्मदायिनी

*bhaktipriyā bhaktigamyā bhaktivaśyā bhayāpahā । śāmbhavī śāradārādhyā śarvāṇī śarmadāyinī*

Verse 42, namas 118–125.

118. भक्तिप्रिया → भक्ति-प्रिया

भक्ति = devotion, a share, participation (from भज् "to share, to worship")
प्रिया = dear to, fond of
"She who delights in devotion."

Vigraha: भक्तिः प्रिया यस्याः सा।

This is the text's definition of भक्ति, and it is technical.

Two kinds first: "primary, mukhya, and secondary, gauṇa. Primary devotion is a particular mental modification called *longing* directed towards Īśvara." The Śāṇḍilya Sūtra 1.2 is cited — "devotion is supreme longing for the Lord" — and Bhāskararāya notes what the word परा in that sūtra implies: "according to the commentator, that there is another kind." The secondary is service, on Śāṇḍilya 1.20, "the attainment of concentration is by gauṇī," with the Garuḍa Purāṇa's root-argument: "the root भज् is repeated in the service, so service is declared by the wise to be an important means."

Then the counts, and they multiply. The Āditya and Garuḍa Purāṇas: "devotion is of eight kinds — even if found in a barbarian, he is best of Brāhmaṇas, he is a sannyāsin, he is prosperous, he is an ascetic and he is a learned man." The Viṣṇu Bhāgavata: nine kinds. The Bṛhannāradīya: "ten kinds of devotion should be known; they are like a conflagration to the forest of sin." And Bhāskararāya's conclusion is inclusive rather than adjudicating: "so there are many kinds of bhakti like the above which should be known. All these are here included in the word Bhakti."

That is the same procedure as 946 पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया, where six competing sets of five sacrifices are listed and none preferred — the number varies, the word covers all of them.

And the Bṛhannāradīya's simile — devotion a conflagration to the forest of sin — is 743 पापारण्यदवानला's compound exactly, where She is the wildfire consuming the forest of sin.

The Śiva Purāṇa closes the entry with a line about what worship is for: "what can mortals do for me, who is ever satisfied and who has accomplished his end? But whatever they do by devotion, externally or internally, I receive." Bhāskararāya also marks the verse: (41).

119. भक्तिगम्या → भक्ति-गम्या

भक्ति = devotion; and per the second reading, a characteristic mark, लक्षण
गम्या = to be reached, attainable; also to be obtained; and per the second reading, to be known
"She who is to be approached by devotion."

Vigraha: भक्त्या गम्या।

The longest entry of the verse, and the first half is an argument that the unmanifest becomes perceptible through devotion.

Kaṭha 4.1 opens it: "the self-existent constrains the senses which turn to external objects; therefore man sees the external objects, not the internal self; but the wise, with eye averted and desirous of immortality, behold the inner self." That is the verse 781 प्रत्यग्रूपा rests on, where the technical vocabulary of अन्तर्मुखत्व against बहिर्मुखत्व is set out.

Then Yoga Sūtra 1.23, "by meditation also upon Īśvara," where the Rājamārtaṇḍa "explains meditation as devotion"; and Vedānta Sūtra 3.2.24, "and in the state of perfect conciliation also the Yogins apprehend the highest Brahman, according to Śruti and Smṛti." Bhāskararāya's gloss: "although Brahman is unmanifest, it becomes perceptible through devotion."

Gītā 11.54 is then quoted for the strongest form of the claim — "by undeviated devotion I may thus be perceived, Arjuna, and known and seen and entered in essence" — with the note that "entered means Salvation, the attainment of Brahman itself, that is to be attained by Devotion alone."

गम्य is then read as "to be obtained" rather than "to be reached," on Chāndogya 2.23.2's "one who resides in the Brahman obtains immortality," where "the word *reside* means devotion"; with Śāṇḍilya 1.4 and Vedānta Sūtra 1.1.4 both cited as saying "of him who is engaged in that, immortality is declared."

The Nityā Tantra supplies the practical form, and its emphasis falls on the teacher: "one who places reliance on the Guru whose characteristics have been already described, and in his teachings, and in the practice taught by him, which destroys the doubts of his mind — thus the devotion which gives everything is the cause of crossing the ocean of saṃsāra and making one firm. Devoid of which, men surely suffer here and hereafter."

And then a wholly different division. भक्ति taken as लक्षण, a defining characteristic, with गम्य as "to be known" — "because the words *satya*, *jñāna* and the rest, each with its own meaning, cannot describe the unqualified Brahman directly." The Triśatī's nama 73 is cited for the same reading, and "in a certain Sūtra of Jaimini the word bhakti is explained as characteristics."

That is a real philosophical point and it bears on 791 सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा, where the Taittirīya formula सत्यं ज्ञानम् is the nama's plain sense: the words do not describe Brahman, they mark it.

Bhāskararāya closes with his own Śivastava and a proverb: "O Lord, I have no power to praise even an atom of your greatness, yet resting on imperfect devotion to you I composed this hymn. *The couch never cries* — so in the world, O Paramaśiva, men succeed by devotion and not by their own power."

This is the first of the four गम्या-namas, and the four differ only in the means: भक्ति here, भावना at 113, ध्यान at 641 ध्यानगम्या, ज्ञान at 980 ज्ञानगम्या.

120. भक्तिवश्या → भक्ति-वश्या

भक्ति = devotion
वश्या = to be controlled, subject to (from वश् "to will, to subdue," gerundive यत्)
"She who is subdued by devotion."

Vigraha: भक्त्या वश्या।

The whole commentary is one quoted line, and it is the point: "O Śiva, though independent, thou art become subservient by devotion."

That is a strong claim placed without argument. 723 स्वतन्त्रा makes Her independent — "as she creates without depending on instruments" — and this nama makes the independence conditional on nobody's devotion. वश्या is the gerundive of the वशम् in वशंकरी at 697 and 978, where She brings all the worlds and the fifth enclosure's deity under control; here the direction reverses.

121. भयापहा → भय-अपहा

भय = fear (from भी "to fear")
अपहा = removing, taking away (अप + हा "to abandon," or अप + हन्)
"The Remover of fear."

Vigraha: भयम् अपहन्तीति भयापहा।

Sandhi: भय + अपहा → भयापहा (आ by 6.1.101).

Taittirīya 2.9.1: "by knowing the bliss of Brahman none fears anything." And then the Vāyu Purāṇa, whose list is entirely practical: "in the forest and other places, in water, on earth, in the presence of a tiger, and before wild beasts and robbers, and specially in all difficulties and diseases, the names of Devī should be repeated."

So the nama's authority is one Upaniṣadic line about fearlessness and one rubric for what to do when frightened. Fear is what solitude produced at 665 एकाकिनी's Bṛhadāraṇyaka citation — "he feared; therefore any one who is lonely fears" — and what Her face does not show at the dissolution, per 924's third reading of दर.

122. शांभवी → शांभवी

शांभवी = belonging to Śambhu; Śiva's consort (vṛddhi derivative of शम्भु, feminine ङीप्)
"Śāmbhavī."

Vigraha: शम्भोः पत्नी शांभवी।

index.html splits this entry mid-sentence, the gloss ending "according to the Yoga Śāstra" and the body opening "it means a Mudrā which is there explained."

Three senses. The wife of Śiva; or "the mother of the devotees of Śambhu."

Then the Śāmbhavī mudrā, defined by the Yoga Śāstra in a formula that is deliberately paradoxical: "the object is within, the sight without closing or opening the eyes is outside — this is called Śāmbhavī mudrā, concealed in all the Tantras." Eyes neither shut nor open, attention inward and gaze outward. That is 781 प्रत्यग्रूपा's inwardness given a bodily technique.

Then the initiations, from Paraśurāma's Kalpa Sūtra 1.32: "there are three initiations — Śāktī, Śāmbhavī and Mantrī," with characteristics given there in detail. And the Devī Bhāgavata's girl-age: "a girl of eight years is called Śāmbhavī."

**That completes the girl-age series to six.** Sarasvatī is two (704), Trimūrti three (628), Subhagā five (761), Caṇḍikā seven (755), Śāmbhavī eight here, Gaurī ten (635) — and Durgā nine at 190, eight verses on. So seven namas of the thousand double as ages in the kumārī-pūjā reckoning, and with Durgā the sequence 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 is nearly continuous.

शम्भु is शम् well-being with भू, so Śāmbhavī is built on the same शम् as शर्मदायिनी three namas on and शमात्मिका at 963.

123. शारदाराध्या → शारदा-आराध्या

शारदा = Śāradā, Sarasvatī; also autumnal, of the autumn or the rainy season (vṛddhi derivative of शरद्); also the clear-minded; also, per the Anekārthadhvanimañjarī, Viṣṇu and Brahmā
आराध्या = to be worshipped (आ + राध्, gerundive यत्)
"She who is worshipped by Śāradā."

Vigraha: शारदया आराध्या।

Sandhi: शारदा + आराध्या → शारदाराध्या (आ by 6.1.101).

Five readings, and they divide on whether शारदा is a person or a season.

As a person: "Śāradā, Sarasvatī, and the deities of speech." As a season: "she is to be worshipped in the spring, or in the rainy season," with the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa — "she should be worshipped in the spring and in the rainy season" — and the Rudrayāmala, "the Raktadaṇḍikā should be worshipped during the nine days in spring." As persons again: "śārada, the clear-minded men"; or the Medinīkośa's sense, one of the āśramas called Sālīna; or the Anekārthadhvanimañjarī's, "Vāsudeva and Brahmā," so that She is worshipped by Viṣṇu and Brahmā.

And the Kālikā Purāṇa's etymology, which makes the name a record of an event: "once upon a time in spring, on the ninth day, you were awakened by the devas; hence you are known in the world, as well as in the seat, by the name Śāradā."

आराध्या for the first of nine times in the text, and the worshippers named across them are a good index of its range: Śāradā here, the inward-faced at 870, consciousness-as-oblation at 918, the adept and the inept at 923, the ten mudrās at 977, nobody in particular at 681, the sun's disc at 715, the heroes at 777, Mārtāṇḍabhairava at 785.

124. शर्वाणी → शर्व-आणी

शर्व = Śarva, Śiva — and specifically, per the Liṅga and Vāyu Purāṇas, Śiva in his earth-form
आणी = the feminine formant आनुक् with ङीष्, the न् retroflexed to ण् after र् (Pāṇini 8.4.2)
"Śarvāṇī — the consort of Śarva."

Vigraha: शर्वस्य पत्नी शर्वाणी।

index.html's gloss and body are duplicates. The whole content is one citation: "she is the wife of Śiva whose body is the Earth. The Liṅga and Vāyu Purāṇas say: Śiva is called Śarva in his earth form, his wife Sukeśī and his son Aṅgāraka."

So this nama and 112 भवानी are the same Purāṇic passage twice — there Bhava is the water-form with Uṣā for wife and Śukra for son, here Śarva is the earth-form with Sukeśī and Aṅgāraka. Two of Śiva's eight forms, twelve namas apart, each with a household. And the ṇatva that gives शर्वाणी its ण is the same rule that gives ब्रह्माणी its ण at 821.
